Title: SEO foundation — metadata, robots, sitemap, OG image
Description:
pfa is a private tool and does no SEO. WorldWeathr is public, so it gets a proportionate pass — the cheap 90%, not an optimisation project.

## Scope

* Next Metadata API in the root layout: `metadataBase` (`https://worldweathr.com`), title template, description, `lang="en"`
* Canonical URLs
* Open Graph + Twitter card
* A **static OG image** built from the Aurora palette ([WEA-9](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-9/design-system-colour-elevation-and-aurora-tokens)) — a generated `opengraph-image` route is fine, but keep it static rather than per-page
* `app/robots.ts`
* `app/sitemap.ts` listing only genuinely public routes
* Every authenticated route exports `robots: { index: false }`

## Watch out

The default for this app is **not indexable**. Only `/` (logged out), `/login`, `/signup` and `/recover` are public. Today, Stats, History and Community are behind an identity and must carry `index: false` — a leaked Community board in search results would expose handles and cities we never intended to publish.

The landing-page *content* is a separate ticket (WEA-31, M2) — there is nothing worth writing prose about until guests can actually do something.

## Done when

* `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` resolve and list the right things
* An OG debugger renders the card correctly
* `curl` on an authenticated route shows the noindex directive

Spec: §12
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Auth endpoints — login, logout, me, csrf
Description:
The rest of the auth surface, ported from `pfa/nest-api/src/users/users.controller.ts`.

## Scope

```
POST   /api/auth/login    → { user, csrfToken }
POST   /api/auth/logout   → { ok }
GET    /api/auth/me       → { user, csrfToken }
GET    /api/auth/csrf     → { csrfToken }
```

* **login** — verify with bcrypt, `clearSessionsForUser`, set `req.session.userId`, `rotateCsrfToken`
* **logout** — `clearCsrfToken`, `session.destroy`, `res.clearCookie('ww.sid')`, guarded by `CsrfGuard`
* **me** — `SessionAuthGuard`, returns the user plus `getOrCreateCsrfToken`
* **csrf** — `SessionAuthGuard`, refresh endpoint the front retries against after a 403

## Watch out

Login must fail **identically** for an unknown email and a wrong password — same status, same message, and ideally comparable timing. Distinguishing them turns the login form into an account-enumeration oracle, which matters more here than usual because the recovery flow is passphrase-based and an attacker who knows an email exists has a concrete next step.

`GET /auth/me` is the front's session probe on every load. It must be cheap and must never 500 on an expired session — 401 is the contract the client's redirect logic depends on.

## Done when

* e2e: login → me → logout → me returns 401
* e2e: logout without the CSRF header returns 403
* e2e: unknown email and wrong password are indistinguishable in the response

Spec: §6, §9
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Passphrase recovery endpoint
Description:
`POST /api/auth/recover`. **No email is sent, ever** — the passphrase set at signup is the recovery factor.

## Scope

`RecoverDto` — `email`, `passphrase`, `newPassword`, `confirmNewPassword`.

1. Look up the user by email
2. Verify `passphraseHash` with bcrypt
3. Hash and store the new password
4. `clearSessionsForUser` — destroy every live session for that account
5. Return `{ ok: true }` and nothing else

## Watch out

This endpoint is a full account-takeover primitive by design. Three things follow from that and none are optional:

* **Step 4 is not a nicety.** If an attacker had a session, rotating the password without destroying sessions leaves them logged in — the recovery would accomplish nothing.
* **Respond identically** whether the email is unknown or the passphrase is wrong. Any difference makes this a two-stage oracle: enumerate emails here, then brute-force the passphrase.
* **Do not** log the request body, and do not return which field failed.

Rate limiting is the real defence and lands in M6 (WEA-49). Note in the PR that until then this endpoint is brute-forceable, so it should not be exposed publicly before M6 ships — or pull WEA-49 forward.

The spec records this whole trade-off as accepted (§6): a leaked passphrase is a takeover with no mailbox check standing in the way. This ticket implements the decision, it does not relitigate it.

## Done when

* e2e: recover → old password rejected, new password works
* e2e: a session opened before recovery is dead afterwards
* e2e: unknown email and wrong passphrase produce identical responses

Spec: §6
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: AuthContext, getServerSession and route-group guards
Description:
Client-side auth plumbing, ported from `pfa/front/src/auth/`.

## Scope

* `AuthProvider` / `useAuth` holding `{ user, csrfToken }` with `setUser`, `setCsrfToken`, `setAuthState`, `clearAuth`
* `getServerSession()` — a server-side `GET /auth/me` forwarding the incoming cookie, used to hydrate the provider with `initialUser` / `initialCsrfToken`
* Route groups: `(public)`, `onboarding`, `(private)`
* `(private)` layout redirects to `/login` when there is no identity, and to `/onboarding` when `onboardedAt` is null
* `SessionWatcher` — reacts to a session dying while the tab is open

## Watch out

Hydrating from the server is what stops the app flashing a logged-out shell on every load. The provider must receive the user **as props from a server component**, not fetch it in a client `useEffect`.

The `onboardedAt` redirect has to be resilient to loops: `/onboarding` itself must not be inside the group that redirects to it.

Guests are **not** handled here — `GuestOrSessionGuard` and the guest identity arrive in M2 (WEA-28). Structure the layout guard so guest support is an added branch rather than a rewrite.

## Done when

* A logged-in reload shows no logged-out flash
* Hitting a private route while logged out lands on `/login`
* A freshly signed-up user lands on `/onboarding` and cannot escape it into the app

Spec: §4, §6
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: useRequestHelper — CSRF header, 403 retry, 401 redirect
Description:
Port `pfa/front/src/helpers/useRequestHelper.ts` — every authenticated call in the app goes through it, so its edge cases are the app's edge cases.

## Scope

* `request(url, options)` — public calls, `withCredentials: true`
* `privateRequest(url, options)` — requires a user; attaches `x-csrf-token` on unsafe methods
* API base resolution: on `localhost` use `NEXT_PUBLIC_REMOTE_HOST_FROM_LOCALHOST`, otherwise same-origin `''`; always prefix `/api`
* **403 on an unsafe method** → refetch `GET /auth/csrf` once, retry with the fresh token
* **401** → hard `window.location.replace('/login')` and return a **permanently pending promise**

## Watch out

The pending-promise trick is deliberate and worth understanding before touching it: returning a never-resolving promise stops the 401 from becoming a TanStack Query error and reaching `error.tsx` while the browser is already navigating away. Without it, users see an error boundary flash during a normal session expiry.

It must **not** fire when already on `/login` (infinite loop) or during SSR (no `window`). Both guards exist in pfa's version — keep them.

The 403 retry happens **once**. A retry loop against a genuinely rejecting server is worse than a clean failure.

## Done when

* Unit tests: header attached on POST but not GET; 403 triggers exactly one refresh + retry; 401 redirects; no redirect when already on `/login`; no redirect during SSR
* A session expiring mid-use lands on `/login` with no error boundary

Spec: §6
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Login, signup and recover screens
Description:
The three public auth screens, built on the design tokens.

## Scope

* `/login` — email + password
* `/signup` — **five fields**: email, password, confirm password, passphrase, confirm passphrase
* `/recover` — email, passphrase, new password, confirm new password
* react-hook-form + Zod 4 resolvers, schemas in `@schemas/auth.ts` and **mirroring the server DTO rules exactly** (password ≥10, passphrase ≥12, confirmations match)
* Shared `AuthCard` / `AuthHeader` / `AuthBrand` shell, as pfa has
* On success, write `{ user, csrfToken }` into `AuthContext` and route onward (signup → `/onboarding`, login → `/`)
* Server errors surfaced inline, not as a toast that vanishes

## Watch out

The signup form needs to **explain the passphrase**, not just collect it. A user who treats it as a throwaway second password has no recovery path at all — there is no email fallback. One line of copy under the field: what it is for, that it cannot be reset, and that it should be written down.

Zod schemas must be kept honest against the DTOs. Two sources of truth for the same rule is the known cost of not sharing a package (§3); the mitigation is that both live in files named for each other and are reviewed together.

Never prefill or autocomplete the passphrase field (`autocomplete="off"`, and no password manager hint that would file it as the password).

## Done when

* All three flows work end to end against the real API
* Client and server reject the same inputs with the same rules
* Screens match the design's dark chrome and use only tokens

Spec: §6, §10
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Onboarding screen — handle and home city
Description:
Signup collects five fields and nothing else, so the `@handle` and home city are collected here — the step every new member passes through exactly once.

## Scope

* `/onboarding`, reachable only when authenticated with `onboardedAt == null`
* Handle field: `@`-prefixed, unique, validated live against the API
* City selection
* `PATCH /api/users/me` setting `handle`, `homeCityId` and stamping `onboardedAt`
* On success, route to `/`

## Watch out

**The real city picker does not exist yet** — it is WEA-20 in M2, because it needs Open-Meteo geocoding. For M1, ship a minimal city input (free text or a tiny hardcoded list) that produces a valid `homeCityId`, and leave a clearly marked seam for WEA-20 to drop the real picker (design 4B) into.

Handle uniqueness must be enforced by the database, not only by the live check. The check is UX; the constraint is correctness, and the gap between them is a race.

Reserve the `guest_` prefix — a member must not be able to pick a handle that impersonates a guest identity (or vice versa) once guest mode lands in M2.

## Done when

* A new signup cannot reach the app without completing this step
* A taken handle is rejected both live and on submit
* `onboardedAt` is set exactly once

Spec: §6, §7
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: deploy-api.sh + nginx /api proxy — M1 production deploy
Description:
Closes M1: the API goes live behind the nginx from [WEA-7](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-7/ovh-dns-nginx-deploy-frontsh-first-production-deploy), and **a real person can sign up and log in on [https://worldweathr.com](<https://worldweathr.com>)**.

## Scope

* `deploy-api.sh` adapted from `pfa/nest-api/deploy-api.sh` — atomic releases, `prisma migrate deploy`, process restart
* nginx `location /api` proxying to the Nest port, on the server block created in [WEA-7](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-7/ovh-dns-nginx-deploy-frontsh-first-production-deploy)
* MySQL 8 database and user provisioned on the VPS
* Redis provisioned (or the existing instance namespaced — the session prefix is `ww:`, so it can safely share pfa's Redis)
* Production `.env` for the API: `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `GUEST_COOKIE_SECRET`, `FRONTEND_URL=https://worldweathr.com`, `COOKIE_SECURE=true`, `PORT`
* Replace the holding page with the real `/login` entry point
* `DEPLOY.md` updated with both scripts and the full env table

## Watch out

This is where the cookie either works or doesn't. If login succeeds but every subsequent request 401s, walk pfa's `DEPLOY.md` checklist in order — it was written from exactly this failure:

1. Is `Set-Cookie` present on the login response?
2. If not → nginx isn't forwarding the headers, or `trust proxy` / `proxy: true` is missing.
3. If present but not stored → `Secure` on an HTTP origin; check the certificate actually terminated.
4. If stored but 401 → `withCredentials` missing client-side.

Same-origin in production means CORS is **not** involved. If you find yourself debugging CORS here, the proxy is misconfigured — resist the urge to loosen `enableCors`.

`SESSION_SECRET` and `GUEST_COOKIE_SECRET` must be distinct, high-entropy, and generated on the server — never reused from pfa.

## Done when

* Signup → onboarding → logout → login all work against [https://worldweathr.com](<https://worldweathr.com>)
* Sessions survive across requests and expire as configured
* Both deploy scripts run cleanly twice in a row

Spec: §11
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Cities module — Open-Meteo geocoding, resolve and nearby
Description:
The `City` table is a **local cache of Open-Meteo geocoding results**, not a reference dataset. Rows are created on demand as users pick places.

## Scope

```
GET   /api/cities/search?q=          proxy geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search
GET   /api/cities/nearby?lat=&lon=   reverse lookup for "Use my location"
POST  /api/cities/resolve            persist a geocoding result, return the City
```

* Search proxies rather than exposing Open-Meteo to the browser, so results can be normalised and rate-limited in one place
* `resolve` upserts on `geonameId` when present, falling back to `@@unique([name, countryCode, latitude, longitude])`
* Always capture `timezone` — everything downstream depends on it

## Watch out

`timezone` **is not optional metadata.** `SkyLog.localDate` is the user's local calendar day, computed from it. A city persisted without a timezone will silently write logs to the wrong day for anyone not on UTC, and the bug will look like "my streak broke for no reason".

Deduplicate carefully. Open-Meteo returns several "Paris" entries (France, Texas, Ontario). The unique key includes coordinates precisely so those stay distinct — do not dedupe on name alone.

Cache search responses briefly; the picker will fire a request per keystroke even with debouncing.

## Done when

* Searching "paris" returns multiple distinct cities with countries
* Resolving the same city twice creates exactly one row
* Every persisted city has a valid IANA timezone

Spec: §8, §9
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: City picker component (design 4B)
Description:
The bottom-sheet picker from design 4B. Replaces the temporary city input left in onboarding by [WEA-17](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-17/onboarding-screen-handle-and-home-city), and is reused by the city switcher in M3.

## Scope

* Bottom sheet, white surface with the `28px 28px 0 0` top radius and the grab handle
* Search field, debounced against `GET /cities/search` — see **Search debounce** below; it is a hard requirement here, not a nicety
* **"Use my location"** — `navigator.geolocation` → `GET /cities/nearby`
* Recent-cities list with `WeatherIcon`, city, country, temperature, and the blue check on the selected row
* Selecting a row calls `POST /cities/resolve` and returns the `City`
* Render the *geocoding unavailable* state from [WEA-62](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-62/open-meteo-kill-switch-disable-every-outbound-call-from-env-without>) — when the Open-Meteo kill switch is off, search must say "City search is temporarily unavailable", never the misleading "No city found". Recent cities still work.

## Watch out

This is the app's **light surface**, and the only place it appears. It overrides the `--wi-*` icon palette (`--wi-cloud: #9db0c8`, `--wi-sun: #eaa63f`, `--wi-rain: #3f6fb5`, …) so the icons stay legible on white. Those overrides come from `tokens/aurora.css` ([WEA-9](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-9/design-system-colour-elevation-and-aurora-tokens)) — do not inline them here.

Geolocation is a permission prompt that can be denied, dismissed, or silently never answered. All three need a path back to the search field; a spinner that waits forever is the default failure and it is bad.

Reuse: build it as a controlled component with `value` / `onSelect`, not wired to onboarding specifically. M3's city switcher mounts the same component.

### Search debounce — the only thing that can multiply Open-Meteo volume

Every other Open-Meteo call in this app is bounded by something that isn't a human: the cron fires once a day per city, `POST /cities/resolve` is a database upsert. **This search field is the single place where one user action can become an unbounded number of outbound calls.** A naïve `onChange` → fetch turns "Marseille" into nine requests to a third-party API, per user, per hesitation. That is the failure mode this section exists to prevent.

* **300ms trailing debounce**, and a **minimum query length** before the first call fires — 3 characters is a sensible floor; below that the result set is noise anyway.
* **Abort the in-flight request** when a newer keystroke lands (`AbortController`). Debouncing alone is not enough: on a slow connection, requests still overlap and a stale response can land after a fresh one and repaint the list with the wrong cities.
* **No call on mount**, and no call for an unchanged value — reopening the sheet, blur/refocus, or a re-render must not re-query a string that was already searched.
* **Cache results per normalised query** for the lifetime of the sheet, so backspacing back to a query already typed costs nothing.
* Pasting a city name is one change event, which is fine — just make sure it stays one request.

## Done when

* Search, geolocation and selection all work
* Icons are legible on the white sheet with no per-screen overrides
* Denying the location permission leaves a usable UI
* Typing `Marseille` at normal speed produces **at most 2** requests to `/cities/search` — verifiable in the network tab, and in `logs/open-meteo.txt` on the API side
* With the [WEA-62](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-62/open-meteo-kill-switch-disable-every-outbound-call-from-env-without>) switch off, the sheet explains itself instead of showing an empty result list

Spec: §10, design 4B
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Open-Meteo forecast client + WMO weather_code mapping
Description:
The only module in the API that talks to the network.

## Scope

* Client for `api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast` with `past_days=92`
* Client for `archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive` (older days)
* Daily variables: `weather_code`, `temperature_2m_max`, `temperature_2m_min`, `wind_speed_10m_max`
* Timeouts, retries with backoff, and a typed result — a third-party outage must not take the app down

## The mapping

| WMO codes | Condition |
| -- | -- |
| 0, 1 | `SUNNY` |
| 2, 3 | `CLOUDY` |
| 45, 48 | `FOGGY` |
| 51–57, 61–67, 80–82 | `RAINY` |
| 71–77, 85, 86 | `SNOWY` |
| 95, 96, 99 | `STORMY` |

## WINDY has no WMO code

This is the judgement call in the whole feature. `WINDY` is derived: `wind_speed_10m_max >= WINDY_THRESHOLD_KPH` (default **30**), and it overrides **only** `SUNNY` and `CLOUDY` — never precipitation, never storms.

That threshold silently sets every user's agreement percentage. It lives in **one named env-configurable constant** and is referenced nowhere else, so it can be re-tuned later without archaeology. Do not scatter the comparison across services.

## Watch out

Never let a failed fetch be recorded as a mismatch. A missing observation is *absent*, and §8 requires it to be excluded from the agreement denominator rather than counted against the user.

## Done when

* Unit tests cover every code in the table, both sides of the wind threshold, and the "windy does not override rain" rule
* A simulated Open-Meteo outage degrades to "forecast unavailable" without a 500

Spec: §8
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: ForecastObservation persistence + daily refresh cron
Description:
Turns the Open-Meteo client into a shared, cached record of what the forecast said.

## Scope

* Idempotent upsert on `@@unique([cityId, localDate])`
* `@nestjs/schedule` cron refreshing today's observation for every city with **at least one user active in the last 30 days** (`User.lastSeenAt`)
* `lastSeenAt` touched on authenticated requests
* On-demand fetch when a read finds a gap

## Why this shape matters

`ForecastObservation` is keyed by **city and day, never by user**. Five hundred users in Paris cost one API call per day, not five hundred. Everything in M3 and M4 — the History match badges, the 30-day grid, the agreement percentage — reads from this table rather than the network, which is what makes those screens cheap.

## Watch out

The cron must be idempotent and safe to run twice. Upsert, never insert.

Scope it by active cities. Iterating every `City` row grows unboundedly as people search for places they never log in.

`localDate` is the **city's** local day, from `City.timezone`. Do not use the server's date, and do not use UTC — a cron firing at 00:30 Paris time is still "yesterday" in New York.

Log failures per city and keep going. One unreachable city must not abort the whole run.

## Done when

* Running the cron twice produces no duplicates and no errors
* A city with no recent users is skipped
* A gap requested by a read is filled on demand

Spec: §5, §8
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: SkyLog module — PUT/GET today, localDate and logCount
Description:
The core write of the product.

## Scope

```
GET  /api/logs/today   → { log | null, forecast | null }
PUT  /api/logs/today     condition, feeling, temperatureC?, mood?
```

* `PUT`**, not** `POST` — one log per user per day, so writing today is idempotent and "Log today's sky" / "Update today's log" are the same call
* `localDate` computed server-side from `City.timezone`; the client never sends a date
* `cityId` stamped from the user's current city at write time
* `User.logCount` incremented **in the same transaction**, and only on first insert for that day — never on an update
* Response includes the day's `ForecastObservation` so the UI can show Match/Differ immediately

## Watch out

`logCount` drives the Community ranking (M5). Incrementing it on every `PUT` instead of only on insert would let anyone climb the board by re-saving the same day — the denormalisation is a performance choice, and this is the correctness cost that comes with it. Guard it with the transaction and test it explicitly.

Never trust a client-supplied date. Deriving `localDate` server-side from the city's timezone is what keeps `@@unique([userId, localDate])` meaningful; accept a date parameter and users can backfill arbitrary history.

`mood` is accepted here but unused until M5. Allow it now so the column and the write path don't need revisiting.

## Done when

* Two `PUT`s on the same day leave one row and `logCount == 1`
* A user in Tokyo logging at 09:00 local writes today, not yesterday
* Unit tests cover the timezone boundary in both directions

Spec: §5, §9
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Port weather-icon to a React WeatherIcon component
Description:
The design ships `weather-icon` as a vanilla custom element. Port it to React: `<WeatherIcon condition bob />`.

## Why port rather than reuse

Custom elements do not server-render — they are inert until `customElements.define` runs client-side. Every screen in this app leans on this icon, several of them above the fold, so shipping it as a web component means a visible pop-in on every page load and nothing at all for a crawler.

## What it actually is

No SVG. Seven conditions built entirely from positioned `div`s, CSS gradients, `container-type: size` and `cqmin` units, so the whole thing scales from a 22px legend swatch to a 174px hero from one `width`/`height`.

* **sunny** — radial core, 8 rays on a 14s spin, breathing halo
* **cloudy** — four stacked lozenges drifting
* **rainy / snowy** — cloud plus three staggered falling drops/flakes
* **stormy** — storm-gradient cloud with a `clip-path` bolt flashing
* **foggy** — four drifting bars at staggered delays
* **windy** — three bars plus a rotated arc
* `bob` — the 3s vertical float used on hero instances only

## Scope

* Keep the `--wi-*` custom-property contract **exactly** — that is what lets one component render on dark chrome, the light sheet and the Aurora gradient without knowing which it is on
* Keyframes come from `animations.css` ([WEA-8](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-8/design-system-styles-structure-globals-entry-base-and-animations)), not from inside the component
* Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: hold every animation, including `bob`
* `aria-label` from the condition; decorative instances get `aria-hidden`

## Done when

* All seven render server-side with no pop-in
* The same instance is legible on all three surfaces with no per-screen overrides
* Reduced-motion stops all animation
* Visual check at 22px and 174px

Spec: §10
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Aurora theming — the condition drives the whole surface
Description:
The signature of the design: picking a condition recolours the entire screen, with a `.7s ease` transition on the background.

## Scope

* An `AuroraSurface` (or provider) that takes a `Condition` and applies the gradient from `tokens/aurora.css`
* The white top-highlight overlay: `radial-gradient(135% 70% at 50% -12%, rgba(255,255,255,.34), transparent 54%)`
* Glass panels on top: `rgba(255,255,255,.13)`, `1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.22)`, `backdrop-filter: blur(9–12px)`
* Sets the on-Aurora `--wi-*` palette for descendants
* `transition: background .7s ease`

## Watch out

Spec: §10, design 3A
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Guest identity — ww.guest cookie and GuestOrSessionGuard
Description:
Lets someone use the app with no account. A guest is a **real** `User` **row** with `isAnonymous = true` — which is why History, Stats and Community will need only a `WHERE` clause, never a second code path.

## Scope

```
GET /api/auth/guest → { user, csrfToken }   creates or resolves a guest identity
```

* Creates a `User` with `isAnonymous = true`, nullable email/password/passphrase, generated handle `guest_` + 6 base32 chars, and the chosen `homeCityId`
* Signed httpOnly cookie `ww.guest` holding the user id — `sameSite=lax`, `secure` in production, **max-age 1 year**, signed with `GUEST_COOKIE_SECRET`
* `GuestOrSessionGuard` — resolves the authenticated session first, falls back to the guest cookie; **the session always wins** when both are present
* Guests get a CSRF token too, keyed to the guest identity
* Apply the guard to `PUT /logs/today`, `GET /logs/today`, `GET /cities/*`

## Why a separate cookie

`ww.sid` has a **10-minute rolling TTL**. A guest identity living only in the Redis session would evaporate over lunch and take their logs with it. `ww.guest` is deliberately independent and long-lived: the session is authentication, this is identity.

## Watch out

Sign the cookie and **verify the signature** before trusting the id — an unsigned guest cookie is an "impersonate any user by editing a cookie" bug, including non-guest users.

Verify the resolved row actually has `isAnonymous = true`. A stale `ww.guest` pointing at an upgraded account must not act as a permanent bypass of login.

Do not create a guest row on a bare page view. Only create one when someone actually logs — otherwise every crawler mints a `User`.

## Done when

* A guest can log without an account and still see it after a day
* A forged/tampered cookie is rejected
* A logged-in member with a leftover guest cookie is treated as the member

Spec: §7
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Guest → member upgrade on signup
Description:
"Keep your 5 days" is the strongest signup argument the product has. This ticket makes it true.

## Scope

When `POST /api/auth/signup` carries a valid `ww.guest` cookie, **upgrade that row** instead of inserting a new one — in a single transaction:

```
email / passwordHash / passphraseHash  ← set
isAnonymous                            ← false
handle                                 ← replaced during onboarding (drops guest_xxxxxx)
```

* Logs, `logCount`, streak and city carry over untouched
* Every past log's weight rises from 0.25 to 1.0 **retroactively**, since weight is derived from `isAnonymous` rather than stored per log
* Clear the `ww.guest` cookie afterwards
* Open a normal member session

## The edge case

If the submitted email **already belongs to a member**: fail with `409`, leave the guest row untouched, and leave the guest cookie in place. The person can log into their existing account; their guest logs stay on the guest identity. Do **not** attempt to merge two real users — that is a different, much harder feature and nobody asked for it.

## Watch out

Weight is derived, never denormalised onto `SkyLog`. If you ever cache a per-log weight, this retroactive upgrade silently stops working.

The whole thing must be one transaction. A partial upgrade — credentials set but `isAnonymous` still true — produces an account that can log in but is still counted as a guest.

## Done when

* e2e: guest logs 3 days → signs up → all 3 logs present, `logCount` intact, `isAnonymous` false
* e2e: guest signs up with an existing member's email → 409, guest row and cookie untouched
* The upgraded user's past logs now count at full weight in aggregates

Spec: §11
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Logs range query with forecast joined per row
Description:
```
GET /api/logs?from=&to=&cityId=   → rows with their ForecastObservation
GET /api/logs/:date               → a single day in detail
```

## Scope

* Range query over `SkyLog` for the current identity, ordered by `localDate` desc
* Each row joined to its `ForecastObservation` on `(cityId, localDate)`
* Per-row `match` boolean derived from `log.condition === observation.condition`
* `cityId` filter, defaulting to the user's current city
* Sensible pagination or a capped range — History is unbounded by nature

## Watch out

`match` is **derived, never stored**. The WMO mapping and the wind threshold can be re-tuned ([WEA-21](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-21/open-meteo-forecast-client-wmo-weather-code-mapping) exists precisely so they can be), and a stored boolean would freeze every past day against an old rule while new days used the new one.

A row with **no** observation is not a mismatch. Return `match: null` and let the UI say "forecast unavailable". §8 requires those days to be excluded from the agreement denominator, and that starts here.

Use the `@@index([cityId, localDate])` — verify the query plan actually hits it rather than assuming.

## Done when

* A 90-day range returns rows with correct match/differ/unknown
* Days with no observation come back as `null`, not `false`
* Query plan uses the index

Spec: §5, §9
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: On-demand forecast backfill for past days
Description:
The cron from [WEA-22](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-22/forecastobservation-persistence-daily-refresh-cron) only fills **today**. History and Stats ask for ranges that predate a user's first visit, or predate the cron existing at all.

## Scope

* Detect gaps in `ForecastObservation` for a requested `(cityId, range)`
* Fill them, choosing the right source:
  * **≤ 92 days old** → the forecast API with `past_days`
  * **older** → the archive API
* Idempotent upsert, batched per city rather than per day
* Trigger it from the History and Stats reads, asynchronously where possible so the response isn't blocked on a slow third party

## Watch out

The archive API **lags several days behind real time**. There is a window where a date is too old for `past_days=92` to be useful and too recent for the archive to have it. Handle that window explicitly — it must resolve to "unavailable", not to an exception or a silent zero.

Do not fan out one HTTP request per missing day. A user opening History for the first time can be missing 90 days at once; that is one or two range requests, not ninety.

Rate-limit backfill per city so a refresh loop on the History screen can't hammer Open-Meteo.

## Done when

* Opening History on a brand-new range fills the gaps and shows badges
* A date inside the forecast/archive gap renders as unavailable
* Backfilling the same range twice makes no second round of requests

Spec: §8

Title: History screen — master–detail (design 4A)
Description:
Dark chrome, two panes: the list of logged days on the left, the selected day rendered in full Aurora colour on the right.

* Eyebrow `Paris · 42 entries`, `h1` "Your logged skies"

Spec: §10, design 4A
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: City switcher — change your active city

Spec: §5, §9

Title: Guest locked preview — History

Spec: §7
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Stats summary — agreement, streak, total logged
Description:
`GET /api/stats/summary`

## The three numbers

**Agreement %** — of days where a `ForecastObservation` exists, the share where your condition matched it. **Scoped to a city** (default: your current one), because comparing calls to a forecast only means something within one place.

**Current streak** — consecutive `localDate` values with a log, counted back from today. **Global across cities** (§9): moving must not break it.

**Total logged** — all-time count for the identity.

## Watch out

The agreement **denominator excludes days with no observation** (§8). Counting a missing forecast as a mismatch quietly penalises users for Open-Meteo's gaps, and it is the single easiest way to make this number a lie.

The streak needs the user's local "today", derived from their city's timezone — not the server's date. A user in Auckland has already started tomorrow.

Decide and document whether *today, not yet logged* breaks the streak. Recommendation: it does **not** — the streak breaks only once a full local day passes with no log. Otherwise everyone's streak reads as broken every morning.

This is called *agreement*, never *accuracy*. `ForecastObservation` is a forecast, not ground truth, and the copy must not imply the user was wrong.

## Done when

* Unit tests: streak across a city change, streak across a timezone boundary, agreement with missing observations interleaved
* Numbers match a hand-computed fixture

Spec: §8, §9
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Stats month grid + condition distribution
Description:
```
GET /api/stats/month?days=30   the match grid
GET /api/stats/distribution    your calls vs the forecast, per condition
```

## Scope

**Month grid** — one cell per day over the window, each `matched` / `differed` / `unlogged` / `no-forecast`. The design shows two states; the data has four, and the extra two must not be silently folded into "differed".

**Distribution** — for each of the seven conditions, how many times **you** called it versus how many times the **forecast** recorded it, over the same window and city. This is the interesting number in the whole app: it shows *where* your perception diverges, not just how often.

## Watch out

Both endpoints are city-scoped and share the summary's window semantics. Extract the window/scope resolution into one place rather than reimplementing it three times — a distribution computed over a different range than the agreement percentage produces two numbers that quietly contradict each other on the same screen.

`unlogged` and `no-forecast` are different failures with different meanings: one is the user's gap, the other is Open-Meteo's. The grid legend must distinguish them or the visualisation is misleading.

## Done when

* Grid and distribution agree with the summary over identical windows
* All four cell states are represented and legible
* A user with sparse logging gets a sensible grid, not a wall of one colour

Spec: §9, design 3B
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Stats screen (design 3B)
Description:
Dark chrome. The payoff for logging every day.

## Scope

Per design 3B:

* Eyebrow `Paris · last 30 days`, `h1` "Your sky vs the forecast"
* **Top row, 3 cards**: the agreement ring (`conic-gradient(#ff8f3c 0 N%, rgba(255,255,255,.12) N% 100%)` with the percentage in a punched-out centre), the streak in days, the all-time total
* **Bottom left**: the day-by-day grid, `repeat(15, 1fr)`, with a legend covering all four states

## Watch out

Load the **dataviz skill** before writing any chart code here. The ring, grid and paired bars have to read as one system, and colour choices need to survive both themes and colour-blind readers. Accent-vs-grey is the design's encoding — do not introduce a third hue without checking it against the palette rules.

The paired bars need a shared, explicit scale. Two bars normalised independently make a 9-vs-7 look like a tie.

Nothing on this screen may imply the user was *wrong*. It is agreement with a forecast, and the footnote is what keeps that honest.

## Done when

* All three cards and both charts render from real data
* Legend covers all four grid states
* Responsive down to 390px without the charts becoming unreadable

Spec: §7
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Mood on the daily log
Description:
The column already exists ([WEA-2](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-2/prisma-7-mysql-full-schema-and-first-migration)) and `PUT /logs/today` already accepts it ([WEA-23](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-23/skylog-module-putget-today-localdate-and-logcount)). This wires up the UI and makes it meaningful.

## Scope

* Four preset moods: **Uplifted** / **Calm** / **Gloomy** / **Unmoved**
* Chip row at the top of the Community screen, plus the phrase *"Today, the weather lifts me up."* reflecting the selection
* Writes through `PUT /logs/today`

## Watch out

Mood is **not** the same as `feeling`. `feeling` (Freezing/Cold/Mild/Hot) is temperature perception and lives on the Today screen. Mood is emotional response and lives on Community. They are different columns, different questions, and different screens; conflating them in the UI copy will confuse everyone including future you.

Four presets and no free text is a deliberate product decision (§2): there is nothing to moderate. Do not add an "other" field.

Setting a mood on Community writes to **today's log**, which may not exist yet. Decide: either create the log, or require a logged day first. Recommendation: require the log, and point them at Today — a mood with no sky attached has nothing to aggregate against.

Spec: §5, design 6A
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Community leaderboard endpoint — ranking, filters, cursor pagination
Description:
`GET /api/community?country=&city=&condition=&feeling=&mood=&includeAnonymous=&cursor=`

## Scope

* All users ranked by **participation** — `logCount` desc, `id` asc as tiebreak
* Each row: rank, handle, city + country, log count, today's condition + feeling, today's mood
* Filters: country, city, condition, feeling, mood
* Cursor pagination
* `includeAnonymous` defaults to the caller's `User.showAnonymous`
* **Users with** `visibleInCommunity = false` **never appear** — excluded from the result set entirely, at any rank, regardless of filters (see WEA-55)

## Watch out

This is the busiest read in the app, and it is why `logCount` is denormalised (§5). Do not "simplify" it into a `COUNT(*) … GROUP BY userId` over `SkyLog` — that is the query that falls over first.

`visibleInCommunity = false` **is a privacy guarantee, not a filter.** It must hold even for the user with the highest `logCount` in the world — a hidden top logger is still hidden. Enforce it in the base query, not in a post-filter that a future caller could forget to apply.

Users with **zero logs** should not appear. The board is ranked by participation; a wall of empty accounts at the bottom is noise.

Only ever expose: handle, city, country, log count, and today's condition/feeling/mood. Never the email, never the exact coordinates, never `lastSeenAt`. Guests appear under their `guest_xxxxxx` handle.

The ranking itself is **unweighted** — it counts days logged, and a guest who logs 200 days really did log 200 days. Weighting applies to *aggregates* (WEA-44), not to the leaderboard order. Getting these two confused makes the board look arbitrary.

## Done when

* Filters compose correctly and the cursor is stable across pages
* `includeAnonymous=false` removes guests entirely
* A user with `visibleInCommunity=false` is absent even when they would rank #1
* No field beyond the allowed set appears in any response

Spec: §7, §9
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Mood distribution + weighted aggregation (guests at 0.25)
Description:
`GET /api/community/mood-distribution` — "How the sky feels today", with the same filters as the leaderboard.

## The weighting

* Members count **1.0**, guests count `ANONYMOUS_VOTE_WEIGHT` = 0.25. Four guests equal one member.
* One env-configurable constant, referenced in exactly one place.
* Weight is **derived from** `User.isAnonymous`, never stored on `SkyLog` — that is what makes the guest→member upgrade ([WEA-29](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-29/guest-member-upgrade-on-signup)) retroactively raise a user's past contributions.
* When `showAnonymous` is off, guests are excluded entirely rather than down-weighted to zero.

## Scope

* Weighted counts per mood over today's logs, filtered
* Percentages for the bar widths
* Both the raw participant count and the weighted total in the response, so the UI can be honest about what it's showing
* **Users with** `visibleInCommunity = false` **are excluded from the aggregate** — a hidden user's mood does not contribute to the distribution (see WEA-55)

## Watch out

Opting out means **out of the aggregate too**, not only off the visible rows. A hidden user whose mood still moved the public distribution would be a partial leak — "log privately" has to mean their data is absent from the Community view entirely.

Return enough for the UI to explain itself. A bar chart showing "60% Uplifted" built from 3 members and 40 guests is technically correct and completely misleading without the counts behind it — the `ConfidenceNote` (WEA-46) needs those numbers.

Rounding: weighted counts are fractional. Decide once whether to round for display or carry decimals, and make sure the percentages still sum to 100.

Clearing a cookie mints a new guest, so this is gameable by construction. The 0.25 weight is the mitigation, not a fix — do not add complexity pretending otherwise.

## Done when

* Unit tests: all-member, all-guest, and mixed populations produce hand-checkable weighted totals
* A `visibleInCommunity=false` user is absent from the distribution
* An upgraded guest's past logs immediately count at 1.0
* Toggling `showAnonymous` changes the distribution as expected

Spec: §7
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: showAnonymous — persisted preference and switch
Description:
One switch controlling whether guest data counts, saved per user.

## Scope

* `PATCH /api/users/me/preferences { showAnonymous }`
* `User.showAnonymous`, default **true**
* Switch rendered in the Community filter row, beside Country / City / Weather / Feeling
* Applies to **every aggregate**: the leaderboard, the mood distribution, and any future city consensus
* Survives reload and follows the user across devices

## Watch out

This is a **saved preference, not a transient filter**, and the difference is the point. The other chips reset on reload; this one does not, because it expresses a standing judgement about what data the user trusts rather than a momentary narrowing.

Apply it consistently. A leaderboard that hides guests while the mood distribution beside it still counts them is worse than not having the switch — the two panels would contradict each other on the same screen.

The switch carries a short inline hint about the trade-off, visible **before** it is toggled (see WEA-46).

## Done when

* Toggling changes both the board and the distribution together
* The setting persists across reload and devices
* Guests have a sensible default (they can read the board; the preference is a member concept)

Spec: §7, §9
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: ConfidenceNote — say when guest data is being counted
Description:
Whenever guest data is counted, the app says so. This is a **requirement, not a footnote**: an aggregate that silently mixes in weighted guest input reads as more authoritative than it is.

## Scope

* A `ConfidenceNote` component directly under any aggregate computed with `showAnonymous = true` — the leaderboard and the mood distribution
* Copy: *"Includes logs from visitors without an account, counted at reduced weight. Less reliable than member data."*
* A short inline hint on the switch itself, so the trade-off is visible **before** toggling, not only after
* With the switch off, a neutral **"Members only"** marker replaces it — the reader always knows which population they are looking at
* Uses the raw and weighted counts from [WEA-44](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-44/mood-distribution-weighted-aggregation-guests-at-025) so it can be specific rather than vague

## The framing, and why it matters

Honest **in both directions**. Every number in this app is self-reported perception: a member can enter nonsense just as easily as a guest can, and "the sky is stormy" is a subjective call even in good faith. The guest flag narrows one specific gap — an unverified identity that costs nothing to mint — it does **not** make the rest ground truth.

So the copy says guest data is **less reliable**, never that member data is *accurate*.

`ForecastObservation` is the only non-self-reported value in the system, which is exactly why that comparison is called *agreement* and never *correctness*. Keep that distinction intact here.

## Watch out

Do not make it a dismissible toast or a tooltip. It belongs in the layout, under the data it qualifies, always present when it applies.

Keep it one short sentence. A paragraph of hedging gets ignored, which defeats the purpose.

## Done when

* The note appears and disappears with the switch, on both aggregates
* The members-only marker is equally visible
* Copy reviewed against the framing above — no claim that member data is accurate

Spec: §7
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Community screen — desktop (design 6A)
Description:
Dark chrome, two columns. **Turn 6 is authoritative** — the Turn 5 friends feed is superseded and is not built.

## Scope

**Left column:**

* Mood card: *"How does today's sky make you feel?"* with the four chips and the resulting phrase in accent
* Search field + filter chips (Country / City / Weather / Feeling) + the `showAnonymous` switch
* Eyebrow "Most active loggers", then the ranked rows: rank number, 44px `WeatherIcon` on the day's Aurora tile, `@handle`, `city, country · N logs`, condition + feeling, and a mood dot with its label

**Right rail:**

* "How the sky feels today" — the weighted mood distribution with its bars and counts
* The `ConfidenceNote` under it
* An explainer card: *"Ranked by participation — the more days you log, the higher you appear. No follows, no feed to police."*
* CTA: "Log today to climb the board"

## Watch out

Row density matters — eight rows should be scannable at a glance, which means the mood dot and the condition tile carry most of the information. Do not let the handle dominate.

Infinite scroll or a "load more" on the cursor; do not fetch everything.

Guests appear as `guest_xxxxxx`. That is intentional and legible — do not disguise them, the whole switch exists so people can see and choose.

The explainer card is doing real work: it tells people the ranking is effort, not popularity. Keep it.

## Done when

* Filters, switch and mood chips all drive the data live
* The `ConfidenceNote` tracks the switch
* Matches 6A at 1200px+ and degrades cleanly to tablet

Spec: §10, design 6A
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Community screen — mobile (design 6B) + M5 deploy
Description:
The mobile layout, and the deploy that completes the four-screen product.

## Scope

Per design 6B:

* `h1` "Community", then the four mood chips
* Horizontally scrolling filter strip: Search, Country, Weather, Feeling, and the `showAnonymous` switch
* Condensed rows: rank, 40px condition tile, `@handle`, `place · N logs`, mood dot
* The mood distribution and `ConfidenceNote` below the list rather than in a rail
* Bottom tab bar with Community active

**Then deploy**: run both scripts, verify the four screens work on the live domain for a member and a guest.

## Watch out

The condensed row drops the condition label and the mood label, keeping only the icon and the dot. Both need accessible names — a colour dot alone is meaningless to a screen reader and to anyone with colour-vision deficiency. Pair every dot with text in the accessibility tree even when it is visually hidden.

The horizontal filter strip must not trap vertical scrolling on touch.

The `ConfidenceNote` still applies on mobile. It is easy to drop it for space; don't.

## Done when

* Community works from 390px up with no layout break against 6A
* Mood dots have accessible names
* All four screens verified live on [https://worldweathr.com](<https://worldweathr.com>) as both a member and a guest

Spec: §10, §11, design 6B
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Rate limiting — auth, recovery and guest creation
Description:
`@nestjs/throttler`. **This is the real defence for passphrase recovery** and should be pulled forward if `/auth/recover` is exposed publicly before M6 ships (see [WEA-13](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-13/passphrase-recovery-endpoint)).

## Scope

| Endpoint | Why |
| -- | -- |
| `POST /auth/login` | credential stuffing |
| `POST /auth/recover` | **passphrase brute force** — the highest-value target in the app |
| `POST /auth/signup` | account spam |
| `GET /auth/guest` | guest-row flooding |
| `GET /cities/search` | it proxies a third party |

* Per-IP limits, tighter on `/auth/recover` than anywhere else
* Storage in the existing Redis so limits hold across restarts
* Correct client IP behind nginx — `trust proxy` is already set, verify the throttler actually reads the forwarded address rather than the proxy's

## Watch out

`/auth/recover` deserves the strictest budget in the app. It is a full account-takeover primitive protected only by a passphrase, with no email step in the way (§6 records this as an accepted risk). Something on the order of a handful of attempts per IP per hour, and consider a per-account counter as well as per-IP — an attacker with many IPs targeting one account is the case a pure IP limit misses entirely.

If the throttler reads the proxy's IP instead of the client's, every user shares one bucket and the limit is simultaneously useless and a self-inflicted outage. Test this behind the real nginx, not just locally.

## Done when

* Each endpoint returns 429 past its budget
* Limits survive an API restart
* Verified behind production nginx that per-IP buckets are actually per-client

Spec: §6, §7
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: helmet + security headers
Description:
## Scope

* `helmet` on the Nest app
* Next security headers in `next.config.ts`
* HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options` / `frame-ancestors`, `Permissions-Policy`
* A CSP that actually holds

## Watch out

The CSP is the hard part here, for one specific reason: the entire visual system is **inline styles and CSS custom properties** — Aurora gradients written as `style` attributes, per-instance `--wi-*` overrides, dynamically computed bar widths. A strict `style-src` will break the app's whole appearance.

Work out `style-src` deliberately rather than reaching for `'unsafe-inline'` on reflex. Nonces or hashes where practical; if `'unsafe-inline'` for styles turns out to be unavoidable, **write down why** in the config so the next person doesn't assume it was laziness.

`Permissions-Policy` must still allow `geolocation` — the city picker's "Use my location" depends on it.

Check the headers do not conflict with the ones nginx already sets; duplicated or contradictory headers are worse than either alone.

## Done when

* No CSP violations in the console on any of the four screens plus the city picker
* Geolocation still works
* A security-headers scanner gives a clean report against [https://worldweathr.com](<https://worldweathr.com>)

Spec: §11
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Seed script — realistic development data
Description:
A `pnpm seed` that produces a database worth developing against, modelled on `pfa/nest-api/scripts/seed.ts`.

## Scope

* ~20 users, a realistic **mix of members and guests** so weighting is actually exercised
* Several cities across different timezones and hemispheres — Paris, Tokyo, São Paulo, Oslo, Lisbon
* 60–90 days of `SkyLog` per user with plausible conditions, feelings and moods, and **deliberate gaps** so streaks break realistically
* Matching `ForecastObservation` rows, with an agreement rate around 60–75% and a few days missing entirely
* Idempotent, and refuses to run against production

## Why it earns its place

Several bugs in this app only appear with realistic data: a leaderboard that looks fine with three users, an agreement percentage that is only wrong when observations are missing, a streak that is only wrong across a timezone boundary, a weighted distribution that is only visibly wrong with a guest-heavy population. Seeding all four conditions makes them findable before production does.

## Watch out

Include the **timezone edge cases on purpose** — a Tokyo user and a São Paulo user logging on the same UTC instant should land on different `localDate` values, and the seed is where you prove it.

Include days with no `ForecastObservation`. If every seeded day has one, the "excluded from the denominator" logic is never exercised in development.

Guard hard against running with a production `DATABASE_URL`.

## Done when

* `pnpm seed` twice leaves a clean, identical database
* Every screen has something meaningful to show
* The guest/member mix visibly changes aggregates when the switch is toggled

Spec: §13
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Playwright end-to-end suites
Description:
The journeys that must never silently break.

## Suites

**1 · Member lifecycle** — signup (5 fields) → onboarding (handle + city) → log today → History shows it → Stats reflects it → logout → login → data intact.

**2 · Guest → member** — land logged out → pick a city → log 3 days → History and Stats show locked previews with the **real counts** → sign up → **all 3 logs survive**, weight rises to 1.0. This is the highest-value test in the suite: it covers the upgrade transaction, the cookie handover and the retroactive weighting, and every one of those is silent when it fails.

**3 · Community weighting** — with a mixed population, toggling `showAnonymous` changes both the leaderboard and the mood distribution **together**, and swaps the `ConfidenceNote` for the members-only marker.

**4 · Session and CSRF** — an expired session redirects to `/login` with no error boundary; an unsafe request without the CSRF header is rejected; the 403 retry recovers transparently.

## Watch out

Run against the seeded database ([WEA-51](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-51/seed-script-realistic-development-data)), not a hand-built fixture, so the tests exercise the same timezone and missing-observation edge cases development does.

Suite 2 needs a genuinely fresh browser context each run — a leftover `ww.guest` cookie makes it pass for the wrong reason.

## Done when

* All four suites pass locally and in a clean environment
* Suite 2 provably fails if the upgrade transaction is broken

Spec: §13
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: SEO pass — per-route metadata, JSON-LD, Lighthouse
Description:
Closes out the SEO scope started in [WEA-11](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-11/seo-foundation-metadata-robots-sitemap-og-image) and [WEA-31](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-31/public-landing-page-server-rendered-indexable). Still proportionate — the cheap remainder, not an optimisation project.

## Scope

* Review `generateMetadata` on every route; confirm titles and descriptions are distinct and truthful
* `WebApplication` JSON-LD on the landing page
* Confirm `robots: { index: false }` really is on all four authenticated screens, after five milestones of route churn
* Lighthouse SEO **and** accessibility run on the landing page and one app screen
* Fix whatever those runs surface

## Watch out

Re-verify the noindex directives rather than trusting [WEA-11](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-11/seo-foundation-metadata-robots-sitemap-og-image). Routes moved between groups across M2–M5, and a Community board leaking into search results would expose handles and cities we never intended to publish — the one SEO mistake here with a real privacy cost.

Keep the accessibility findings in scope: the mood dots ([WEA-48](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-48/community-screen-mobile-design-6b-m5-deploy)), the condition tiles and the charts ([WEA-40](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-40/stats-screen-design-3b)) are the likely offenders, and they are cheaper to fix now than after anyone relies on them.

## Explicitly out of scope

Per-city landing pages (`/paris-france`). They would be the real long-tail play and the data model already supports them — recorded in §15 as a future option, deliberately not now.

## Done when

* Lighthouse SEO ≥ 95 on the landing page
* No authenticated route is indexable
* Accessibility findings triaged, with anything deferred written down

Spec: §12, §15
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Deploy changelog wiring
Description:
Port pfa's deploy-changelog mechanism so each successful deploy records what shipped.

## Scope

* `deploy-front.sh` / `deploy-api.sh` append an entry (newest first) listing the commits shipped in that version **with their WEA ticket numbers**
* Logs live at a stable path **outside** the release directories so they survive the atomic symlink switch
* Only commits since that app's previous deploy, tracked with `.last-<app>` marker files
* Exposed at `https://worldweathr.com/deploys-front.txt` and `/deploys-api.txt`, behind HTTP Basic Auth
* Exact-match nginx locations so they take priority over the Next proxy and expose **only** those two files

## Watch out

The exact-match (`location = /deploys-front.txt`) matters. A prefix match would shadow real routes or expose the whole directory.

Keep the logs outside the release directories or the atomic switch deletes your history on the next deploy — the entire reason pfa puts them at `/var/www/<app>/deploy-logs/`.

Set up the `.htpasswd` before the location block goes live, not after. An unauthenticated window exposes your commit messages and ticket numbers publicly.

## Done when

* Two consecutive deploys produce two correct entries with WEA numbers
* Both URLs require auth and serve only those files
* Logs survive a release switch

Spec: §11
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Community visibility opt-out — visibleInCommunity toggle
Description:
Lets a user log **privately** — keep their own Today / History / Stats while not appearing on the Community board at all. The `visibleInCommunity` column already exists ([WEA-2](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-2/prisma-7-mysql-full-schema-and-first-migration)); this wires up the control and enforces it.

## Scope

* Extend `PATCH /api/users/me/preferences` to accept `visibleInCommunity` alongside `showAnonymous` (same endpoint [WEA-45](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-45/showanonymous-persisted-preference-and-switch) owns)
* `User.visibleInCommunity`, default **true**, applies to members and guests alike
* The exclusion in the leaderboard ([WEA-43](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-43/community-leaderboard-endpoint-ranking-filters-cursor-pagination)) and the mood distribution ([WEA-44](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-44/mood-distribution-weighted-aggregation-guests-at-025)) reads this column — this ticket owns the toggle and the acceptance test that the exclusion actually holds end to end
* **UI**: a privacy toggle in a small account menu opened from the avatar in the app chrome, with one line of copy — *"Show me on the Community board."* Reflect the current state on the Community screen too, so a hidden user can see they've opted out (and turn it back on) from where it matters.

## Two switches, do not conflate them

This is **not** the `showAnonymous` switch ([WEA-45](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-45/showanonymous-persisted-preference-and-switch)), and the tickets must keep them apart:

* `showAnonymous` — a **viewing** preference, in the Community **filter row**: whether the guest data *you look at* is counted.
* `visibleInCommunity` — a **privacy** preference, in the **account menu**: whether *you* are shown to, and counted for, everyone else.

Different columns, different meaning, different homes. A reviewer who sees "another Community boolean toggle" and merges them has created a bug where hiding yourself also changes what you see.

## Watch out

Opting out removes you from the leaderboard **and** the aggregates ([WEA-44](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-44/mood-distribution-weighted-aggregation-guests-at-025)), not just the visible rows — otherwise it's a partial opt-out that still leaks your mood into the public distribution.

Default is **visible**. Turning it off is the deliberate act; don't silently hide anyone.

Your own Stats, History and daily log are untouched — the toggle only governs what *others* see. Make sure no personal view accidentally starts filtering on it.

## Done when

* Toggling off removes the user from both the board and the mood distribution within one reload
* Toggling back on restores them
* The user's own Stats/History are identical either way
* e2e proves a hidden #1-ranked logger does not appear on the board
* `showAnonymous` and `visibleInCommunity` remain visibly distinct controls in distinct places

Spec: §7 (Community visibility)
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: i18n foundation (FR/EN) — homemade dictionary, LocaleProvider and live language switch
Description:
WorldWeathr ships **bilingual (FR / EN) from day one**. This reverses the "No i18n in this phase" non-goal in the design spec — the app must be multilingual from the start, so the machinery lands in M1, before any screen copy is written, and every screen ([WEA-16](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-16/login-signup-and-recover-screens), [WEA-17](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-17/onboarding-screen-handle-and-home-city) and beyond) consumes the dictionary instead of hardcoded English.

We reuse `pfa`'s homemade i18n system **verbatim** — zero external library, compiler-enforced FR↔EN parity, live switching (re-render, no reload) of text, dates and numbers. Currency is not in scope (pfa's was fixed EUR; WorldWeathr has none).

**Reference implementation:** `pfa/front/docs/i18n.md`, `pfa/front/src/i18n/`, `pfa/front/src/text/`.

## Scope

**Dictionaries —** `src/text/`

* `fr/<zone>.ts` = source of truth; `en/<zone>.ts` typed `const zone: typeof frZone = {…}` so a missing key, an extra key or a diverging function signature **fails** `tsc`.
* `index.ts` exports the `{ fr, en }` dictionary + `Dictionary` / `TextZone` types.
* Seed the first zones as screens land (e.g. `common`, `auth`, `onboarding`, `nav`).

**Machinery —** `src/i18n/`

* `config.ts` — `SUPPORTED_LOCALES = ["en", "fr"]`, `DEFAULT_LOCALE = "en"`, `LOCALE_LABELS` (endonyms), `NUMBER_LOCALES` (`en-US` / `fr-FR`), the `localStorage` key.
* `LocaleContext.tsx` — `LocaleProvider` (mounted in `app/providers.tsx`) + `useLocale()`. **Must never remount the tree on switch** (no `key={locale}`) — that would reset `AuthContext` to its server value (historical pfa bug).
* `useTranslations.ts` — `useTranslations("<zone>")` → that zone's object for the active locale.
* `useFormat.ts` — reactive number helpers bound to the active locale (raw non-reactive helpers stay in `@lib/format`, reserved for pure code).
* `useDateLocale.ts` — the active `date-fns` locale (+ a pure-code map).
* `interpolate.ts` — `{token}` template rendering (ICU-style, as in next-intl): **one key = one sentence**, word order lives in the dictionary, JSX styling stays in the component; an unsupplied token renders literally so typos surface on screen.
* Plurals via small functions (no ICU plural syntax for two locales); when only EN pluralises, FR keeps a `_`-prefixed param so both signatures stay identical.
* `pickSupportedLocale.ts` — `navigator.languages` → supported locale → `DEFAULT_LOCALE` fallback.
* `useUpdateLanguage.ts` — optimistic switch: context + `localStorage` + `PATCH /users/me { language }` (session + CSRF via `useRequestHelper`, [WEA-15](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-15/userequesthelper-csrf-header-403-retry-401-redirect)); revert + error toast on failure.
* `LocaleUserSync.tsx` — applies `user.language` from `/me` to the context inside the authenticated layout (cross-device source of truth); depends on `AuthContext` ([WEA-14](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-14/authcontext-getserversession-and-route-group-guards)).

**Language switcher UI** — built on the design tokens ([WEA-8](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-8/design-system-styles-structure-globals-entry-base-and-animations) / [WEA-9](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-9/design-system-colour-elevation-and-aurora-tokens) / [WEA-10](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-10/design-system-typography-and-radius-tokens)), data-driven on `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` (nothing else to touch when a third language is added).

## Locale resolution

* **Signed-in init:** `user.language` ?? `localStorage` ?? `pickSupportedLocale(navigator.languages)` ?? `DEFAULT_LOCALE`.
* **Anonymous / first-visit init:** `localStorage` ?? browser ?? `DEFAULT_LOCALE`.
* Guests get a real `User` row (`ww.guest`, [WEA-28](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-28/guest-identity-wwguest-cookie-and-guestorsessionguard)), so a guest's choice also persists to `user.language` once that row exists — `localStorage` is just the first-paint hint before it.
* Signup ([WEA-5](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-5/signup-endpoint-email-password-and-passphrase)) carries `pickSupportedLocale(navigator.languages)` in the payload.
* The persistence contract (schema field, DTO validation, endpoints) lives in the backend ticket.

## Usage rules (enforced in review)

1. Never import `@text/<zone>` directly — always `useTranslations`.
2. Never import `@lib/format` directly in React — always `useFormat`.
3. **No text evaluated at import time** — no zone destructure at module scope; Zod messages via a `makeSchema(t)` factory called inside the component, never at module scope.
4. Pure / non-hook helpers take the locale (or the texts) **as parameters**.
5. Only user-facing copy goes in dictionaries. Code and comments stay English-only.

## Default locale — `en` (decided)

`DEFAULT_LOCALE` and the SSR fallback are `en` — it matches the English design and the SEO `lang="en"` foundation ([WEA-11](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-11/seo-foundation-metadata-robots-sitemap-og-image)), with FR auto-selected for FR browsers after hydration. This deliberately diverges from pfa (which defaults to `fr`). `User.language`'s DB default must equal it (`en`, [WEA-57](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-57/userlanguage-persistence-schema-field-signup-patch-usersme-me-exposure)).

## SSR / SEO note (coordinate with [WEA-11](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-11/seo-foundation-metadata-robots-sitemap-og-image))

pfa renders the default locale on the server and applies the stored locale after hydration — a brief flash on a hard reload in the non-default locale, accepted, **no SSR cookie/middleware**. Same trade-off here. [WEA-11](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-11/seo-foundation-metadata-robots-sitemap-og-image) currently hardcodes `<html lang="en">`; since `en` is now the default this is correct for the server render, but it must emit the **resolved** locale after hydration. Reading a locale cookie in the root layout to give crawlers the correct `lang` with no flash is a possible later refinement — out of scope here, noted so [WEA-11](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-11/seo-foundation-metadata-robots-sitemap-og-image) accounts for it.

## Acceptance

* Toggling the language switch re-renders copy, dates and numbers with **no reload**.
* A missing or extra EN key fails `pnpm build` (`tsc`).
* Reload preserves the chosen locale (`localStorage`; and `user.language` once signed in).
* No hardcoded UI strings in shipped screens — everything routes through the dictionary.

Related: [WEA-6](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-6/scaffold-the-nextjs-front-temporary-holding-page) (front scaffold), [WEA-8](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-8/design-system-styles-structure-globals-entry-base-and-animations) / [WEA-9](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-9/design-system-colour-elevation-and-aurora-tokens) / [WEA-10](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-10/design-system-typography-and-radius-tokens) (design system), [WEA-11](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-11/seo-foundation-metadata-robots-sitemap-og-image) (SEO `lang`), [WEA-14](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-14/authcontext-getserversession-and-route-group-guards) (AuthContext), [WEA-15](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-15/userequesthelper-csrf-header-403-retry-401-redirect) (useRequestHelper), [WEA-16](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-16/login-signup-and-recover-screens) (auth screens), [WEA-17](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-17/onboarding-screen-handle-and-home-city) (onboarding). Title: User.language persistence — schema field, signup + PATCH /users/me, /me exposure
Description:
Backend half of the bilingual (FR / EN) foundation (companion to [WEA-56](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-56/i18n-foundation-fren-homemade-dictionary-localeprovider-and-live)). The chosen locale is a **per-user field** so it follows the account across devices and survives the guest→member upgrade. Because guests already get a real `User` row ([WEA-28](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-28/guest-identity-wwguest-cookie-and-guestorsessionguard)), `user.language` is the single source of truth for everyone — no separate anonymous store on the server.

Mirrors `pfa`'s backend i18n contract: one column, `@IsIn` validation, exposed on `/me`, settable at signup and via `PATCH /users/me`.

## Scope

**Prisma (**`User`**)** — add:

```prisma
language  String  @default("en")
```

* **Folded into** [WEA-2](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-2/prisma-7-mysql-full-schema-and-first-migration)**'s first migration**, alongside `handle`, `showAnonymous`, `visibleInCommunity` — **not** a follow-up migration. The spec's schema-once goal ("designed once … never migrate the core tables") means the column ships with the initial schema.
* The DB default is `en` — matching the front's `DEFAULT_LOCALE` ([WEA-56](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-56/i18n-foundation-fren-homemade-dictionary-localeprovider-and-live)).

**Validation & DTOs**

* `@IsIn(["en", "fr"])` for the `language` field.
* Accept optional `language` on the **signup** DTO ([WEA-5](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-5/signup-endpoint-email-password-and-passphrase)) — the front sends `pickSupportedLocale(navigator.languages)`; default `en` when absent.
* Accept `language` on `UpdateUserMeDto` for `PATCH /users/me` (the endpoint [WEA-17](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-17/onboarding-screen-handle-and-home-city) introduces for `handle` / `homeCityId` / `onboardedAt`). It is a profile field like `handle` — keep it on `PATCH /users/me`, **not** on `PATCH /users/me/preferences` (that endpoint is for viewing preferences such as `showAnonymous`).

**Exposure**

* Include `language` in the `/me` payload ([WEA-12](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-12/auth-endpoints-login-logout-me-csrf)) so the front's `LocaleUserSync` can apply it.

**Guest → member upgrade (**[WEA-29](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-29/guest-member-upgrade-on-signup)**)**

* Carry the guest row's `language` over on upgrade — a guest who picked FR stays FR after signup.

## Acceptance

* Signup with `language: "fr"` persists it; `/me` returns `language: "fr"`.
* `PATCH /users/me { "language": "en" }` updates it; an invalid value → **400**.
* The `language` column is present in the **initial** migration — no second migration for i18n.
* A guest who set FR keeps FR through the upgrade to a member account.

Related: [WEA-56](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-56/i18n-foundation-fren-homemade-dictionary-localeprovider-and-live) (front foundation), [WEA-2](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-2/prisma-7-mysql-full-schema-and-first-migration) (schema + first migration), [WEA-5](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-5/signup-endpoint-email-password-and-passphrase) (signup), [WEA-12](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-12/auth-endpoints-login-logout-me-csrf) (`/me`), [WEA-17](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-17/onboarding-screen-handle-and-home-city) (`PATCH /users/me`), [WEA-28](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-28/guest-identity-wwguest-cookie-and-guestorsessionguard) (guest identity), [WEA-29](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-29/guest-member-upgrade-on-signup) (guest→member upgrade).

Title: Design Zeus: scope, stack, ports, registry model & security
Description:
**Phase:** Foundations · the design/spec ticket that unblocks the rest.

Write a short design spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/…-zeus-design.md`) settling the decisions before any code:

* **Architecture** — runs *on* ks-b (needs local pm2/nginx/filesystem access). NestJS API + Next dashboard, same stack family as pfa/worldweathr.
* **Zeus's own ports** — propose API block `6600–6699` (api `6600`) + front `3003`; verify free with `ss -ltnp` first, per the fleet convention.
* **Port-registry data model** — apps → services, each service `{ role: front|api, port, block, pm2Name, nginxLocation, ecosystemPath, healthUrl }`. Encode the convention (`6N00–6N99` API block, `30xx` front).
* **Control surface** — which pm2 / nginx operations Zeus is allowed to run, and how (shell-out vs library).
* **Security model** — admin auth, exposure (tunnel vs IP allowlist), sudo scope, audit trail.

Done when: spec written, reviewed, and the port allocation for Zeus is confirmed free and recorded.

* Each API sits in a free `6N00` block; fronts on `30xx`.

Description:
**Phase:** Monitoring.

Give the fleet a live status screen:

Title: Process control: start/stop/restart/reload via pm2 (+ audit log)
Description:
**Phase:** Control.

Control apps from the UI instead of manual SSH + pm2:

* Start / stop / restart / reload each pm2 app; backend shells out to `pm2`.
* Confirmation on destructive actions; full audit log (who / what / when / result).
* Guardrail: Zeus must never stop or kill **itself** into an unrecoverable state.

Title: Safe port reassignment: ecosystem + nginx + reload (atomic + rollback)
Description:
**Phase:** Control · the payoff feature, and the riskiest.

Change an app's port from the registry, safely:

* Rewrite the app's `ecosystem.config.cjs` (`-p` arg + `PORT` env) **and** its nginx `proxy_pass`.
* Then `nginx -t && nginx -s reload` + `pm2 reload`.
* **Atomic with rollback** on any failure; collision guard against the registry; fully audited.

Done when: reassigning a port is a one-click, safe operation instead of hand-editing multiple files across the server.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Security hardening & audit trail
Description:
**Phase:** Security (cross-cutting) · closes the gaps left by the scaffold.

Zeus can start/stop processes and rewrite nginx, so it must be locked down:

* **Admin-only authz** on every control / reassignment endpoint.
* **Not casually public** — bound behind an SSH tunnel, or an IP allowlist + basic auth in front of nginx.
* **Least-privilege sudoers** — only the exact `nginx -t` / `nginx -s reload` commands Zeus needs, nothing broader.
* **Complete, tamper-evident audit log** of every control action.

Done when: Zeus can control the fleet but is not a soft target, and every action is traceable.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Forecast-drift ingestion — retain daily forecast snapshots + settle observed truth
Description:
New in the **schema v2 / forecast-drift** amendment. Lead-time forecast verification needs the forecast **as it was issued N days earlier** — the daily/hourly forecast tables only keep the latest value, so this pipeline retains history.

## Scope

* Extend the weather cron to fetch the **forward horizon** (`forecast_days=8` on the same Open-Meteo `/v1/forecast` call — no extra request) and **insert one** `DailyForecastSnapshot` **per target day** with `issuedDate = today`, `leadDays = 0..7`. Upsert on `@@unique([cityId, targetDate, issuedDate])` (retain per issue-day; a 2nd run the same day just refreshes it).
* **Settle step:** once a day is 1–2 days past, write its archive observed value into `DailyForecast` so it becomes reality.
* Non-fatal on gaps (base §8 rule).

## Notes

* Deferred out of M2 (see [WEA-22](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-22/forecastobservation-persistence-daily-refresh-cron)) to keep the MVP lean.
* Snapshot data accrues **forward-only** — it can't be reconstructed from the archive; optionally seed past leads via Open-Meteo's **Historical Forecast API**. The sooner this ships, the sooner lead-time data banks.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-forecast-drift-design.md` §4.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Forecast-drift endpoints — GET /stats/forecast-drift[/:date]
Description:

## Endpoints (under `stats`)

* `GET /stats/forecast-drift?cityId=&from=&to=` → aggregate: for each `leadDays`, condition **match-rate** and temperature **MAE**, each computed **vs reality** and **vs your call** (the member's last log of the day). City-scoped.
* `GET /stats/forecast-drift/:date?cityId=` → per-day: the lead-by-lead forecasts + reality + your call.
* Member-only (guest gets the locked Stats preview).

Depends on the forecast-drift **ingestion** ticket (needs `DailyForecastSnapshot` + settled `DailyForecast`). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-forecast-drift-design.md` §5, §7.
