Title: E4a — Materials: material model, base colour and mesh scale
Description:
Stage one of two of "Materials" (E4). Today a triangle's surface is a single string baked into the shape data — either a `rgba(...)` fill or a texture key — read once in `Triangle.fill` and never changeable at runtime (`src/primitives/Triangle.ts`, `fillFlat` and the `options.textures.get(this.material)` lookup above it; `src/data/shapes/*`).

This ticket introduces the runtime material model: a texture mode, a base colour that tints the live mesh, and a uniform mesh scale. It keeps the authored per-triangle slot as the per-triangle override, so the cube can go on mixing four flat faces with two subdivided textured ones while the whole mesh still answers to one material object.

**E4b — procedural textures and tiling** follows: checker and UV-grid generators, spherical UV generation, the pattern-based texture fill and UV SCALE. E4b depends on this and on nothing else.

**Unblocks**

* The five BASE swatches — shape-tab
* SCALE slider in the TRANSFORM section — shape-tab
* Two of the four MATERIAL texture chips (AUTHORED, SOLID) — shape-tab
* SHAPE INFO's MATERIAL row, and its TEXTURES row, which switch from registry-derived to runtime-derived — shape-info (`src/ui/MaterialSummary.ts`)
* The viewport HUD texture chip — viewport-hud (reads the same summary)
* The status bar texture segment — status (reads the same summary)

## Approach

### The authored slot stays; no shape-file migration

Every shape file writes its colours per triangle — `sphere` alternates two `rgba(...)` strings by `(lat + lon) % 2` (`src/data/shapes/sphere.ts` L33–L37), `menger` picks six checkered face colours per cell (L79–L86), `cuboctahedron` colours by face arity through `colorForFace` (`src/data/builder.ts` L227). Rewriting those into per-mesh materials would destroy the thing that makes the registry worth looking at. **The authored slot** `triangle[3]` **is not migrated.** It is reclassified once, at mesh build time, into an `AuthoredMaterial`:

```
type AuthoredMaterial =
  | { kind: "color"; css: string; rgba: [number, number, number, number] }
  | { kind: "texture"; key: string; uv: [UV, UV, UV] };
```

Classification must not sniff the string. `MaterialSummary`'s private `isTextureKey` currently tests `!material.startsWith("rgba")` and shape-info's acceptance criteria pin that to exactly one occurrence in the tree; a second copy inside `Triangle` would break it, and the test is wrong anyway the moment a shape author writes `#rrggbb`. Instead `src/textures/TextureRegistry.ts` gains the declared key set that already drives the `load()` call at boot (`dog`, `galaxy`, plus E4b's procedural keys) and an `isTextureKey(slot)` predicate. The registry already has `has()`, but that answers "is this image decoded yet", which is a different question and must not be used for classification — a slow-decoding texture would classify as a colour. Classification is membership in that set. The `startsWith("rgba")` test is then deleted, and shape-info's criterion "`grep -rn "startsWith(\"rgba\")" src` returns exactly one hit" becomes "returns zero hits" — amend that ticket in the same PR.

### The runtime material

```
type TextureMode = "authored" | "checker" | "uvGrid" | "solid";
interface MeshMaterial { mode: TextureMode; baseColor: string; uvScale: number; }
```

One `MeshMaterial` instance lives on `Main` and is passed **by reference** into `buildMesh`, so a change reaches the meshes that are already on screen — including both meshes alive during a shape transition (`ShapeTransitionMachine.getActiveMeshes()`). `Mesh.setMaterial(material)` loops its triangles the way `setTransform` loops its points; `Triangle.setMaterial` re-resolves and caches. (The draft cited `changeFocal` / `changeOffsetZ` as the pattern to copy — E2 deleted both when the shared `Camera` record replaced them.) Nothing is resolved per frame.

Resolution, one table, one function `resolveMaterial(authored, material)`:

| mode | triangle authored as colour | triangle authored as texture |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `authored` | authored colour × base colour | authored texture, authored UVs, `uvScale` applied |
| `checker` | procedural checker, generated UVs | procedural checker, authored UVs |
| `uvGrid` | procedural UV grid, generated UVs | procedural UV grid, authored UVs |
| `solid` | base colour flat | base colour flat, texture suppressed |

The per-triangle override is the left-hand column existing at all: the authored slot always wins on *which UVs* to use and, in `authored` mode, on what is drawn. **This ticket ships the** `authored` **and** `solid` **rows**; the two procedural rows are E4b, and their chips stay marked until it lands.

### Base colour is a multiplier, not a replacement

`out_c = round(authored_c × base_c / 255)` per channel, alpha taken from the authored colour. Multiply preserves each shape's internal contrast — the sphere stays a checker, the Menger sponge stays six-coloured — while the swatch visibly tints the whole mesh. White is the identity, so **the default swatch is the white one**, not shape-tab's `--color-swatch-red`: the first frame after this ticket must be pixel-identical to the first frame before it. Amend shape-tab's default; the palette and its order are unchanged.

Parsing the authored string needs no colour parser. Set `ctx.fillStyle = css` on a scratch 1×1 context and read `ctx.fillStyle` back: the browser normalises any CSS colour to `#rrggbb` or `rgba(r, g, b, a)`. Parse those two forms, once, at build time.

In `solid` the mode's product is white so the rule collapses to "the fill is the base colour", and in E4b's procedural modes the base colour is the ink the texture is generated with. One rule everywhere.

### Mesh scale

**Scale folds into** `ShapeRig`**, not into the projection.** The draft said the opposite — `Point3D.modelScale`, `Mesh.changeScale` looping every point, and "no scale matrix, the mesh transform untouched" — and every reason it gave has since expired. Do not build it that way.

* **It reintroduces what E2 removed.** `Camera` exists because two public fields on `Point3D` were written through `Mesh` at 3960 writes per zoom tick on the torus knot; its header says so. `Mesh.changeScale(v)` looping `modelScale` is that same shape at 3960 writes per SCALE tick. The draft's instruction to "copy `changeFocal` line for line" cannot be followed regardless: E2 deleted `changeFocal`.
* **It would break clipping silently.** `Point3D.isClipped` calls `camera.clips(this.z)`, and `Camera.clips` tests `depthAt(z) = z + eyeDistance`. A scale applied inside `convert3D2D` never reaches that test, so the near plane would judge unscaled depth and the draft's own "at SCALE 300 nothing inverts because E2's near plane rejects those triangles" could not hold. `Mesh.renderMesh`'s depth binning (`triangle.depth + pass.eyeDistance`) and the Z-BUFFER histogram inherit the same error.
* **Its stated reason is gone.** It wanted scale kept "a model property independent of whatever the camera rig is doing". [COS-434](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-434/e1d-give-the-shape-back-its-own-orientation-and-the-camera-rows-of-its) (E1d) split `ShapeRig` out of `CameraRig`, so there is now a model transform that is not the camera, and that is where a model property belongs.

The correction:

* `ShapeRig` gains `scale` (1.0 at rest) and a `Matrix3D.scaleMatrix(factor)` builder. `pose()` becomes `S_scale · roll · pitch · yaw`, so the scale sits innermost and is applied about the model origin — which is also the centre of rotation, exactly as the draft wanted.
* Cost is zero per vertex: `setFromSource` already performs the full 4x4 multiply, and the factor is one number on one object rather than one field on each of 3960 points.
* No compounding, for the reason the draft already conceded: `setFromSource` rebuilds every vertex from pristine `sx/sy/sz` each frame, so there is always an identity to return to.
* Clipping, the painter's sort and the depth histogram all become correct without further work, because all three read `z` after the transform rather than before it.
* `Point3D` is not touched by this ticket at all. Neither is `Triangle`'s projection path.

UI 10..300 maps to 0.1..3.0. **No cap and no guard belongs anywhere here** — E2's near plane rejects what a large scale pushes behind the eye, and it now genuinely sees the scaled depth.

Amend [COS-434](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-434/e1d-give-the-shape-back-its-own-orientation-and-the-camera-rows-of-its), which carries the opposite instruction ("Do not fold SCALE into ShapeRig") written before the projection path had been re-read.

### `MaterialSummary` becomes runtime-derived

`src/ui/texLabel.ts` no longer exists. [COS-377](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-377/t06-give-the-material-derivation-a-single-owner) (T06, "give the material derivation a single owner") replaced its two free functions with `src/ui/MaterialSummary.ts` — a class built once per shape from an `Object3D`, exposing `textureKeys` and `label`, with the three consumers sharing one field. The consolidation the draft was reaching for has already happened; what remains is making the derivation read the runtime material instead of only the authored geometry.

* `MaterialSummary`'s constructor takes the shared `MeshMaterial` alongside the `Object3D`, and `label` widens from `"TEXTURED" | "SOLID"` to `"TEXTURED" | "CHECKER" | "UV GRID" | "SOLID"`. In `authored` mode it yields `TEXTURED` when the shape has any texture-authored triangle and `SOLID` when it does not — today's behaviour, preserved.
* `textureKeys` returns the keys actually sampled: authored keys in `authored` mode, empty in `solid`, and E4b's generated key in the procedural modes.
* It is rebuilt on a material change as well as on a shape change, since the material is now scene state. `Main` owns both triggers.
* The private `isTextureKey` helper — which is where `startsWith("rgba")` lives now — is deleted in favour of membership in the declared key set on `TextureRegistry`.

The draft's criterion still applies with one file renamed: `grep -rn 'startsWith("rgba")' src` returns zero hits, and classification goes through the registry's declared keys.

### Chip labels: `NO TEXTURE` is renamed

The mockup's fourth chip is `NO TEXTURE`, which in an engine whose shapes ship their own materials would either be a synonym for SOLID or the only state in which the dog and galaxy textures are visible. Rename it **AUTHORED** and make it the default. Four chips, two columns, no layout change; shape-tab's chip list and its `CHECKER` default are amended in the same PR. Same reason as the white swatch: the default state is the frame the renderer already draws.

## Constraints and risks

* **The first frame must not change.** Defaults are mode `authored`, base colour white, UV scale 8 (inert until E4b), scale 100. Verify by screenshot diff against `master`, not by eye.
* **Opacity must keep working.** `TriangleRenderOptions.opacity` is applied via `globalAlpha` before the fill (L129–L131) and the coupling with backface culling is owned by shape-tab. This is a test, not a change.
* `convert3D2D` **is no longer contended by this ticket.** The draft planned a multiplication on three coordinates there; with scale moved into `ShapeRig` this ticket does not touch the projection at all. E7 still factors it into `project(out)` and E2b still adds polygon clipping — neither collides with anything here.
* **Order.** E4a lands after E2 and after E6, and before E4b. E2 supplies the near plane that makes the scale cap unnecessary. E6 splits `Triangle.render` into `project()` / `isFrontFacing()` / `fill()`; the resolved-fill cache belongs inside E6's `fill()`, so building it against the un-split `render()` means writing it twice. E3a also parses the authored `rgba(...)` string once at construction for its shade multiply — that is this ticket's `AuthoredMaterial.rgba` and must be one parse, so E4a lands before E3a.
* **Registry counts must not move.** SHAPE INFO TRIANGLES, the primitive chip meta line and GEOMETRY TRIANGLES are registry counts (D6). Nothing here adds or removes a triangle.
* **RESET owns the new slices** (D7): texture mode, base colour and mesh scale all return to the defaults above through the toolbar's single reset path.

## Departures decided during implementation

Four changes to the approach above, each made after reading the tree and each landed with its reasoning recorded in the code.

**1. The colour parse is a regex (**`src/rendering/cssColor.ts`**), not a scratch canvas.** The section above says "no colour parser — set `ctx.fillStyle` and read it back". That needs a DOM, and the multiply blend is exactly the kind of pure derivation this epic keeps moving into the node test environment; a blend that can only be exercised through a canvas is a blend nothing asserts. Coverage is bounded and checked: every authored colour in the registry is `rgba(r, g, b, a)` (0 hex, 0 named colours) and `getComputedStyle` returns `rgb(r, g, b)`. The parser covers those plus `#rgb` / `#rrggbb`; anything else passes through unblended rather than painting black, and a test asserts no registry triangle falls into that case.

**2.** `--color-swatch-white` **becomes a literal** `#ffffff`**.** It aliased `--color-text-primary` (`#eaf0ff`). As a multiplier that is not the identity — it tints every shape blue and drops ~8% of every channel — so the pixel-identical first frame failed on the default swatch. The token is now a literal with the reason recorded beside it in `colors.css`.

**3.** `isTextureKey` **lives in** `src/textures/textureKeys.ts`**, not on** `TextureRegistry`**.** `Triangle` classifies its authored slot at construction and has no registry then — the registry only arrives at render time through `TriangleRenderOptions`. The declared key set is therefore its own module, imported by both `Triangle` and `MaterialSummary`, and it also owns the key→URL record `TextureRegistry.load` consumes so the two cannot drift. `TextureRegistry` is untouched, which settles this ticket's own warning structurally: `has()` cannot be misused for classification if classification never sits beside it.

**4.** `Mesh.boundingRadius` **follows the transform.** Not in the plan above, and SCALE breaks it without this. `Surface3D` sets the Z-buffer's bin edges to `camera.distance ± mesh.boundingRadius`, folded from the registry's raw coordinates — at SCALE 3.0 every depth sample falls outside that window and the histogram saturates at both ends. `setTransform` now derives the uniform factor from the matrix's first column (one `sqrt` per mesh per frame), which is exact because the linear part of this composition is always uniform-scale × rotation.

Smaller, and worth knowing before reading the diff:

* `ShapeAngles` **is renamed** `ShapePose`**, and** `setAngles` **→** `setPose`**.** Scale is not an angle, and `setAngles({ scale })` would be a lie. Three call sites.
* `MaterialLabel` **stays** `"TEXTURED" | "SOLID"`**.** The section above widens it to four values now, but `CHECKER` and `UV GRID` are unreachable until E4b — a union member nothing can produce is dead code with a comment attached. E4b widens it when it can also return them.
* **The registry-wide identity test replaces part of the screenshot criterion.** `src/rendering/__tests__/material.test.ts` asserts that at the defaults every triangle of all twenty shapes resolves to the colour it was authored with, compared parsed rather than as strings. That settles the material half of "the first frame must not change" by construction; the geometry half is `snapshot:geometry`'s and the transform half is `ShapeRig`'s. What is left for the screenshot pass is layout and CSS.

Title: E3a — Face normals and the directional key light
Description:
First of four parts of "Shading pipeline" (E3). The console advertises a six-mode shading pipeline, a directional key light with four parameters, and three rasteriser flags. The engine behind it computes no normal, has no light, and fills every triangle with a colour resolved from the string baked into its data tuple.

**This part adds face normals and one directional key light with Lambert and Blinn-Phong terms. No rasteriser change — it keeps** `context.fill()`**.** It is shippable on its own and visibly changes the frame. E3b (depth-buffered rasteriser), E3c (the four per-pixel modes) and E3d (dithering, edge AA) follow.

**Unblocks**

* The four LIGHTING sliders AZIMUTH, ELEVATION, AMBIENT, SPECULAR — render-tab
* The `LGT` / `KEY_LIGHT` scene-graph row, including its visibility toggle — scene-graph
* E5b's ground shadow, which needs a light direction in world space and cannot be built on a viewer-locked one

The FLAT chip is **not** on that list, and the draft was wrong to put it there: `ShadingSection.ts:33` already ships FLAT with no placeholder affordance, because "not wireframe" is a real state the rasteriser really has. What this ticket changes is what FLAT *means* — a lit flat fill instead of an unlit one. `modeLabel.ts` keeps its two-value `ShadingMode` and needs no edit; do not widen it here.

## Rebase note — this ticket was written before four of its dependencies landed

Drafted 2026-07-28, against a tree that no longer exists. Everything below has been corrected against the current source; the corrections are listed here rather than silently applied, because several of them change what the work is.

**Paths.** `src/ui/uiState.ts` is now `src/ui/UIStateStore.ts`, a class, and it already declares `lightAzimuth` / `lightElevation` / `lightAmbient` / `lightSpecular` (L94–L97) with the comment marking them E3 placeholders. `src/index.ts` is now twelve lines of ignition; the composition root is `src/app/Main.ts`.

**The placeholder markers are not in** `src/index.html`**.** The four lighting rows get theirs from `LightingSection.ts` — a shared `placeholder` option passed to each `SliderRow`, plus `buildHint()` and `HINT_ID = "ph-lighting"`. The KEY_LIGHT row gets its from `sceneRows.ts:37` (`placeholder: true`) against the shared `ph-scene-row` hint at `index.html:156`, whose text names the lighting model as one of two reasons. Removing the light's half of that sentence without removing the sky/floor half is part of this ticket; the row itself belongs to E7.

**E6 already split the render path.** `Triangle.render` (`Triangle.ts:155`) is now `project()` / `isFrontFacing()` / `fill()`, and `Mesh.renderMesh` (`Mesh.ts:99`) runs them as three timed passes with a `survivors` array between the second and the third. The shade multiply goes inside `fill()`, which means it runs on survivors only — see Approach.

**E5a landed, so the light-space question the draft closed is open again.** The draft said "there is no ground plane to elevate from until E5a". There is one now: `GROUND_Y` (`worldScale.ts`), `GroundProjection`, `GroundFloor`, `GroundGrid`. The draft's eye-space light is no longer the obvious reading, and E5b's shadow makes it the wrong one. Resolved below.

**E4a landed.** `AuthoredMaterial.rgba` holds the parsed channels (`src/rendering/material.ts`), as the draft assumed. What the draft could not know is that the channels reaching the canvas are `ResolvedMaterial.fill`, not the authored ones — the BASE swatch multiplies first. The light multiplies what E4a resolved, not what the registry authored.

**Line numbers.** All of the draft's citations have moved. The load-bearing ones today: `Point3D.zValue` at `Point3D.ts:46` with `x`/`y` private at L7–L8; `Triangle.a/b/c` private at `Triangle.ts:66–68`; `Mesh.points/triangles` private readonly at `Mesh.ts:51–52`; the 2D backface test at `Triangle.ts:201–208`; the painter's sort at `Mesh.ts:205–207`.

**The epic-premise correction the draft opens with still stands** and is now partly discharged. `Mesh.sortByDepth()` does sort, back-to-front on the mean z, so it is a painter's algorithm and not an unsorted walk. Of the three real defects the draft names, all three survive: the sort is still per mesh, centroid ordering is still wrong on `menger` / `cross` / `torusKnot`, and it still runs every frame in place. All three are E3b's to fix, not this ticket's. Keep the sort exactly as it is.

## Approach

### Accessors

`Point3D` exposes only `zValue`. Add `xValue` / `yValue` getters in the same style. `MeshFactory.ts:52–56` records the deferral by name — E6 left these to "whichever of E3a or E5b lands first and actually needs it". E5b ([COS-247](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-247/e5b-ground-shadow-distance-fog-and-the-layer-pass-count)) is still Backlog, so this ticket adds them and E5b consumes them. One definition.

### Normals live in `Triangle`, not in a `Mesh.computeNormals()` pass

The draft routed the normal pass into `Mesh` to avoid widening `Triangle.a/b/c`. That does not work: `Mesh` cannot reach a triangle's vertices either — they are private on `Triangle`, and `Mesh` holds `Triangle` instances, not their points. Either way something has to be widened.

`Triangle` already owns its three points and, since E6, already owns `fill()`. So the face normal is computed inside `Triangle`, from fields it already has, and nothing is widened at all beyond the two `Point3D` getters. That also puts the cost in the right place: `fill()` is called only on `survivors`, so a backface-culled or near-plane-clipped triangle costs no normal. On a closed solid that is roughly half the mesh, which a whole-mesh pass would have paid for twice over.

The points *are* the transformed positions — `setTransform` rewrites every vertex from its pristine source each frame (`Mesh.ts:178`), so there is no separate model matrix and no object-space shortcut. Normals are per-frame, always.

**Do not reach for** `Vec3Math`**.** It exists, it has `cross` / `dot` / `normalise`, and it is the wrong tool: its own header says it stays tuple math because it runs at import time in the generators, and every method allocates a fresh array. On the render path that is several arrays per drawn triangle per frame — precisely the allocation churn `Triangle.ts:70–76` records this codebase's early tickets removing. Write the arithmetic out on scalars.

### Sign convention

After transform, x is right, y is **down** (canvas convention, from `convert3D2D`'s `centerY + y * scale`), and z increases away from the eye — `Camera.depthAt(z) = z + eyeDistance`, so the eye sits at `z = −eyeDistance`, negative.

* `Nraw = (b − a) × (c − a)`.
* `isFrontFacing()` computes `v1x·v2y − v1y·v2x` on the projected vertices and returns `> 0`. If the three vertices shared one perspective scale `s`, that expression is exactly `s²·Nraw.z`. So the existing test is `sign(Nraw.z)`, and **front-facing means** `Nraw.z > 0`.
* The outward normal used for lighting is `N̂ = −Nraw / |Nraw|`, which points toward the eye on visible faces.

The agreement between the two is a real test, not a comment: build a cube through `MeshFactory`, project it, and assert `isFrontFacing()` matches `Nraw.z > 0` on every face. `Point3D`, `Camera`, `RenderTarget` and `Triangle` all construct under the node environment — `projection.test.ts` already does exactly this — so it belongs in the vitest suite rather than in a boot-time assertion.

### The light is fixed in the world, not in the viewer

This is the draft's one reversal, and it is forced.

E5b ([COS-247](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-247/e5b-ground-shadow-distance-fog-and-the-layer-pass-count)) is blocked by this ticket and adds a **ground shadow**. A shadow is cast onto the ground plane, in world coordinates; a light defined in eye space has no fixed relationship to that plane and cannot cast a coherent one. Choosing eye space here would mean E5b either re-derives the light or throws this one away. Beyond that: since E1c the camera moves the world rather than the object, and since E5a there is a visible horizon — a key light welded to the viewer would leave the highlight motionless while the ground swings past it, which reads as shading painted onto the texture.

So the direction is built in world space and rotated into eye space once per frame:

```
// world, y down, so "up" is −y
Lx =  cos(e)·cos(a)
Ly = −sin(e)
Lz =  cos(e)·sin(a)
```

then multiplied by the camera's rotation. **That rotation is already threaded to where it is needed**: `Surface3D.render` receives `cameraTransform: this.rig.viewMatrix()`, which is `C · T(−target)` — a pure translation composed after a rotation, so its upper-left 3×3 *is* the world→eye rotation, and a direction ignores the translation column. No new `CameraRig` API, and correctly no turntable in it: the spin rides the object matrix, so the light does not chase the shape around.

One 3-vector rotation per frame, not per triangle.

Azimuth's zero and its direction of travel are fixed by one constraint rather than asserted here: the shipped defaults (135°, 42°) must still read as an upper-left key at the opening camera pose. Check it during implementation and write the resulting convention into the file.

### Shading, per face

* `kd = max(0, N̂ · L̂)`; `ambient = AMBIENT/100`; `shade = ambient + (1 − ambient)·kd`.
* Blinn-Phong specular: `V̂ = normalise(eye − p̄)`, the eye at `(0, 0, −camera.distance)` in eye space and `p̄` the face centroid; `Ĥ = normalise(L̂ + V̂)`; `spec = (SPECULAR/100)·max(0, N̂·Ĥ)^32`. The shininess exponent is fixed at 32 — the mockup has no slider for it, do not invent one.
* `out.rgb = clamp(resolved.rgb · shade + 255·spec, 0, 255)`.

**Shade what E4a resolved, not what the registry authored.** `AuthoredMaterial.rgba` is the parse this ticket must not duplicate, but the channels that reach the canvas have already been through the BASE multiply. `ResolvedMaterial` carries a formatted string today; it needs to carry the numeric channels alongside it so the light can multiply them without re-parsing. That is a small addition to `material.ts`, not a second parser, and it keeps the "no second colour parse" criterion honest.

Quantise `shade` to 1/64 steps and memoise the output string on `resolved + step`, so the cache holds at most 64 entries per distinct material. Rebuilding a fill string per triangle per frame is 7920 allocations on the torus knot.

### Degenerate faces

Real in this data, not hypothetical. `SphereGenerator` emits `lonSegments + 1` = 13 coincident points at `theta = 0` and 13 more at `theta = π` (`addVertices`), and `addFaces` builds triangles from them — every triangle in the first and last latitude band has two coincident vertices, so `|Nraw|` is 0. Guard on `|Nraw| < 1e-9` and skip lighting for that face rather than writing `NaN` into a colour string, which paints nothing and is invisible in a stack trace.

### Textured faces

`context.fill()` cannot modulate a `drawImage`. Shade a textured face with a second pass: after `AffineTextureMapper.draw()` returns, fill `rgba(0, 0, 0, 1 − shade)` over the same triangle path. The mapper opens and closes its own `save`/`restore` pair, so the overlay sits inside `fill()`'s outer pair and inherits its `globalAlpha` — which is correct, an overlay on a half-transparent face should be half-transparent too. It is an approximation of a multiply and it darkens only; it disappears in E3b, where the texel is multiplied per pixel.

### Where the values come from

`Main` reads the four store values and the KEY_LIGHT visibility, builds the eye-space direction from `rig.viewMatrix()`, and hands a `Lighting` down through `TriangleRenderOptions` — the same seam `textures` already uses (`Main.paint`, `Main.ts:842`). The four `SliderRow.onInput` handlers gain a `renderPausedFrame()` push so a drag moves the frame while the loop is stopped, matching every other live row.

`Lighting` is a class: it holds the direction, the three scalars and the quantised cache. If it passes ~160 lines the direction derivation splits out as a pure module beside it.

## Constraints and risks

* **KEY_LIGHT visibility.** The scene-graph row's toggle must actually kill the light — ambient only — not dim a label. Rows 2 and 3 stay placeholders; they belong to E7.
* **The opening frame changes, deliberately, and this is the first de-mock ticket where that is true.** Every previous one in this epic could claim a pixel-identical first frame. This one cannot: a lit shape is the whole deliverable. Run `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` anyway — geometry must be byte-identical, since nothing here touches a vertex.
* **The cost lands in RASTER**, in E6's timing bracket, because `fill()` is where the shading runs. That is honest — it is per-drawn-triangle work — but the FRAME TIME card will show RASTER grow and it should be read as the light, not as a regression.
* **Do not touch layout.** Per the epic's rules: if a real label does not fit its chip, that is a bug here, not licence to redesign.
* **Do not touch the painter's sort.** Its three defects are E3b's.
* **Not in scope, named so they do not creep in:** near-plane clipping (E2b), shadows (E5b), multiple lights, per-material shininess, smoothing groups, and any of the five non-FLAT shading chips.
* **Order.** After E6, E2, E4a and E5a — all Done. Downstream: E3b, E5b and E7 all wait on this.

## Files

* `src/primitives/Point3D.ts` — `xValue` / `yValue` getters alongside `zValue`
* `src/primitives/Triangle.ts` — the face normal and the shade multiply inside `fill()`, plus the textured-face overlay
* `src/rendering/material.ts` — `ResolvedMaterial` carries the resolved channels alongside the formatted string
* `src/rendering/Lighting.ts` — new. Direction from azimuth/elevation, the world→eye rotation, Lambert and Blinn-Phong, ambient, and the quantised shade cache
* `src/rendering/__tests__/Lighting.test.ts` — new
* `src/primitives/__tests__/projection.test.ts` — the normal-sign agreement on every cube face
* `src/ui/inspector/LightingSection.ts` — the four rows lose their placeholder affordance and gain an `onChange` that reaches the engine
* `src/ui/scene/sceneRows.ts`, `src/index.html` — KEY_LIGHT stops being a placeholder; the shared hint loses its lighting clause
* `src/app/Main.ts` — owns the `Lighting`, wires the four sliders and the KEY_LIGHT toggle, keeps `renderFrame` and `renderPausedFrame` on one code path

## Done when

- [X] Face normals are recomputed per frame from the transformed points, and a vitest case confirms `Nraw.z > 0` agrees with `isFrontFacing()` on every `cube` face
- [X] Moving AZIMUTH, ELEVATION, AMBIENT or SPECULAR visibly changes the frame, paused as well as running; AMBIENT at 100 flattens shading completely and SPECULAR at 0 removes every highlight

- [X] Colour strings are cached — and the cache allocates nothing on a hit, see Departures

- [X] The BASE swatch still tints, and the light multiplies the tinted colour rather than the authored one
- [X] The placeholder affordance is gone from the four lighting rows and from KEY_LIGHT, and no other placeholder marker is removed
- [X] RESET restores the four lighting values (D7)

- [X] `typecheck`, `lint`, `lint:rules` and `test` all pass — 153 tests / 17 suites, up from 122 / 15
- [X] Everything above holds at `max-width: 899px` as well as on desktop, with no layout change

## Departures from the rebased spec

Four, each landed with its reasoning in the code.

**1. The shade cache is two-level, not one string key.** The spec said "memoise on `material + step`, at most 64 entries per distinct material", which predates specular being in the same string: the output depends on both terms, and building a `${fill}|${shade}|${spec}` key would allocate a string per triangle per frame to look up a cache whose whole job is to avoid allocating a string per triangle per frame. `ShadeCache` keys a `Map` on the fill string the caller already holds, then indexes a sparse array by `shadeStep * 17 + specStep`. Zero allocation on a hit. The bound is 65 x 17 sparse slots per distinct colour rather than 64 flat, and the registry's shapes carry between two and six colours each.

**2.** `Lighting` **split at 167 code lines.** The house limit is ~160 and nothing comparable in `src/` exceeds 143. `ShadeCache` took the memo table, the string building and the two step counts — it owns the quantisation because the resolution *is* the table's dimensions, and `Lighting` imports the counts rather than declaring its own. 117 / 61 after the split.

**3.** `ShapeThumbnails` **got a light of its own.** Not in the spec, and forced by making `lighting` required on `TriangleRenderOptions`: the picker chips go through the real rasteriser, and an unlit chip beside a lit viewport is the second source of truth that class exists to refuse. Its own instance at the shipped defaults, posed by the same matrix the thumbnail mesh is, so the chips do not chase the LIGHTING rows — they are painted once from `init()` and re-rendering twenty meshes per slider tick would be a poor trade.

**4. The sign test is asserted under ORTHOGRAPHIC, plus a second case.** The spec's identity — `isFrontFacing()` agrees with `Nraw.z > 0` — is only exact when all three vertices share one projection scale, which perspective does not give a face running away from the eye. It is pinned under orthographic where it is exact, and backed by the geometric claim it stands in for: `-Nraw` points away from the origin on every face of the cube and the sphere, which holds under any projection and is the property the shading actually depends on.

## Verified in the frame

Chrome MCP is not connected in this environment, so the walk ran through headless Chrome over CDP. `master` was checked out into a worktree and screenshotted at the same pose for the comparisons.

* The cube's textured faces darken by orientation: the dog face turned up toward the key stays bright while the galaxy face turned away drops hard. Confirmed against `master` at an identical pose with SPIN zeroed.

* `.placeholder-hint` is a 1x1 clipped screen-reader element, so removing the lighting one cannot reflow anything — the no-layout-change criterion holds by construction rather than by inspection.

Title: E3b — Software scanline rasteriser with a depth buffer
Description:
Second of four parts of "Shading pipeline" (E3), and **the load-bearing item of the whole epic** — everything per-pixel waits on it. Canvas 2D has no z-buffer and no way to bolt one onto `fill()`. A real depth buffer means owning the rasteriser: `putImageData`-backed scanline fills, not `context.fill()`.

It delivers the Z-BUFFER toggle and correct concave self-occlusion, and it fixes the three painter's-algorithm defects E3a documented: the per-mesh sort that composites the two transition meshes in array order, centroid ordering failing on `menger` / `cross` / `torusKnot`, and 103k getter-heavy comparisons per frame on the torus knot.

**Unblocks**

* The Z-BUFFER pipeline toggle — render-tab
* Correct self-occlusion on the concave shapes
* The per-pixel machinery E3c's GOURAUD / DEPTH / NORMALS modes and E3d's two passes both need

## Approach

Buffers are allocated from `renderTarget.width/height` (E9a's shared module), never from literals, and reallocated on `setSize` so E9b does not have to reopen the rasteriser. At today's 1024 × 640:

* colour: `ImageData(1024, 640)`, 655 360 px, 2 621 440 bytes.
* depth: `Float32Array(655360)`, 2 621 440 bytes.

Store `1/d` where `d` is E2's eye-space depth (`z + fl/k`), the same denominator the projection already divides by. `1/d` interpolates linearly in screen space and `d` does not, so the depth test is `if (invD > depth[i])` — nearer is larger — and one linear interpolation per pixel is exact. Rasterise with edge functions over the triangle's screen bounding box, incrementing the three edge values and `invD` per pixel; roughly 12–20 ops per candidate pixel.

Per-frame cost to expect, and the number this ticket must actually measure rather than assume:

* clears: `depth.fill(Infinity)` plus the colour clear, 5.2 MB of typed-array writes, ~0.3–0.8 ms.
* `putImageData` of a full frame: one 2.6 MB upload, ~0.5–2 ms depending on browser.
* inner loop: at ~15 ops/px, a 16.7 ms budget leaves room for roughly 1–2 M pixel iterations per frame once everything else is paid for. Full canvas coverage is 655k, so that is 2–3× overdraw over the whole frame, or full overdraw over the ~30% of the frame a shape covers at the default zoom. It fits, but not with margin.
* per-triangle setup on `torusKnot` (7920 triangles): project three vertices, bbox, edge coefficients — order 1–3 ms on its own. Small triangles mean setup, not fill, dominates on that shape.

Two mitigations, both required rather than optional:

1. **Dirty rect.** Track the union screen bbox of the submitted triangles and clear/upload only that region — `putImageData(img, 0, 0, dx, dy, dw, dh)` takes a dirty rectangle.
2. **Background as the clear source.** `BackgroundRenderer.render` redraws an identical sky gradient, sky bitmap, atmosphere, checker floor and vignette every frame with no per-frame inputs (`src/rendering/BackgroundRenderer.ts` L16–L25). Snapshot it once with `getImageData` and clear the colour buffer with `data.set(snapshot)` — a 2.6 MB copy, cheaper than redrawing gradients, and it removes the background cost from the frame entirely. Invalidate the snapshot on a layer-flag change (world-tab's `setLayers`, E5's `setWorld`) and on E9b's `resize`. **The snapshot stops being valid outright once E5b lands**: its ground-shadow blob depends on the mesh bounds and therefore changes every frame. If E5b is already in, the snapshot covers sky + atmosphere + floor + grid only, and the shadow and vignette are drawn per frame after the mesh — say which passes the snapshot covers rather than assuming the whole background is static.

`putImageData` ignores `globalAlpha` and all compositing, so it cannot blend the mesh over an untouched background; seeding the colour buffer from the snapshot is what makes src-over blending work, and it is also what makes the existing OPACITY slider (`TriangleRenderOptions.opacity`) survive, as a per-pixel blend against the buffer.

**The near-plane guard is E2's, not this ticket's.** `d` going non-positive at reachable zoom settings is a bug that exists today and that `1/d` would amplify — it flips sign and inverts the depth test. E2 has already added `near` / `far` to the shared camera record and rejects those triangles in `Triangle.render` before projection. **Consume E2's rejection; do not add a second epsilon.** Proper near-plane clipping (splitting the triangle at the plane) is E2b — link it, do not half-implement it here.

**The Z-BUFFER toggle selects the backend.** ON = the depth-buffered rasteriser; OFF = the existing `Triangle.render` painter path unchanged. That gives the flag a real meaning, and gives a fallback if the perf gate fails. Structure it as `src/rendering/Rasterizer.ts` alongside the existing path, with `Surface3D.render` choosing; keep `Triangle.render` intact so OFF is a genuine A/B.

Keep `Mesh.renderMesh`'s depth sort even with the buffer on: E3d's edge antialiasing blends at silhouettes, and blended pixels still need back-to-front order.

## Constraints and risks

* **60fps is the risk, not correctness.** The rasteriser must be measured against `frameMs`, which the frame-time ticket already exports. Gate: `sphere` (240 triangles) and `cube` (792) hold ≥ 55 fps, `torusKnot` (7920) and `menger` (2112) hold ≥ 30 fps with Z-BUFFER on. If the gate fails, Z-BUFFER ships defaulting OFF and the render-tab default flips with it; do not ship a default that halves the frame rate to satisfy a mockup.
* **The frame gets uglier before it gets better.** Between this ticket and E3d the mesh has hard aliased edges — `context.fill()` is antialiased by the browser and a hand-written rasteriser is not. Land E3d in the same release or keep Z-BUFFER off by default until it does.
* **Two rasterisers to keep working.** Wireframe, backface culling and opacity all reach the rasteriser through `TriangleRenderOptions` (`Triangle.ts` L61–L65) and must behave identically on both backends. Same for the affine texture path, which is reimplemented per pixel here — the subdivision-based warping workaround documented in `src/data/builder.ts` stays valid, and perspective-correct UVs become possible for free once `1/d` is interpolated, but that is a change in appearance and should be a deliberate, separately noted step.
* **The drawn count contract holds (D6).** `Surface3D.render` still returns the number of triangles drawn. Under the rasteriser, "drawn" means passed culling and E2's near plane; triangles fully rejected by the depth test still count, otherwise the number would flicker with occlusion.
* `stop()` **zeroes** `renderedTriangles` **on pause** (`src/index.ts` L577–L584) and `renderPausedFrame` re-renders on control changes. Both call sites must go through the same backend selection; a paused frame rendered by the other backend would visibly jump.
* **Transitions.** `getRenderables()` returns two meshes with `offsetX` / `offsetY` during the 1250ms transition. One shared depth buffer across both is correct and is what fixes the per-mesh sort defect, but the offsets must be applied before the depth test, not after.
* **Order.** After E6, E2 and E3a. E6 splits `Triangle.render` into `project()` / `isFrontFacing()` / `fill()` and replaces the `Point2D` projection fields with scalars — that is exactly the seam this rasteriser needs. E2 supplies the near plane and `d`. E3a supplies the face normals the flat shade uses. E9a's `renderTarget` is where the buffer dimensions come from.

## Files

* `src/primitives/Point3D.ts` — document that the projection denominator is what the depth buffer stores the reciprocal of
* `src/primitives/Triangle.ts` — expose the projected vertices and `d` for the rasteriser; keep `render()` as the painter-path backend
* `src/primitives/Mesh.ts` — submit triangles to the selected backend; keep the existing depth sort
* `src/primitives/Surface3D.ts` — choose the backend from `uiState.zbuffer`, own the colour and depth buffers, the background snapshot, the dirty rect and the `putImageData` present; keep the drawn-count return value
* `src/rendering/Rasterizer.ts` — new. Edge-function triangle fill, `1/d` depth test, flat shade, affine texel sampling
* `src/rendering/BackgroundRenderer.ts` — expose the frame snapshot used as the colour-buffer clear source
* `src/ui/uiState.ts` — the `zbuffer` boolean stops being inert
* `src/index.html` — remove the placeholder markers from the Z-BUFFER row

## Done when

- [ ] Z-BUFFER ON routes through `Rasterizer` and OFF through the unchanged `Triangle.render` path, and the two produce the same silhouette on `cube`
- [ ] `menger`, `cross` and `torusKnot` self-occlude correctly with Z-BUFFER on, verified against a named frame where the painter path is visibly wrong
- [ ] During a shape transition both meshes share one depth buffer and interpenetrate correctly
- [ ] Triangles behind the near plane are skipped by E2's rejection; this ticket adds no epsilon of its own, and dragging the zoom slider to maximum on `menger` produces no mirrored faces

Title: E3c — GOURAUD, DEPTH, NORMALS and POINTS modes
Description:
Third of four parts of "Shading pipeline" (E3). E3a gave the engine face normals and a key light; E3b gave it a depth-buffered rasteriser. This ticket adds the four remaining shading modes, which is what finally makes all six SHADING MODE chips do something real and lets the mockup's cosmetic CSS filters be deleted rather than de-mocked.

Needs E3a for normals and E3b for per-pixel interpolation. POINTS alone does not need E3b and can land first inside this ticket.

**Unblocks**

* SHADING MODE chips POINTS, GOURAUD, DEPTH, NORMALS — render-tab. The `PREVIEW` note on the SHADING MODE header goes away with them.
* The viewport HUD mode chip and the six `[data-shading-mode="…"] … canvas { filter: … }` cosmetic rules, which are **deleted rather than de-mocked** — viewport-hud
* SHAPE INFO's SHADING row — shape-info: stops being a two-valued `WIRE`/`FLAT` derivation and reads all six labels from `modeLabel()`
* The status bar's mode segment — status

## Approach

* **POINTS**: project every `Point3D`, depth-test it, write a 2 × 2 block. Costs `points.length` per frame — 3960 on the torus knot (`PATH_SEGMENTS 220 × TUBE_SEGMENTS 18`), 4224 on the Menger sponge, which is the registry maximum. Works on both backends; on the painter path it just draws every point.
* **GOURAUD**: vertex normals are the area-weighted sum of adjacent face normals, accumulated over the shared points array each frame. `Triangle` holds `Point3D` references, not indices, so pass the indices already available at `src/index.ts` L404–L415 into the constructor and accumulate into a `Float32Array(points.length * 3)`. Interpolate the three vertex shades per pixel in the rasteriser. Two honest caveats to record: the cube's four flat-coloured faces share the eight corner points (`src/data/shapes/cube.ts` L20–L29 — the other two faces are subdivided texture grids with their own vertices), so averaging rounds those corners; and the generated shapes duplicate their seam column (`lon = 0` and `lon = LON_SEGMENTS` are distinct points in `sphere.ts`, `donut.ts`, `torusKnot.ts`), so a seam line will show. This data has no smoothing groups and adding them is not this ticket.
* **DEPTH**: greyscale from the depth buffer. Normalise against the per-frame min/max of the submitted `1/d` rather than inventing a range — and note that E2's `near`/`far` are the view volume, not the shape's extent, so they are the wrong normalisation for a legible image. E6 has already re-derived the z-buffer histogram's axis labels from the real depth range; use the same two numbers so the widget and the mode agree.
* **NORMALS**: `rgb = N̂ · 0.5 + 0.5`. Flat per face is enough. Because y is down, the green channel reads inverted against the usual convention — negate y for display and say so in a comment.

## Constraints and risks

* `FILTERS` **must not survive.** The viewport-hud ticket ships six cosmetic CSS filter rules keyed off `data-shading-mode`. This ticket deletes the rules and the attribute's styling hook; the attribute itself may stay if something else reads it.
* **Do not touch layout.** If a real six-mode label does not fit its chip or the HUD chip, that is a bug here, not licence to redesign. `GOURAUD` is the longest label and the render-tab ticket already sized for it at 320px.
* **GOURAUD's artefacts are shipped knowingly.** The cube-corner rounding and the seam line are properties of this shape data, not bugs in the interpolation — document them in the PR with screenshots rather than silently shipping them or chasing an unwrap.
* **Not in scope:** smoothing groups, per-material shininess, multiple lights.
* **Order.** After E3a and E3b. E6's `project()` / `isFrontFacing()` / `fill()` split is the seam POINTS and the per-pixel modes both hook into.

* `src/primitives/Triangle.ts` — the vertex indices for Gouraud accumulation
* `src/primitives/Mesh.ts` — vertex-normal accumulation alongside E3a's `computeNormals()`
* `src/rendering/Rasterizer.ts` — Gouraud shade interpolation, depth-to-greyscale, normal-to-rgb, point rendering
* `src/ui/shadingMode.ts` — no change to `modeLabel()`; the placeholder affordances are removed from its consumers
* `src/index.ts` — pass `shadingMode` into `Surface3D.render`'s options
* `src/index.html` — remove `data-placeholder`, `title` and `aria-describedby` from the four remaining shading chips

- [ ] DEPTH normalises against the per-frame depth range, with no hardcoded near/far, and agrees with the z-buffer histogram's axis

Title: E3d — Dithering and edge antialiasing
Description:
Last of four parts of "Shading pipeline" (E3). Two per-pixel passes inside E3b's rasteriser, and the ticket that pays off a regression E3b knowingly introduced.

**Unblocks**

* PIPELINE toggles DITHERING and EDGE ANTIALIAS — render-tab

## Approach

* **DITHERING** must do something visible or it is another lie. Implement as quantisation to 5 bits per channel plus a 4 × 4 ordered Bayer offset, which is what makes it worth having: it kills the Mach banding on large Gouraud gradients. One table lookup and one add per pixel.
* **EDGE ANTIALIAS** repairs the regression E3b introduces. `context.fill()` is antialiased by the browser; a hand-written rasteriser writes hard edges, so the frame gets visibly worse when Z-BUFFER goes on. Estimate per-pixel coverage from the edge functions — a boundary pixel's coverage is the signed edge distance divided by the edge gradient magnitude, clamped to [0,1] — and blend against the buffer at those pixels only. Edge blending is not depth-correct at silhouettes; that is standard and acceptable, note it.

## Constraints and risks

* **This ticket is what makes Z-BUFFER shippable ON by default.** E3b explicitly says the frame is uglier between it and this ticket, and that Z-BUFFER should stay off by default until edge antialiasing lands. Landing this in the same release as E3b is the preferred path; if it slips, the default stays OFF and the render-tab default flips with it.
* **Both passes need the back-to-front sort E3b kept.** Blended edge pixels are order-dependent, which is exactly why `Mesh.renderMesh`'s depth sort survives the depth buffer.
* **Dithering must be a no-op on flat colour.** A 5-bit quantisation of an already-flat fill has to land back on the same value, or every FLAT frame acquires visible noise. Verify that before verifying the gradient case.
* **Per-pixel cost.** Both passes run inside the inner loop E3b measured against a tight budget. Measure `frameMs` with each toggle independently and record it against E3b's baseline; if either pass breaks the perf gate on `torusKnot`, say so rather than shipping a toggle that costs 10 fps silently.
* **Order.** After E3b, which owns the rasteriser and the edge functions both passes read. After E3c if Gouraud is to be the thing dithering is demonstrated on.

## Files

* `src/rendering/Rasterizer.ts` — the Bayer dither pass and the coverage-based edge blend
* `src/ui/uiState.ts` — the `dither` / `edgeAA` booleans stop being inert
* `src/index.html` — remove `data-placeholder`, `title` and `aria-describedby` from the DITHERING and EDGE ANTIALIAS rows

## Done when

- [ ] DITHERING visibly removes banding on a large GOURAUD gradient and is a no-op on flat colour
- [ ] EDGE ANTIALIAS on makes rasteriser edges match the smoothness of the painter path; off shows the hard edges, so the toggle is provably doing work
- [ ] Edge blending's depth-incorrectness at silhouettes is noted in code rather than left to be discovered
- [ ] `frameMs` measured with each toggle independently and recorded against E3b's baseline
- [ ] The placeholder markers are gone from the DITHERING and EDGE ANTIALIAS rows
- [ ] RESET restores both flags (D7)
- [ ] Everything above holds at `max-width: 899px` as well as on desktop, with no layout change

Title: E4b — Procedural textures, spherical UVs and tiling
Description:
Stage two of two of "Materials" (E4). E4a shipped the material model, the base-colour multiply and mesh scale, and left the CHECKER and UV GRID chips marked. This ticket generates those two textures, gives the nineteen un-UV'd primitives coordinates to sample them with, and replaces the texture fill path with a repeating pattern so UV SCALE can tile.

**Unblocks**

* The CHECKER and UV GRID texture chips — shape-tab
* UV SCALE slider — shape-tab

Nothing in the epic is blocked *by* it, and it is taken ahead of E3b ([COS-242](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-242/e3b-software-scanline-rasteriser-with-a-depth-buffer)) for an ordering reason rather than a size one: E3b reimplements the texture path per pixel, and this ticket's own draft already says the UV→pixel conversion must be one shared helper and not two. Landing E4b first means E3b writes a consumer; landing it second means retrofitting two backends and re-opening E3b's perf gate with ten times as many textured triangles.

## Rebase note — this ticket was written before five of its dependencies landed

Drafted 2026-07-28. Two of the files it names to edit do not exist, and four of its premises are wrong. Listed rather than silently applied, because three of them change what the work is.

**Paths.** `src/textures/textures.ts` is gone — the map is now `TextureRegistry` (a class holding `Map<string, HTMLImageElement>`) and the key/URL record plus `isTextureKey` are `src/textures/textureKeys.ts`. `src/data/builder.ts` is `src/data/builders/MeshBuilder.ts`. `src/index.ts` is twelve lines of ignition; the composition root is `src/app/Main.ts`. `src/ui/uiState.ts` is `src/ui/UIStateStore.ts`. `src/ui/texLabel.ts` is `src/ui/MaterialSummary.ts`, a class, and its own header records the rename. There is no `src/ui/inspector/shapeTab.ts` — the chips and the UV SCALE row are built by `MaterialSection.ts`.

**The placeholder markers are not in** `src/index.html`**.** Every one of them is built in JS by `MaterialSection`: `HINT_ID = "ph-shape-material"`, `HINT_TEXT`, `buildHint()`, the `placeholder` option on the CHECKER and UV GRID chip descriptors (L62, L64) and the same option on the UV SCALE `SliderRow` (L128). `index.html` carries no marker for any of the three. Nothing in it is edited by this ticket.

`AffineTextureMapper` **exists, and its ownership has to change.** E6 moved the affine solve and the clip/`drawImage` pair out of `Triangle` into `src/rendering/AffineTextureMapper.ts`, one instance per triangle — "an empty object per triangle at mesh-build time and nothing at all per frame", which was the right trade for a class that held nothing. It stops being right here: the pattern cache and the scratch matrix are shared state, and 8192 copies of a four-entry cache is a defect rather than a trade. It becomes one shared collaborator on `TriangleRenderOptions`, beside `textures` and `lighting`. Note the allocation is net neutral: this removes one mapper per triangle and adds one UV triple per triangle.

**E3a landed, and textured faces are already washed.** `Triangle.shadeTexture` fills `rgba(0,0,0,1−shade)` over a successful texture draw. The procedural textures inherit that, which is correct and needs no work — but it means CHECKER on the torus knot pays for a normal, a wash *and* a pattern fill per face.

**The torus-knot count moved.** `220 × 18 × 2 = 7920` is stale; `TorusKnotGenerator` is budget-driven at `TRIANGLE_BUDGET = 8192` and picks its tube segments to fit. The order-of-magnitude argument stands, the number does not.

### Four corrections that change the work

**1. UV SCALE cannot apply in AUTHORED, and the draft asks for both.** "UV SCALE tiles … on both the authored cube faces" and "with defaults (AUTHORED / white / uv 8) every primitive still renders pixel-identically" cannot both hold: the default scale is 8, so tiling the authored faces would open the console on a dog repeated 64 times. Resolved the way the draft's own constraint line reads — "UV SCALE 8 is inert until a procedural mode is picked". **The scale applies in** `checker` **and** `uvGrid` **only, and there it applies to authored and generated UVs alike**, which is what makes the cube's two subdivided faces tile with the other four. It is resolved in `resolveMaterial` as a new `ResolvedMaterial.uvScale` rather than read on the render path, so the rule lives where every other material decision lives and a scale change travels the existing `changeMaterial` → `Mesh.setMaterial` route.

**2. "Pixel-identical to the E4a baseline" is neither achievable nor wanted.** E3a already lit every frame, so the E4a baseline is gone. And the pattern fill deliberately changes the cube's two textured faces: the clip/`drawImage` pair antialiases the clip edge and the image edge separately, which is the subdivision crosshatch E3a's verification confirmed on `master`. Removing it is a deliverable, not a regression. The criterion becomes: unchanged everywhere except those two faces, where the 14×14 seams disappear — verified by screenshot against `master`, not against a stale baseline.

**3. Spherical projection is not injective, and today that paints a hole.** It reads a direction and discards the radius, so two vertices on one ray from the origin get identical UVs — reachable on `cross` and `menger`, which have coplanar faces at different depths along the same axis. `uvDet === 0` then makes `AffineTextureMapper.draw` return false, `Triangle.fill` returns false, and the triangle is neither painted nor counted. `fill()` **must fall back to the flat path when the textured draw fails**, which also makes `ResolvedMaterial.fill`/`rgba` load-bearing for the first time. The draft's pole guard is real but is the smaller half of this.

**4. The** `v` **formula assumes y up; this engine's y is down.** `convert3D2D` is `centerY + y * scale`, so +y renders downward, and the registry's own convention confirms it: the galaxy face's `p00` is model y = −100 at `v = 0`, so texture-top is screen-top. `v = 0.5 − asin(y/r)/π` would map the model's underside to the top of the texture. It is `v = 0.5 + asin(y/r)/π`. Invisible on a checker, visible on a UV grid, which is exactly what a UV grid is for.

## Approach

### The two generators are a class, not a module of functions

`src/textures/ProceduralTextures.ts` owns two 64×64 `HTMLCanvasElement`s and repaints them in place. A module that holds state and repaints it is a class here; the draft's `procedural.ts` predates that rule being applied to this folder.

Repainting **in place** is what keeps the registry out of it: the two canvases are handed to `TextureRegistry` once at boot and never replaced, so a base-colour change repaints pixels behind a key that is already registered. `TextureRegistry`'s map widens to `HTMLImageElement | HTMLCanvasElement` and gains one method to adopt a canvas; `Triangle` reads only `width`/`height` and hands the source to a canvas draw, so both satisfy it.

The base colour is the ink, which is E4a's rule everywhere else. CHECKER alternates the base colour with the base colour darkened, so it reads at every swatch rather than only against a dark ground. UV GRID is a lined grid in the base colour with one filled cell, so orientation and mirroring are visible — a grid with no asymmetry cannot show the distortion it exists to show.

### Generated UVs, at mesh-build time, from the registry coordinates

`MeshFactory.build` already holds `object3D.points`, which is the pristine table — never the live `Point3D`s, which `setTransform` rewrites every frame. `src/rendering/uvProjection.ts` is a pure derivation beside `worldScale`, `lightDirection` and `cssColor`:

```
r = |p|
u = 0.5 + atan2(p.z, p.x) / (2π)
v = 0.5 + asin(clamp(p.y / r, −1, 1)) / π     // + , not − : y is down here
```

computed once per point, then read per triangle. **Seam**: a triangle whose `max(u) − min(u) > 0.5` straddles `u = 0/1` and would run the whole texture backwards across the face; add 1 to every `u < 0.5` in that triangle. The fix is applied before the scale multiply, so it stays contiguous at every UV SCALE. **Pole**: `r < 1e-6` falls back to `[0, 0]`.

Authored UVs win, and they win by not being overwritten: the factory fills the same three constructor slots only when the registry tuple has none. `Triangle`'s UVs stop being optional at runtime while staying optional in the registry, and its header says so.

### The pattern fill

`Triangle`'s texture branch cannot tile: UVs outside `[0..1]` map the triangle outside the drawn image and it comes out blank. The clip/`drawImage` pair is replaced by a repeating pattern in the shared mapper:

* the affine solve is unchanged, but UVs become pixels as `u × uvScale × w`;
* one `CanvasPattern` per texture, cached — `createPattern(source, "repeat")`;
* `pattern.setTransform(matrix)` per triangle, `fillStyle = pattern`, fill the triangle path.

One `save`/`restore` pair disappears, `globalAlpha` still applies so OPACITY is a test rather than a change, and tiling is free. The affine is still not perspective-correct — `MeshBuilder`'s subdivision rationale is untouched.

Two allocation notes, because both are per-textured-triangle-per-frame otherwise. `setTransform` copies the matrix it is given, so **one mutable** `DOMMatrix` **is reused** across every triangle rather than constructed per draw. And `createPattern` snapshots its source, so a cached pattern does **not** see a repainted canvas: the cache is invalidated when `ProceduralTextures` redraws, which is the one moment it can go stale.

The draft's "keep clip/`drawImage` as the `uvScale === 1` fallback if `DOMMatrix` is missing" is dropped. Two live texture backends, kept to hedge a type every target browser has had for years, is the maintenance cost E3b is about to pay honestly.

### Wiring

`MaterialSection`'s UV SCALE row gains an `onUvScale` that reaches `Main.changeMaterial({ uvScale })`, the same route the chips and swatches already take, so RESET and the paused frame both work with no new path. A base-colour change additionally repaints the two canvases and invalidates the pattern cache before the repaint.

`ShapeThumbnails` needs a mapper of its own, for the reason it needed a `Lighting` of its own in E3a: the chips go through the real rasteriser.

`MaterialSummary.MaterialLabel` widens to include `CHECKER` and `UV GRID`, and `textureKeys` returns the generated key in those modes — the union member that was dead code with a comment attached becomes producible.

## Constraints and risks

* **Procedural modes are the expensive path.** The cube textures 784 triangles today; CHECKER on the torus knot textures up to 8192, each now paying a normal, a pattern fill and a wash. Measure on `torusKnot` and `menger` and let the frame-time widget show it rather than hiding the mode.
* **Spherical UVs are a projection, not an unwrap.** On `cross` and `menger` the checker will look arbitrary on faces facing away from the axis. That is honest, and it is what UV GRID is for — do not chase a better unwrap here.
* **The opening frame changes only where the seams were.** Default is AUTHORED / white / uv 8, and uvScale is inert there.
* **Registry counts must not move.** Generated UVs are per-triangle attributes; nothing here adds or removes a triangle. `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` must be byte-identical.
* **No file under** `src/data/shapes/` **is modified.**
* **Not in scope:** perspective-correct UVs (E3b gets them free once `1/d` is interpolated), near-plane clipping with UV interpolation (E2b/[COS-418](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-418/e2b-near-plane-polygon-clipping-with-uv-interpolation)), any per-pixel sampling.

## Files

* `src/rendering/uvProjection.ts` — new; spherical UVs with the seam and pole guards
* `src/textures/ProceduralTextures.ts` — new; the two canvases and their repaint
* `src/textures/TextureRegistry.ts` — widen to `HTMLImageElement | HTMLCanvasElement`, adopt a canvas
* `src/textures/textureKeys.ts` — the two procedural keys join the declared set without a URL
* `src/rendering/AffineTextureMapper.ts` — shared rather than per-triangle; pattern cache, reused matrix, `uvScale`
* `src/rendering/material.ts` — the procedural branches, and `ResolvedMaterial.uvScale`
* `src/primitives/Triangle.ts` — the shared mapper through the options; flat fallback when a textured draw fails
* `src/primitives/MeshFactory.ts` — generate UVs where the registry has none
* `src/app/Main.ts` — owns `ProceduralTextures`; UV SCALE reaches `changeMaterial`; the base colour repaints and invalidates
* `src/ui/inspector/MaterialSection.ts`, `src/ui/inspector/ShapeTab.ts` — the placeholder affordance comes off the two chips and the UV SCALE row, and `onUvScale` is threaded
* `src/ui/MaterialSummary.ts` — `MaterialLabel` widens; procedural modes report their key
* `src/ui/UIStateStore.ts` — `uvScale` stops being inert
* `src/ui/inspector/ShapeThumbnails.ts` — its own mapper

## Done when

- [X] The placeholder affordance is gone from UV SCALE and the CHECKER and UV GRID chips — the two chip descriptors, the slider option, `HINT_ID`, `HINT_TEXT` and `buildHint()` — and no other placeholder marker is removed
- [X] CHECKER and UV GRID apply to every primitive, including the nineteen with no authored UVs, with no smeared triangle at the projection seam
- [X] Both textures are generated with the base colour as their ink and repaint when the swatch changes, with the pattern cache invalidated so the change is visible
- [X] UV SCALE tiles in the procedural modes — 1 shows one copy, 16 shows sixteen — over the cube's authored faces and its generated ones alike, and is inert in AUTHORED and SOLID
- [X] The cube's authored UVs are never overwritten by generated ones
- [X] Generated UVs come from `src/data/data.ts` coordinates, never from live `Point3D`s
- [X] A triangle whose UVs are degenerate falls back to a flat lit fill rather than going unpainted, and `cross` and `menger` show no holes in either procedural mode
- [X] `v` is verified upright against the cube's authored galaxy face, using the UV grid's asymmetric cell
- [X] The default frame is unchanged — screenshot-compared against `master` at a pinned pose, including the cube's two textured faces (see Verified in the frame for why the seam claim was withdrawn)
- [X] Opacity still works on the pattern fill path, and the E3a wash still darkens a procedural face by orientation
- [X] One `CanvasPattern` per texture and one `DOMMatrix` for the whole scene — nothing per triangle per frame
- [X] `MaterialSummary` returns CHECKER and UV GRID, and SHAPE INFO MATERIAL, the HUD chip and the status segment agree
- [X] Frame time on `torusKnot` and `menger` in CHECKER mode recorded against the AUTHORED baseline
- [X] RESET restores UV scale 8 (D7)
- [X] `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` is byte-identical across all twenty shapes; no file under `src/data/shapes/` is modified
- [X] `typecheck`, `lint`, `lint:rules` and `test` all pass

## Departures from the rebased spec

Three, on top of the four corrections the rebase note already records.

**1.** `AffineTextureMapper` **lost its** `Point2D` **contract as well as its per-triangle ownership.** The rebase note called the ownership change; the second half surfaced in implementation. D8 settled the options literal over four positional arguments with an allocation argument — the ticket's form allocated two fresh tuples per call where a flat literal allocates one object — and the same arithmetic now points at the three `Point2D` instances inside that literal. They were affordable while only the cube's 784 faces took the texture path; in a procedural mode every triangle does, which is up to 8192 a frame on the torus knot. The request carries six scalars instead. Four objects per textured triangle per frame become one.

**2.** `Triangle.fill()` **returns true on every path now.** The only branch that could report false was the textured one, and correction 3 turned that failure into a fallback rather than a silent skip. The boolean is kept rather than dropped for `void`: `Mesh` counts drawn triangles, draw calls and fill rate off it, and E3b's second backend has a genuinely not-drawn state to report through it. Said out loud at the method rather than left to be discovered.

**3.** `sphericalUVs` **takes the whole** `Object3D` **and returns null per authored face.** The draft implied a per-point projection plus a separate seam helper, which is a four-argument call at the loop — a table and three indices — for a rule that has to compose with the authored-wins one anyway. One argument, one return, and the two rules live together where the header can explain both. `MeshFactory` indexes it and stays a two-line change.

## Verified in the frame

Chrome MCP is not connected in this environment, so the walk ran through headless Chrome over CDP. `master` was checked out into a worktree on a second port; every comparison below pins an identical pose first — the turntable accumulates while a page loads, and two runs left to themselves land at different yaw, which is what made an early reading look like a regression it was not.

* CHECKER and UV GRID land on every primitive tried: sphere, cube, cross, Menger sponge, donut, torus knot. **No holes** on the cross or the sponge, which is correction 3 doing its job.
* UV SCALE tiles: one copy at 1, sixteen at 16, on the sphere's generated coordinates and on the cube's authored ones alike.
* The swatch repaints both textures and the pattern cache drops — red, blue and back to white each land on the next frame rather than one behind.

Title: E5a — Ground under the camera: shared projector, grid and world units
Description:
Stage one of two of "World layers" (E5). `BackgroundRenderer` draws a sky gradient, a sky bitmap, an atmosphere haze, a perspective checker floor and a vignette unconditionally, every frame, in canvas space (`src/rendering/BackgroundRenderer.ts` L16–L26) — its floor has its own hand-rolled projector with its own focal, its own centre and its own horizon, none of which is the scene camera. Nothing in that stack responds to zoom or focal length, and there is no grid and no world-unit concept at all.

This ticket puts the ground under the scene camera's own projection, adds a world grid with a step in metres, and defines the one constant that makes the status bar's `units: metres` true instead of decorative. **E5b — shadow and fog** follows and depends on this for the projector and the fog curve's home.

**Unblocks**

* ENVIRONMENT's GRID OVERLAY toggle and the GRID STEP slider — world-tab
* The GRID quick toggle — quick-toggles (the only placeholder of the five)
* The `G grid` shortcut chip's placeholder affordance — shortcuts. Its `SHORTCUTS` status moves from `pendingFeature` to `pendingHandler`; `S` and `F` stay `pendingHandler` either way, because the missing piece there is the `keydown` listener, which is E8
* The `units: metres` status segment — status

## Approach

### `setLayers` already exists — extend it, do not re-ship it

`setLayers({sky, floor})` is settled: D11 assigns it to the world-tab UI ticket, and that ticket ships it as a hard deliverable. SKY DOME and CHECKER FLOOR are therefore **not** in this ticket's Unblocks list. This ticket extends the same object to `{sky, floor, grid, shadow}` and adds `setWorld({fog, gridStepMetres})`, keeping world-tab's rule that flags are settable after construction and never passed through the constructor, because the renderer is built once at boot with fixed `{width, height, skyImage}` (`src/index.ts` L677–L681). E7 also lists `setLayers` as a fallback deliverable; it is not one for either ticket — world-tab owns it, both consume it, and there is exactly one switch.

### One ground projection, shared by the floor and the grid

The scene camera is `Point3D.convert3D2D`: for a point `(x, y, z)`,

```
s(z)    = fl / (fl + z + zOffset)
screenX = centerX + x·s(z)
screenY = centerY + y·s(z)
```

with the centre read from E9a's shared render target, never from literals. Put the ground at a constant `y = GROUND_Y` (screen +y is down, so the ground is a positive y) and the whole ground plane follows from that one formula:

* the horizon is `y = centerY`, because `s → 0` as `z → ∞`;
* every line of constant `x` converges on the principal point, and every line of constant `z` is horizontal — a perspective map takes straight lines to straight lines, so each grid line is one `moveTo`/`lineTo`;
* the plane responds to ZOOM (`zOffset`) and FOV (`fl`) for free, which is the entire point: the current floor responds to neither.

**E2 owns the orthographic branch.** Under orthographic the ground has no vanishing point and the grid degenerates to parallel lines; consume E2's projection mode rather than writing a second branch here.

Near clip is not optional. `s` blows up and then inverts as the denominator passes zero, so every segment is clipped parametrically to `z ≥ zNear` — trimmed along the segment, not dropped, or a line that begins behind the eye disappears instead of running off the bottom of the frame. Use E2's near plane, floored at 40 engine units: a mesh vertex at `d = 1` is a dot, but a ground line runs continuously to the eye and at `d = 1` a single segment covers the screen several times over.

`renderFloor` **is re-derived on this projector.** Its current one (L76–L93) uses `focal = width·0.95`, `centerX = width·0.6`, `horizonY = height·0.57` and a 1.75 camera height, putting its vanishing line at `y ≈ 365` while the grid's is at the render target centre. Two horizons in one frame is worse than either alone. Re-derive the floor, and move the atmosphere haze and horizon glow (L57–L74) onto the same horizon so the composition holds together. The `destination-out` fade mask and the floor tint (L123–L138) keep working unchanged against the new horizon value.

This is also a large performance win. Today the floor fills `144 columns × 57 rows ≈ 8200` quads per frame under everything else. Derived from the world instead of from screen fractions, with the cell equal to the grid step, it is `(zFar − zNear)/step` rows by `2·xHalf/step` columns — about 320 quads at a 4 m step over a 60 m depth and ±40 m width. Measure before and after; this is likely the biggest single frame-time change in the epic.

### The grid

Strokes on top of the floor, in the same pass order (sky, atmosphere, floor, grid, shadow, vignette), so the mesh still draws over all of it.

* Step comes from GRID STEP in metres through `metresToUnits` (below). Lines at every multiple of the step in `x` and in `z`, plus a heavier line on the two axes.
* Draw far to near, and fade each line with the same fog curve the mesh uses — **E5b owns that curve**; until it lands, fade with a plain linear falloff and swap it for the shared curve when E5b merges.
* Skip any row whose projected y gap from the previous row is under 1.5 px — the standard grid guard, and cheap since the rows are already ordered.
* Colours cannot come from CSS: canvas 2D cannot read custom properties. Add them to `src/ui/chartTokens.ts`, which the tokens ticket sanctions as the single hand-mirrored copy of `colors.css` and which world-tab already extended with `bgApp: "#05091A"` for exactly this reason. Do not create a second mirror module — world-tab explicitly rules that out, so this ticket ships no `worldColors.ts`.
* Build the grid from plain world coordinates through the shared projector function, not from `Point3D` instances — allocating vertices per frame would be waste.

Note honestly what this grid does and does not do: after E1a the camera rig rotates the *mesh*, not a camera, so the grid is fixed in world space and the shape spins inside it. It answers to zoom and focal length only. Record the follow-up: if a real view transform ever lands, the grid and `convert3D2D` must route through it together, not diverge.

### World units

`src/rendering/worldScale.ts`: `UNITS_PER_METRE = 100`, `metresToUnits`, `unitsToMetres`. The constant is not arbitrary — every primitive is authored to roughly a 100-unit radius (sphere radius 100, cube ±100, cuboctahedron circumradius 100, Menger 210 across), so 100 units to the metre makes the on-screen object a 2 m thing, and `GROUND_Y = metresToUnits(1.75) = 175` keeps the 1.75 eye height the current floor code already assumes (L80). The shapes then hover about 0.7 m above the ground, which is what E5b's shadow height falloff expresses.

GRID STEP is authored in metres and converted here; `units: metres` in the status bar stops being a placeholder because there is now exactly one conversion in the tree and a control denominated in it.

## Constraints and risks

* **The picture changes.** Moving the horizon from `y ≈ 365` to the render-target centre and the floor centre from `0.6·width` to the canvas centre is a deliberate change to a composition someone tuned by hand. It is the price of a floor that answers to the camera; get it looked at before merge rather than after.
* **This ticket does not resize the canvas** and does not re-construct `BackgroundRenderer` or `ShapeTransitionMachine`. It must not add a comment asserting the size is fixed: E9b makes it fluid, so every horizon, extent and centre this ticket derives comes from the shared render target.
* `renderVignette` **stays unconditional** (world-tab's ruling) and stays inside the background pass, so it still does not tint the mesh. Do not quietly change that here.
* **The scene-graph FLOOR_01 and ENV_01 rows are not this ticket's.** Their visibility toggles gain a real target once the layer flags exist, but the row semantics belong to E7.
* **E7's** `FloorObject` **info record** is written against the *current* `renderFloor` constants (`cellWidth 3.4`, `cellDepth 4.2`, 144 columns, horizon `0.57 h`, `focal 0.95 w`, camera height 1.75) — this ticket deletes or re-derives every one of them, so E7's record must be written against the new projector.
* **E3b snapshots the background** as its colour-buffer clear source; this ticket's passes are all static, so the snapshot stays valid — E5b is what breaks it.
* **RESET owns the new slices** (D7): grid off, grid step 4 m, sky and floor on.
* Every new canvas colour is a mirrored constant with a comment pointing at its token. No `getComputedStyle` in the render loop.

## Files

* `src/rendering/worldScale.ts` — new; `UNITS_PER_METRE`, `metresToUnits`, `unitsToMetres`, `GROUND_Y`
* `src/rendering/groundProjection.ts` — new; the shared `s(z)` projector, the ground point projection and the parametric near clip
* `src/rendering/groundGrid.ts` — new; the grid lines, the step-in-metres conversion and the sub-pixel guard
* `src/ui/chartTokens.ts` — extended with the grid colours alongside the existing chart colours and world-tab's `bgApp`; no new mirror module
* `src/rendering/BackgroundRenderer.ts` — widen world-tab's `setLayers` to `{sky, floor, grid, shadow}` and add `setWorld({fog, gridStepMetres})`; `renderFloor` re-derived on the shared projector; atmosphere anchored to the new horizon; the grid call
* `src/index.ts` — world state on `Main`; `changeGridStep` / layer setters mirroring `changeZoom` (apply, then `renderPausedFrame()`); pass `focal` and `zOffset` into the render call
* `src/ui/uiState.ts` — `grid`, `gridStep` stop being inert
* `src/ui/shortcuts.ts` — the `G` binding moves to `pendingHandler`
* `src/ui/inspector/worldTab.ts`, `src/ui/quickToggles.ts`, `src/index.html` — remove the placeholder affordance from GRID OVERLAY, GRID STEP, the GRID pill and the `units: metres` segment
* Amended tickets: `quick-toggles` and `shortcuts` (GRID is no longer a placeholder)

- [ ] `data-placeholder="true"` with its `title` and `aria-describedby` is gone from GRID OVERLAY, GRID STEP, the GRID quick-toggle pill, the `G` shortcut chip and the `units: metres` status segment — and GROUND SHADOW, FOG and DRAW CALLS still carry theirs, unchanged
- [ ] The floor and the grid share one horizon and one vanishing point, and both move when the ZOOM slider or the FOV slider moves

- [ ] World-tab's SKY DOME and CHECKER FLOOR still toggle real layers through the widened `setLayers`, the vignette is still unconditional, and with the sky off the frame still flat-fills from `chartTokens.bgApp` — a regression check on an existing feature, not a deliverable of this ticket
