Title: E5b — Ground shadow, distance fog and the layer-pass count
Description:
Stage two of two of "World layers" (E5). E5a put the ground under the scene camera and added the grid and world units. This ticket adds the two layers that need to know about the mesh: a projected ground shadow and distance fog. It also counts the layer passes one at a time, which is what makes the draw-call number describe the frame rather than round it off.

Depends on E5a for the shared projector and for `setWorld`.

**Unblocks**

* ENVIRONMENT's GROUND SHADOW toggle and the FOG slider — the last two placeholder controls in the WORLD tab
* DRAW CALLS stops rounding the whole background pass down to 1

---

## Rebased onto the tree of 2026-08-07

Drafted 2026-07-28, against a tree that has since taken E6, E3a, E5a and the OOP conversion. Eleven premises no longer hold; each is corrected below rather than applied silently.

**1. The file list moved.** `src/index.ts` → `src/app/Main.ts`, `src/ui/uiState.ts` → `src/ui/UIStateStore.ts`, `src/ui/inspector/worldTab.ts` → `src/ui/inspector/EnvironmentSection.ts` (the section builds the rows; the tab only composes sections).

**2.** `src/index.html` **carries no placeholder for either control.** GROUND SHADOW and FOG are built in JS and take a `placeholder` option, exactly as E4a's texture chips did. The six `data-placeholder` nodes left in the markup are five E8 buttons and one E7 selection rect, and none of them is this ticket's. The affordance comes off in `EnvironmentSection.ts`, and the shared `#ph-world-layer` hint span goes with it — a hint nothing describes is dead markup.

**3.** `Point3D.xValue` **/** `yValue` **already exist.** E3a added them, and Point3D's own comment already names `Mesh.getBounds` as the second consumer. Nothing to add.

**4. DRAW CALLS is already real and has no placeholder.** E6 landed `RenderStats` and `GeometryWidget` prints the count. Its settled definition is *one per drawn triangle plus one for the background pass*, and it is the second half that is wrong: `Surface3D` adds a single flat `addDrawCall()` for the whole background whether that pass painted two layers or six. This ticket's contribution is therefore narrower and sharper than the draft's — the background counts the layers it actually painted. `Surface3D.render`'s signature and return value are untouched; the accumulator rides on the existing request object.

**5.** `render(context, view)` **is already an options object.** `BackgroundRenderRequest` has carried `{ context, camera, renderTarget, cameraTransform }` since E5a. The shadow blobs and the stats accumulator join it as fields; no signature is reshaped.

**6. The draft's closed-form ellipse does not survive E5a.** `r·s(cz)` and `GROUND_Y·(s(cz−r) − s(cz+r))/2` describe an axis-aligned ellipse about a fixed vanishing point, which is what the ground projector was before it learned about the camera. `GroundProjection.project(x, z)` now runs the world point through the camera matrix, so the shadow has to tilt with roll and slide with pitch like every other ground layer.

Replaced by the projected basis, which is shorter as well as correct:

```
C = ground.project(cx, cz)
U = ground.project(cx + r, cz) − C
V = ground.project(cx, cz + r) − C
```

then a unit circle drawn under `transform(U.x, U.y, V.x, V.y, C.x, C.y)`. Exact for the affine part, tilts and foreshortens for free, and the radial gradient is still one gradient covering both axes — which is what the draft's scale transform was for.

**7. The floor's fade gradients were already dealt with, by E5a.** The "hand-tuned fade gradients" the draft wants replaced are `GroundFloor.drawFade`, and E5a already replaced the *distance* fade with the radius-based rim dissolve `fadeAt`. What is left in `drawFade` is a horizon tint, not a distance fade. Removing it changes the FOG 0 frame, which this same ticket forbids. Kept.

**8. The grid's falloff is multiplied, not replaced** — and here two of the draft's own acceptance criteria contradict each other. "FOG 0 renders identically to the E5a baseline" and "the grid's interim linear falloff is replaced by the shared curve" cannot both hold: at FOG 0 the shared curve is 1 everywhere, so replacing the falloff makes the grid stop dissolving at its rim on the *default* frame. Identical-at-FOG-0 wins, because it is the epic-wide rule. The falloff stays as what it actually is — the grid's own rim dissolve, the depth-space twin of GroundFloor's radius-based one — and fog multiplies on top of it. Its header comment is corrected to stop calling itself an interim fog.

**9. Fog is a class, not a bag on the render options.** The draft hangs `fog?: { amount, color, near, falloff }` off `TriangleRenderOptions`. `Triangle.fill` has no eye distance to add to `Triangle.depth` — that lives on `MeshRenderPass` — and the shape this repo already has for exactly this problem is `Lighting`: a class on the options, holding the values *and* the camera, with `overlayFor()` returning a string or null. Fog follows it. The pure curve sits beside it in `fogCurve.ts` the way `lightDirection.ts` sits beside `Lighting.ts`, which also gets it into `pnpm test` — that suite runs in node and a class holding four numbers is assertable there.

The file names follow: `Fog.ts` and `fogCurve.ts`, not the draft's single `fog.ts`, which would collide with `Fog.ts` on a case-insensitive filesystem.

**10.** `FOG_FALLOFF` **goes through** `worldScale`**.** 900 units is 9 m, and `metresToUnits` has been the one home for that conversion since E5a.

**11.** `dNear` **is already being computed.** `Surface3D.render` folds `boundingRadius` over the renderables for E6's depth bins and sets the range to `camera.distance ± radius`. Fog's near edge is that same `camera.distance − radius`, read rather than re-derived. And `changeFog` does not mirror `changeZoom`: Main's world path is `syncWorldLayers()`, one re-read of the store pushed to the renderer, already ending in `renderPausedFrame()`. Both controls join it rather than growing handlers of their own.

---

## Approach

### Ground shadow

A projected blob, not a projected mesh. Filling 8008 shadow triangles for the torus knot would roughly double the rasteriser's work for something the eye reads as a smudge.

* `Mesh.getBounds()` folds min/max over the mesh's points, which the frame transform has already written, so the bounds are the current orientation's. Called only while the layer is on — `BackgroundRenderer.shadow` already exposes the flag — so it costs nothing when it is off. One pass over at most 4224 points (the Menger sponge, the registry maximum), negligible against the fill.
* Centre the ground circle at `(cx, cz)` from the bounds, radius `r` the mean of the two horizontal half-extents. Project it through the shared `GroundProjection` as the basis above, so one blob is one `arc()` under one transform.
* Opacity falls with the gap between the mesh's lowest point and the ground: `h = GROUND_Y − maxY` (y is down in this engine, so the largest y *is* the lowest point), `alpha = lerp(0.42, 0.10, clamp(h / 400, 0, 1))`. A radial gradient from `rgba(0,0,0,alpha)` to transparent.
* During a shape transition `getRenderables()` returns two meshes with screen-space `offsetX` / `offsetY`. One blob per renderable with that renderable's offset applied, or the shadow detaches from the shape mid-flight.
* Drawn inside `paintGround`, after the floor and the grid — so it follows the ground under the camera automatically, including the pass `renderGroundOverlay` makes when the eye has dropped below the plane.

### Distance fog

One curve, three consumers.

```
d = camera.distance + z               // the projection denominator: distance from the eye
f = amount · (1 − exp(−(d − near) / FOG_FALLOFF))
```

`near = camera.distance − sceneRadius`, so the near side of the shape reads as unfogged. `FOG_FALLOFF = metresToUnits(9)`. Exponential rather than linear because that is what atmosphere does and this repo's README is a maths explainer.

* **Mesh**: `TriangleRenderOptions` gains `fog: Fog`, required for the reason `lighting` is. After the triangle's own fill, if `f > 0.02`, fill the same path again with the fog colour at `f`. `Triangle.depth` is the mean z the painter's sort already computes, so the factor is free; the second fill is the cost.
* **Floor and grid**: the same `f` at each cell centre and each line endpoint, multiplied into the alpha each already carries.
* **Fog colour follows the sky**: the sky gradient's ground-side stop when SKY DOME is on, `--color-bg-app` when it is off. Fog that does not match what it fades into looks like a grey wash. Both go in `chartTokens`, and the sky gradient reads the same token rather than restating the hex.

Default FOG is **0**, not the shipped 18: the second fill is a real per-triangle cost, and the default frame must stay the frame the renderer draws today.

**Where the mesh fog fill lives.** E6 split `Triangle.render` into `project()` / `isFrontFacing()` / `fill()`; the fog overlay is a post-fill pass inside `fill()`, over the same traced path, and it applies to the textured branch as well as the flat one. Order inside `fill()`: material, then E3a's shade wash, then fog — then E3d's edge blend when it lands.

### Layer-pass count

One `addDrawCall()` per layer that actually touched the canvas — sky gradient, sky bitmap, atmosphere, floor, grid, shadow, vignette — replacing the single flat increment `Surface3D` makes for the whole background. The count then varies with the environment toggles, which is what makes the number worth printing. The mesh side is unchanged: one per drawn triangle, E6's own accounting.

## Constraints and risks

* **Fog costs a second fill per drawn triangle.** At FOG 100 on the torus knot that is up to 8008 extra fills. Default 0, threshold at `f > 0.02` so a nearly-clear frame skips the pass entirely, and the worst case is measured in the PR.
* **The shadow reads mesh bounds every frame**, once per renderable, ordered before the background pass. Gated on the layer flag so an off toggle folds nothing.
* **This breaks E3b's background snapshot.** E3b caches the background once and uses it as the depth-buffered rasteriser's colour-buffer clear source, assuming every background pass is static. The shadow depends on the mesh bounds and changes every frame. Snapshot-able: sky, atmosphere, floor, grid. Per frame, after the mesh: shadow, vignette. Recorded on [COS-242](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-242/e3b-software-scanline-rasteriser-with-a-depth-buffer) as well as here.
* **This ticket does not resize the canvas.** Every extent it computes reads E9a's shared render target, never a 1024 or 640 literal.
* `renderVignette` **stays unconditional** and stays inside the background pass.
* **RESET owns the new defaults**: shadow off, fog 0. Both are registered slices already, so this is a value change rather than new wiring.
* Fog colours are mirrored constants in `src/ui/chartTokens.ts`. No second mirror module, no `getComputedStyle` on the render loop.
* **Order.** After E5a, E6 and E3a — all landed. Before E7.

## Files

* `src/rendering/fogCurve.ts` — new; the exponential curve and the sky-dependent colour, pure and asserted in node
* `src/rendering/Fog.ts` — new; the class the three consumers hold, mirroring `Lighting`
* `src/rendering/GroundShadow.ts` — new; the projected blob and its gradient
* `src/rendering/__tests__/fog.test.ts` — new
* `src/ui/chartTokens.ts` — the two fog colours and the sky horizon stop
* `src/rendering/BackgroundRenderer.ts` — holds the `Fog`, draws the shadow, counts one draw call per painted layer
* `src/rendering/GroundFloor.ts`, `src/rendering/GroundGrid.ts` — fog multiplied into the alpha each already carries
* `src/primitives/Surface3D.ts` — folds the bounds when the layer is on and puts the blobs on the background request
* `src/primitives/Mesh.ts` — `getBounds()`
* `src/primitives/Triangle.ts` — `TriangleRenderOptions.fog` and the overlay fill
* `src/app/Main.ts` — owns the `Fog`, pushes it through `syncWorldLayers()` and `paint()`
* `src/ui/inspector/EnvironmentSection.ts` — FOG default 0, the placeholder affordance and its hint span removed

Title: E7 — Scene model: real scene objects, per-object visibility, selection and projected bounds
Description:
The console presents a scene of four objects; the engine has one mesh and a background painter. The scene graph renders three hardcoded placeholder rows, SHAPE INFO's kind note is the literal `MESH`, the status bar's selected id follows the active primitive rather than the selection, and the viewport's selection bracket is a fixed percentage rectangle that ignores the geometry it claims to bracket. This ticket introduces object identity — a `Scene` of `SceneObject`s with a kind, an id, a visibility flag and a per-object info record — and drives every one of those surfaces off it. `Surface3D.render` already takes an array of renderables, so the rendering side is close to free; what is missing is everything above it.

**Unblocks**

* Scene-graph rows 2 to 4 (`PLN FLOOR_01`, `ENV SKY_DOME`, `LGT KEY_LIGHT`) and their `data-placeholder="true"` markers (scene-graph)
* The visibility toggles on rows 2 and 3, which today flip a glyph and change nothing on canvas (scene-graph)
* SHAPE INFO's header kind note, currently the constant literal `MESH` (shape-info)
* The info/story swap when a non-mesh object is selected — the mockup's `STATIC_INFO` behaviour, which the scene-graph ticket recorded as "selecting rows 2–4 changes nothing else" (scene-graph, shape-info, shape-story)
* The status bar's `<id> selected` segment, whose multi-object case is marked as owned here (status)
* The viewport selection bracket rect, hardcoded at `left: 39.2%; top: 31.9%` with a 190px square desktop / `22.4% × 35.8%` mobile (viewport-hud)

## Approach

### The model

New `src/scene/`:

* `SceneObject.ts` — `interface SceneObject { id: string; kind: "MSH" | "PLN" | "ENV" | "LGT"; visible: boolean; triangleCount: number | null; renderables(): MeshRenderRequest[]; bounds(): ScreenRect | null; info: SceneObjectInfo }`. `triangleCount: null` renders as the em dash the scene-graph row already handles for a zero count.
* `Scene.ts` — the ordered object list, `byId()`, and `renderables()` returning the flattened, visibility-filtered `MeshRenderRequest[]`. That array is what goes into `Surface3D.render` (`src/primitives/Surface3D.ts` L23–L48), which needs no change at all: it iterates whatever it is handed and draws the background first (L27), so a hidden mesh still leaves sky, floor and vignette.

Four objects, in the design's fixed order:

* `MeshObject` — wraps `ShapeTransitionMachine`; `renderables()` delegates to `getRenderables()` (`src/animations/shapeTransitionMachine.ts` L192–L194); id from `sceneObjectId(primitiveKey)` (shell's module, D5); `triangleCount` is the **drawn** count (D6).
* `FloorObject` (`PLN`, `FLOOR_01`) and `SkyObject` (`ENV`, `SKY_DOME`) — not geometry. `BackgroundRenderer.render()` draws sky, atmosphere, floor and vignette in canvas space. Their `renderables()` returns `[]` and their `triangleCount` is `null`, which is the honest answer: the checker floor is canvas quads, not two triangles as the mockup claims. Visibility binds to `BackgroundRenderer.setLayers` — **owned and shipped by the world-tab ticket** (D11) and widened by E5a to `{sky, floor, grid, shadow}`. Consume it; this ticket does not ship a fallback copy. There is exactly one switch and world-tab owns it.
* `LightObject` (`LGT`, `KEY_LIGHT`) — E3a has given the engine a directional key light, so this row's visibility flag has a real target: hiding it leaves ambient-only shading. Its info record is real too.

### Per-object info records

The mockup's `STATIC_INFO` has no repo equivalent, so build one: `SceneObjectInfo { kindLabel: string; rows: { label: string; value: string }[]; story: { title: string; paragraphs: string[]; footer: { label: string; value: string }[] } }` in `src/scene/sceneObjectInfo.ts`.

Every value must be derived from an engine constant, with the constant named in a code comment. Nothing invented:

* **Mesh** — exactly what `syncShapeInfoPanel` computes today (`src/index.ts` L283–L315): NAME, POINTS, TRIANGLES (registry count), TEXTURES via `textureNames()`, OPACITY, plus SHADING and MATERIAL; story from `shapeInfo[key]`.
* **Floor** — **write this record against E5a's projector, not the old constants.** E5a deletes or re-derives every one of `cellWidth 3.4`, `cellDepth 4.2`, 144 columns, horizon `0.57 h`, focal `0.95 w` and camera height 1.75: the horizon moves to the render target centre, the focal becomes the camera's, and the cell size becomes the grid step in metres. Quote the new constants and export them from their module rather than retyping them. Do not let this record become the only surviving reference to a hand-tuned constant nobody uses any more.
* **Sky** — gradient stop count and the four stops (`BackgroundRenderer` L30–L33), bitmap coverage `0.62 h` (L41), `ALPHA 0.90` (L52).
* **Light** — azimuth, elevation, ambient and specular from E3a's lighting slice, plus the Blinn-Phong shininess constant 32. A record that reads the live light, not a fabricated one.

### Selection drives the panels

`uiState.sceneSelection` already exists (shell, D2; the scene-graph ticket writes it). SHAPE INFO and SHAPE STORY currently ignore it and stay bound to the active primitive. Subscribe both to the selection and render the selected object's record. Three things this must not break:

1. **The fade.** `animateShapeInfoPanel` (`src/index.ts` L334–L358) runs a 180ms fade-out, swaps the text, then fades in, on `#shapeInfoPanelContent` which the shape-info ticket kept wrapping both cards. Selection change must reuse that same path, not a second animation.
2. **The element-id contract.** `Main`'s constructor resolves the ids via `getElementById` and throws `"UI controls are missing."` if any is absent (`src/index.ts` L130–L177). They include `shapeInfoName`, `shapeInfoPoints`, `shapeInfoTriangles`, `shapeInfoTextures`, `shapeInfoOpacity` and the shape-info ticket's `shapeInfoKind` / `shapeInfoShading` / `shapeInfoMaterial`. Making the row list data-driven means the labels stop being literal markup — the shape-info ticket writes them literally on purpose. Preferred path: render `.info-row` pairs from the record into `.info-list`, keep the legacy ids on the mesh template's value spans, and migrate those five constructor lookups out of the constructor in the same change. It touches D2's contract, so coordinate it explicitly in the PR; the fallback is keeping the ids and accepting a mesh-shaped template.
3. **Opacity writes.** `changeOpacity` calls `syncShapeInfoOpacity()` (`src/index.ts` L261–L270, L279–L281), which writes straight into `shapeInfoOpacityNode` on every slider input. With a non-mesh object selected that row means something else. Route the write through the selected object's record so it is dropped when the mesh is not selected.

Two rules survive from the UI epic: picking a primitive returns selection to the mesh row (D11), and the mesh row keeps one id and one row through the 1250ms transition even though `getRenderables()` returns two meshes — the id flips when `currentPrimitiveName` does (`src/index.ts` L468–L488) and the count is the sum.

The status bar reads the same selection through `setField` rather than the active primitive.

### Screen-space bounding box

The bracket needs the projected AABB of the selected object. For the mesh, take it from the points, not the triangles: `Mesh` holds `points` and `triangles` separately (`src/primitives/Mesh.ts` L5–L6) and the current code projects each `Point3D` once per incident triangle — roughly five times over. One pass over `this.points` is 143 projections on the sphere against its 720 (240 triangles × 3), and 3960 on the torus knot against its 23760.

Add `Point3D.project(out: {x: number; y: number}): boolean` writing into a reused object and returning `false` when the vertex fails E2's near plane, and have `convert3D2D()` call it so the projection formula exists once. **E2's near plane is the honest version of the guard** — do not add a second `denominator > 0` test. If fewer than three vertices survive, hide the bracket for that frame.

Then `Mesh.projectedBounds(offsetX, offsetY): ScreenRect | null` accumulates min/max, clamped to the render target's extent — **read it from E9a's shared target, never from a 1024 or 640 literal** — so a partly off-screen mesh cannot push the bracket outside the card. **Take the bounds from E6's transform pass rather than adding a second projection loop**; E5b's `Mesh.getBounds()` is a third fold over the same array. The three tickets must not each walk the geometry.

The HUD consumes it as percentages of the stage — `left = minX / width * 100`, `top = minY / height * 100`, and likewise for width and height — written as four custom properties (`--sel-left`, `--sel-top`, `--sel-w`, `--sel-h`) on the bracket element, with `viewport.css` consuming them. Same markup, same absolute positioning, no layout change, and the mobile percentage box works identically.

Update the bracket **every frame**, not on the 90ms display gate: it is four custom-property writes on one element, far cheaper than a single triangle fill, and at 90ms the bracket visibly trails a rotating mesh. Say so in the code next to the write, because every other telemetry value in this console is deliberately throttled.

Non-mesh objects: `FLOOR_01` brackets the region below E5a's horizon, full width; `SKY_DOME` brackets the whole stage; `KEY_LIGHT` is directional and has no position, so its bracket and label badge stay hidden.

### This is large — three independent pieces

1. Scene model, scene-graph rows, per-object visibility. No panel changes; the info panels stay bound to the mesh.
2. Per-object info and story records plus the selection swap. Touches the constructor id contract, so it carries the boot risk.
3. Projected selection bounds. Independent of 1 and 2 for the mesh case and can land first or last.

## Constraints and risks

* `Surface3D.render` **draws the background unconditionally** before iterating renderables, so floor and sky visibility can only be honoured inside `BackgroundRenderer`, never by filtering the renderables array. Mesh visibility is the opposite: filter before the call.
* **One** `setLayers`**, one owner.** D11 assigns it to world-tab, E5a widens it. Two switches for the same layer is the failure mode here; toggling from either surface must move the other.
* **The boot path can break loudly.** The constructor throws if any id is missing; a data-driven info list that drops one takes the whole app down at startup rather than degrading. Verify boot before and after in both branches, and correct D2's id count in the shell ticket in the same PR.
* **Selection must not interfere with the render loop.** Selecting a light while a shape transition is running, or switching shape while a light is selected, both have to be exercised — the fade timeout and the transition queue are independent state machines and this ticket now couples a third input to both.
* **Cost**: one extra pass over `Mesh.points` per frame for the AABB — 5 points on the pyramid, 143 on the sphere, 4224 on the Menger sponge, which is the registry maximum — against a triangle loop several times larger. Negligible, but do not let it become per-triangle, and reuse E6's transform pass.
* **No layout changes.** Non-mesh records must fill the same seven-row shape SHAPE INFO ships; a record with four rows changes the card height and that is a bug in this ticket, not a licence to redesign.
* **Do not invent copy.** If a value for the floor, sky or light cannot be traced to a constant in the source, the row does not ship.
* **Order.** E7 lands last of the rendering tickets — after world-tab, E5, E6, E3 and E2. World-tab ships the `setLayers` this ticket binds visibility to; E5a widens it and re-derives every floor constant the `FloorObject` record quotes; E6 supplies the transform pass the projected AABB reuses and the `RenderStats` return that shares this ticket's two call sites (`src/index.ts` L500, L512); E3a gives `KEY_LIGHT` something to switch off; E2's near plane is the guard `Point3D.project(out)` needs. Nothing downstream depends on E7.

## Files

* `src/scene/Scene.ts` — new: ordered object list, `renderables()`, `byId()`
* `src/scene/SceneObject.ts` — new: the interface and `ScreenRect`
* `src/scene/objects/MeshObject.ts`, `FloorObject.ts`, `SkyObject.ts`, `LightObject.ts` — new
* `src/scene/sceneObjectInfo.ts` — new: the per-object info and story records
* `src/primitives/Mesh.ts` — `projectedBounds()`, reusing E6's transform pass
* `src/primitives/Point3D.ts` — `project(out)` consuming E2's near plane; `convert3D2D()` delegates to it
* `src/rendering/BackgroundRenderer.ts` — export the floor and sky constants (E5a's, not the old ones)
* `src/index.ts` — construct the `Scene`, render `scene.renderables()` at L500 and L512, publish selection and bounds, route the opacity write through the selected record, reset selection on primitive change
* `src/ui/sceneGraph.ts` — rows built from `Scene` instead of the hardcoded four; remove the row 2–4 placeholder markers
* `src/ui/uiState.ts` — selection and per-object visibility slices
* `src/ui/viewportHud.ts` — bracket rect and label from the selection; delete the placeholder constants
* `src/ui/statusBar.ts` — selected id from the selection
* `src/styles/components/viewport.css` — bracket consumes `--sel-*`; delete the hardcoded percentages and the 190px square in both branches
* `src/index.html` — SHAPE INFO row template becomes the record's render target

## Done when

- [ ] `Scene` holds the four objects in the design's order, `Surface3D.render` receives `scene.renderables()`, and hidden objects never reach it
- [ ] Scene-graph rows 2 to 4 render id, kind and count from scene objects; `data-placeholder="true"` is gone from all three rows and their visibility buttons
- [ ] Hiding `FLOOR_01` removes the checker floor, hiding `SKY_DOME` removes the sky gradient and bitmap, and hiding `KEY_LIGHT` leaves ambient-only shading — all through the single `BackgroundRenderer.setLayers` and E3a's lighting slice; toggling the same layer from the world tab moves the scene-graph row and vice versa
- [ ] Floor and sky rows show the em dash rather than a fabricated triangle count
- [ ] SHAPE INFO's header note shows the selected object's kind and the literal `MESH` placeholder is gone
- [ ] Selecting a non-mesh row swaps SHAPE INFO's rows and SHAPE STORY's prose to that object's record through the existing 180ms fade, with unchanged card height and no row wrapping at 320px
- [ ] Every non-mesh row value is traceable to a named engine constant in a code comment, and the floor record quotes E5a's constants rather than the deleted ones
- [ ] Dragging the opacity slider with a non-mesh object selected does not write into the panel
- [ ] The status bar's `<id> selected` follows the scene selection, not the active primitive
- [ ] Picking a primitive returns selection to the mesh row, and the mesh row keeps one id and a summed count through the 1250ms transition
- [ ] The viewport bracket tracks the projected AABB of the selected mesh every frame, and the hardcoded `39.2% / 31.9%` origin, the 190px desktop square and the `22.4% × 35.8%` mobile box are gone from `viewport.css`

- [ ] The bracket reads the render target's extent, never a 1024 or 640 literal

Title: E8 — Session actions and keyboard
Description:
Five toolbar buttons and eight shortcut chips currently document behaviour that does not exist: `grep -rn keydown src/` returns nothing, and STEP, CAPTURE PNG, SAVE PRESET, LOAD and COPY CODE are inert nodes carrying the placeholder affordance. This ticket adds the session layer — step a single frame while paused, export the framebuffer, save and load a scene preset, copy a snippet — and one `keydown` handler that dispatches through the same `SHORTCUTS` table the chips render from. Click and key paths share one action registry, so a chip can never name a key the handler does not bind, and a button can never do something no chip documents.

**Unblocks**

* STEP, CAPTURE PNG, SAVE PRESET, LOAD, COPY CODE — desktop action cluster and mobile action row, ten `data-placeholder="true"` nodes in total (toolbar ticket)
* All eight shortcut chips: `SPACE pause`, `W wireframe`, `G grid`, `C culling`, `R reset`, `S sky`, `F floor`, `1-N shape` (shortcuts ticket). E5a has already moved `G` from `pendingFeature` to `pendingHandler`, so it is live here with the rest.
* Nothing else. The mobile GESTURES card is pointer work owned by E1b.

## Approach

**One action registry.** New `src/ui/actions.ts` exporting `ActionId` (`stepFrame`, `capturePng`, `savePreset`, `loadPreset`, `copyCode`, `togglePause`, `toggleWireframe`, `toggleBackfaceCulling`, `resetControls`, `toggleSky`, `toggleFloor`, `toggleGrid`, `selectPrimitive`), a `registerAction(id, fn)` / `runAction(id, arg?)` pair, and nothing else. `Main.init` registers the implementations. Buttons are bound by a single delegated `click` listener on `#app` reading `data-action` off `event.target.closest('[data-action]')` — that binds both branch mounts at once, the same way `setField` writes to every `[data-field]` node, and it means no ticket has to know that the toolbar exists twice in the DOM.

**The keyboard handler reads** `SHORTCUTS`**, not keys.** `src/ui/shortcuts.ts` already exports `{ keyLabel, keys, action, status, handler? }`; this ticket types `handler` as `ActionId`, adds `'live'` to the status union, and flips the pending-handler entries to `live`. One `window` `keydown` listener added in `Main.init` and removed in `destroy()`:

* Bail on `event.repeat`, on `event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey || event.altKey`, and when `event.target.closest('input, select, textarea, button, [contenteditable=""], [contenteditable="true"]')` matches. Without the last guard, SPACE with focus on the PAUSE button toggles twice — once from the button's native activation, once from the global handler.
* Match `event.key.toLowerCase()` against each binding's `keys`, skipping any entry whose status is `pendingFeature`. Gating on `status` rather than on a hardcoded exclusion list is the point: a binding becomes live the moment its feature ticket flips the field, with no edit here.
* SPACE is `' '` and needs `preventDefault()` (it scrolls the page).
* Digits dispatch `selectPrimitive` with `Number(key) - 1`, resolved against `Object.keys(data)` and ignored when out of range, then `requestPrimitiveChange(name)`.
* Correction to carry into `src/ui/shortcuts.ts` while here: the range is derived as `1-${Object.keys(data).length}`, but there is no two-digit key. [COS-201](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-201/epic-polyhedra-from-the-symmetries-of-things) adds roughly ten more polyhedra, so clamp the derivation to `Math.min(count, 9)` for both the label and the `keys` array, or the chip will promise `1-18`.

**STEP.** `renderFrame` early-returns while `!isPlaying` (`src/index.ts` L490–L492) and `renderPausedFrame` (L507) repaints without advancing anything. Extract the body of `renderFrame` into `advanceAndRender(now)` — transition update, `syncTransitionQueue`, the per-frame mesh transform, `surface3D.render` — and have `renderFrame` call it when playing and `stepFrame()` call it when paused.

E1a has already replaced `rotateMesh` with `rig.advance(dt)` plus one `mesh.setTransform(rig.matrix())` over `getActiveMeshes()`, so write `advanceAndRender` against the rig. The synthetic clock below therefore also drives the spin accumulator, and a step advances the turntable by exactly one frame's worth of degrees. `stepFrame()` advances that synthetic clock rather than passing `performance.now()`:

* Seed `this.pausedClock = performance.now()` in `togglePause` on the stop branch.
* Each step: `this.pausedClock += FRAME_STEP_MS` (1000/60), then `advanceAndRender(this.pausedClock)`.

The synthetic clock is load-bearing. `StateMachine.createUpdate` computes progress as `(now - currentStateStartedAt) / duration` (`src/animations/StateMachine.ts` L116–L123), so stepping with wall-clock time after a thirty-second pause would complete a queued 1250 ms shape transition in a single step. On resume, `start()` already calls `transitionMachine.syncClock(performance.now())`, and `rebaseTime` shifts `currentStateStartedAt` by `now - lastUpdatedAt` (L97–L101) — `lastUpdatedAt` is the synthetic value the last step wrote, so the transition picks up exactly where stepping left it.

Step publishes `trisDrawn` and `frameMs` through `setField` (`stop()` zeroed both at L581–L583) but must **not** call `fpsCounter()`: that pushes into the one-second ring buffer and the FRAMERATE sparkline, and the fps readout is deliberately 0 while paused. Say so in a comment next to the call site.

**CAPTURE PNG.** `canvas.toBlob(blob => …, 'image/png')`, then an object URL on a synthetic `<a download>`, revoked on the next task. Use `toBlob`, not `toDataURL` — the data URL for a 1024 × 640 frame is a multi-megabyte string built synchronously on the main thread, and after E9b the backing store can be several times larger. Tainting is not a risk: `sky.avif`, `border-collie.jpeg` and `galaxy.jpeg` are imported through Vite (`src/index.ts` L13–L15) and resolve to same-origin URLs under `base: "/3dengine"`, and neither `loadImageAsset` (L57–L63) nor `loadTextures` sets `crossOrigin`, so the canvas is never tainted and `toBlob` will not throw `SecurityError`. Filename `3dengine-<primitive>-<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>.png`. Capture the current bitmap without re-rendering, so a paused frame exports exactly what is on screen.

**Preset save and load: a downloaded JSON file, not localStorage.** The toolbar draws SAVE PRESET and LOAD as two separate buttons, which only reads as export/import; a localStorage pair needs a slot picker the design does not contain, and this epic must not add a widget. File presets are also shareable and survive a cleared origin. Format `{ app: "3dengine", version: 1, savedAt, state }`, written through the same blob-download helper as CAPTURE. LOAD is a hidden `<input type="file" accept="application/json">` clicked programmatically, with `input.value = ''` before `click()` so re-selecting the same file fires `change` again.

New `src/ui/scenePreset.ts` owns one serialiser used by SAVE PRESET **and** COPY CODE, so the two can never disagree. `serialiseScene()` collects the current primitive key, the slider values via `Controls.getNumericValue`, `wireframeEnabled`, `backfaceCullingEnabled`, and a snapshot of every registered `uiState` slice — add `snapshot()` / `hydrate(partial)` to the same slice registry that already backs `resetAll()` (shell ticket, D7), so a slice added by a later ticket is serialised without editing this module. `applyScene(preset)` validates before it touches anything: wrong `app` or `version` rejects outright, unknown keys are ignored, numbers are clamped to each input's own `min`/`max`, an unknown primitive falls back to the current one. Application order is `resetControls`'s order with file values instead of defaults.

**COPY CODE.** `navigator.clipboard.writeText(snippet)`, built from the same `serialiseScene()`:

```ts
// 3dengine BUILD 0.9.4 — 2026-07-28
applyScene({ primitive: "cuboctahedron", zoom: 50, pitch: 0, yaw: 0, roll: 0,
             spin: 24, opacity: 100, wireframe: false, backfaceCulling: true });
```

**Feedback without a toast.** The console has no notification surface. Flash the pressed button's own label — `COPIED` for 1200 ms on success, `FAILED` for 1200 ms on a rejected clipboard write or a malformed preset, then restore the original `textContent` (including COPY CODE's escaped `</> COPY CODE`) — and `console.warn` the reason. One helper, used by all three fallible actions. This is a rebuild addition; the design has no button state, so record it in a code comment.

**Placeholder removal.** Drop `data-placeholder`, `title` and `aria-describedby` from the five buttons in both mounts and give each a `data-action`. Flip the `SHORTCUTS` entries to `live` so `shortcutsPanel.ts` stops applying the pending affordance.

## Constraints and risks

* Global key bindings are hostile to future text entry: once this lands, pressing `s` anywhere outside a form control toggles the sky. The focus guard is the only thing that makes that survivable, so every input a later ticket adds must be a real `<input>` / `<textarea>` or it will eat shortcuts.
* The listener is added once in `Main.init` and removed in `destroy()`. Vite HMR re-executing the module without a teardown double-binds and every key fires twice — wire `import.meta.hot?.dispose()` to `destroy()`. **E1b already added a** `destroy()`**-shaped teardown for its pointer listeners; this must be the same one, not a second.**
* Stepping does not feed the fps ring buffer, so the FRAMERATE sparkline flatlines while the user steps. That is correct (there is no frame rate) but it looks like a bug; comment it.
* A step during a queued shape transition advances the transition by one frame, not to completion. Verify by pressing STEP ten times mid-switch and seeing ten frames of travel.
* Preset files are user-supplied JSON. Never `eval`, never assign a parsed value straight to `input.value` without clamping, never route one into `innerHTML`. Only the primitive key is a string, and it is checked against `Object.keys(data)`.
* Presets are not forward-compatible by construction: one saved before a later de-mock ticket adds a slice loads with that slice at its default. That is the intent — bump `version` only when a slice's *meaning* changes, not when one is added.
* `navigator.clipboard` needs a secure context and a user gesture; both hold for localhost, the https deploy and a button click. Do not add an `execCommand('copy')` fallback — flash `FAILED` instead.
* No layout change. The label flashes are all shorter than the labels they replace (`COPIED` vs `</> COPY CODE`, `FAILED` vs `SAVE PRESET`), so the action cluster only ever narrows; do not add a `min-width` to compensate.
* If this has to be split, the seam is [registry + keyboard + STEP] against [capture + preset + copy], which are all serialisation and file plumbing. Do not split the registry from the keyboard handler — the shared table is the entire point of the ticket.
* **Order.** E8 lands after E1 and after E5a. E1a rewrote `renderFrame` and deleted `rotateMesh`, which is the body `advanceAndRender` extracts, and it owns the frame clock and `requestRender()` that `stepFrame` must not duplicate. E5a made `G` real. `serialiseScene()` snapshots every registered `uiState` slice, so every de-mock ticket that adds a slice is serialised automatically; that is why this ticket can land before or after E2, E3, E4, E6, E7 and E9b without touching them.

## Files

* `src/ui/actions.ts` — new; `ActionId`, the registry, the delegated `data-action` click listener
* `src/ui/scenePreset.ts` — new; `serialiseScene()`, `applyScene()`, the validator, the code snippet
* `src/ui/download.ts` — new; the blob → object URL → `<a download>` → revoke helper, shared by CAPTURE PNG and SAVE PRESET
* `src/ui/shortcuts.ts` — `handler` typed as `ActionId`, `'live'` added to the status union, entries flipped, the shape-key range clamped at 9
* `src/ui/shortcutsPanel.ts` — stop applying the pending affordance to `live` entries
* `src/ui/uiState.ts` — `snapshot()` / `hydrate(partial)` over the existing slice registry
* `src/index.ts` — `advanceAndRender(now)` extracted from `renderFrame`, `stepFrame()`, `pausedClock`, action registration, the `keydown` listener, `destroy()`
* `src/index.html` — `data-action` on all ten action-button nodes, placeholder attributes removed, the hidden file input added

## Done when

- [ ] Exactly one `keydown` listener exists in the repo, added in `Main.init` and removed in `destroy()`; `grep -rn "keydown" src/` returns the one `addEventListener` and its `removeEventListener`
- [ ] All eight chips act on their key
- [ ] No key string appears outside `SHORTCUTS` — not in the markup, not in `src/index.ts`, not in the CSS
- [ ] Keys are ignored while focus is inside an input, select, textarea or button, while ctrl/meta/alt is held, and on auto-repeat; SPACE with the PAUSE button focused toggles the loop exactly once
- [ ] STEP advances exactly one frame while paused: the drawn-triangle count and frame time update, the fps readout stays 0, uptime keeps its own clock, the turntable advances by one frame's degrees, and ten presses mid-transition advance the shape switch by ten frames instead of completing it
- [ ] STEP is a no-op while the loop is running
- [ ] CAPTURE PNG downloads a PNG matching the canvas backing store, throws no `SecurityError`, and does not freeze the tab
- [ ] SAVE PRESET downloads JSON; LOAD restores every slider, both flags, the primitive and every registered `uiState` slice in one repaint; loading the same file twice in a row works
- [ ] A malformed, foreign-`app` or wrong-`version` file leaves the scene untouched and flashes `FAILED`
- [ ] COPY CODE writes a snippet built from the same `serialiseScene()` as SAVE PRESET, flashes `COPIED`, and restores the escaped `</> COPY CODE` label exactly
- [ ] `destroy()` is the same teardown E1b added, not a second one, and HMR does not double-bind either listener set
- [ ] `data-placeholder`, `title` and `aria-describedby` are gone from all ten action-button nodes in `src/index.html`, and the remaining `data-placeholder` hits belong only to other de-mock tickets

Title: E9b — Resize, DPR and the pixel budget
Description:
Stage two of two of "Resizable render target" (E9), and **the last ticket of the de-mock epic**. E9a decoupled the projection from the canvas at scale 1 — a shared `renderTarget`, the viewport centre out of `Point3D`, the rotation neutrals named. This ticket makes the render target actually follow its box, at device-pixel resolution, with a pixel budget so a large window degrades resolution instead of frame rate.

It lands last on purpose: it invalidates every fixed-size assumption the other tickets were written against, and a software rasteriser's cost is linear in pixels, so E3b's and E5a's perf gates must be measured at a known size first.

**Unblocks**

* A fluid viewport: `.viewportStage`'s `aspect-ratio: 16/10` letterbox comes out on desktop and the canvas fills the viewport card (viewport-hud)
* The resolution HUD chip stops being a boot-time constant and tracks the live backing store, desktop and mobile (viewport-hud)
* SYSTEM's BUFFER and COLOR BUFFER rows recompute on resize instead of once at boot (system)
* CAMERA's ASPECT becomes live; FOV becomes constant-by-construction rather than constant-by-accident (camera)
* DPR-correct rendering: the raster is no longer bilinearly upscaled by the compositor on any retina display (viewport-hud, system)

## Approach

**Device pixels everywhere, no base canvas transform.** Set `canvas.width = Math.round(cssWidth · dprEffective)` and `canvas.height = Math.round(cssHeight · dprEffective)`, and leave the context transform at identity. Do **not** use `ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0)` as the DPR strategy: `Triangle`'s texture branch calls `context.setTransform(m11, m12, m21, m22, dx, dy)` (`src/primitives/Triangle.ts` L220) for every textured triangle, which is absolute and wipes the base scale — the dog and galaxy textures would draw at `1/dpr` size, offset, inside a correctly placed clip. Working in device pixels also means `renderTarget.scale` absorbs DPR for free.

One consequence to handle: `Triangle.render` hardcodes `context.lineWidth = 1` (L135), which is a half-thickness hairline at DPR 2. Add `lineWidth?: number` to `TriangleRenderOptions` (default 1) and pass `renderTarget.scale` from `Main`'s two `surface3D.render` calls.

`BackgroundRenderer.resize(width, height)`**.** `width` / `height` are `readonly` (L2–L3) and everything else derives from them at draw time — the sky gradient, the sky bitmap's cover scale, the horizon, the floor, the vignette. Dropping `readonly` and adding a setter is the entire change. E5a has already re-derived the floor and the horizon from the shared render target, so those follow automatically; the checker floor's column count and extent now come from the grid step in world units, so a wider target shows more ground rather than a stretched grid.

`ShapeTransitionMachine.resize(width, height)`**.** `travelX` / `travelY` are computed once into the context (L152–L153) as `width + margin` / `height + margin`, and both animating states read `context.travelY` on every tick, so writing the two fields is sufficient and an in-flight transition follows the new size. Store `margin` on the context so `resize` can recompute it — today the `?? 160` default is consumed in the constructor and forgotten.

`Main.resize(cssWidth, cssHeight)`**.** Compute the backing size, return early if it is unchanged, set `canvas.width` / `canvas.height`, then `renderTarget.setSize`, `backgroundRenderer.resize`, `transitionMachine.resize`, then `renderPausedFrame()` — assigning `canvas.width` clears the bitmap, so a paused viewport goes blank until the next resize otherwise.

**The observer.** One `ResizeObserver` on `.viewportStage`, constructed in `Main.init` and disconnected in the `destroy()` E1b and E8 already share. Prefer `entry.devicePixelContentBoxSize[0]` where available — it is already in device pixels and immune to fractional-CSS rounding — falling back to `contentBoxSize` / `contentRect` multiplied by `devicePixelRatio`. Round to integers and compare against the current backing size so a sub-pixel layout change does not reallocate the bitmap. A DPR change from dragging the window to another display does not reliably fire `resize`, so re-run the same path from the `matchMedia('(resolution: Xdppx)')` listener the SYSTEM widget already arms rather than adding a second listener. Coalesce to one resize per rAF tick: `ResizeObserver` fires every frame during a drag, and each resize reallocates the bitmap and repaints the entire background.

**Pixel budget, not optional.** This is a software rasteriser filling on the main thread, so cost is linear in `width × height`. Today's 1024 × 640 is 0.65 MP; a 1400px-wide centre column at DPR 2 is 2800 × 1750 = 4.9 MP, roughly 7.5× the fill work per frame. Introduce `MAX_RENDER_PIXELS` (start at 1.6 MP, about 1600 × 1000) and derive `dprEffective = Math.min(devicePixelRatio, Math.sqrt(MAX_RENDER_PIXELS / (cssW · cssH)))`, so a large window degrades resolution instead of frame rate. The clamp is visible rather than hidden, because the resolution HUD chip reports the real backing store.

**Buffers that must be reallocated.** E3b's colour `ImageData` and depth `Float32Array` are allocated from `renderTarget.width/height` and reallocate on `setSize` — E3b was written for this, so it is a call, not a reopening. Its background snapshot must also be invalidated on every resize.

**Downstream readouts.** The three widgets that computed from the canvas once at boot subscribe to the resize path and publish through `setField`, so both branch mounts update from one write: the resolution HUD chip, SYSTEM's BUFFER and COLOR BUFFER (`width · height · 4 / 1048576`, 2 decimals), and CAMERA's ASPECT. E2's `fl = (height / 2) / tan(fov / 2)` recomputes on resize, and because E9a's `scale` multiplies *after* the perspective divide, vertical FOV stays 93.7° at every size. Leave the FRAMERATE sparkline alone — it owns a separate canvas with `dpr = 2` pinned by its own ticket and its own size check inside `drawFps()`, and must not be attached to this observer.

**CSS.** `src/styles/components/viewport.css` drops `aspect-ratio: 16 / 10` from `.viewportStage` on desktop and lets the stage fill the card (`position: absolute; inset: 0`). That is the one sanctioned layout change in this epic: the letterbox *is* the placeholder. Mobile keeps the card's own `aspect-ratio: 16 / 10`, so the stage keeps its shape there and HUD anchoring is untouched in both branches.

## Constraints and risks

* **The invariant from E9a still holds.** At 1024 × 640 with DPR 1 every projected coordinate must be identical to the pre-E9 build. Keep the boot-time assertion.
* **Fill cost is linear in pixels.** Without the pixel cap, a maximised window on a 4K display turns a 60 fps scene into a slideshow — a software rasteriser has no GPU to absorb it.
* **Reallocating the backing store clears it**, so every resize must repaint; a paused viewport that is not explicitly re-rendered goes blank.
* **A resize during a shape transition** moves `travelX` / `travelY` under a running lerp and the incoming mesh jumps. Accepted — deferring resize until the machine is idle leaves the canvas stale for up to 1250 ms, which is worse.
* **Affine texture mapping already shears** (see the header comment in `Triangle.ts`); at higher resolution those artifacts are more visible, not less. That belongs to E4b, not here.
* **Stale "the canvas is fixed" claims must be corrected in this PR.** The UI tickets `system`, `camera`, `viewport-hud` (which carries an explicit "No canvas resize is attempted" acceptance criterion) and `world-tab` all state it in prose, as do E1a, E2, E3b, E5a and E7. Those notes and any code comments repeating them are now wrong — fix them here, or the next reader re-derives the constants.
* **No** `data-placeholder` **node belongs to this ticket**: the resolution chip and the BUFFER / COLOR BUFFER rows were real-but-frozen, not marked. The equivalent criterion is that none of them can report a stale number after a resize, and that no comment in `src/` still claims a fixed 1024 × 640.
* **Order.** Last in the epic. Every ticket that allocates from the render target (E3b), derives a horizon or ground extent (E5a, E5b), compares fill rate against a pixel count (E6) or clamps a bracket to the stage (E7) is already written to read `renderTarget`, so this is a `setSize` call plus an observer rather than a reopening of four tickets.

## Files

* `src/rendering/renderTarget.ts` — `setSize` becomes live rather than boot-only
* `src/primitives/Triangle.ts` — `lineWidth?: number` on `TriangleRenderOptions`, used by the wireframe stroke
* `src/rendering/BackgroundRenderer.ts` — `resize(width, height)`, `readonly` dropped from the two fields; snapshot invalidation
* `src/animations/shapeTransitionMachine.ts` — `resize(width, height)`, `margin` kept on the context
* `src/index.ts` — `resize()`, the `ResizeObserver`, the DPR `matchMedia` hook, teardown in the shared `destroy()`, the `setField` writes, `lineWidth` passed to both render calls
* `src/index.html` — canvas keeps `width="1024" height="640"` as the pre-observer seed
* `src/styles/components/viewport.css` — desktop stage fills the card; mobile unchanged
* `src/ui/viewportHud.ts`, `src/ui/telemetry/SystemWidget.ts`, `src/ui/telemetry/CameraWidget.ts` — recompute on resize instead of at boot

## Done when

- [ ] At 1024 × 640 with DPR 1 the rendered frame is pixel-identical to the pre-E9 build, and the boot-time invariant assertion still passes
- [ ] Dragging the window from 900px to 1800px wide re-rasterises the scene at the new size with no letterbox, no stretch, and the mesh at the same fraction of the frame
- [ ] Vertical FOV measures 93.7° at every viewport size; ASPECT tracks `canvas.width / canvas.height`
- [ ] On a DPR 2 display the raster is sharp — text-free edges show no compositor upscaling — and textured faces are drawn at the correct scale and position, proving no base canvas transform was introduced
- [ ] Wireframe strokes keep their apparent thickness at DPR 1 and DPR 2
- [ ] Backing pixels never exceed `MAX_RENDER_PIXELS`; a maximised window on a large display reduces resolution rather than frame rate, and the resolution chip shows the clamped figure
- [ ] Resizing while paused leaves a correctly rendered frame on screen, not a blank canvas
- [ ] E3b's colour and depth buffers reallocate on resize and its background snapshot is invalidated
- [ ] The resolution chip, SYSTEM BUFFER and COLOR BUFFER, and CAMERA ASPECT all update on resize in both branches through a single `setField` write each; COLOR BUFFER still reads `2.50 MB` at 1024 × 640
- [ ] `ResizeObserver` fires at most one resize per animation frame during a continuous drag, and is disconnected in the shared `destroy()`
- [ ] Moving the window to a display with a different `devicePixelRatio` re-rasterises without a window resize
- [ ] The FRAMERATE sparkline canvas is untouched and still resizes itself at its pinned DPR 2
- [ ] No comment or ticket implementation note in `src/` still asserts that the canvas is fixed at 1024 × 640, and the four UI tickets plus five engine tickets that said so in prose are corrected in this PR
- [ ] `npm run build` passes

Title: Epic: Spira — self-hosted Linear replacement
Description:
Parent for the whole Spira build. Full spec: `docs/specs/2026-07-29-spira-design.md`.

## Phases

| Code | Phase |
| -- | -- |
| F | Foundations — scaffold, Prisma schema, dev environment |
| A | Auth — session, CSRF, login, rate limiting |
| P | API — route-handler conventions, projects, issues, labels, relations, views |
| U | UI shell — layout, sidebar, design tokens, settings |
| R | Projects — list, create/edit, overview page |
| I | Issues — markdown, list layout, detail page, creation |
| V | Filters & saved views |
| E | Epics & relations |
| S | Search |
| M | Migration from Linear |
| C | MCP connector |
| D | Deploy on ks-b |

## Sequencing notes

`F → A → P` is a hard chain: nothing renders before the API exists. `U`, `R`, `I` follow. `V`, `E`, `S` can proceed in any order once `I` lands. `C` needs `P` only, so it can run in parallel with UI work. `D` can be provisioned early and refined at the end.

## Migration runs last, all of it

`M1` → `M4` all happen at the end, once Spira is functional: CSV export from Linear, importer written against that real file, renumbering with legacy identifiers preserved, then cutover.

Nothing in `M` runs early. Linear stays in use for the other projects throughout the build, so an earlier export would be stale on arrival — and the app is developed against seed data, which needs no real ticket data at all.

Note that the rendering side of the legacy story is *not* in `M`: the `legacyIdentifier` column (`F2`), resolving both identifier forms (`P3`), showing both in rows and headers (`I3`, `I5`), the `301` redirect (`I5`), reference chips (`I2`) and search over both (`S1`) are all built long before any import exists. `M` only supplies the data.

## The only irreversible moment

Cancelling the Linear subscription, in `M4` step 6. Export first.

## Definition of done for v1

Projects, issues, six statuses, multiple labels, epics, blocking relations, filters, saved views, list layout, project overview, markdown with cross-reference chips, search across new and legacy identifiers, every Linear project imported, MCP connector working, running on ks-b.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: M1 — Full CSV export of the Linear workspace
Description:
**When: at the end**, once Spira is functional. Not before — Linear stays in use throughout the build, with tickets still being filed for the other projects, so any earlier export is stale on arrival.

## Do

Export all projects from Linear as CSV. Commit the file to the Spira repo — it is both the migration input and the fixture `M2`'s tests run against.

Record alongside it:

* the exact column list and order
* how `Description` encodes markdown, newlines and embedded commas
* how `Labels` packs several labels into one cell
* how `Parent issue` identifies the parent — identifier or UUID
* date formats and timezone

`M2` is written against this actual file, not an assumed schema.

## Optional top-up while the workspace is still live

The CSV is unlikely to carry comment threads or issue relations. If either is wanted, the Linear MCP connector reaches both — `list_comments` and `get_issue` with `includeRelations` — and can be run in the same session to produce a JSON side-file. Independent of the CSV path and skippable.

## Done when

The export is committed and its columns are documented.

Title: F2 — Prisma schema and first migration
Description:
Prisma 7 with `@prisma/adapter-mariadb` against MySQL, same setup as PFA's `nest-api`.

## Models

`User`, `Project`, `WorkflowState`, `Label`, `Issue`, `IssueLabel`, `IssueRelation`, `SavedView`, `ApiToken`. Full field list in the spec, §5. Sessions live in Redis, not here.

## Points that matter

* `Issue.identifier` is a **stored, uniquely indexed column** — never derived at read time. Renaming or re-keying a project must not move existing identifiers.
* `Issue.legacyIdentifier` is nullable and uniquely indexed. Both identifier columns are searched.
* `@@unique([projectId, number])` guards the per-project counter.
* `Project.issueCounter` holds the last allocated number.
* `Issue.epicId` is a self-relation; `isEpic` marks the parent. No recursive structures anywhere.
* `IssueRelation` is `@@unique([fromIssueId, toIssueId, type])`.
* `Issue.sortOrder` is a float, so a row can be inserted between two others without renumbering.

Declare indexes that MySQL auto-creates alongside FK constraints explicitly, with matching names — PFA learned this the hard way, otherwise `migrate diff` reports drift forever.

## Done when

`prisma migrate dev` applies cleanly, `prisma migrate diff` reports no drift, generated client type-checks.

Title: F3 — Dev environment: MySQL, Redis, env config and seed
Description:
Make the project runnable from a clean checkout.

## Scope

* Local MySQL and Redis (docker-compose is fine; PFA runs `redis-server` via `concurrently`, either works)
* Typed env loading with zod, failing loudly at boot on a missing variable: `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `COOKIE_SECURE`, `APP_URL`
* `.env.example` documenting every variable
* Seed script creating:
  * the single user account, password hashed with bcryptjs
  * the six workflow states — `Backlog` (backlog), `Todo` (unstarted), `In Progress` (started), `In Review` (started), `Done` (completed), `Canceled` (canceled)
  * a handful of labels and one demo project with issues, so UI work has something to render before the import lands

## Done when

A fresh clone reaches a working app with seeded data through a documented sequence of commands.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: A1 — Session layer: Redis store and httpOnly cookie
Description:
PFA's session model transposed off Express, since there is no `express-session` here.

## Behaviour

* Session id in an httpOnly cookie `spira.sid`: `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` in production, `Path=/`
* `COOKIE_SECURE=false` escape hatch for running over plain HTTP, as PFA has
* Session record in Redis under a `spira:` prefix, rolling TTL refreshed on each authenticated request
* Session id is cryptographically random, never derived from the user id

## API

* `createSession(userId)` → id + cookie
* `getSession()` → session or null, Node runtime
* `requireSession()` → session or throws 401
* `destroySession()`

## The runtime boundary — do not blur this

Next middleware runs on Edge, where a Redis client cannot run. Therefore:

* **middleware** only checks whether the `spira.sid` cookie exists and redirects to `/login` if not. It is a UX shortcut, **not** a security boundary.
* `requireSession()` on the Node runtime is the only authorisation point, called by every Server Component page and every route handler.

A forged cookie passes middleware and fails `requireSession()`. That is the intended design. If authorisation ever moves into middleware it silently becomes unenforceable.

## Done when

Unit tests cover creation, retrieval, expiry and destruction; an integration test confirms a forged cookie is rejected server-side.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: A2 — CSRF token: mint, rotate and validate
Description:
Port of `pfa/nest-api/src/users/csrf-token.util.ts` and `guards/csrf.guard.ts`.

## Behaviour

* A random 32-byte hex token is minted into the session at login and returned to the client
* Every unsafe verb (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) must echo it in `X-CSRF-Token` (accept `X-XSRF-Token` too, as PFA does)
* Comparison uses `timingSafeEqual`, with a length check first since `timingSafeEqual` throws on mismatched lengths
* Safe verbs (`GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`) skip the check
* Requests with no authenticated session skip the check — there is no ambient credential to abuse, and login itself is a POST
* Token rotates on login, is cleared on logout

## Client side

The token is exposed to the browser (readable cookie or bootstrapped into the app shell) and attached automatically by the shared fetch wrapper, so no call site has to remember it.

## Not applicable to API tokens

`ApiToken` bearer auth (`C1`) bypasses CSRF entirely: the credential is not ambient, so there is nothing to forge.

## Done when

Unit tests cover valid, missing, wrong-length and mismatched tokens; an integration test confirms a mutation without the header returns 403.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: A3 — Login, logout and route protection
Description:
Single account, no signup — the user is seeded by `F3`.

## Scope

* `POST /api/auth/login` — email + password, bcryptjs compare, creates the session and mints the CSRF token
* `POST /api/auth/logout` — destroys the session, clears the cookie and the token
* Login page under `app/(auth)/login`, react-hook-form + zod, matching Linear's visual language
* Middleware redirects to `/login` when the `spira.sid` cookie is absent, and away from `/login` when it is present
* Every page under `app/(app)` and every route handler calls `requireSession()`

## Deliberately absent

No signup route, no password reset by email, no account creation UI. Adding a second user is a database operation, and that is the correct level of friction for a single-user app.

## Error handling

Wrong email and wrong password return the same generic message and take the same time — no user enumeration.

## Done when

Playwright covers: login succeeds, wrong password fails, a protected page redirects when logged out, logout invalidates the session server-side (not just client-side).
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: A4 — Login rate limiting and password change
Description:
## Rate limiting

Redis counter keyed by IP on `POST /api/auth/login`, with escalating lockout (for instance 5 attempts, then a growing delay). Counter resets on success.

Read the client IP from `X-Forwarded-For` first — behind nginx the socket address is always the proxy. Take the first entry, trimmed, and fall back to the socket address, exactly as PFA's request logger does.

## Password change

`PATCH /api/auth/password` requiring the current password, plus a form under settings. Changing the password destroys **all** other sessions for the account.

## Done when

An integration test confirms lockout kicks in and clears, and that changing the password invalidates a session established beforehand.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: P1 — Route handler conventions: validation, error shape, auth wrapper
Description:
The foundation every other `P` ticket builds on. Worth getting right once.

## Scope

* A wrapper composing: session or API-token auth → CSRF check (cookie auth only) → zod parse of body and query → handler → serialised response
* One error shape across the whole API: `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`, with codes stable enough for the MCP connector to branch on
* Mapping domain errors to status codes: 400 validation, 401 no session, 403 CSRF, 404 missing, 409 conflict (duplicate project key, identifier collision)
* Zod schemas colocated with each resource and **reused by the forms**, so client and server validation cannot drift
* A typed client-side fetch wrapper that attaches `X-CSRF-Token` automatically

## Why REST rather than server actions

The MCP connector needs a callable HTTP surface. If mutations existed only as server actions, every rule would need a second implementation. One write path, two callers.

## Done when

A trivial resource round-trips through the wrapper, and tests cover each error mapping.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: P2 — Projects API
Description:
`GET /api/projects`, `POST /api/projects`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /api/projects/[id]`.

## Fields

`key`, `name`, `icon`, `color`, `summary`, `description` (markdown), `statusId`, `priority`, `startDate`, `targetDate`.

## Key rules

* 2–5 characters, `[A-Z0-9]`, uppercase, unique across projects — a duplicate returns 409
* Suggested from the first three letters of the name, but always editable, because the suggestion is not always usable (`1991chat` → `199`)
* **Changing a key does not renumber existing issues.** `identifier` is stored, so historical identifiers stay valid forever. This is intentional and must be reflected in the UI copy.

## Deletion

Deleting a project with issues is refused with 409. Archiving is the supported path.

## Listing

Returns issue counts and completion ratio per project, computed in SQL rather than by loading issues.

## Done when

CRUD covered by integration tests, including the 409 paths and the key-change-does-not-renumber guarantee.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: P3 — Issues API and identifier allocation
Description:
The core of the whole app.

## Endpoints

* `GET /api/issues` with filters: project, state, label (multi, include/exclude), priority, epic, `isEpic`, text query; grouping and ordering; pagination
* `POST /api/issues`
* `GET|PATCH|DELETE /api/issues/[identifier]` — resolving **both** `identifier` and `legacyIdentifier`

## Identifier allocation

Inside one transaction: lock the project row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), increment `issueCounter`, write `{key}-{counter}` into `identifier` and the number into `number`.

The lock is what makes concurrent creates safe. Two simultaneous creates in the same project must produce `PFA-12` and `PFA-13`, never two `PFA-12`s and never a gap. There is one user, but the MCP connector and the browser are two clients, and a batch import is a third.

## Status transitions

Setting a state of type `completed` stamps `completedAt`; `canceled` stamps `canceledAt`; moving back out clears them.

## Done when

Integration tests cover CRUD, filtering, resolution by legacy identifier, and a concurrency test firing parallel creates and asserting a contiguous, collision-free sequence.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: P4 — Labels API and issue-label assignment
Description:
Labels are workspace-wide, not per-project — the same `Bug` should mean the same thing everywhere, and per-project label sets would multiply the same concepts across six projects.

## Endpoints

* `GET|POST /api/labels`, `PATCH|DELETE /api/labels/[id]`
* Label assignment through the issue `PATCH`: the client sends the full label set and the server reconciles, matching Linear's MCP semantics

## Rules

* Name unique, case-insensitive; 409 on duplicate
* Colour stored as hex
* Deleting a label removes it from every issue rather than refusing — a label is metadata, not structure

## Done when

CRUD and reconciliation are covered, including assigning several labels to one issue and removing one of them.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: P5 — Epic assignment and relations API
Description:
## Epics

An epic is an ordinary issue with `isEpic = true`, so it has its own identifier, description, status, priority and labels — exactly like `COS-201` does in Linear today. Other issues point at it through `epicId`.

Two invariants, enforced in the service layer because MySQL `CHECK` cannot express the subquery:

* `epicId` may only reference an issue whose `isEpic` is `true`
* an issue with `isEpic = true` must have `epicId = null`

Together these make the hierarchy exactly one level deep. No recursion, no recursive CTEs, no cycle detection beyond a direct self-reference.

Conversion rules: an issue can become an epic if it has no `epicId`; an epic can revert to a normal issue only when it has no children — refuse with 409 and a clear message rather than cascading.

`GET /api/issues/[identifier]/children` returns the contained issues plus the progress ratio, computed as `count(children where state.type = 'completed') / count(children)`.

## Relations

`POST|DELETE /api/issues/[identifier]/relations` with `{ type, targetIdentifier }`.

* A block is stored **once**, as `{from: A, to: B, type: 'blocks'}`, read as "A blocks B". "Blocked by" is the same row read backwards. Storing one direction makes it structurally impossible for the two views to disagree.
* `related` is symmetric and normalised on write (lower id first), so the pair exists once.
* Self-relations are refused. Duplicate relations are idempotent, not an error.

## Done when

Unit tests cover both epic invariants, both conversion rules, relation normalisation and the symmetric read.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: P6 — Saved views API
Description:
`GET|POST /api/views`, `PATCH|DELETE /api/views/[id]`.

A saved view stores a filter set, grouping, ordering and layout, scoped either to one project or to the whole workspace.

## Filter serialisation

The stored `filters` JSON and the URL query string produced by nuqs (`V1`) must be **the same shape**, with one serialiser shared by both. Saving a view then becomes "persist the current query", and opening a view becomes "push these params into the URL" — no translation layer, nothing to keep in sync.

Validate the JSON with zod on read as well as write: a view saved before a filter type changed must fail loudly rather than render a silently wrong list.

## Done when

A view round-trips: build a filter in the URL, save it, reload from the saved view, and get an identical query string back.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: U1 — App shell: sidebar, header and navigation
Description:
The persistent frame every page renders inside, copying Linear's layout.

## Scope

* Fixed left sidebar: account block at the top, then Projects and Views, then the per-project section with its own Issues and Views entries
* Breadcrumb header with the tab row underneath (Overview / Issues), matching the project pages in the screenshots
* Content area with the filter bar slot above the list
* Collapsible sidebar, state persisted
* Loading and empty states for each region

## Out of scope

Command palette, keyboard shortcuts, notification inbox — all excluded from v1.

## Done when

Navigation works between projects, issues and views, and the shell holds together at narrow widths without the body scrolling horizontally.

Title: U2 — Design tokens and dark theme
Description:
Define the visual language once, in one file, rather than scattering arbitrary values through components — the mistake PFA is currently unwinding under its `design system` label.

## Scope

* Tailwind v4 CSS-first tokens: background layers, borders, text hierarchy, accent, status colours, radii, spacing scale, typography scale
* Dark theme as the default, light theme available through next-themes, both driven by the same token names
* Status colours and icons for the six workflow states, and the priority icon set, defined once and consumed everywhere
* Label chips rendering from a stored hex with readable contrast in both themes

## Done when

A page renders correctly in both themes with no hardcoded colour anywhere outside the token file.

Title: R1 — Projects list page
Description:
The equivalent of Linear's `Projects` table.

## Columns

Icon and name, key, issue count, completion percentage, status, priority, target date.

## Behaviour

* Rows link to the project overview
* Sortable by name, issue count and completion
* Counts come from the aggregated query in `P2`, not from loading issues client-side
* Empty state with a create action

## Done when

The six imported projects render with correct counts and percentages.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: R2 — Project create/edit form and the key rules
Description:
Form for name, key, icon, colour, summary, description, status, priority and dates.

## Key field

* Auto-fills from the first three letters of the name, uppercased, while the field is untouched; stops following the name once edited by hand
* Live uniqueness check, inline error on collision
* Validates 2–5 characters, `[A-Z0-9]`

The auto-suggestion is a convenience, not a rule: `1991chat` suggests `199`, which is unusable and becomes `CHT` manually. The form must make overriding obvious rather than fighting it.

## Editing an existing key

Show an explicit warning: **existing issues keep their current identifiers**, only new issues use the new key. This is intentional — identifiers are stored, so old references never break — but it is surprising if unstated.

## Done when

Creating a project with a colliding key is blocked inline, and changing an existing key leaves every existing identifier untouched.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: R3 — Project overview page
Description:
The project description page, copying Linear's overview tab — the layout visible on the `Exalus` project in the screenshots.

## Scope

* Icon, name, editable summary line
* Properties row: status, priority, dates
* Markdown description rendered through the `I2` pipeline, editable in place
* Progress block: scope and completed counts, breakdown by status
* Tabs: Overview / Issues

## Out of scope

Project updates, resources/documents, milestones, members and lead — all cut from v1.

## Done when

A project's description renders with full markdown, including cross-reference chips, and edits persist.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: I1 — Markdown editor with live preview
Description:
Descriptions are stored as raw markdown. The editor is a textarea with a live preview beside it, not a WYSIWYG.

## Accepted trade-off

The rendered result is identical to Linear's; the typing experience is not — `## Titre` appears as literal markdown while typing. This was chosen knowingly for simplicity over a ProseMirror stack.

Because storage is plain markdown, swapping in a rich-text editor later is purely additive and needs no data migration. That option stays open.

## Scope

* Split editor / preview, toggleable, preview using the same renderer as `I2`
* A small toolbar for the common marks (bold, italic, code, link, list, heading), each also available through the usual keystrokes
* Tab inserts indentation instead of leaving the field
* Autosize, and unsaved-change protection on navigation

## Done when

A description containing headings, lists, inline code, fenced code and links round-trips unchanged through save and reload.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: I2 — Markdown renderer and ticket reference chips
Description:
Renders stored markdown, and turns ticket identifiers written in the text into live chips — the inline references visible throughout `COS-177` today.

## Rendering

Markdown pipeline with sanitisation, GFM tables, fenced code with syntax highlighting, task lists. Styled with the `U2` tokens.

## Reference auto-linking

At render time, any token matching `[A-Z0-9]{2,5}-\d+` is resolved against **both** `identifier` and `legacyIdentifier`. On a hit it becomes a chip showing the state icon, the identifier and the title, linking to the issue. On a miss it stays plain text.

Resolving legacy identifiers matters more than it looks: every imported description is full of `COS-xxx` references written when that was the only scheme. They must render as working chips without rewriting a single description.

Resolution is batched — one lookup per render pass for all references on the page, not one query per token.

## Done when

An imported description containing several `COS-xxx` references renders them as working chips pointing at the renumbered issues, and an unknown identifier renders as plain text without erroring.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: I3 — Issue list layout grouped by status
Description:
The only layout in v1. Board layout is explicitly out of scope, and so is drag & drop.

## Structure

Collapsible group headers per status with the status icon, name and count, exactly like the screenshots. Rows underneath.

## Row

Identifier — with the legacy identifier beside it, subdued, when present — status icon, title, epic breadcrumb when the issue belongs to one, label chips, priority icon, date.

## Behaviour

* Row click opens the issue; the context menu changes status, priority, labels and epic inline
* Groups collapse and the state persists
* Long lists paginate or virtualise; PFA alone brings 147 issues

## Done when

The imported issues render grouped by status with correct counts, and inline status changes persist optimistically.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: I4 — Display properties and ordering
Description:
Linear's display popover, minus what v1 does not have.

## Scope

* Toggles for the columns shown on a row: identifier, status, priority, labels, created, updated
* Grouping: status, project, epic, priority, or none
* Ordering: priority, created, updated, manual
* Show/hide empty groups

## Persistence

These settings live in the URL alongside the filters, through the same nuqs serialiser as `V1`, so they are captured by a saved view and survive a reload or a shared link.

## Done when

Toggling a property updates the URL, survives a reload, and is captured when saving a view.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: I5 — Issue detail page and properties panel
Description:
Route `/issue/[identifier]`, resolving both the new and the legacy identifier.

## Layout

Copying the issue page in the screenshots: title and rendered description on the left, properties panel on the right.

## Header

The identifier, with the legacy one beside it when present — **PFA-12** `COS-177` — and the breadcrumb: project › epic › issue.

## Properties panel

Status, priority, labels, project, epic. Below it, the relations block (`E2`) and, for an epic, the contained issues (`E1`).

## Legacy URL handling

`/issue/COS-177` responds `301` to `/issue/PFA-12`. A pasted legacy URL from an old PR still lands on the right issue rather than 404ing.

## Done when

Both identifier forms resolve, the redirect works, and every property edits in place with an optimistic update.
