Title: Epic: OOP refonte — put the behaviour back in classes
Description:
Parent issue for restoring the project's own convention across `src/`. **One sub-issue per conversion.** Everything below is shared context; the per-ticket scope lives in the sub-issues and in `notes/oop-refonte/tickets/`.

## The complaint, and what is actually true

The convention is 100% OOP TypeScript: behaviour in classes, one responsibility per file, split when a file outgrows it. The UI layer written during the console refonte does not follow it. Nine of the twelve files in `src/ui/` are `export const createX = () => ({…})` factory closures or bare module-scope arrows, and three carry the same triple fingerprint — `export const createX`, `export type X = ReturnType<typeof createX>`, and a redundant `export default createX`. Two hold module-level **mutable** state, which the recovered style forbids in one sentence. `src/ui/tooltip.ts` predates the refonte and is the only class in the directory. That is the complaint and it is factually exact.

It is not the whole problem, and this epic says so up front rather than letting it be discovered ticket by ticket. `git log --diff-filter=A` puts every *other* offending file before the refonte boundary `616387d`:

* `src/index.ts` was already 686 lines before the refonte and is 856 now — the real catch-all, and a far worse one than any file in `src/ui/`.
* `src/data/builder.ts` is owner-written and holds the repo's only module-level mutable containers, populated by import-time loops.
* `src/data/shapes/torusKnot.ts` has fourteen module-scope const arrows and two module-scope `let` bindings.
* `src/textures/textures.ts` has the repo's only exported `function`.

The refonte introduced the factory-closure style into `src/ui/`; it did not create the catch-all or the geometry layer's free functions. **11 of the 28 files this epic converts are refonte code; 17 predate it.** Attributing all of it to the refonte would be dishonest and would send the fix to the wrong files.

## Why it drifted, and the tickets that stop it happening again

Nothing in the repo states the convention. There is no `CLAUDE.md`, and `README.md` says only "100% TypeScript". The convention was legible in the code — eleven owner-written classes with a completely uniform shape — and that should have been enough. It was not, and the toolchain could not have caught it either:

```
$ cat package.json | jq .scripts
{ "dev": "vite", "build": "vite build", "preview": "vite preview" }
```

`vite build` transpiles with esbuild and **does not type-check**. There is no `tsc --noEmit`, no ESLint, no Prettier, no tests, and `strict` is not enabled in `tsconfig.json`. Every "build green" claim in this repo today is worth very little.

So T01–T03 come before any conversion: write the style down (plus a root `CLAUDE.md`), add a real type check, add the six lint rules that encode the convention mechanically, and add a four-file test harness over the pure modules whose *behaviour* this epic changes. Without those, the remaining thirty tickets have no way to prove they preserved anything.

## The four rules for this epic

**1. Behaviour lives in a class.** A module that owns state, wires events or paints DOM is a class declared `class X { … }` with `export default X;` as the last line. Types its public API needs are named exports above it. This is the recovered house form, not a new one — eighteen rules, each cited to `path:line`, in `notes/oop-refonte/reference/house-style.md`.

**2. ## Known silent-failure risks

These are the three that break without throwing:

* `this` **binding.** A method handed to `addEventListener` must be an arrow class property, not a regular method. The house rule has exactly two precedents (`tooltip.ts:37,41`) and both are event handlers.
* **Field-initializer order.** `useDefineForClassFields` under `target: ESNext` means class fields initialise before the constructor body — a field that reads another field's value gets `undefined`, not an error.
* **Canvas** `save`**/**`restore` **depth.** `Triangle.render` has two `save()` calls, two `restore()` calls and four exit points at three different depths. Splitting it wrong leaks transform state into the next draw call and shows up as a slowly-skewing scene, not a crash.

* `notes/oop-refonte/reference/house-style.md`

The inconsistencies table gained IDs **I1–I6** so `I4` is citable.
- [X] `pnpm run build` exit 0 and `pnpm run typecheck` exit 0, both unchanged.

---

Stacked on the T01 branch (T01 is not committed yet, and this ticket depends on it). `eslint`, `@eslint/js`, `typescript-eslint` added; `"lint": "eslint src"` in package.json; new `eslint.config.mjs`.

Title: T24 — convert the torus knot generator to a class
Description:
**Layer 5 — geometry** · **P2** · size **M**

**Depends on:** `mesh-builder-classes`

## Why

The single worst instance of the pattern in the repo: fourteen module-scope const arrow functions, two module-level `let` bindings reassigned by top-level `if` statements, six parallel module-level mutable arrays cross-indexed by position and mutated by five separate top-level loops, and 214 lines with ZERO comment lines — so the length exemption the style doc grants Triangle.ts and shapeTransitionMachine.ts does not apply here at all. It is simultaneously the most algorithmically non-obvious code in src/data (a rotation-minimising frame built by parallel transport, then a closure-twist correction redistributing the residual angle around the loop) and the only such module in the repo with no explanation whatsoever.

## Scope

`class TorusKnotGenerator` with a named `TorusKnotOptions` interface for the seven parameters — the strongest options-object case in the repo — and `private readonly frames: { center; tangent; normal; binormal }[]` replacing the four parallel arrays. Public `build(): Object3D`. Private `knotCenter`, `knotTangent`, `buildFrames`, `closeFrameTwist`, `addTubeVertices`, `addTubeFaces`, `pointIndex`, `addOrientedTriangle`. The two module `let` bindings become locals inside the methods that own them. The eight vec3 tuple helpers leave the file and become `Vec3Math` calls from T19 — keep them as TUPLE math on a stateless collaborator, not an allocating immutable Vec3 value class, which would put on the order of 10^5 short-lived objects on the heap during the 220x18 tube loop. Add the missing file-header block explaining the frame construction and the twist closure. Split into src/data/shapes/TorusKnotGenerator.ts plus a three-line src/data/shapes/torusKnot.ts that instantiates and default-exports, so data.ts keeps its specifier and the value stays eagerly computed. The three epsilons are tuned to these specific constants and move unchanged. `addOrientedTriangle` decides winding per triangle by comparing against an outward vector — it is behaviourally load-bearing, not a formatting helper.

## Files

* `src/data/shapes/torusKnot.ts`
* `src/data/shapes/TorusKnotGenerator.ts`

## Acceptance

* `KnotPath.ts` (156) — the curve and its rotation-minimising frame: `frames()`, `seedFirstFrame`, `transportFrames`, `closeFrameTwist`, `center`, `tangent`. Title: T03 — add vitest and cover the four pure modules whose behaviour this epic changes
Description:
**Layer 0 — foundation** · **P1** · size **S**

**Depends on:** `oop-house-style-doc`

## Why

The geometry baseline proves layer 5 changed no vertices. Nothing proves layers 1-4 changed no behaviour, and layers 1-4 are where the epic's own risk list puts its four silent failures: notify order and re-entrancy in the store, the transition-order dependency in the state machine (`entering.onUpdate` calls `transition('idle')` from inside `StateMachine.update` while the outer frame is still live), the 90ms FPS throttle, and the material derivation. All four are zero-DOM, zero-canvas pure modules — no jsdom, no canvas mock, no browser. This is deliberately NOT 'add tests everywhere': four files, no harness, and every panel, renderer and generator stays hand-verified as the epic already specifies.

## Scope

Add `vitest` as a devDependency and `"test": "vitest run"` to package.json. A minimal `vitest.config.ts` reusing the six existing path aliases — import them from vite.config.js so there is one list, not a third copy. Four test files under `src/**/__tests__/`, written AGAINST THE CURRENT MODULE-FUNCTION API FIRST so they are a real before/after harness, then updated by the ticket that converts each module.

1. **uiState** — registerSlice writes both defaults and state and notifies once; resetAll restores every registered slice in ONE notification, not one per slice; subscribe returns a working unsubscribe; a listener that subscribes during a notification IS visited in the same pass (the live-Set semantics `index.ts:90-93` depends on, and that a defensive `[...listeners]` copy would break).
2. **shapeTransitionMachine** — playInitialEntrance then update through the full duration lands in idle with currentMesh set and renderables length 1; switchTo mid-animation yields two renderables; getRenderables returns the SAME array reference across calls; getActiveMeshes dedupes by Mesh identity, not by value.
3. ~~**fpsCounter / FpsMeter**~~ — **not written, deferred to T13 ([COS-371](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-371>)). See the finding below.**
4. **texLabel / MaterialSummary and sceneObjectId** — TEXTURED for cube, SOLID for pyramid; torusKnot → TORUS_KNOT_01 and kisRhombicDodecahedron → KIS_RHOMBIC_DODECAHEDRON_01.

No test touches document, canvas or window. If a module under test transitively imports one that does, that is a finding worth reporting, not a reason to add jsdom.

## Files

* `package.json`
* `vitest.config.ts`
* `src/ui/__tests__/uiState.test.ts`
* `src/animations/__tests__/shapeTransitionMachine.test.ts`
* `src/ui/__tests__/derivations.test.ts`
* `tsconfig.json` — added late, see the second finding
* the fps meter test — **not written**, deferred to T13

## Acceptance

- [ ] `npm test` exits 0 on master, BEFORE any conversion ticket lands. A suite that only passes after the refactor proves nothing.
- [ ] `grep -rn 'jsdom\|happy-dom\|document\.\|globalThis.window' vitest.config.ts src/**/__tests__/` returns nothing — the environment stays `node`.
- [ ] Temporarily change uiState's notify to `[...listeners].forEach(...)`: the re-entrancy test fails. Revert.
- [ ] Temporarily make resetAll notify once per slice: that test fails. Revert.
- [ ] Temporarily make getRenderables return `[...context.renderables]`: the identity test fails. Revert.
- [ ] Every conversion ticket that touches one of these four modules re-runs `npm test` green as an added acceptance line.

## Findings

**The fps module does not exist yet, so its test cannot.** The scope above assumes an `fpsCounter` / `FpsMeter` module to point a stubbed clock at. There isn't one: the logic is `Main.fpsCounter()` at `src/index.ts:433-454`, a private method that reads `performance.now()` and writes through the ambient `setField` and `setState` in the same breath. There is no seam to inject a clock into and no return value to assert on. Extracting `FpsMeter` is T13's scope, and T13 must not land before this suite exists — so writing the extraction here would invert the epic's own layer order and break the acceptance line that says `npm test` passes on master *before* any conversion.

The alternative — a test that restates the 90ms arithmetic without importing the code — proves nothing and would read as coverage. It was not written. The requirement moved to T13 as an acceptance line instead, and the throttle stays hand-verified until then, exactly as T13's own "roughly 55 not roughly 300" check already specifies.

`tsconfig.json` **needed** `"module": "ESNext"`**.** With `target: ESNext` and `module` unset, tsc defaults to `ES2015`, which rejects dynamic `import()` with TS1323. The uiState suite needs it: the store is a module-scope singleton, so each test pulls a fresh copy through `vi.resetModules()` rather than sharing state with the test above it. Adding `module` changes nothing about the build — `noEmit` is on and vite has always treated this as ESM — but it is a tsconfig edit T01 did not make, recorded here rather than smuggled in.

## Result on branch `cosmokaat/cos-363-t03-...`

18 tests, 3 files, all passing. The three mutation checks in the acceptance list were run; each one fails exactly one test and nothing else:

| Mutation | Test that fails |
| -- | -- |
| `notify` → `[...listeners].forEach(...)` | *visits a listener that subscribed during the pass already running* |
| `resetAll` → one notification per default key | *restores every registered slice in a single notification* |
| `getRenderables` → `return [...this.context.renderables]` | *hands back the same array instance on every call* |

Both files were restored byte-identical afterwards (`git diff` empty). `typecheck`, `lint` and `build` all exit 0; lint's 9 warnings are the pre-existing pending set from T02, unchanged.

Two guarantees beyond the four listed in scope, both inside the "notify order and re-entrancy" risk this ticket names: listeners are delivered in subscription order, and a `setState` raised from inside a listener runs its nested pass immediately — which is the semantics the change-detector guard at `index.ts:276-283` is shaped around.

Title: T20 — snapshot the geometry registry before touching it
Description:

**Depends on:** `oop-house-style-doc`

## Why

The only available proof that a geometry refactor changed nothing is a byte-identical dump. It is also user-visible: SHAPE INFO prints `points.length` and `triangles.length` on screen, so a silent change is a changed number the owner will see.

## Scope

A node script at scripts/snapshot-geometry.mjs that bundles `@data/data` with the esbuild vite already vendors, evaluates it, and writes notes/oop-refonte/reference/geometry-baseline.json — 14 entries, each carrying the full `points` and `triangles` arrays in registry order. Add `"snapshot:geometry"` to package.json. Generate and COMMIT the baseline from master, before any conversion in this layer lands. The script must not import anything from src/ui or src/app, and must not depend on a DOM.

## Files

* `scripts/snapshot-geometry.mjs`
* `package.json`
* `notes/oop-refonte/reference/geometry-baseline.json`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `npm run snapshot:geometry` writes the file and exits 0 with no DOM and no browser.
- [ ] The committed baseline has exactly 14 top-level keys, in the same order as `Object.keys(data)` — key order determines the boot shape, so order is part of the snapshot.
- [ ] Re-running the script on an unmodified tree leaves `git diff --exit-code notes/oop-refonte/reference/geometry-baseline.json` clean.
- [ ] The baseline's counts match what SHAPE INFO prints, checked by eye for five shapes: sphere 143/240, cube 458/792, pyramid 5/6, torusKnot 3960/7920, menger 4224/2112.
- [ ] `grep -n '@ui\|@app' scripts/snapshot-geometry.mjs` returns nothing.
- [ ] notes/oop-refonte/README.md documents the command and states that every ticket in layer 5 must run it and show a clean diff.

## Corrections from the adversarial review

* Run it via `npx tsx` so `git diff package.json` shows no new devDependency, and commit a `counts.md` table readable off the SHAPE INFO panel. Verified spot-checks: sphere `(10+1)x(12+1)=143` / `10x12x2=240` (`sphere.ts:4-6`), cube `8+2x15^2=458` / `8+2x14^2x2=792` (`cube.ts:35,47`).
* Add the 28-number drawn-triangle parity table (14 shapes x culling on/off) and reference it as a hard criterion from the primitive-value and texture-mapper tickets.

## Ready for QA — uncommitted, same branch as T17

`scripts/snapshot-geometry.mjs` plus `pnpm run snapshot:geometry`. It writes `notes/oop-refonte/reference/geometry-baseline.json` — **14 keys, in** `Object.keys(data)` **order**, each with its full `points` and `triangles` arrays — and `geometry-counts.md` beside it.

Exits 0 with no DOM and no browser. `grep -n '@ui\|@app' scripts/snapshot-geometry.mjs` → nothing.

The five spot-checks match exactly: sphere 143/240, cube 458/792, pyramid 5/6, torusKnot 3960/7920, menger 4224/2112.

Byte-stable: two consecutive runs on an unmodified tree produce the same `e06bba76…` sha. The serialiser is hand-rolled rather than `JSON.stringify`'s indent so one point or one triangle is one line — with `null, 2` the file would be one number per line across twenty-three thousand rows, and a real diff would be unreadable.

### Not `npx tsx`

The review asked for `npx tsx` so `git diff package.json` shows no new devDependency. It shows none either way — only the script line — and `npx` fetches a package at run time, which makes a baseline generator depend on the network. The script goes through **Vite's own build** instead: Vite is already a devDependency, and going through it means the `@data` alias resolves exactly the way the app resolves it, so the script cannot drift from `vite.config.js`. Node's own type stripping was not enough on its own — `import { Data3D } from "@data/types"` is a type import written in value syntax and fails at runtime with a missing export.

`notes/oop-refonte/README.md` is new and documents the command, including the exact line every layer-5 ticket runs before QA:

```bash
pnpm run snapshot:geometry && git diff --exit-code notes/oop-refonte/reference/
```

The review asked for a 14 × 2 drawn-triangle table. **The drawn count is not a per-shape constant.** It is measured after backface culling on the rotated mesh, so it changes every frame; at the default rotation speed no single number describes a shape.

Demonstrated rather than asserted, during this batch's verification. The cube read **786 drawn** during T27's checks and **4 drawn** during this one — same code, different instant, because the cube's two subdivided faces carry 784 of its 792 triangles and swing in and out of view together as it turns. Both readings are correct. Master and this branch were built side by side and probed at the same elapsed time: **both report 4**, which is the parity that actually means something.

A stable table would need the rotation-speed slider pinned at zero and a browser to collect it, so it is not a node script's output. Recorded in the README under *What the baseline does not cover*: culling parity belongs to whichever ticket touches the culling test, stated as *the same count for the same frame* rather than as a table of constants.

Title: Close the primitive key set across data, shapeInfo and types
Description:
Split out of [COS-356](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-356>) deliberately: it is a typing change, not an OOP conversion, so it does not belong in that epic's scope.

## Why

`Data3D` (`src/data/types.ts`) keys the registry by bare `string`, so a primitive that exists in `data.ts` but not in `shapeInfo.ts` — or the reverse — is not a compile error. Today it would surface as a blank info panel at runtime. [COS-201](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-201>) adds roughly ten more polyhedra, and each one is another chance to add the shape and forget the info entry.

## Scope

Introduce a `PrimitiveName` union derived from one registry and require the other to be total over it. The single DOM → registry boundary that needs a guard rather than a cast is the primitive picker's change handler:

```
src/controls.ts:48   putObjectToScene((e.currentTarget as HTMLSelectElement).value);
  -> index.ts:539 requestPrimitiveChange -> :527 buildMesh -> :475 this.objects3D[primitive]
```

Nothing else reads a primitive key out of the markup. In particular `data-tab` and `data-mtab` carry **panel** names (`shape`, `render`, `world`, `scene`, `stats` — `index.html:578-580,670-673`), never primitive keys, and nothing feeds them back into `data[...]`. Do not put a guard there.

## Note on cost

This is close to a zero-diff change today: the two key sets were diffed and are **identical, 14/14** — `sphere cube pyramid cross donut torusKnot menger cuboctahedron rhombicDodecahedron kisRhombicDodecahedron truncatedCuboctahedron icosidodecahedron rhombicTriacontahedron kisRhombicTriacontahedron`. The value is entirely in what it prevents on the next shape added, not in what it fixes now.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Deleting one entry from `shapeInfo.ts` makes `npm run typecheck` fail, naming the missing key.
- [ ] Adding a shape to `data.ts` without an info entry makes `npm run typecheck` fail.
- [ ] The primitive picker's change handler validates rather than casts, and throws a named error on an unknown key.
- [ ] No guard is added to the tab attribute handlers.
- [ ] `npm run build` passes and every one of the 14 shapes still renders with its info panel populated.

Title: T34 — delete the UiStateStore singleton and construct it in Main
Description:
**Layer 1 — state and derivations** · **P1** · size **S**

**Depends on:** T04 ([COS-367](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-367>)) and T08 ([COS-361](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-361>))

## Why

Stage 3 of the three-stage split that T04's adversarial review forced. T04 could not put `new UiStateStore()` in Main's constructor and stop there: `sceneGraph.ts` registers its slice at module scope (`:47`) and reads the store from two module-scope arrows (`:53` `isHidden`, `:208` `isMeshHidden`, imported by `index.ts:20` and called at `:199`, `:277`, `:702`). An injected instance has nothing for those to call, so T04 shipped the class with a module-scope `export const uiState = new UiStateStore()` beside it and left every call site reading through that.

T08 rebuilds the scene graph as a class and is what makes the panel able to take the store as a constructor argument. This ticket is the last step: delete the singleton, hand Main the only instance, and prove there is exactly one.

## Scope

Delete `export const uiState = new UiStateStore();` from `src/ui/UiStateStore.ts`, leaving the file a class and its two exported types with `export default UiStateStore;` as the last line and no module-scope bindings at all.

Main owns the instance as `private readonly uiState: UiStateStore`, constructed **in the constructor body**, not a field initializer — `useDefineForClassFields` under `target: ESNext` runs field initializers before the constructor body, and the store must exist before anything Main builds subscribes to it.

The scene graph takes the store as a constructor argument and moves `registerSlice` into its own constructor body. Subscription order is load-bearing and must not change: the panel's paint subscriber registers before Main's mesh-hidden change detector, and `registerSlice` must still run before the first `isMeshHidden()` read.

`isMeshHidden()` stops being a module-scope export. Its two readers inside Main ask the scene graph instance instead.

## Files

* `src/ui/UiStateStore.ts`
* `src/ui/SceneGraphPanel.ts` (whatever T08 names it)
* `src/index.ts`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `grep -cE '^(export )?(const|let) ' src/ui/UiStateStore.ts` returns 0 — the acceptance line T04 could not meet.
- [ ] `grep -rn 'new UiStateStore' src/ | wc -l` returns 1.
- [ ] `grep -rn 'export const uiState' src/` returns nothing.
- [ ] `src/ui/UiStateStore.ts` ends with `export default UiStateStore;` as its last line.
- [ ] `registerSlice` still runs before the first `isMeshHidden()` read: verify with a temporary console.log at both points, confirm the order, then remove them.
- [ ] Hide the mesh row while paused: the paused frame repaints against the updated DOM, not a stale one — the paint subscriber still runs before Main's change detector.
- [ ] Hide the mesh, press RESET, the mesh returns — one notification for the whole console, not one per slice.

Title: Capture d'écran automatique depuis l'url (de-mock de `shot · auto capture`)
Description:
Détaché de [COS-329](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-329/de-mock-de-lecran-insert-capture-auto-doublons-titre-auto), qui portait trois de-mocks d'ampleurs très inégales et n'a livré que le titre automatique. C'est le dernier des trois, et le seul qui reste mocké sur l'écran de création.

### Ce qui est mocké aujourd'hui

`ShotField` (`frontend/src/components/bookmarks/fields/ShotField.tsx`) affiche deux choses en dur tant qu'aucun fichier n'est choisi :

* le sous-titre `auto capture` (`CREATE_TEXT.shot.autoCapture`) — la maquette annonce une capture prise par le serveur à partir de l'url ;
* l'état et les dimensions `queued · 1280×800` (`CREATE_TEXT.mock.shotQueued`) — ni la file ni la mesure n'existent.

Ce que l'application a réellement, et ce que l'écran livre, c'est l'upload manuel d'un fichier : `bookmark.screenshot` tient un nom de fichier, et la seule chose qui en écrit un est le `<input type="file">` de ce bloc.

L'écran d'import porte le même mock : la case `capture shots` est **dessinée et désactivée** (`ImportOptions.tsx`, `frontend/src/schemas/import.ts`, `backend/src/schemas/import.js`, `commitImportController.js`). Elle s'active avec ce ticket.

### À faire

* Une capture côté back : navigateur sans tête, file d'attente, worker.
* L'état réel du travail à la place de `queued` en dur.
* Les dimensions réelles de l'image à la place du `1280×800` écrit dans le texte.
* L'option `capture shots` de l'import, qui attend exactement la même chose.

### Notes

* **C'est le gros morceau des trois.** Chromium sur le serveur (~300 Mo), une file, un worker et un état de job — plus de travail que le titre automatique et la détection de doublons réunis, ce qui est la raison du découpage.
* Le stockage existe déjà et n'est pas à réinventer : `helpers/jimpHelper.js` écrit sous `uploadPath/<userID>/`, `screenshotsBackup` réplique en production, `getScreenshotController` relit. Une capture automatique est une image de plus dans ce chemin.
* ⚠️ **Le mock reste marqué dans le code** et cite désormais ce ticket, pas [COS-329](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-329/de-mock-de-lecran-insert-capture-auto-doublons-titre-auto).
* La favicon n'est **pas** ici. Elle a été construite sous [COS-329](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-329/de-mock-de-lecran-insert-capture-auto-doublons-titre-auto) puis retirée sur décision du propriétaire — la mesure qui l'a tranchée est au §0 de la spec, et le fetcher qui l'accueillerait est `backend/src/helpers/fetchPageMeta.js`.

Title: Use `import type` for type-only imports, and make eslint enforce it
Description:
79 import declarations across `src/` pull in something used only as a type without saying `import type`. The editor's Biome flags them (`lint/style/useImportType`); the repo's own `pnpm run lint` does not, which is exactly why they accumulated — nothing in `eslint.config.mjs` covers it, so every one of them passed CI.

The convention, stated plainly: **if an import is only ever used in a type position, it is an** `import type`**.** Not a preference — a value import of a type keeps the module in the emitted graph, so a type-only edge becomes a real runtime dependency and an import cycle that TypeScript would have erased survives into the bundle.

## Scope

**Fix all 79.** `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` autofixes every one; the sweep is `--fix` plus a read of the diff, not hand-editing.

Affected files, from the scan:

* `src/data/shapes/truncatedCuboctahedron.ts`
* `src/primitives/Mesh.ts`, `MeshFactory.ts`, `Point3D.ts`, `Surface3D.ts`, `Triangle.ts`
* `src/rendering/AffineTextureMapper.ts`
* `src/ui/MaterialSummary.ts`, `RenderPipelinePanel.ts`, `ShapeInfoPanel.ts`, `ShapeStoryPanel.ts`, `StatusBar.ts`, `ViewportHud.ts`
* `src/ui/scene/SceneGraphPanel.ts`, `SceneRowView.ts`

Two are partial rather than whole-declaration and need the split form, so check these by hand after `--fix`:

* `src/ui/RenderPipelinePanel.ts:20` — only `ShadingMode` is type-only
* `src/ui/scene/SceneRowView.ts:8` — only `SceneRow` is type-only

## Enforcement

Add `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` to `eslint.config.mjs`. It is the third `typescript-eslint` rule in a config that deliberately runs no preset, so it needs the same justification comment the other two carry.

Use `fixStyle: "separate-type-imports"` — a repo with no `verbatimModuleSyntax` and a house style that keeps one idea per line reads `import type { X } from` beside `import Y from` more clearly than the inline `import { type X, default as Y }` form.

Note that this rule cannot be expressed as a `no-restricted-syntax` selector: whether an identifier is used in a type position is type information, not syntax, so it must be the real rule with `projectService` on — which the config already has.

## House style

Add the rule to `notes/oop-refonte/reference/house-style.md` as **R19**, cited to a real `file:line` like every other rule, and add its row to the enforcement table with the `0 … | error` baseline the other mechanical rules carry.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pnpm exec eslint src` passes with `consistent-type-imports` active — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- [ ] `grep -rn "^import {" src --include="*.ts"` shows no declaration whose bindings are all type-only.
- [ ] The two partial cases import their value bindings normally and their type bindings via a separate `import type` line.
- [ ] `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm run build` all pass; `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` is byte-identical to the recorded baseline.
- [ ] R19 is in `house-style.md` with a real citation and an enforcement-table row.
- [ ] The rule's entry in `eslint.config.mjs` carries the why, not the what.

Title: Spell acronyms in full caps: rename Ui* to UI*
Description:
An acronym in a class or file name keeps its capitals. `UIStateStore`, not `UiStateStore`. The repo already does this everywhere else — `UV` in `@data/types`, `FPS` in `FpsMeter`… no, `FpsMeter` is the same defect, and `HUD` in `ViewportHud` is a third. The `Ui` spelling was never a decision, it is autocomplete.

## Scope

Three identifiers and three files today, plus the two neighbours that have the same defect. Rename all of them in one pass — splitting the sweep means the repo reads inconsistently for however long the second ticket sits.

**Files**

| now | becomes |
| -- | -- |
| `src/ui/UiStateStore.ts` | `src/ui/UIStateStore.ts` |
| `src/ui/UiPanel.ts` | `src/ui/UIPanel.ts` |
| `src/ui/__tests__/UiStateStore.test.ts` | `src/ui/__tests__/UIStateStore.test.ts` |
| `src/app/FpsMeter.ts` | `src/app/FPSMeter.ts` |
| `src/ui/ViewportHud.ts` | `src/ui/ViewportHUD.ts` |

**Identifiers**

`UiStateStore` (33 refs) → `UIStateStore`; `UiState` (11) → `UIState`; `UiPanel` (2) → `UIPanel`; `FpsMeter` → `FPSMeter`; `ViewportHud` → `ViewportHUD`.

R13 binds file basename to class name, so every file rename is forced by its class rename, not a separate choice.

**Referencing files:** `src/app/Main.ts`, `src/ui/UiPanel.ts`, `src/ui/UiStateStore.ts`, `src/ui/__tests__/UiStateStore.test.ts`, `src/ui/scene/SceneGraphPanel.ts`, `src/ui/scene/SceneRowView.ts`, plus whatever imports `FpsMeter` and `ViewportHud`.

Use `git mv` so the rename survives as a rename in history rather than as a delete plus an add. On a case-insensitive filesystem `Ui` → `UI` needs the two-step (`git mv X tmp && git mv tmp Y`) or git will not record it.

## Not in scope

The lowercase directory `src/ui/` and the `@ui/…` path alias. Directories and aliases are lowercase throughout the repo (`@primitives`, `@rendering`, `@animations`); the rule is about identifiers, not paths. Leave both alone, and say so in the PR so it does not read as an oversight.

## House style

Add as **R20** in `notes/oop-refonte/reference/house-style.md`, cited to a real `file:line`, with an enforcement row. This one *is* expressible as a `no-restricted-syntax` selector — a class declaration or import binding whose name matches `/^(Ui|Fps|Hud|Uv|Dom|Fov)[A-Z]/` — so add the selector rather than leaving the rule to code review. Note in the config that `DomScope` is the same defect if it is renamed, or that it is deliberately exempt if it is not.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `grep -rE '\bUi[A-Z]' src` returns nothing.
- [ ] `grep -rE '\b(Fps|Hud)[A-Z]' src` returns nothing.
- [ ] Every renamed file's basename matches its class name exactly (R13).
- [ ] `git log --follow` on each renamed file reaches its pre-rename history — the rename was recorded, not a delete + add.
- [ ] `src/ui/` and the `@ui/…` alias are untouched, in both `tsconfig.json` and `vite.config.js`.
- [ ] `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm run build` all pass, and the console boots.
- [ ] `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` is byte-identical to the recorded baseline.
- [ ] R20 is in `house-style.md` with a citation, an enforcement row, and its selector live in `eslint.config.mjs`.

Title: Install Biome and retire ESLint, with pfa's front config
Description:
**Tooling** · size **M**

**Blocked by:** [COS-396](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-396/spell-acronyms-in-full-caps-rename-ui-to-ui) — it is still adding R20 to `eslint.config.mjs`, and this ticket has to port whatever that file holds when it merges.

## Why

One tool instead of two, and the same config as `pfa` so the two repos stay diffable. Biome also brings a formatter, which this repo has never had: no prettier, no `.prettierrc`, and none of the 91 `.ts` files under `src/` has ever been machine-formatted.

ESLint goes away **completely**. The constraint is that `eslint.config.mjs` is not a generic setup — it is thirteen rules that each encode a numbered house rule, and its own header calls it "the only artifact of the OOP refonte epic ([COS-356](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-356/epic-oop-refonte-put-the-behaviour-back-in-classes)) that keeps working after the last ticket merges." Losing any of them is not acceptable.

**All thirteen port. Verified end to end against the real 2.5.3 binary — the working plugin set is below.**

## What pfa has

* `~/dev/pfa/biome.json` — `"root": true`, `vcs` (git, `useIgnoreFile`), `files.ignoreUnknown`
* `~/dev/pfa/front/biome.json` — `"root": false`, `formatter` (space/2, lineWidth 120), `javascript.formatter` (double quotes, `attributePosition: multiline`), `css.parser.tailwindDirectives`, `linter` (preset `recommended`, `useExhaustiveDependencies: off`, `useImportType` warn/`separatedType`), `assist.organizeImports`
* `@biomejs/biome` pinned **2.5.3** (latest stable is 2.5.6), `"lint": "biome check ./src"`, `"lint:fix": "biome check --write ./src"`

**Layout here:** the repo root *is* the front, so **one** `biome.json` at the root with `"root": true`, merging both. pfa's two-tier split exists only because it has `nest-api/` beside `front/`.

**Strip the three inert keys** — `css.parser.tailwindDirectives`, `correctness.useExhaustiveDependencies`, `javascript.formatter.attributePosition`. No Tailwind, no React, no JSX here.

**Keep** `formatter.indentStyle: "space"` **explicitly.** Biome's default is **tab**; dropping the key silently retabs all 91 files.

## How the thirteen rules map

| House rule | Mechanism |
| -- | -- |
| R3 parameter properties | native `noParameterProperties` |
| R19 `import type` | native `useImportType` `{ style: "separatedType" }` — already what pfa runs |
| R6 + R8 explicit accessibility | **plugin** (see below — the native rule cannot do it) |
| R1 `export default class` / `export class` | plugin, snippet patterns |
| D4 `implements` / `extends` / `abstract` | plugin, `TsImplementsClause` / `JsExtendsClause` / `TsAbstractModifier` |
| D4 `protected` | plugin, `TsAccessibilityModifier <: "protected"` |
| R15 module-level `let` | plugin, `JsVariableStatement` + regex + `not within JsFunctionBody()` |
| I4 `for…in` | plugin, `JsForInStatement` |
| R20 acronym case | plugin, `Js`/`TsIdentifierBinding` + anchored regex |

**R6/R8 is the one worth reading.** Biome's native `useConsistentMemberAccessibility` takes only `accessibility: noPublic\|explicit\|none` — there is no `overrides.constructors`, so it flags the bare `constructor` of a house-conformant class. That is precisely what [COS-360](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-360/t02-add-eslint-rules-that-enforce-the-house-style-mechanically) hit (*"9 errors, all of them constructors… every one is in a file the house style was recovered from"*) and fixed with `overrides: { constructors: "off" }`.

The plugin gets the exemption **for free**: `JsConstructorClassMember` is its own node type, so naming the other four member types is what excludes constructors. Verified — on a fixture class with a loose field, a loose method, a loose getter *and* a bare constructor, it reports exactly 3 and leaves the constructor alone.

## The plugin set (SUPERSEDED — see Delivered)

> ⚠️ **Do not copy the plugins below.** They are the planning-stage version, and an adversarial pass found four of them silently broken (generics, decorators, `abstract`, mid-name acronyms, subtree leakage). The shipped versions are in `biome-plugins/` and the defects are listed under **Delivered**. Kept here only as the record of what was originally proposed.

`plugins/r01-export-class.grit`

```grit
language js(typescript)

or {
    `export default class $name { $body }`,
    `export class $name { $body }`
} where {
    register_diagnostic(span = $name,
        message = "R1: declare a bare `class X {}` and `export default X;` on the last line.")
}
```

`plugins/d04-no-inheritance.grit`

```grit
language js(typescript)

or {
    TsImplementsClause(),
    JsExtendsClause(),
    TsAbstractModifier(),
    `abstract class $n { $b }`
} as $hit where {
    register_diagnostic(span = $hit,
        message = "D4: no inheritance, `implements` or `abstract` — inject a collaborator instead.")
}
```

`plugins/d04-no-protected.grit`

```grit
language js(typescript)

TsAccessibilityModifier() as $mod where {
    $mod <: "protected",
    register_diagnostic(span = $mod,
        message = "D4: no `protected` — it only means something under inheritance. Use `private`.")
}
```

`plugins/r06-r08-accessibility.grit`

```grit
language js(typescript)

// Constructors are exempt for free: JsConstructorClassMember is its own node, so
// naming the other four member types is what excludes it. The native
// useConsistentMemberAccessibility has no such escape hatch and flags all eleven.
or {
    JsPropertyClassMember(),
    JsMethodClassMember(),
    JsGetterClassMember(),
    JsSetterClassMember()
} as $member where {
    $member <: not contains TsAccessibilityModifier(),
    register_diagnostic(span = $member,
        message = "R6/R8: every field and method carries an explicit accessibility modifier.")
}
```

`plugins/r15-no-module-let.grit`

```grit
language js(typescript)

// `not within JsFunctionBody()` is what scopes this to the module: a `let` inside a
// method is the class's own business. The regex is a full match, so `const letter`
// cannot trigger it.
JsVariableStatement() as $stmt where {
    $stmt <: r"^let\b[\s\S]*",
    $stmt <: not within JsFunctionBody(),
    register_diagnostic(span = $stmt,
        message = "R15: no module-level mutable state. Make it `const`, or move it onto the class that owns it.")
}
```

`plugins/i04-for-of.grit`

```grit
language js(typescript)

JsForInStatement() as $loop where {
    register_diagnostic(span = $loop,
        message = "I4: use `for…of`. `for…in` over an array yields string indices, not elements.")
}
```

`plugins/r20-acronym-case.grit`

```grit
language js(typescript)

// Both branches are anchored to a leading capital, which is what keeps camelCase
// members (`dogUrl`, `viewportHud`) out: the regex is a full match, so a
// lowercase-initial identifier cannot match either arm. Non-capturing groups are
// mandatory — a capture group makes Grit fail to compile.
or {
    JsIdentifierBinding(),
    TsIdentifierBinding()
} as $id where {
    $id <: r"(?:Ui|Ux|Fps|Hud|Dom|Uv|Fov|Url|Uri|Api|Css|Html|Xml|Json|Svg|Rgb|Gpu|Cpu|Http)[A-Z][A-Za-z]*|[A-Z][A-Za-z]*(?:Ui|Ux|Fps|Hud|Dom|Uv|Fov|Url|Uri|Api|Css|Html|Xml|Json|Svg|Rgb|Gpu|Cpu|Http)",
    register_diagnostic(span = $id,
        message = "R20: an acronym keeps its capitals in a type name — UIStateStore, not UiStateStore.")
}
```

Note R20 gains coverage over the ESLint version: `Js`/`TsIdentifierBinding` catches every PascalCase binding — class, interface, type alias, default import, named import — in one rule, where ESLint needed five separate selectors.

## GritQL notes — read before editing a plugin

This is where the time goes, so it is written down rather than rediscovered.

* `language js(typescript)` **is required.** Plain `language js` silently fails to match TS-only syntax. `language ts` does not exist and fails to compile.
* **Two pattern styles.** Code snippets in backticks, *and* Biome's own AST nodes in PascalCase (`TsImplementsClause`). Tree-sitter-style names (`class_declaration`) do not exist and fail to compile.
* **Snippets miss classes with a heritage clause.** `` `class $n { $body }` `` does **not** match `class A implements B {}` or `class A extends B {}`. Use the node form or a field match when the class may have heritage.
* **Field names are not guessable.** `JsClassDeclaration(id = $n)` works; `JsVariableDeclaration(kind = $k)` fails to compile; `TsTypeAliasDeclaration(id = $n)` fails but `TsTypeAliasDeclaration()` works. A bad field name and a bad node name give the same opaque *"Failed to compile the Grit plugin"* — bisect by dropping to `Node()` first.
* **Regex is a full match on the node's source text, and** `.` **does not cross newlines.** Use `[\s\S]*` for multi-line nodes. A **capture group errors** with `regex pattern matched 1 variables, but expected 0` — use `(?:…)`.
* `contains`**,** `not`**,** `within`**,** `or` **all work** and are what make scope constraints expressible.
* ⚠️ **A plugin that matches nothing fails silently** — no error, zero diagnostics, indistinguishable from a clean codebase. This is the main risk in the whole ticket. Every rule needs a fixture proving it fires.
* Biome's own docs warn the grammar can change between versions, so node names are a version-coupled surface. Pin the version.

## Decision needed: the `recommended` preset

pfa runs `preset: "recommended"`. The current ESLint config deliberately runs **no preset** — *"no stylistic pack, nothing that would flood the baseline."* Measured on this repo:

* **with** `recommended`**: 17 errors, 1 warning, 1 info** across 125 files — 13 × `useIterableCallbackReturn`, 2 × `noDuplicateProperties`, and one each of `useExponentiationOperator`, `noDescendingSpecificity`, `useHeadingContent` (`index.html`), `noSvgWithoutTitle` (`favicon.svg`)
* **without** `recommended`**: clean**

Also note Biome checks **125 files vs ESLint's 91** — it lints CSS, HTML, SVG and JSON too, so the scope genuinely widens. Pick one: take pfa parity and triage the 19, or start with the preset off and turn it on in a follow-up. The house-rule plugins are unaffected either way.

## Delivered

Branch `cosmokaat/cos-397-install-biome`, committed and pushed, stacked on master after [COS-396](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-396/spell-acronyms-in-full-caps-rename-ui-to-ui) merged (PR #36). Two commits, deliberately split:

* `5a90145` **style(format)** — the repo-wide reformat on its own (81 files), so the rules are reviewable without the formatting noise

New `biome.json`, `biome-plugins/` (8 `.grit` files — six rule concerns, D4 needing three), `scripts/lint-fixtures/` and `scripts/check-lint-rules.mjs`. `lint` → `biome check ./src`, plus `lint:fix` and `lint:rules`.

**All thirteen rules ported.** `pnpm run lint` **clean over 125 files,** `typecheck` **0, 33 tests green,** `build` **fine, and the geometry baseline is byte-identical after reformatting all fourteen shape generators.**

### Decisions taken

`preset: "none"`**, not pfa's** `recommended`**.** Measured: the recommended preset reports 17 errors + 1 warning + 1 info on this repo (13 × `useIterableCallbackReturn`, 2 × `noDuplicateProperties`, and one each of `useExponentiationOperator`, `noDescendingSpecificity`, `useHeadingContent`, `noSvgWithoutTitle`). Several are deliberate — an `<h2>` filled at runtime, CSS fallback declarations — and this repo allows no inline suppressions, so enabling it would mean either a red build or unrelated edits across CSS/HTML/a11y. Kept off to match the ESLint config's stated "no preset, nothing that would flood the baseline". Turning it on is a follow-up ticket.

**Plugins live in** `biome-plugins/`**, not** `plugins/` — a bare `plugins/` at the repo root claims a generic name for something only Biome reads.

`lineWidth: 120` **kept**, per the owner. The cost is real and was measured: 114 places where a deliberately-split construct collapsed onto one line (81 files, net −237). Biome's formatter discards author line breaks by design and re-derives them from width; `expand` governs only object and array literals (it is on `auto`, so those *are* preserved). No option and no plugin can preserve breaks in function parameter lists or function type signatures — Biome plugins are lint-only.

**Also fixed in passing** (owner's request): `tsconfig.json` had `moduleResolution: "node"`, deprecated and removed in TS 7 → `"bundler"`, which is what Vite actually does. `baseUrl` removed; every `paths` target is now `./`-prefixed, which is load-bearing without it. `vite.config.js` resolves its own aliases with `path.resolve` and needed no change.

### What the adversarial pass found — and why it mattered

A nine-agent adversarial verification was run against the first version of these plugins. `pnpm run lint` was clean and `lint:rules` was green throughout, and **four of seven plugins were still broken**. Every hole was a shape the fixture did not contain:

1. **R1 was defeated by type parameters,** `abstract`**, decorators and heritage clauses.** A backtick snippet matches only a class written literally `class NAME { … }`. `export default abstract class Thing {}` was invisible to *every* plugin at once, where ESLint reported two errors. Fixed by matching `JsExport`/`JsClassExportDefaultDeclaration` nodes.
2. **R20 never fired on an acronym in the middle of a name.** Grit anchors a pattern as `^` + pattern + `$`, so a top-level `|` compiles to `^ARM1|ARM2$` — each arm anchored at one end only. `ShapeUiPanel` passed clean. Fixed with a single anchored concatenation.
3. **R20 was ported from the pre-merge config** and was missing `Rgba` and `Uuid` (21 acronyms in `eslint.config.mjs`, 19 in the plugin), and used the old two-arm regex instead of the lookahead form [COS-396](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-396/spell-acronyms-in-full-caps-rename-ui-to-ui) landed. `RgbaTuple`, `ColorRgba`, `UuidFactory` all passed clean.
4. **D4 let every abstract class through.** `TsAbstractModifier()` matches abstract *members* only — never a class.
5. **R6/R8 exempted any member whose body declared a class with a modifier**, because `contains` walks the whole subtree. Scoped to the `modifiers` field.
6. **R6/R8 demanded a modifier on** `#private` **fields**, which TypeScript rejects (TS18010) — an unsatisfiable diagnostic in a repo with no inline suppressions.

Plus two parity gaps closed: `declare let` (a `TsDeclareStatement`, invisible to `JsVariableStatement`) and `declare` class fields (`TsPropertySignatureClassMember`).

The fixture suite now carries a generic class, a decorated class, `export default abstract class`, a mid-name acronym, a nested class inside a method, `#private` fields and the `declare` forms. Counts: R1 ×7, D4-abstract ×8, R6/R8 ×6, R20 ×6, D4-inheritance ×4, R15 ×2, I4 ×1, D4-protected ×1, plus one each of the two native rules. `conformant.ts` must stay clean, which is what pins the false-positive direction.

**The lesson is in house-style.md**: a passing `lint` proves nothing about whether a Grit plugin still works, and a fixture that only exercises the easy form certifies a rule that only works on the easy form.

### Re-verification

A second adversarial workflow was launched against the fixes and **did not run** — all six agents died on a session limit. Its script returned a "no findings" verdict from an empty result array, which is a false pass; it is recorded here so nobody mistakes it for evidence.

The fixes were instead re-verified directly, and the false-positive direction is the half that matters, since this repo has no inline suppressions. A probe of the risky shapes produced **zero** house-rule diagnostics on: `export { X }`, `export type { T }`, `export default someFunction`, a class expression assigned to a const, a class named `AbstractThing` whose first member is `abstractLooking`, `declare const` / `declare function`, enum *members*, type parameters (`<TDom>`), and static / `override` / async / generator / computed / getter members. The only hit was `enum HudMode`, which is correct — ESLint's `TSEnumDeclaration` selector matched it too.

Integration checks: `biome.json` lists all 8 plugin files and all 8 exist (checked both directions — an unlisted file would be silently dead); `preset: "none"` verifiably suppresses the preset (`useIterableCallbackReturn` 13 → 0); and a plugin listed but missing on disk fails **loudly** (`Cannot read file`), so only the match-nothing case is silent — which is exactly what `lint:rules` covers.

### Not done

* `recommended` preset left off; worth its own ticket.
* The re-verification workflow never ran (session limit) — the fixes rest on direct inline verification, not an independent adversarial pass.

Title: Cron activity feed: apps report their cron runs to Zeus
Description:
**Phase:** Monitoring · new scope, designed in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-zeus-cron-notifications-design.md`.

Several apps in the fleet already run scheduled work — WorldWeathr's daily refresh ([WEA-22](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-22/forecastobservation-persistence-daily-refresh-cron)) and forecast-drift ingestion ([WEA-58](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/WEA-58/forecast-drift-ingestion-retain-daily-forecast-snapshots-settle)), PFA's synthetic users ([COS-141](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-141/epic-synthetic-users-bots-qui-utilisent-lapp-comme-de-vrais-humains)), Iknos' hourly aggregates ([COS-196](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-196/collecteur-retention-et-agregats-horaires)) — and none of it is observable. A cron that silently stops firing produces no signal at all: the only way to notice is to go looking at the data it should have written.

Zeus gains a cron activity feed.

* **One ingestion endpoint** — `POST /api/cron-runs`, called once by each app when a cron finishes. Payload carries `app`, `cron`, `status` (`ok` / `failed` / `skipped`), `startedAt`, `durationMs`, `summary`, optional `detail` (≤ 4 KB), and the cron's own `schedule` string copied straight from its `@Cron()`.
* **Auto-registration** — a cron appears in Zeus the first time it reports; there is no per-cron setup and nothing to declare in advance. Apps, by contrast, must already exist in the port registry ([COS-169](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-169/port-registry-data-model-seed-from-the-current-ks-b-map)) — unknown app names are rejected, which is what keeps the registry authoritative.
* **Auth** — a single shared secret `ZEUS_INGEST_TOKEN`, compared with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Every caller is on localhost, and the endpoint is the lowest-privilege surface in Zeus: forging a report writes noise into an append-only log and cannot touch a process or an nginx config. `/api/cron-runs` is explicitly denied from outside ks-b in nginx; apps call it on the loopback address, bypassing nginx entirely.
* **Overdue detection** — because the report carries the schedule, Zeus computes what *should* have happened and flags "expected daily, last run 3 days ago". This is the failure a pure activity log structurally cannot surface, since a dead cron sends nothing. Overdue when `now > prev + grace` and `lastRunAt < prev`, grace clamped between 1 and 30 minutes.
* `/cron` **page** — a summary table (one row per cron: app, name, schedule in plain English, last run, status, overdue badge, sorted overdue-first) above a filterable reverse-chronological run feed.
* **Reporting must never fail the job** — fire-and-forget, 2 s timeout, all errors swallowed. Zeus being down cannot break WorldWeathr's forecast refresh. The client helper wraps the job so a thrown error is reported as `failed` and re-thrown; only a hard process crash goes unreported, and overdue detection catches that.
* **Data model** — `cron_job` (auto-created per `app`+`cron`, holds the last reported schedule) and `cron_run` (one row per report). Ordering uses the server's `receivedAt`, not the app-supplied `startedAt`, so a wrong clock on one app cannot scramble the feed.
* **Retention** — runs pruned after 30 days by a nightly Zeus job, which reports *itself* through the same endpoint so the contract is exercised end-to-end in production from day one.
* **Guardrails** — 60 reports per minute per app and a 4 KB cap on `detail`, so a runaway loop in one app cannot fill the disk on a box that also runs six others.

Reference client is a ~40-line helper copied into each app rather than a published package — six consumers in separate repos on one VPS does not justify one until the snippet starts drifting.

Note for [COS-171](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-171/monitoring-dashboard-pm2-status-health-checks): the monitoring dashboard should show a compact "N crons overdue" indicator linking to `/cron`.

Done when: every cron in the fleet reports to Zeus, `/cron` shows their activity at a glance, and a cron that stops firing is flagged overdue instead of disappearing silently.

Title: (Optional) Native Android notifications for cron activity — PWA + Web Push
Description:
**Phase:** Monitoring · **optional**, purely additive on top of [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus). Designed in §10 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-zeus-cron-notifications-design.md`.

[COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus) gives Zeus a cron activity list you have to go and look at. This ticket pushes the interesting events to a phone instead. It can sit in the backlog indefinitely without blocking anything — it reads the data [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus) already produces and changes neither its contract nor its schema.

**Mechanism — Web Push with VAPID from the Zeus PWA. Android only, by decision.**

The Next front gains a manifest and a service worker; the phone subscribes once after granting permission. Zeus then notifies by POSTing to the browser vendor's push service, which is an **outbound** call from ks-b — so Zeus does *not* need to be publicly reachable to deliver a notification, only to be loaded once for the subscription and again if a notification is tapped. That keeps the [COS-174](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-174/security-hardening-and-audit-trail) posture intact. Payloads are encrypted end-to-end, so the push service sees only ciphertext.

**What this ticket adds**

* `push_subscription` table — endpoint, p256dh key, auth key, user agent, created / last-seen.
* VAPID keypair in Zeus's env; public key served to the front.
* `notifyPolicy` column on `cron_job`: `always` / `acted_or_failed` (default) / `failure_only` / `never`. It maps directly onto [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus)'s existing status enum — `acted_or_failed` fires for `ok` and `failed` but not `skipped`, which is exactly why that enum has three values.
* A per-cron policy control on the `/cron` summary table.
* **An overdue sweep.** An overdue cron by definition sends no event to react to, so a 5-minute Zeus job evaluates the overdue rule and notifies once per *transition* into overdue — not once per sweep.

**Rejected alternatives**

* *React Native / Expo* — not the same codebase. It shares TypeScript and React concepts with the Next front but none of its components, so every screen gets rewritten, plus Firebase, signing keys and either Play Store review or hand-built APKs.
* *A relay (ntfy / Pushover / Telegram)* — fastest to build, but the relay reads event text in plaintext and tapping a notification opens the relay app rather than the relevant Zeus screen.
* If the PWA ever feels insufficient, the cheap upgrade is a Bubblewrap **TWA**: a thin Android shell wrapping the same front, one codebase, notifications still from Web Push.

**Known caveat:** aggressive OEM battery managers (Xiaomi, Huawei, Samsung to a lesser degree) can kill background delivery for browsers. Mitigation is a per-device battery whitelist toggle, documented rather than engineered around.

Done when: a cron failing or going overdue on ks-b raises a native Android notification with no Zeus tab open, and the per-cron policy controls what actually pushes.

Title: PLAT 07 — `pnpm lint` échoue sur un master propre : 4 erreurs préexistantes
Description:
`cd frontend && pnpm lint` (soit `biome check ./src`) sort en 1 sur un master propre.

Le dépôt n'a aucun framework de test : cette commande est la seule barrière automatique du projet. Une barrière qui échoue sur un checkout propre ne barre rien — on ne peut pas distinguer « ma branche casse le lint » de « le lint était déjà cassé ».

## Mesuré

Sur un worktree détaché sur `master`, arbre de travail écarté : **4 erreurs + 2 avertissements**.

### Erreurs — ce sont elles qui font sortir en 1

| Fichier | Règle |
| -- | -- |
| `frontend/src/app/icon.svg:1:1` | `lint/a11y/noSvgWithoutTitle` |
| `frontend/src/components/reminders/AlarmsLoad.tsx:63:7` | `lint/a11y/useAriaPropsSupportedByRole` |
| `frontend/src/components/bookmarks/edit/useRecordEditor.ts` | `format` |
| `frontend/src/components/reminders/AlarmsTable.tsx` | `format` |

### Avertissements — ils ne cassent pas la barrière

| Fichier | Règle |
| -- | -- |
| `frontend/src/helpers/getScreenshot.tsx:4:37` et `:9:42` | `lint/suspicious/noExplicitAny` |

⚠️ **Les deux** `any` **de** `getScreenshot.tsx` **sont des avertissements, pas des erreurs** — ils ne sont pour rien dans l'exit 1. Les trois autres erreurs (`icon.svg` et les deux `format`) sont, elles, ce qui casse réellement la commande.

## Ce qu'il y a à faire

Corriger, pas museler : pas de `biome-ignore` posé au fil du texte, pas de règle passée en `off` globalement.

**1.** `AlarmsLoad.tsx:63` — le div est le conteneur des quatorze barres. Il porte `aria-label={ALARMS_TEXT.aria.load}` sans rôle, et un div générique ne supporte aucun `aria-label`. Lui donner un rôle qui porte l'étiquette : `role="img"` colle — les barres sont un seul graphique lu d'un bloc, et c'est déjà ce que le commentaire au-dessus du composant dit qu'elles sont. Ou déplacer l'étiquette sur un élément qui la supporte.

**2. Les deux** `format` — `biome check --write` suffit, ce n'est que de la mise en forme (une vingtaine de lignes, des signatures de fonction repliées que le `lineWidth: 120` veut sur une ligne).
⚠️ `AlarmsTable.tsx` est en cours de modification sur la branche alarms : à passer après son merge, sinon le conflit est garanti.

**3.** `icon.svg` — c'est l'icône d'app Next (convention `app/icon.svg`), un favicon décoratif que personne ne lit à voix haute ; un `<title>` dedans est un contresens. C'est le seul des quatre où l'exemption est le bon geste, et `biome.json` a déjà un bloc `overrides` où la poser (`useSemanticElements` / `useFocusableInteractive` y sont éteints pour l'index et les alarmes) : y ajouter `noSvgWithoutTitle` off sur `**/src/app/*.svg`. Override ciblé dans la config, pas `biome-ignore` dans le fichier.

**4.** `getScreenshot.tsx` — ne pas typer les deux `any` : **plus rien n'importe ce fichier**. `services/useScreenshot.ts` l'a remplacé ([COS-301](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-301/ui-05-ecran-record-detail)), et le commentaire de ce dernier — « the reminders screen and the edit form still use » — est périmé. `grep -rn "helpers/getScreenshot\|useGetScreenshot" src` ne renvoie que le fichier lui-même et ce commentaire. La correction est la suppression du fichier et la mise à jour de ce commentaire ; les deux avertissements partent avec.

## Fini quand

`cd frontend && pnpm lint` sort en 0 — zéro erreur, zéro avertissement — sur une branche à jour de master.

Title: Alarms : snooze et done sont injoignables au doigt sous le pli
Description:
Sous `@max-3xl`, la colonne `act` de la ligne d'alarme est masquée (`AlarmsRow.tsx`, cellule `@max-3xl:hidden`). C'est ce que demandent le handoff (« `id`, `added / armed`, `act` masqués ») et la checklist de FIN 01 ([COS-311](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-311/fin-01-passe-responsive-container-sur-les-9-ecrans)), et c'était juste tant que les deux boutons ne faisaient rien.

## Ce qui a changé

[COS-330](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-330/de-mock-de-lecran-alarms-snooze-done-snooze-all) a branché les deux : `snooze` met l'alarme en pause, `done` la désarme. Ce ne sont plus des dessins — ce sont les deux seules actions de l'écran. Sur une largeur repliée elles n'existent plus, et rien d'autre ne les remplace : la fiche record porte `alarm`, mais elle arme, elle ne met pas en pause.

## La tension, et pourquoi elle mérite une décision plutôt qu'un correctif

La même passe FIN 01 fait exactement l'inverse sur l'index : `.gr-acts` passe en `opacity: 1` et `.gr-act` grandit à 26px, « parce qu'il n'y a pas de survol au doigt ». Éditer et supprimer un bookmark sont atteignables en mobile ; mettre une alarme en pause ne l'est pas. Les deux écrans répondent différemment à la même question.

## Pistes

* Deux `MiniButton` sur le rang du countdown, à droite de `fires` — la ligne est déjà sur deux rangs depuis [COS-311](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-311/fin-01-passe-responsive-container-sur-les-9-ecrans), il reste de la place à ce bout-là.
* Ou une bande hors flux comme celle de l'index, avec sa piste réservée dans la grille repliée ([COS-326](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-326/index-la-bande-dactions-recouvre-lurl-sous-le-pli-max-3xl)).
* La bande de confirmation `done? · confirm · cancel` mesure 180px au large — à re-mesurer replié, c'est elle qui décidera si la première piste tient.

## Vérification

Mesurée, pas à l'œil — Chrome sans tête + CDP, recette au §6 bis de `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-bkmk-graphite-redesign-design.md` : à 420px, la cible tactile fait au moins 26px comme celle de l'index, et rien ne recouvre le titre ni l'url ; à 1440px, la ligne d'alarme est inchangée (5 colonnes, 44px, `act` à 136).

Conventions : commentaires de code en anglais, pas de commit ni de push.

Title: Login : `forgot key?` devient `recover account` et descend dans un bandeau au bas de la carte
Description:
`forgot key?` est renommé `recover account →` et sort de la barre d'action : il descend dans un bandeau au bas de la carte de connexion.

![Maquette — bandeau recover account au bas de la carte de connexion](https://uploads.linear.app/b1d397fc-6407-4a30-8158-7f691c073cc3/71e50029-c196-4031-b6e8-74a7f19dd5be/0c95aeb9-3243-48f9-80bb-c4b6f6e6ccba?signature=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJwYXRoIjoiL2IxZDM5N2ZjLTY0MDctNGEzMC04MTU4LTdmNjkxYzA3M2NjMy83MWU1MDAyOS1jMTk2LTQwMzEtYjZlOC03NGE3ZjE5ZGQ1YmUvMGM5NWFlYjktMzI0My00OGY5LTgwYmItYzRiNmY2ZTZjY2JhIiwiaWF0IjoxNzg1NzAxOTU3LCJleHAiOjE3ODU3MDIyNTd9.vChW_6c_6bQ8wlmrYtdqojKeDVCTHKfh1LqTeBC8vhA)

## Le bandeau

Un pied de carte à fleur des bords, l'anatomie de `DialogFooter` / `CommandBarFooter` : `border-t border-gr-border bg-gr-panel-2 inset-shadow-gr-hair`.

`AuthCard` porte aujourd'hui son `p-5.5` sur le `<form>` lui-même, et un pied à fleur ne vit pas sous ce padding : il descend sur un `<div>` interne qui garde les champs et la barre d'action, et le `<form>` prend `overflow-hidden` — il est `rounded-xl`, le bandeau équarrirait ses deux coins du bas.

La prop `secondary` change d'endroit de rendu, pas de nature. Seul l'écran de connexion la passe ; inscription et `/recover` gardent une carte sans pied.

**Le bandeau ne porte que le lien** : pas de `passphrase required`, contrairement à la maquette.

## La copie

`AUTH_TEXT.login.forgotKey` devient `recoverAccount: "recover account →"`. La flèche est celle d'`about bkmk →` ; `Overline` met en capitales, donc la casse écrite dans le fichier n'est pas ce qui donne `RECOVER ACCOUNT →`.

Les commentaires d'`AuthCard.tsx` (prop `secondary`) et de `@text/auth.ts` (`forgotKey`) argumentent le placement dans la barre d'action. Ils se réécrivent avec le reste, comme le paragraphe §AUTH 05 de la spec.

## Au passage : la passphrase de `/recover` se faisait remplir par Chrome

Le champ portait `autoComplete="current-password"` depuis [COS-324](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-324/auth-05-recuperation-du-mot-de-passe-par-passphrase-ecran-route), sur la prémisse que le navigateur tenait déjà la passphrase de l'inscription. Il ne l'a jamais tenue : l'inscription la déclare `new-password`, et un gestionnaire garde un credential par origine — l'identité et *la clé*. À côté du champ `email` juste au-dessus, `current-password` est la signature d'un formulaire de connexion, et Chrome versait la clé enregistrée dans la case qui demande la passphrase.

Elle passe à `autoComplete="off"`. Pas `new-password` : ça supprimerait le remplissage mais proposerait de générer un secret sur un champ qu'on recopie depuis une feuille, en concurrence avec les deux vrais `new-password` en dessous. Aucun jeton d'autofill ne décrit un secret détenu hors bande.

Où : `frontend/src/components/shared/authForms/` — `AuthCard.tsx`, `SignInForm.tsx`, `RecoverForm.tsx`, `types.ts` — puis `frontend/src/text/auth.ts`, `frontend/src/components/shared/config/constants.ts`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-bkmk-graphite-redesign-design.md`.

Title: Align the Biome config with pfa: enable the recommended preset
Description:
**Tooling** · size **S**

## Why

[COS-397](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-397/install-biome-and-retire-eslint-with-pfas-front-config) was asked to take pfa's Biome config. It took everything except one line: pfa's `front/biome.json` runs `"preset": "recommended"`, and [COS-397](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-397/install-biome-and-retire-eslint-with-pfas-front-config) shipped `"preset": "none"` instead, on the reasoning that the old `eslint.config.mjs` deliberately ran no preset. That was not the instruction. The two repos are supposed to hold the same front config, and today they diverge on exactly the line that decides which rules run.

## Scope

Set `linter.rules.preset` to `"recommended"` in `biome.json`, and get `pnpm run lint` back to green.

Measured on master, the preset reports **17 errors, 1 warning, 1 info** across 125 files:

| Rule | Count | Nature |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `suspicious/useIterableCallbackReturn` | 13 | concise arrows in `forEach` returning a value `forEach` discards |
| `suspicious/noDuplicateProperties` | 2 | CSS — at least one is a deliberate fallback declaration |
| `style/useExponentiationOperator` | 1 | `Math.pow(x, 3)` → `x ** 3`, auto-fixable |
| `style/noDescendingSpecificity` | 1 | CSS ordering |
| `a11y/useHeadingContent` | 1 | the empty `<h2 id="shapeStoryTitle">` that JS fills at runtime |
| `a11y/noSvgWithoutTitle` | 1 | `favicon.svg` has no `<title>` |

Fix the mechanical ones. Where a finding encodes a deliberate choice, switch **that rule** off in `biome.json` rather than contorting the code — which is what pfa already does one line below the preset, with `correctness.useExhaustiveDependencies: "off"`. A per-rule entry in the config is ordinary configuration, not an inline suppression, so it does not touch the repo's no-suppressions rule.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `biome.json` carries `"preset": "recommended"`.
- [ ] `pnpm run lint` exits 0.
- [ ] Every rule switched off carries a comment saying why, and the count of them is small.
- [ ] `pnpm run lint:rules`, `typecheck`, `test` and `build` all still green.
- [ ] `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` leaves `geometry-baseline.json` byte-identical.
- [ ] house-style.md's mechanical-enforcement section no longer claims the preset is off.

---

## Delivered

Branch `cosmokaat/cos-403-align-the-biome-config-with-pfa-enable-the-recommended`, one commit `37ac8f0`, pushed. 14 files, +78 / −28.

`biome.json` now carries `"preset": "recommended"`, matching pfa.

**Fixed:** 13 `forEach` callbacks given a block body; `input[type="range"]` base rule moved above the scoped one in `slider.css`; `<title>` added to `favicon.svg`.

**Two rules off**, same pattern pfa uses one line below its own preset:

* `suspicious/noDuplicateProperties` — `.viewportStage` repeats `width` as a container-query-unit fallback; `reset.css` repeats `content` as shipped by the reset it came from.
* `a11y/useHeadingContent` — `#shapeStoryTitle` is filled by `ShapeStoryPanel` at runtime; placeholder markup would flash the wrong shape name.

`Math.pow` **left alone.** `useExponentiationOperator` is severity `info`, so it does not fail lint. `pnpm run lint` exits 0 reporting `Found 1 info`.

**Cost: +26 lines**, entirely the `forEach` bodies — Biome's formatter never keeps a block body on one line.

### Footgun found

`biome.json` is strict JSON. A `//` comment does **not** raise a config error — Biome falls back to its built-in defaults, whose `indentStyle` is **tab**, so the next `lint:fix` retabs all 91 files and the house-style plugins stop running entirely. The only symptom is a formatter diff, which reads as a formatting problem rather than a dead config. Now documented in `CLAUDE.md` and `house-style.md`, and every explanation lives in the docs rather than the config.

### Verification

* `pnpm run lint` exit 0 · `pnpm run lint:rules` all 10 rules firing · `typecheck` 0 · 33 tests · `build` fine
* `geometry-baseline.json` **byte-identical** after edits to `CrossGenerator`, `MengerSpongeGenerator` and `MeshBuilder`

Title: Menu utilisateur : câbler le changement de mot de passe et la passphrase de récupération
Description:
## Pourquoi

[COS-321](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-321/ui-12-menu-utilisateur-dans-le-chrome-mot-de-passe-langue-mockee-log) a livré le menu de compte mais **deux entrées sur quatre restent dessinées et désactivées** : `change password` et `set recovery passphrase`. Le ticket le disait lui-même — `change password` demandait une route à re-câbler, "à trancher en ouvrant le ticket", et la passphrase demandait "un column read et un formulaire qui demande le mot de passe courant". Ce ticket est ce qui les câble.

Sans lui, les 11 comptes qui prédatent la colonne `recovery_passphrase` n'ont toujours aucun moyen de s'en poser une ([COS-324](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-324/auth-05-recuperation-du-mot-de-passe-par-passphrase-ecran-route) ne fait que la consommer), et personne ne peut changer son mot de passe une fois connecté.

## Le parcours

Menu de compte → `change password` ou `set/change recovery passphrase` → une modale (mêmes primitives que la modale d'édition, `ui/dialog`) demandant le **mot de passe courant** plus le secret à poser, avec sa confirmation.

* `change password` : mot de passe courant + nouveau mot de passe (12–72) + confirmation.
* `set/change recovery passphrase` : mot de passe courant + passphrase (20–72) + confirmation. Le libellé de l'entrée et le titre de la modale suivent `hasRecoveryPassphrase` : « set » quand il n'y en a pas, « change » sinon.

## Backend

* `PATCH /users/me/password` — `sessionAuthMiddleware` + `csrfMiddleware`. Body `{currentPassword, newPassword}`. Mauvais mot de passe courant → **400** générique (pas 401 : un 401 déclenche la redirection automatique vers `/login` côté client — `useRequestHelper` — ce qui serait faux ici, la session reste valide). Bon mot de passe → hash, `UPDATE`, puis on **repasse par** `establishSession` (le helper que sign-in/sign-up partagent déjà) : la session est régénérée, toute autre session du compte tombe, le jeton CSRF tourne, et la réponse est `{user, csrfToken}` — qui change son mot de passe reste connecté ici, et est protégé si une session traînait ailleurs.
* `PATCH /users/me/passphrase` — mêmes garde-fous. Body `{currentPassword, recoveryPassphrase}`. Même vérification du mot de passe courant, puis `UPDATE recovery_passphrase`. Réponse `{hasRecoveryPassphrase: true}`. Aucun impact sur la session : ce n'est pas un identifiant de connexion.
* `currentPassword` est validé en `z.string().min(1)`, **sans** minimum de longueur — comme le mot de passe de `signInBodySchema` — pour que les comptes dont le mot de passe est antérieur à la règle des 12 caractères ([COS-298](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-298/ui-02-ecran-signup-jauge-de-force-case-import)) puissent encore le prouver. Le **nouveau** secret, lui, porte les bornes réelles (mot de passe 12–72, passphrase 20–72, comme l'inscription).
* `GET /users/me`, et les réponses de connexion/inscription (`AuthUserSchema` est partagé par les trois), gagnent `hasRecoveryPassphrase: boolean`, dérivé de la colonne — jamais le hash.
* Pas de limitation de débit sur les deux nouvelles routes : la connexion elle-même n'en a pas encore, ce ne serait pas cohérent d'en poser une ici en premier.
* Aucune migration : `recovery_passphrase` existe déjà depuis [COS-298](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-298/ui-02-ecran-signup-jauge-de-force-case-import).

## Frontend

* Deux modales `ui/dialog` (mêmes primitives que la modale d'édition), formulaire `react-hook-form` + zod, champs `AuthField`/`RevealToggle`. Le mot de passe courant n'a **pas** d'œil (raisonnement [COS-297](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-297/ui-01-ecran-login) : c'est un secret déjà connu qu'on prouve, pas un secret qu'on choisit et qu'on relit) ; le nouveau secret et sa confirmation en ont un, partagé comme sur l'inscription.
* Nouveau module `@text/account.ts` pour la copie des deux modales.
* Deux services (`useChangePasswordService`, `useSetRecoveryPassphraseService`) via `privateRequest`.
* `UserMenu` : le libellé de l'entrée passphrase suit `hasRecoveryPassphrase` (« set » / « change »).
* Pas de jauge de force dans ces modales — seulement les bornes, comme le reste des réglages du compte.
* **Revu le 2026-08-02, sur retour du propriétaire.** Pas de point oxide sur l'entrée passphrase : un indicateur rouge à cet endroit lisait comme une alerte plutôt que comme une information — [COS-321](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-321/ui-12-menu-utilisateur-dans-le-chrome-mot-de-passe-langue-mockee-log) le demandait, ce ticket l'annule. Et `log out` passe du variant `destructive` (oxide) à un nouveau variant `primary` sur `ui/dropdown-menu` (le teal `gr-accent`, celui de `ready` dans `StatusBar`) : se déconnecter ne détruit rien, et le sign-in suivant l'annule intégralement — contrairement à une suppression.

## Périmètre

* **Pas de point oxide sur l'e-mail du chrome.** [COS-321](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-321/ui-12-menu-utilisateur-dans-le-chrome-mot-de-passe-langue-mockee-log) laissait la question "à trancher" ; tranché hors périmètre pour ce ticket — `TopChrome.tsx` ne change pas.
* **Pas de tests automatisés.** Ni `backend` ni `frontend` n'en ont aujourd'hui (le script `test` du backend est un stub) — vérification manuelle, comme le reste du chantier GRAPHITE.
* Pas de jauge de force sur le nouveau mot de passe.

## Done

* `change password` et `set/change recovery passphrase` ne sont plus désactivées dans le menu.
* Changer son mot de passe avec le bon mot de passe courant fonctionne, garde la session courante active, et déconnecte toute autre session du compte.
* Mauvais mot de passe courant → refusé sur les deux formulaires, sans déconnecter personne (pas de redirection vers `/login`).
* Poser une passphrase sur un compte qui n'en a pas fait passer son entrée de menu de "set" à "change".
* `GET /users/me` renvoie `hasRecoveryPassphrase`, jamais la valeur elle-même.

Title: UI : page Logs Apache/nginx — IP visibles + whois/géoloc à la demande (ks-b attaqué quotidiennement)
Description:
**Contexte**

ks-b est attaqué quotidiennement (scans, brute-force, bots). Pas de vue exploitable aujourd'hui pour repérer rapidement les IPs suspectes dans les access/error logs Apache et nginx. Distinct de [COS-197](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-197/ui-page-logs-recherche-filtres-live-tail) qui porte sur les logs applicatifs (PM2/pino), pas les logs serveur.

**Objectif**

Une page qui pretty-print les logs Apache et nginx (access + error), avec l'IP source mise en évidence sur chaque ligne, et un bouton par ligne pour lancer un lookup whois + géolocalisation **à la demande uniquement**.

**1. Ingestion / parsing**

* Parser les formats access log nginx (combined) et Apache (combined/common), + error logs.
* Extraire et afficher clairement : IP, timestamp, méthode, route, statut, user-agent, référent.
* Tolérant aux lignes malformées (ne doit pas planter sur une ligne inattendue).

**2. Affichage**

* IP mise en valeur visuellement (colonne dédiée / badge), copiable en un clic.
* Filtres : IP, plage temporelle, code statut, service (apache/nginx).
* Regroupement optionnel par IP pour repérer la fréquence de hits d'une même IP (utile pour un scan).

**3. Whois / géolocalisation à la demande**

* Bouton par ligne (ou par IP groupée) qui déclenche le lookup **uniquement au clic**.
* Contrainte forte : **aucun appel automatique/continu** vers une API externe — volume de plusieurs milliers de lignes/jour, donc inacceptable en coût comme en rate-limit.
* Résultat mis en cache côté serveur (par IP, TTL long — pays/ASN ne changent pas) pour qu'un re-clic sur la même IP ne redéclenche pas d'appel externe.
* Pistes gratuites à évaluer : [ip-api.com](<http://ip-api.com>) ou [ipwho.is](<http://ipwho.is>) (whois + géoloc combinés, gratuits avec rate limit), ou géoloc 100% locale via base MaxMind GeoLite2 (pas d'appel réseau du tout) + `whois` côté serveur pour le whois seul.

**Hors scope**

* Blocage automatique des IPs (fail2ban / firewall).
* Alertes automatiques sur pattern d'attaque.
* Export.

**Done**

- [ ] Access/error logs Apache et nginx affichés pretty-printés, IP visible sur chaque ligne.
- [ ] Clic sur une ligne (ou l'IP) déclenche whois + géoloc, sans aucun appel automatique en arrière-plan.
- [ ] Résultat whois/géoloc mis en cache — un re-clic sur la même IP ne redéclenche pas d'appel externe.
- [ ] Tient plusieurs milliers de lignes/jour sans dégrader la page.
