Title: Telemetry cards overflow their row and are painted over by the row below
Description:
Every card in the first telemetry row is taller than the row that holds it, so its bottom band is drawn underneath the second row's cards. Three widgets lose their last element to it: FRAMERATE loses the bottom half of the MIN / AVG / MAX / DROPPED tiles, FRAME TIME loses the FILL RATE footer, and GEOMETRY loses the whole POLY BUDGET footer — label, value and bar.

It reads as three unfinished cards rather than as one layout fault, which is why it has survived three widget tickets: each looks like a bug in the widget that lost its footer, and none of them is.

## The cause is one declaration

`.telemetryRow` is `flex-wrap: wrap` (`src/styles/layout.css:117`). A wrapping flex container sizes its line from the line's own content, and `align-content` only ever *grows* a line — it cannot shrink one to fit the container. So the line takes the tallest card's max-content height and every card stretches to it, overflowing the row box, which carries no `overflow` of its own.

The tallest card is FRAMERATE, and what makes it tall is `canvas#fpsChart`: a canvas with no `height` attribute has an intrinsic 150px, and `flex: 1` with `min-height: 0` still contributes that 150px to the container's max-content height.

Measured at 1440x900, on `master` and unchanged since:

| box | height |
| -- | -- |
| `.telemetryRow` | 128px |
| `.framerate` / `.frame-time` / `.geometry` | 216px each |

Flipping the one declaration to `flex-wrap: nowrap` in the inspector brings all three cards to exactly 128px and every footer and tile row paints. That is the diagnosis, not the proposed fix — wrapping is deliberate (`layout.css:115` — "Wraps rather than crushing"), so the fix has to keep the wrap and stop the line being sized by the canvas's intrinsic height.

## Two candidate fixes

1. Give `#fpsChart` a definite basis so it contributes nothing intrinsic — `height: 0` alongside its existing `flex: 1`. Smallest change, and it keeps the wrap. Touches `src/styles/components/framerate.css`, which is [COS-223](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-223/framerate-widget)'s file.
2. Size the telemetry rows from a token rather than from their content, so a card can never set the line height. Larger, and it belongs to the shell.

Option 1 first unless it turns out the canvas is not the only card that can drive the line — [COS-226](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-226/z-buffer-histogram-widget) (z-buffer) and [COS-227](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-227/camera-stats-widget) (camera) both land in the second row and neither is built yet, so the second row is empty today and cannot show the same fault.

## Not a regression

`master` measures identically for the two cards that exist there, so this predates [COS-225](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-225/geometry-widget) and was not introduced by it. [COS-225](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-225/geometry-widget) is simply the third widget to lose its footer to it.

## Done when

- [ ] At 1440x900 the FRAMERATE tiles, the FILL RATE footer and the POLY BUDGET footer are all fully visible
- [ ] Card height equals row height for every card in the row, verified by measurement rather than by eye
- [ ] `.telemetryRow` still wraps rather than crushing its cards below `--size-card-min-w`
- [ ] No card in the row paints outside its own box at any window width from 900px up

Title: Frame-rate cap: RENDER LOOP chips in the RENDER tab
Description:
A control to cap the render loop, so the console can be run at 30 fps or 60 fps instead of whatever the display gives it.

**This is a new feature, not a restoration.** It is worth writing down because it was assumed otherwise: the pre-refonte app never had a frame-rate control. Its loop was a bare `requestAnimationFrame(step)` with no throttle — the same shape as today's `src/app/RenderLoop.ts` — and its six sliders were zoom, opacity, pitch, yaw, roll and rotation speed. `git log -S` finds no `fpsLimit`, `targetFps`, `maxFps` or `setInterval` anywhere in the history. There is no dormant code to revive.

Nor is it in the Claude Design mockup, which draws a `RENDER LOOP 61 fps` readout but no control beside it. So the placement and the control shape are decisions this ticket makes rather than extracts.

## Control

A segmented chip row, **not** a slider: the cap has three values anyone wants, and a range input invites 47 fps and needs a value column to explain itself.

* Lives in the **RENDER tab**, as its own group under PIPELINE. Section title `RENDER LOOP`.
* Three chips: `30` · `60` · `MAX`. `MAX` is uncapped — the loop runs at whatever the display offers, which is the behaviour today and stays the default.
* Built from the existing chip primitive at `--size-chip-mode` (26px desktop, 44px mobile), with `.is-on` marking the active one. It is the same recipe the segmented toggle uses, so it needs no new CSS beyond the group's own layout.
* Mobile ships it too — the RENDER tab exists at both breakpoints and the chips already resolve to a 44px touch target.

`MAX` cannot raise the rate above the display refresh: `requestAnimationFrame` is the only clock here, so the control only ever removes frames. On a 120Hz display `60` is a real cap and `MAX` gives 120.

## Engine

`RenderLoop` gains a target and gates `onFrame` on it. The accumulator has to be drift-corrected — `lastFrameAt = timestamp - (elapsed % interval)` rather than `lastFrameAt = timestamp` — or a 30fps cap against a 60Hz display lands on 20fps, because every other frame misses the deadline by a hair and waits a whole extra one.

The rAF callback keeps rescheduling itself unconditionally; only the `onFrame` call is gated. Suppressed frames must not touch `FPSMeter`, so the readout reports the rate actually rendered rather than the rate offered.

## Two consequences, one accepted and one fixed

**The spin slows, and that is accepted.** `CameraController.rotate()` applies a fixed angle per *rendered frame*, not per second — which is exactly why the CAMERA card labels the row `°/f`. At a 30fps cap the shape visibly rotates at half speed. Decided on 2026-08-04 to leave the per-frame model alone and document it: making rotation time-based changes how the engine looks at its default setting and rewrites the SPIN RATE derivation, which is de-mock E1's work, not a UI control's. Note it in a code comment beside the cap so the next person does not read it as a bug.

**DROPPED must stop being absolute.** `FramerateWidget` counts a dropped frame as anything under a hard-coded `DROP_THRESHOLD_FPS = 40`. Under a 30fps cap that is every single frame. Replace the constant with a ratio of the active target: `2/3` reproduces today's behaviour exactly at 60fps (40 / 60 = 0.667) and scales correctly to 20fps under a 30 cap. The widget therefore has to be told the target.

## RESET

The cap is a scene control, so it registers a `UIStateStore` slice with `MAX` as its default and RESET restores it — automatically, through `resetAll()`, without the reset handler being edited.

## Files

* `src/index.html` — the chip group in the RENDER tab body
* `src/ui/RenderPipelinePanel.ts` — or a small `FrameRateChips` class beside it; owns the chips and publishes the target
* `src/app/RenderLoop.ts` — the target, the drift-corrected gate
* `src/app/Main.ts` — wire the chips to the loop and hand the target to the framerate widget
* `src/ui/telemetry/FramerateWidget.ts` — drop threshold becomes a ratio of the target
* `src/ui/UIStateStore.ts` — the slice
* `src/styles/components/chip.css` is consumed, not extended

## Ordering

[COS-230](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-230/render-tab-shading-mode-pipeline-lighting) rebuilds the RENDER tab and is still in Backlog. If this lands first, [COS-230](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-230/render-tab-shading-mode-pipeline-lighting) has to keep the group rather than rebuilding over it; if [COS-230](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-230/render-tab-shading-mode-pipeline-lighting) lands first, this is a drop-in. Either order works — say which in the branch.

## Done when

- [ ] Three chips render in the RENDER tab at both breakpoints, `MAX` active by default, one active at a time
- [ ] Selecting `30` holds the measured fps at 30 ± 1 on a 60Hz display, and `60` holds 60 on a 120Hz display
- [ ] The cap is drift-corrected: a 30fps cap on a 60Hz display reads 30, never 20
- [ ] `FPSMeter` and the framerate sparkline report the rendered rate, not the offered one
- [ ] DROPPED reads ~0 under a steady 30fps cap, and its threshold is derived from the target rather than a constant
- [ ] RESET returns the cap to `MAX`
- [ ] The per-frame rotation consequence is recorded in a code comment beside the cap
- [ ] No raw hex/px outside the token files

Title: Group the primitive picker into families, and decide where a shape's family is declared
Description:
The picker [COS-229](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-229/shape-tab-primitive-picker-transform-material) ships is one flat list of fourteen shapes, and it is already long enough that finding a solid means reading all of it. It gets worse rather than better: [COS-201](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-201/epic-polyhedra-from-the-symmetries-of-things) adds roughly ten more polyhedra to the same list, at which point two thirds of it is one family of mathematical solids with near-identical names — RHOMBDOD, KISRHDOD, TRCUBOCT, ICOSIDOD, RHOMBTRI, KISRHTRI.

Sections fix the scanning problem. The substance of this ticket is not the markup, it is **where a shape declares which family it belongs to**, because that decision is the thing every future shape has to satisfy.

## The real question

Four candidate homes, and they are not equivalent.

**1. A required** `family` **field on** `ShapeInfo` **(**`src/data/shapeInfo.ts`**).** Recommended. That record is already per-shape, already keyed by the same registry key, and already carries the convention this needs — its own comment says a required field is required on purpose, so *"a shape that lands without one is a compile error rather than an em dash nobody notices"*. A `family` typed as a union rather than a string means a typo is a compile error too. Adding a shape to `data.ts` without classifying it stops the build, which is exactly the failure mode we want.

**2. A separate** `shapeFamilies.ts` **mapping family → key list.** Leaves the data files untouched, and creates a second list of registry keys that can drift from the registry. That is the duplication the epic's one-derivation rule exists to prevent: a shape added to `data.ts` and forgotten here would silently vanish from the picker rather than failing loudly.

**3. Derive it from what is already there** — MathWorld links in `references`, or the `generator` string. Clever and wrong. It couples the picker's grouping to editorial copy, so rewording a generator description silently regroups the UI.

**4. A** `tags: string[]` **array instead of one family.** More power than the problem has: the picker needs exactly one section per option, so multiple tags would need a precedence rule invented to break ties. Worth it only if filtering or search is coming, which nothing currently plans. If it is, say so and this becomes the answer instead.

Whichever wins, the **section order and section titles need their own small ordered table** — a `Record` cannot express order meaningfully, and the display name is not the enum value.

## Proposed families for the current fourteen

| Section | Shapes |
| -- | -- |
| PRIMITIVES | sphere, cube, pyramid, cross |
| SURFACES | donut, torusKnot |
| FRACTALS | menger |
| POLYHEDRA | cuboctahedron, rhombicDodecahedron, kisRhombicDodecahedron, truncatedCuboctahedron, icosidodecahedron, rhombicTriacontahedron, kisRhombicTriacontahedron |

That is the split the registry already has implicitly, and it is the one [COS-201](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-201/epic-polyhedra-from-the-symmetries-of-things) grows — its ten additions all land in POLYHEDRA and no other section moves. A one-shape FRACTALS section looks thin today and is the correct place for a Sierpinski or a Julia set later; merging it into SURFACES now would only have to be undone.

## The do-nothing option, stated so it is a choice

Fourteen entries in a scrolling popup is not unusable, and sections cost a data-model decision that binds every future shape. If [COS-201](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-201/epic-polyhedra-from-the-symmetries-of-things) slips, this can wait. It should not wait *past* [COS-201](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-201/epic-polyhedra-from-the-symmetries-of-things) — classifying twenty-four shapes retroactively is the same work plus the reading.

## Picker changes

`ShapePicker.setOptions` currently takes a flat `ShapeOption[]`. It would take groups instead, and the class keeps its flat `Map` internals so `setActive`, the keyboard path and the trigger face are untouched.

* Section headers are not options: they must not be focusable, must not be pickable, and must be announced as group labels. In a `role="listbox"` that means `role="group"` with `aria-label`, wrapping the options — not a bare heading element between them, which screen readers would read as loose text inside a listbox.
* The header is a new small label recipe in `inspector.css`; do not reuse `.section-title`, which is the tab's own heading voice and would compete with PRIMITIVE directly above.
* The PRIMITIVE header count stays the true total across all sections.
* Within a section, registry order is kept — it is already the order the picker lists them in and the first key is still the boot shape.

## Files

* `src/data/shapeInfo.ts` — the `family` field on every entry, plus the union type (if option 1 wins)
* `src/data/shapeFamilies.ts` — new; the ordered section table (titles and order), whichever option wins
* `src/ui/inspector/ShapePicker.ts` — grouped `setOptions`, `role="group"` wrappers
* `src/ui/inspector/PrimitiveSection.ts` — builds the groups from the family table rather than one flat map
* `src/styles/inspector.css` — the group-label rule

## Done when

- [ ] Every registry key declares a family, and a shape added without one fails the build rather than rendering ungrouped
- [ ] A mistyped family name is a compile error, not a section that silently never appears
- [ ] The picker renders the sections in a declared order, with registry order preserved inside each
- [ ] Section headers are not reachable by keyboard and are announced as group labels, not as options
- [ ] The PRIMITIVE header count is the total across sections
- [ ] Adding the [COS-201](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-201/epic-polyhedra-from-the-symmetries-of-things) polyhedra requires no edit to the picker or to the family table beyond the shapes' own entries
- [ ] No raw hex/px outside the token files

Depends on [COS-229](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-229/shape-tab-primitive-picker-transform-material), which introduces the picker.

Title: Ship the torus knot family: 5₁, 7₁ and 8₁₉ alongside the trefoil
Description:
The registry has one torus knot, the trefoil, and the generator behind it is already general. [MathWorld's TorusKnot article](<https://mathworld.wolfram.com/TorusKnot.html>) draws four in a row — 3₁, 5₁, 7₁ and 8₁₉ — and three of them are a few lines of configuration away.

## This is nearly free, and that is the point

`TorusKnotGenerator` already takes `p` and `q` through `TorusKnotOptions`; `src/data/shapes/torusKnot.ts` is six lines that call `new TorusKnotGenerator().build()` and take the defaults `DEFAULT_P = 2`, `DEFAULT_Q = 3`. A (p, q) knot is therefore a new shape file and a registry entry — **no engine change, no new generator, no new maths**.

| Knot | (p, q) | Common name |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 3₁ | (2, 3) | trefoil — **already shipped** as `torusKnot` |
| 5₁ | (2, 5) | Solomon's seal / cinquefoil |
| 7₁ | (2, 7) | septafoil |
| 8₁₉ | (3, 4) | the first with p > 2 |

**Guard to state in code:** `gcd(p, q)` **must be 1.** With a common factor the curve closes early and produces a *link* — several separate loops — not a knot. (2, 4) is two interlocked circles, and it would render as a plausible-looking object that is mathematically the wrong thing. A generator that accepts it silently is the bug to prevent.

## The two decisions this ticket has to make

**1. Segment count has to scale with the knot, or the dense ones look faceted.** The path is swept at `DEFAULT_PATH_SEGMENTS = 220` for the trefoil. A (2,7) winds more than twice as far around the torus for the same parameter range, so 220 frames spread over a longer curve gives visibly straight sections. Derive the count from p and q rather than adding four literals.

**2. That runs straight into the poly budget, and it is a repo-wide consequence.** Triangles are `pathSegments × tubeSegments × 2`, so the trefoil is 220 × 18 × 2 = **7920** — already the densest shape in the registry, and `POLY_BUDGET` in `GeometryWidget` is derived as the next power of two above the registry maximum, currently **8192**. Any knot that needs more path segments at the same tube resolution pushes the maximum past 8192, the budget doubles to 16384, and **every other shape's POLY BUDGET bar halves** overnight. Two ways out, and the ticket should pick one deliberately:

* Keep every knot at or under 8192 triangles by trading tube segments for path segments as p and q grow. The denser knots get a slightly less round tube, which is barely visible at these radii and keeps the budget stable.
* Let the budget move to 16384 and accept that the bar reads lower for all fourteen existing shapes. Honest, but it makes a widget regress for a reason that has nothing to do with that widget.

The first is recommended. Whichever is chosen, record it — the budget is derived, so it will move silently otherwise.

## What each new shape needs beyond the geometry

* **A** `shapeInfo` **entry**, all required fields: `title`, `description`, `geometricFeature`, `densityLabel`, `generator`, `textureSummary`, plus `references` to the MathWorld and Wikipedia pages. The file's own convention is that these are required so a shape cannot land without them.
* **A short chip label** in `src/ui/primitiveChipLabel.ts`. `TKNOT` is taken by the trefoil and the derived fallback would give `TORUSKNO` for a key like `torusKnot25`. Either name the keys for the knots (`cinquefoilKnot`, `septafoilKnot`) and let the map do the shortening, or key them `torusKnot25` / `torusKnot27` / `torusKnot34` and map to `TK25` / `TK27` / `TK34` — self-documenting about (p, q), which reads better beside four near-identical thumbnails.
* **A family**, once [COS-409](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-409/group-the-primitive-picker-into-families-and-decide-where-a-shapes>) lands. Four knots is enough to argue for a KNOTS section of its own rather than folding them into SURFACES beside the plain torus — worth revisiting [COS-409](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-409/group-the-primitive-picker-into-families-and-decide-where-a-shapes)'s proposed split when this ships.
* **A regenerated geometry baseline.** `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` rewrites `notes/oop-refonte/reference/geometry-baseline.json` and `geometry-counts.md`, both of which enumerate the registry. That run is part of the ticket, not a follow-up.

## Not in scope

The article also covers non-torus knots and the crossing-number sequence (OEIS A051764). Only (p, q) torus knots are reachable from this generator; anything else is a different construction and a different ticket.

## Done when

- [ ] 5₁ (2,5), 7₁ (2,7) and 8₁₉ (3,4) render, each recognisably the knot MathWorld draws
- [ ] Path segments are derived from p and q, not four hardcoded numbers, and no knot shows visible flat sections along the tube
- [ ] `gcd(p, q) !== 1` is rejected loudly rather than producing a link
- [ ] The poly-budget decision is made explicitly and recorded; if the budget moves, it moves because someone chose it
- [ ] Each knot has a complete `shapeInfo` entry with MathWorld and Wikipedia references, and a short chip label that is not the derived fallback
- [ ] The picker's thumbnails distinguish the four knots at 44px — if they do not, say so, because that is what the thumbnail is for
- [ ] `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` has been rerun and the baseline and counts committed
- [ ] `pnpm run typecheck`, `lint`, `test` and `lint:rules` pass

Title: PLAT 08 — Mise en production du refacto GRAPHITE : scripts de déploiement, migrations, bascule nginx
Description:
Le refacto est terminé et n'est jamais sorti de la machine de dev. La prod de `bkmk.1991computer.com` fait toujours tourner l'app de 2023 : `bkmk-server` en ligne depuis 8 mois, un front statique servi par nginx, et une base qui n'a reçu aucune des migrations écrites depuis juillet.

Ce ticket est le déploiement, et les trois choses qui l'empêchent d'être un simple `rsync`.

## 1. Il n'y a pas de script de déploiement

`/var/www/bkmk` n'est même pas un dépôt git — le déploiement a toujours été manuel. pfa a `deploy-front.sh` et `deploy-api.sh` : releases horodatées, bascule atomique, `.bak` pour le rollback, `pm2 startOrReload`, changelog de déploiement. On reprend cette forme, telle quelle, pour les deux périmètres.

Le script back porte en plus **ce que pfa n'a pas besoin de faire** : un dump nommé avant la migration, puis `pnpm migrate`.

## 2. Le front cesse d'être statique — c'est le vrai piège

nginx sert aujourd'hui `/var/www/bkmk/public_html` en fichiers (`try_files $uri $uri.html /index.html`). Le nouveau front est Next 16 App Router avec un `headers()` asynchrone et une lecture de session côté serveur (`getServerSession`) : **il doit tourner comme un process node**, et nginx doit le proxifier.

Déployer le build dans `public_html` comme avant donne un site blanc. La bascule se fait en même temps que le reste :

* `bkmk-front` sous pm2, `next start` sur 3100, écoute sur 127.0.0.1
* le bloc `location /` passe de `try_files` à `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3100`
* `location /api/` ne bouge pas — il proxifie déjà vers 5100

L'ancien front s'authentifie avec un JWT en `localStorage` et la nouvelle API n'accepte que le cookie de session : back et front doivent basculer ensemble, sinon le site est cassé dans l'intervalle.

## 3. La prod n'a aucune des 5 migrations

`schema_migrations` n'existe pas là-bas. C'est le cas simple décrit dans `backend/src/db/migrations/README.md` : ni `mark` ni `baseline`, juste `pnpm migrate` qui applique les cinq dans l'ordre.

Sans elles : l'inscription répond 500 sur `recovery_passphrase`, un import répond 500 sur `import_run`, et snooze n'a pas de colonne où écrire.

## 4. Le filet de sécurité se détruit tout seul

Le dump est **un fichier unique, écrasé sur place, deux fois par jour, sans rétention**. Si une migration abîme des données et qu'on s'en aperçoit le lendemain, le cron de minuit a déjà écrasé la seule copie avec la version abîmée.

Un dump nommé et daté avant la migration, c'est l'étape 1 et pas une précaution optionnelle.

## 5. La sauvegarde des captures écrit à côté depuis novembre 2024

`screenshotsBackup.js` lit `BKMK_BACKUP_INVOICES_SERVER_PATH` — un nom **pfa**, recopié. L'environnement définit `BKMK_BACKUP_SCREENSHOTS_SERVER_PATH`. Le littéral rend donc `${undefined}${userID}`, et 21 mois de captures sont parties dans un répertoire `undefined3` au lieu de `screenshotsUpload/3`.

Rien n'est perdu : 20 fichiers, à un répertoire de distance, aucun recouvrement avec les 208 correctement classés. Vérifié en direct — une capture créée le 04/08/2026 à 16:23:45 est arrivée à 16:24:45 dans `undefined3` (le `setTimeout` d'une minute de `sshRaw.copy`).

Le même nom de variable est encore dans `bkmk-next`, donc **le refacto embarque le bug** s'il n'est pas corrigé avant.

Deux fichiers de 2023 et mi-2024 ne sont jamais arrivés du tout : `sshRaw.copy` logue l'erreur sftp et ne réessaie pas. Hors périmètre ici.

## Aussi, tant qu'on y est

`sftp error:  undefined` dans les logs est la ligne de **succès** : le callback de `fastPut` logue sans condition, et `undefined` veut dire « pas d'erreur ». Elle imprime le mot « error » à chaque copie réussie depuis des années, et c'est la ligne qu'on va lire pour vérifier le déploiement.

## Périmètre

* `backend/deploy-api.sh` et `frontend/deploy-front.sh`, sur le modèle pfa, avec rollback
* `frontend/ecosystem.config.cjs` — suivi en git, le front n'a aucun secret
* correction du nom de variable dans `screenshotsBackup.js`
* les 20 fichiers de `undefined3` remis dans `screenshotsUpload/3`, puis suppression du répertoire
* bascule du bloc nginx, `nginx -t` avant reload
* `JWT_SECRET` devient mort côté prod — [COS-294](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-294/auth-02-backend-csrf-double-submit-retrait-du-jwt) a retiré le JWT

## Hors périmètre

Pas de rétention sur les dumps, pas de reprise sur erreur sftp. Les deux méritent leur ticket.

Title: Index : recolorer les stars (rose) et les barres de priority (bleu)
Description:
## Constat

* **Stars** (`Stars.tsx`, `StarsField.tsx`) sont peintes en `text-gr-accent-2` (`#7d3714`, oxyde) — c'est la valeur du handoff (`--accent-2` : "étoiles, alarme imminente"), donc pas un bug, un écart esthétique à assumer.
* **Priority bars** (`PriorityBars.tsx`) n'a que 2 tons pour 4 niveaux : `gr-fg-2` (`#0c0d0c`) seulement pour `highest`, `gr-fg-3` (`#474944`) pour `low`/`medium`/`high` confondus. La longueur des barres est aujourd'hui le seul signal — la couleur ne distingue que `highest` du reste.

## Changement demandé

1. **Stars → rose** `rgb(252, 3, 130)` / `#fc0382`.
2. **Priority bars → 4 tons de bleu**, un ton fixe par *position* de barre (pas par niveau), du plus clair à gauche au plus foncé à droite — inspiré d'une palette [coolors.co](<http://coolors.co>) fournie par l'utilisateur.
3. **URL de la ligne index →** `--fg-4` au lieu de `--fg-3`, pour mieux la distinguer du titre (`--fg-2`).

## Point d'attention technique

`gr-accent-2` et `gr-fg-2`/`gr-fg-3` sont des tokens **partagés** : oxyde (`gr-accent-2`) habille aussi les erreurs, le flux destructif et l'alarme imminente (~30 usages) ; `gr-fg-2`/`gr-fg-3` sont l'encre du texte courant sur 38/24 fichiers. Repeindre ces tokens directement changerait aussi les messages d'erreur, la modale de suppression et l'alarme imminente.

→ Créer des tokens dédiés dans le bloc GRAPHITE de `styles/tokens/colors.css` plutôt que de toucher `--color-gr-accent-2` / `--color-gr-fg-2` / `--color-gr-fg-3`, et ne rebrancher que les fichiers listés ci-dessous.

## Fichiers concernés

* `frontend/styles/tokens/colors.css` — nouveaux tokens
* `frontend/src/components/ds/Stars.tsx:30`
* `frontend/src/components/bookmarks/fields/StarsField.tsx:75`
* `frontend/src/components/ds/PriorityBars.tsx`
* `frontend/src/components/bookmarks/IndexRow.tsx:148` — couleur de l'url (ajouté en cours d'implémentation, demande de l'utilisateur)

## Valeurs retenues

Le bleu n'existait nulle part dans la palette GRAPHITE (fond/encre en gris, `accent` teal, `accent-2`/`danger` oxyde). Un premier essai avec 4 tons désaturés peints *par niveau* (tout le run rempli d'une ligne prend un seul ton) a été rejeté à l'écran : sur `highest` (4/4), les 4 barres affichaient le même bleu. Un premier jeu de valeurs venait d'une palette [coolors.co](<http://coolors.co>) fournie par l'utilisateur, mais l'écart de teinte entre bar 1 et bar 2 était bien plus grand qu'entre bar 3 et bar 4 (72 % → 42 % → 34 % → 27 % de luminosité) — pas régulier, et bar 4 trop proche du noir. Valeurs finales : même teinte (~210°) et saturation (75 %), luminosité en pas égaux de 76 % à 38 %, peintes *par position* :

| position | token | valeur |
| -- | -- | -- |
| bar 1 (low) | `--color-gr-pri-1` | `#94c2f0` |
| bar 2 (medium) | `--color-gr-pri-2` | `#5aa1e7` |
| bar 3 (high) | `--color-gr-pri-3` | `#207fdf` |
| bar 4 (highest) | `--color-gr-pri-4` | `#1861aa` |

Un niveau `n` affiche les barres `1..n` dans leurs tons respectifs et éteint le reste (`--fg-4` à 40%) : la couleur est un dégradé fixe par position, pas un ton par ligne.

**Stars :** `--color-gr-star` corrigé à `#fc0382` (rose plus chaud que le rose/magenta `#fc03f4` du premier essai).

## Definition of done

* Stars (`IndexRow`, `RecordFields`, `StarsField`) en `#fc0382`.
* Priority bars (`IndexRow`, `RecordFields`) : dégradé fixe et régulier par position de barre, `--gr-pri-1` (bar 1, clair) → `--gr-pri-4` (bar 4, foncé mais pas noir).
* URL de `IndexRow` en `--fg-4` (au lieu de `--fg-3`), pour se distinguer du titre.
* `gr-accent-2`, `gr-fg-2`, `gr-fg-3` inchangés partout ailleurs (erreurs, destructif, alarme imminente, texte courant).

Title: Shell : contour de focus natif du navigateur sur les onglets au clavier, pas l'anneau `gr-ring` du DS
Description:
Repéré au clavier : sur les onglets du shell (`index`, `new`, `import`, `alarms`), le focus affiche le contour bleu natif du navigateur, pas la bague `gr-ring` du DS.

## Constat

Reproduire : `pnpm dev` sur le front (:3100), ouvrir `/bookmarks/`, cliquer une fois dans la page puis `Tab` jusqu'à un onglet.

Les deux `<nav>` d'onglets sortis de [COS-292](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-292/ds-03-shell-applicatif-chrome-haut-barre-de-statut-tab-bar-mobile) n'ont **aucune classe de focus**, sur la même liste `SHELL_TABS` :

* `TopChrome.tsx:56-70` — le `<Link>` de chaque onglet du chrome (`.gr-strip`) ne porte que des classes de mise en page et de couleur.
* `TabBar.tsx:31-43` — même `<Link>`, même trou, sur la barre du bas (`.gr-tabbar`, sous `@max-3xl`) : le même bug, deux fois.
* `TopChrome.tsx:45-51` — le lien du wordmark `BKMK`, premier élément focusable de la ligne. Repéré en QA (capture de l'utilisateur), pas dans le grep initial : sans bordure ni fond, il n'y avait rien à comparer visuellement aux onglets tant qu'on ne l'avait pas testé au clavier.

Description:
**Constat** Sous `@max-3xl` (viewport étroit), rien dans le chrome ne donne accès au menu utilisateur. Dans `TopChrome.tsx`, le bloc qui porte `about` et `UserMenu` est `@max-3xl:hidden` : ```
{SHELL_TEXT.about} {email && }
``` Et `TabBar.tsx` (la nav du bas sous `@max-3xl`) ne porte que les 4 tabs modules de `SHELL_TABS` — rien sur le compte. Résultat : `log out` n'est joignable nulle part sur mobile, un utilisateur connecté ne peut pas se déconnecter depuis l'app. Le trou existe depuis [COS-321](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-321/ui-12-menu-utilisateur-dans-le-chrome-mot-de-passe-langue-mockee-log) (menu utilisateur ajouté au chrome) : jamais porté côté étroit, `UserMenu` est resté dans le même bloc masqué que `about`. **Comportement attendu** Reprendre le pattern déjà en place côté pfa (`~/dev/pfa/front/src/components/shared/navBar/NavBar.tsx` + `userMenu/DrawerAccountSection.tsx`, [COS-161](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-161/navbar-flouter-la-page-quand-un-overlay-souvre-animer-le-calendrier)/[COS-163](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-163/mobile-sous-menu-langue-hors-ecran-bloc-compte-en-bas-du-drawer)) : un déclencheur hamburger dans le chrome, visible seulement là où le bloc `about` + `UserMenu` disparaît aujourd'hui, qui ouvre un panneau latéral où : * le reste de l'app derrière le panneau passe en scrim flouté — le token existe déjà (`bg-gr-scrim backdrop-blur-[3px]`, utilisé dans `ui/dialog.tsx` et `ui/alert-dialog.tsx`), pas besoin d'en créer un nouveau ; * le menu utilisateur (donc `log out`) est épinglé en bas du panneau, comme le `mt-auto` de `DrawerAccountSection` côté pfa. **Ce que le panneau porte — et ce qu'il ne porte pas** Le contenu est exactement ce que `@max-3xl:hidden` cache aujourd'hui : le lien `about` et le `UserMenu` existant (mot de passe, passphrase, langue désactivée, log out) — pas plus. Les 4 tabs modules restent dans `TabBar`, qui fonctionne déjà sous `@max-3xl` ; ce ticket ne les duplique pas dans le panneau. **Points d'attention** * Container query, pas media query : le déclencheur doit suivre `@max-3xl` comme le reste du chrome (`TabBar` le documente : « Not "mobile", narrow »), pas un `lg:hidden` façon pfa. * `AppShell.tsx` documente que tout ce qui est porté (`portal`) vers `document.body` — un `Dialog` Radix, un toast — sort du `@container` et perd tous les `@max-3xl`. Si le panneau s'appuie sur un composant qui porte hors de l'arbre, vérifier qu'il reste dans le `@container` d'`AppShell`, sinon ses propres variantes `@max-3xl` ne résoudront jamais. * Pas de primitive de panneau latéral dans `ui/` aujourd'hui (`dialog`, `alert-dialog`, `dropdown-menu`, `popover`, pas de `sheet`) — à construire ou ajouter. * `@text/shell.ts` n'a que `aria.modules` et `aria.home` pour l'instant ; le déclencheur et le panneau auront besoin des leurs. **Référence** Captures mobile de pfa fournies en conversation (hamburger dans le chrome, panneau qui floute le fond, menu compte en bas). Source : `NavBar.tsx` (déclencheur, scrim, `aside`, lock du scroll) et `DrawerAccountSection.tsx` (bloc compte `mt-auto`) — pattern à reprendre, pas à copier tel quel : pfa flotte en `lg:hidden` + classes CSS maison (`pfa-drawer`, `pfa-scrim`), bkmk reste en `@max-3xl` + tokens `gr-*`.

Title: Delete select.css — dead since the primitive picker stopped being a native select
Description:
`src/styles/components/select.css` is 228 lines of CSS with nothing left to style. Its own header already says so: *"*[COS-229](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-229/shape-tab-primitive-picker-transform-material) *deletes this file."* [COS-229](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-229/shape-tab-primitive-picker-transform-material) shipped and the file is still here.

## Verified dead

* No `<select>` element anywhere in `src/index.html` — the only remaining match is a code comment explaining why a native select could not do the job.
* No `.select`, `.select__input` or `.select__chevron` reference anywhere under `src/ui/` or `src/app/`.
* Still imported: `src/styles/main.css:17` — `@import url(components/select.css);`

[COS-343](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-343/select-control-primitive-the-primitive-pickers-interim-skin) wrote it as the primitive picker's interim skin while the control was still a native `<select>`. [COS-229](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-229/shape-tab-primitive-picker-transform-material) replaced that control with the hand-built `ShapePicker` (`src/ui/inspector/ShapePicker.ts`), which builds `.shape-picker__trigger` and `.shape-picker__list` and needs none of it.

## Read this before deleting — one part was NOT dead

The `@supports (appearance: base-select)` block carried a genuine cross-fade on `::picker(select)`, with `@starting-style` and two `allow-discrete` entries. That animation was lost with the element it was attached to, and the hand-built list opened as a hard cut until [COS-230](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-230/render-tab-shading-mode-pipeline-lighting) restored an equivalent fade on `.shape-picker__list` in `src/styles/inspector.css`.

So the fade is already carried over — but the reasoning behind it is not. That block's comments explain things the replacement rule still depends on and does not restate:

* why the surface steps to `--color-tab-active-bg` rather than reusing `--color-panel-bg` (cross-fading a surface onto its own colour moves it 5 luminance levels out of 256, so the transition ran correctly and looked like nothing happened; the step takes it to 14)
* why it is alpha only and nothing moves (a slide reads as a menu rather than as part of the panel)
* why it is deliberately **not** gated on `prefers-reduced-motion` (that preference targets motion that can trigger vestibular symptoms — travel, parallax, scale — and a cross-fade in place is the standard exception; gating it would hand anyone with Reduce Motion on the exact hard cut the fade exists to remove)

Move whatever of that reasoning is still load-bearing into `inspector.css` beside the `.shape-picker__list` rule, or into `notes/ui-refonte/`, before the file goes. Deleting it silently loses three rulings that were argued once and would otherwise be re-litigated.

## Done when

- [ ] `src/styles/components/select.css` is gone
- [ ] Its `@import` is removed from `src/styles/main.css`
- [ ] The three rulings above survive somewhere a future reader will find them
- [ ] The primitive picker looks and behaves identically at both breakpoints, fade included
- [ ] `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run typecheck` pass

Title: Verrouiller les inscriptions : formulaire désactivé + API bloquée, togglable par env var
Description:
## Contexte

L'app est censée n'être utilisée que par le owner. N'importe qui peut aujourd'hui créer un compte via `/signup` ou en tapant directement `POST /users/add` — il faut fermer les deux portes, en urgence.

## Ce qui doit changer

**Front (**`/signup`**) :** la page et le formulaire restent affichés tels quels. Les 5 champs (email, mot de passe, confirmation, passphrase de récupération, confirmation) et le bouton d'inscription passent `disabled` — pas de bannière ni de message, on suit le pattern déjà établi sur `UserMenu` (item visible mais inerte). Le formulaire de connexion (`/login`) n'est pas concerné.

**API (**`POST /users/add`**) :** doit refuser la requête indépendamment de l'état du front, sinon la désactivation front n'est qu'une façade. Un appel direct à l'API doit être bloqué en 403, avant toute validation ou accès DB.

**Toggle :** une variable d'env de chaque côté, lue avec la même convention que `COOKIE_SECURE` (comparaison de string, pas de parsing booléen) :

* back : `SIGNUPS_ENABLED` (`!== "false"` → activé par défaut si absent, pour ne rien casser ailleurs)
* front : `NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNUPS_ENABLED` (même logique, nécessaire pour désactiver côté client)

Sur cette instance précisément, les deux sont mises à `"false"` dès ce ticket — c'est le but de l'urgence.

## Hors scope

* `POST /users/recover` (réinitialisation via passphrase) : ne crée pas de compte, reste actif.
* `/login` : non concerné.
* Aucun autre point d'entrée de création de compte n'existe (pas d'OAuth, pas de flux d'invitation).

Title: E2b — Near-plane polygon clipping with UV interpolation
Description:
Split off from E2 ([COS-236](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-236/e2-projection-orthographic-fov-and-clip-planes)), which added the near plane but rejects against it per triangle rather than clipping to it.

E2's `Camera.clips(z)` drops a whole triangle the moment any one of its three vertices falls outside the view volume. That is the right first move — it replaced a vertex behind the eye projecting mirrored across the vanishing point, which painted a smear, with a triangle that is simply not drawn. But the artefact it leaves is a **hole**: at zoom 100 the near cap of a sphere does not fade off the front of the frame, it vanishes a whole face at a time, and the silhouette that remains has a ragged edge that moves in steps rather than continuously.

Real clipping fixes that, and it is a genuine piece of work rather than a tightening of the test.

## Approach

Sutherland–Hodgman against the single near plane, in camera space, before projection.

A triangle straddling `d = near` falls into three cases:

* three vertices in front — emit it unchanged (the overwhelming majority, and the path that must stay free)
* three behind — emit nothing (what E2 already does)
* one or two in front — the intersection is a quad or a triangle, so **one or two triangles come out where one went in**

The parametric intersection along an edge is `t = (near − d_a) / (d_b − d_a)`, and every attribute is interpolated by the same `t`.

## Why it is not a two-line change

* `Triangle.render` **has to emit geometry it does not own.** Today a triangle projects three points it holds and fills one path. A clipped triangle is one or two *new* triangles whose vertices exist only for this frame, so either `render` grows a scratch buffer of projected vertices or the clip moves up into `Mesh.renderMesh`, which is where the painter's sort already lives. Deciding which is most of the design.
* **UVs interpolate too.** `src/primitives/Triangle.ts` carries `uva` / `uvb` / `uvc` straight into `AffineTextureMapper`, which solves an affine map from three vertex/UV pairs. A clipped fragment needs `uv = uv_a + t · (uv_b − uv_a)` per introduced vertex — correct here precisely because the interpolation is linear in camera space, not in screen space.
* **The material comes along.** Flat-filled fragments keep the parent's colour; textured ones keep the parent's texture key. Trivial, but it has to be carried rather than defaulted.
* **The counts move.** `Surface3D.render` returns drawn triangles; one submitted triangle can now draw as two, so the GEOMETRY card's `submitted − drawn` derivation (D6) stops being an over-count and starts being able to go negative. That derivation needs revisiting with this, and E6's real instrumentation is where the two counts finally separate.

## Constraints

* The fast path must stay fast: three depths compared, and an untouched triangle takes the same route it does today. The clip only allocates when it fires.
* Backface culling stays a 2D test on the projected result and is unaffected — the sign is preserved by the clip because every introduced vertex lies on an edge of the original.
* The far plane does not need this. It is inert across everything the two controls reach (E2 sets it at 5000 against a maximum reachable depth of ~4719), and a shape that crossed it would be beyond the point where a hole matters.
* E3b's depth buffer changes the shape of this: with a per-pixel depth key the clip still has to happen — a rasteriser cannot interpolate 1/d through a sign change either — but the fragments it emits go through a scanline pass rather than `ctx.fill()`. Landing E2b first is fine; landing it after E3b means writing it once against the rasteriser instead of twice.

## Done when

- [ ] A triangle straddling the near plane is split rather than dropped, and the silhouette edge moves continuously as the zoom slider crosses the plane
- [ ] Textured faces keep their mapping across the split: the cube's galaxy face shows no seam or jump at the clip boundary
- [ ] Three-in-front triangles allocate nothing and take the same path they do today
- [ ] Backface culling, the painter's sort and the opacity path all still work on emitted fragments
- [ ] The GEOMETRY card's culled derivation is corrected for a draw count that can now exceed the submitted count

Title: bkmk's database has no scheduled backup — only pre-deploy dumps exist
Description:
bkmk's database is dumped **only when the app is deployed**. There is no scheduled backup of any kind.

## Evidence, checked on ks-b 2026-08-05

* `crontab -l` as `debian` — empty. `sudo crontab -l` as root — empty.
* `systemctl list-timers --all` — nine timers, all of them system units (certbot, logrotate, apt, fstrim, e2scrub, man-db, tmpfiles, dpkg-db-backup). None belongs to bkmk.
* The repo has no scheduler: `@nestjs/schedule` is not a dependency of `backend/`, and there is no cron code anywhere in it.
* The only dumps on the box are the ones the deploy script writes:

```
/var/www/bkmk/db-backups/bkmkdump-pre-deploy-20260804-211205.sql
/var/www/bkmk/db-backups/bkmkdump-pre-deploy-20260805-010137.sql
```

So the recovery point is "the last time bkmk was deployed", and the data-loss window is however long it has been since. There is also no offsite copy — the dumps sit on the same VPS as the database they protect, so anything that takes the box takes both.

This was already known in the abstract: the Zeus backups spec (`docs/design/zeus-db-backups-addendum-prompt.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-zeus-db-backups-ticket.md`) records that "`bkmk` was meant to do the same and currently doesn't". This ticket is the concrete confirmation, with the check that proves it.

## Why Zeus will not catch this on its own

Zeus's cron activity feed ([COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus)) flags a cron that **was** reporting and stopped. It has nothing to say about one that never existed — no report means no row, and no row means nothing to be overdue. A missing backup job is invisible to it by construction.

That is worth knowing generally: the cron feed covers regression, not absence.

## What to do

pfa already solves exactly this, in ~60 lines, and it is worth copying rather than reinventing:

* `pfa/nest-api/src/infrastructure/db-backup/db-backup-cron.service.ts` — `@Cron("0 0 */12 * * *")`, `mysqldump` to a local path, then hands the file off.
* `pfa/nest-api/src/infrastructure/ssh-backup/ssh-backup.service.ts` — copies it to the backup VPS.

bkmk's API is moving to NestJS shortly, which is the natural moment: the service ports across with the config keys renamed, and nothing has to be written from scratch.

Two things to fix while copying, both visible in pfa's version:

1. **It fails silently.** The `catch` only calls `this.logger.error`, so a backup that has been failing for weeks looks exactly like one that works unless someone reads pm2's log. Report the run to Zeus instead (`docs/reporting/README.md` in the Zeus repo) — `ok` / `failed` / `skipped`, with the dump size in `detail`. Then a backup that stops working shows up on `/cron` as overdue or failed.
2. **It skips silently on missing config.** An early `return` when `DB_USER` / `PFA_DUMP_PATH` / the remote path are unset means a misconfigured deploy produces no backups and no signal. Report that case as `skipped` with a summary naming the missing key.

If Zeus's own centralised backups feature ships first (draft spec, not yet ticketed), it supersedes this — but that is not scheduled and this is a live data-loss exposure, so it should not wait on it.

## Done when

bkmk's database is dumped on a schedule, the dump reaches the offsite backup VPS, and a failed or skipped run is visible in Zeus rather than only in pm2's log.

Title: Report the DB backup cron to Zeus
Description:
Zeus's cron activity feed is live ([COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus)). pfa is the first app to adopt it, because it is the one with a real scheduled job already running.

## Why pfa first

`nest-api/src/infrastructure/db-backup/db-backup-cron.service.ts` runs `@Cron("0 0 */12 * * *")` — a `mysqldump` copied to the backup VPS, twice a day. Right now nothing about it is observable, in two distinct ways, and both are in the code:

* **A failure is only a log line.** The `catch` calls `this.logger.error("mysqlDump failed: ...")` and stops there. A backup that has been failing for three weeks looks exactly like one that works unless somebody reads pm2's log on purpose.
* **A misconfiguration is silent.** The method `return`s early when `config.enabled` is false, when `sshBackup.enabled` is false, or when any of `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` / `DB` / `PFA_DUMP_PATH` / `PFA_BACKUP_SERVER_PATH` is missing. A deploy that drops one env var produces no backups and no signal whatsoever.

Both become visible the moment the job reports, and the second one is exactly what Zeus's `skipped` status exists for.

## Scope

1. Copy `docs/reporting/zeus-report.ts` from the Zeus repo into `nest-api/src/infrastructure/zeus-report.ts`. Zero dependencies — it uses only `fetch`, `AbortSignal.timeout` and `process.env`, and needs no adapter or build step.
2. Add three variables to pfa's pm2 ecosystem file, and to `.env` for local:

```
ZEUS_INGEST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6600/api/cron-runs
ZEUS_INGEST_TOKEN=<the same value as Zeus's own ZEUS_INGEST_TOKEN>
ZEUS_APP_NAME=pfa
```

`pfa` already exists in Zeus's port registry, which is what the ingestion endpoint validates against. Unset token or app name makes the helper a silent no-op, so local development is unaffected.

3. Wrap the body of `handleDbBackup` in `withZeusReport("db-backup", "0 0 */12 * * *", ...)` and return an outcome rather than falling off the end:

| Situation | Report |
| -- | -- |
| Dump written and copied to the backup VPS | `ok`, summary naming the remote path, `detail` carrying the dump's size in bytes |
| Backup disabled, or a config key missing | `skipped`, summary naming the reason or the missing key |
| `mysqldump` or the ssh copy throws | `failed` — the wrapper reports it and rethrows, so existing error handling is untouched |

## Two things not to get wrong

* **Do not pass a timezone.** The `@Cron` pins none, so it fires in the process's zone — UTC on ks-b — which is exactly what Zeus assumes by default. Passing `Europe/Paris` would make Zeus expect every run two hours early in summer and flag a healthy job as overdue.
* `"0 0 */12 * * *"` **is a six-field expression** (seconds first). Zeus accepts five and six fields precisely because `@nestjs/schedule` emits both, so it is copied verbatim with no translation.

The contract, its rules and the responses are in `docs/reporting/README.md` in the Zeus repo. The client must never fail the job: fire-and-forget, 2s timeout, all errors swallowed — Zeus being down cannot break a backup.

## Done when

`/cron` shows `pfa / db-backup` with a run every twelve hours, a failed dump reads `failed` there instead of only in pm2's log, and a backup skipped for missing configuration says so. Any cron pfa grows later — the synthetic-users daily run of [COS-141](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-141/epic-synthetic-users-bots-qui-utilisent-lapp-comme-de-vrais-humains), for instance — wraps the same way and needs no further setup.

Title: Database migrations: apps sync their migration history to Zeus
Description:
**Phase:** Monitoring · new scope, designed in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-zeus-db-migrations-design.md`.

Today, knowing whether a migration actually applied to `pfa`'s database — or any other fleet app's — means SSH into ks-b and running that app's own status command by hand, one app at a time. There's no fleet-wide view and no record beyond each app's own local tracking table. This closes that gap the same way [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus) already did for cron.

* **Not one report per event, like cron — a sync, because a durable local record already exists.** Migration tools already keep their own history (Prisma's `_prisma_migrations`, bkmk's own `schema_migrations`, [COS-332](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-332/plat-06-runner-de-migrations-et-table-schema-migrations)). Rather than reporting one migration at a time as it happens, each app's deploy script reads its own tool's full known history and POSTs all of it to `POST /api/db-migrations` in one batch, every deploy. Zeus inserts whatever `(app, migration)` pairs it hasn't seen and silently skips the rest.
* **That one design choice buys backfill for free.** The first time any app's (newly added) sync step runs, everything it has ever applied is by definition new to Zeus — so that single request seeds its full history. There's no separate import tool to build or maintain. The same choice makes the feed self-healing: if Zeus is unreachable during one deploy, the next deploy's sync simply includes what was missed.
* **Why push, not Zeus polling its own read-only MySQL access (already used for the backups design):** migration tooling isn't uniform across the fleet — `pfa`/`conway`/`worldweathr`/`zeus` use Prisma, `bkmk` has its own hand-rolled runner, and both `1991chat` (mocked backend, a job-exercise app) and `hiwaysim` (front-only) have no database at all. Polling would mean a bespoke adapter per tool, forever; a normalized report doesn't care what ran the migration.
* **Auth, exposure, rate limit** — identical to cron and the external-calls design: shared secret `ZEUS_INGEST_TOKEN`, loopback-only, 60 req/min per app, reusing the existing guards (nothing new).
* **Data model** — one `DbMigration` row per individual migration, not per batch: app, migration name, status (`success`/`failed`), `appliedAt`, `durationMs`, `summary`, `detail`, plus `source` (`reported`/`backfilled`, assigned by Zeus depending on whether the app had any history before this request). No retention pruning — unlike cron runs, migrations are rare and permanently significant.
* **UI** — a third tab on the existing `/cron` page (alongside Cron and External calls), same summary-table-plus-feed shape, plus a section on App Detail.
* **Known gap, not solved here:** bkmk's own runner only ever records a *successful* migration — a failed one leaves no row anywhere to sync. Closing that needs a small addition to bkmk's runner or deploy script (see the design doc, open question 2).

Full design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-zeus-db-migrations-design.md`.

Done when: every migration ever applied to any fleet app's database — past or future — is visible in Zeus, per app, with its name, when it ran, whether it succeeded, and how long it took, without SSH.

Title: External API call observability: apps report dependency failures and rollups to Zeus
Description:
**Phase:** Monitoring · extends the reporting contract built for cron activity ([COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus)). Full design in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-zeus-external-api-calls-design.md`.

Apps in the fleet call third-party APIs — WorldWeathr calls Open-Meteo, and others will call others — and none of it is observable today. If a dependency starts erroring, or an app is approaching a provider's rate limit, nothing shows that until a user notices something broken downstream.

* **Two ingestion endpoints, not one — a deliberate call.** `POST /api/external-call-failures` reports each failure individually, immediately. `POST /api/external-call-rollups` reports a 5-minute aggregate (`totalCalls`, `failedCalls`, avg/max duration) per dependency actually called in that window. Reporting every call the way cron reports every run would blow past the existing 60 req/min/app throttle on success traffic alone and reproduce the raw log Zeus's own design brief excludes; rollups-only would answer reliability and quota but leave debugging with no browsable failure history. This shape gets all three (reliability, quota, debugging) without any one costing the others.
* `withExternalCall(api, fn)` wraps a call, counts every attempt in memory, reports a failure immediately (fire-and-forget, 2s timeout, rethrows unchanged — same three rules as cron reporting), and flushes the counters as one rollup per `api` slug every 5 minutes. A best-effort flush also fires on `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`, since pm2 restarts on every deploy and 5 minutes of counts would otherwise vanish on every release.
* **Auth, exposure** — identical to cron: shared secret, loopback-only, reuses `IngestTokenGuard` and the throttler guard (relocated to `nest-api/src/reporting/guards/`, not duplicated — cron's own controller is repointed at the same import, no behavior change).
* **Data model** — `ExternalApi` (auto-registers on the first report from a given app+api pair, never pruned — a dependency gone quiet for months should still show as one that exists, same as an idle cron job), `ExternalCallFailure` and `ExternalCallRollup` (append-only, and **kept forever by default, like cron runs** — a nightly prune job exists but deletes nothing unless `ZEUS_EXTERNAL_CALL_RETENTION_DAYS` is set, mirroring `ZEUS_CRON_RETENTION_DAYS`). Rollups are the heavier table — 288 rows a day per dependency — but half a million rows a year is nothing for MySQL, and a year of them is the only way to answer "was this dependency always this slow".
* **Health signal** — two states, not more: `healthy` (a rollup with zero failures, nothing failed since) or `failing` (a failure not yet covered by a later healthy rollup). No schedule to compare against here, unlike cron's overdue detection, so no third "overdue" state — a dash until the first report arrives for a dependency.
* **UI** — a second tab on the existing `/cron` page, same summary-table-plus-feed shape (sorted failing-first), plus a read-only section on App Detail.
* **Explicitly out of scope**: push notifications (cron's own push ticket doesn't exist yet either), configurable per-dependency quota thresholds, a fleet-dashboard "N dependencies failing" indicator (a future integration point, same as [COS-171](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-171/monitoring-dashboard-pm2-status-health-checks) was noted but not built for cron), and reporting every successful call individually — that's the log-viewer shape Zeus's design brief already excludes.

Done when: every external dependency any fleet app calls is visible in Zeus — whether it's currently healthy, its recent call and failure volume, and a browsable history of its failures — without SSH.

Title: Deploy activity log: apps report each deploy to Zeus
Description:
**Phase:** Monitoring · sibling to [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus), same reporting shape applied to a deploy instead of a cron run. Full design in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-zeus-deploy-activity-ticket.md` — lighter than [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus)'s own spec; several details below are genuinely still open and need settling during implementation, not guessed at here.

Zeus currently has no visibility into deploys at all. Every app on `ks-b` deploys through the same custom shell script (the one `pfa` already runs, and the one Zeus itself reuses for its own deploys per [COS-168](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-168/scaffold-zeus-next-front-nest-api-admin-only-auth-deploy-on-ks-b)) — not CI/CD, no pipeline, no third-party provider. Zeus just doesn't know what that script does: which build is live on each app, whether the last deploy succeeded, or what commits shipped.

* **Reuse** [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus)'s reporting architecture wholesale. The deploy script POSTs once, when it finishes, to a shared-secret, localhost-only endpoint — same auth model (shared secret, `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, never proxied publicly), same "`app` must already exist in the registry" guard, same non-negotiable rule that reporting must never fail the deploy if Zeus is unreachable.
* **Per report:** `app`, `buildNumber` (whatever the script already produces — unconfirmed, see below), `commits` (sha + message, since the last successful deploy), `status` (`success` / `failed` / `rolled_back`), `startedAt`, `durationMs`.
* **UI** — summary table (latest build/status per app) + reverse-chronological feed, filterable by app and status, mirroring `/cron`'s split. **Row click opens a modal** with the full commit list — a new interaction for Zeus (existing Audit rows expand inline instead), deliberate because a commit list needs more room than an inline expand gives it.
* **Zeus observes, never controls** — no trigger, retry, or rollback button. A rollback is something the deploy script itself decides and reports, the same boundary [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus) already draws for crons.
* Separate stream from the Audit log ([COS-172](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-172/process-control-startstoprestartreload-via-pm2-audit-log)), not a new Audit row type. Audit means an action *Zeus* performed; a deploy is the app's own script acting, reported passively. Net effect: `rolled back` will legitimately appear in both places for unrelated reasons (a reverted port reassignment vs. a reverted release) — worth one line of UI copy disambiguating them.
* **Narrows, not reverses, the design brief's "Deployment or CI features" exclusion** to read-only deploy observability only — the same call the cron feature already made for scheduling.

**The three open questions, answered while building (2026-08-07):**

1. **New top-level** `/deploys` **page.** The nav item, the route and the placeholder screen were already there from the mockup pass, so the decision had in effect been taken; this records it. No deploys panel on App Detail in this pass — one placement, not two.
2. **There is no build number on this fleet, and none was invented.** Both scripts build `RELEASE_NAME="release-${TIMESTAMP}-${GIT_BRANCH}-${GIT_HASH}"` and nothing else — no counter anywhere that could produce the mockup's `#128`. Zeus stores that release name as the build's identity: unique per deploy, and the name of a directory still on the box under `releases/`. The UI leads with the short commit hash and keeps the release name for the modal. A Zeus-side counter was considered and rejected — a number no other tool on the box would agree with, invented to match a mockup.
3. **Yes, the scripts already know their commits** — the answer that made this much smaller than expected. `write_deploy_log` already computes exactly the wanted range (`git log --no-merges` from a marker file holding the last deployed commit) to write the served changelog. Reporting reuses it. The one real dependency that fell out: the marker is on the server and gets moved at the end of a successful deploy, so the base is now resolved **once** at the top of `deploy()` and shared, or the changelog and the report would disagree.

**Also decided during implementation:**

* **One row per app *and role*, not per app.** Every app here deploys front and API through two separate scripts; the mockup's one-row-per-app table would have collapsed two independent histories and shown whichever was newer.
* **The summary table is built from the registry**, not from deploy rows — so a service that has never reported says so. A table built from reports cannot show the apps that aren't reporting, which is the first thing worth knowing.
* **Two paths:** `POST /api/deploy-reports` (write, `deny all` in nginx) and `GET /api/deploys` (read, session). One path could not have been both.
* **The report is sent from ks-b over ssh**, since the endpoint is loopback-only and a deploy script runs on a laptop. The URL and token are read there from Zeus's own `.env`, so no repository carries either.
* **A manual** `./deploy-*.sh rollback` **reports too**, as `rolled_back` with no commits — it changes what is live.

**What shipped**

* Schema: `Deploy` + `DeployCommit` + `DeployStatus`, migration `20260806222144_deploy_activity`.
* `IngestModule` — the shared secret, rate limit and guards, extracted out of `cron/` so both reporters use one copy.
* `deploys` module: ingest, summary, filtered feed, per-deploy detail. 8 new tests, 82 passing.
* `/deploys` screen: summary table + feed, filters by app/role/status in the URL, row click opens the commit modal (the first modal-instead-of-inline-expand in Zeus).
* Both deploy scripts report success / failed / rolled_back, with the commit range.
* Docs: reporting contract, DEPLOY.md setup, §7 of the design brief narrowed rather than contradicted.

**Live on ks-b 2026-08-07.** Deployed, migration applied, and `/deploys` is showing rows. Verified before that against a scratch database end to end: the real script client → `202` → summary, filtered feed and per-deploy detail, plus every rejection case (`401` no/bad token, `400` unknown app, bad role, bad status, short sha, bad date) and commit-message escaping against quotes, backslashes, `$`, backticks, tabs and emoji.

Done when: every deploy of every fleet app is visible in Zeus — build number, status (including rollback), and the commits it shipped — without SSH.

Title: Database backups: on-demand local dump + history
Description:
**Phase:** Control (same category as [COS-172](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-172/process-control-startstoprestartreload-via-pm2-audit-log), [COS-173](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-173/safe-port-reassignment-ecosystem-nginx-reload-atomic-rollback)) — not Monitoring. First of two tickets from the same design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-zeus-db-backups-ticket.md`); the second is offsite replication, tracked separately and blocked by this one. A third, optional idea in that doc — scheduled/automatic dumps — is deliberately not ticketed yet; it's additive to this one whenever it's wanted.

Today, backing up an app's database means SSH into `ks-b`, finding the right connection string, and running `mysqldump` by hand — no record of which apps have ever been backed up, when, or whether the last dump actually succeeded.

* **A control action, not an observation** — the opposite shape from cron/deploy activity, which are apps reporting themselves passively. Here the owner asks *Zeus* to go do something, the same category as process control ([COS-172](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-172/process-control-startstoprestartreload-via-pm2-audit-log)) and port reassignment ([COS-173](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-173/safe-port-reassignment-ecosystem-nginx-reload-atomic-rollback)). Zeus already reads and writes files on other apps' behalf for port reassignment; this extends that same "Zeus acts directly on the box" capability to running `mysqldump` against another app's database.
* **One shared MySQL instance, one schema per app** (same topology locally and on `ks-b`) means Zeus needs exactly one dedicated, read-only MySQL credential plus an app→schema lookup — not a secret pulled from every app's own `.env`.
* `/backups` **page**: one button per app, "Dump now," plus a fleet-wide reverse-chronological history (status, file path, size, duration). Session-authenticated ([COS-168](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-168/scaffold-zeus-next-front-nest-api-admin-only-auth-deploy-on-ks-b)) — not the shared-secret ingestion pattern cron/deploy use, since this is Zeus acting on its owner's request, not another app reporting in.
* **Data model** — `db_dump`: status (`running`/`success`/`failed`), `triggeredBy` (`manual` for now), timing, `filePath`, `fileSizeBytes`, `checksumSha256` (confirms a copied file wasn't truncated), `errorMessage`.
* **Retention is count-based, not time-based** — a dump's cost is disk space and dumps vary wildly in size. Keep the last `ZEUS_BACKUP_RETENTION_COUNT` (default 7, needs a real-disk-budget check) successful dumps per app; failed dumps prune after 7 days regardless.
* **Every trigger and outcome gets an Audit log entry** — deliberately the opposite call from cron/deploy activity: this *is* Zeus performing an action on the box, the same category as a `pm2 restart`. The dedicated `/backups` page still exists for the size/checksum/duration detail an Audit one-liner can't hold.
* **Security**: a partial dump from a disk-full or killed `mysqldump` is deleted and recorded `failed`, never left as a truncated file that looks complete. `POST /api/apps/zeus/dumps` is rejected server-side, not just hidden in the UI — Zeus's own database lives in the same shared instance, and dumping it is a deliberate exclusion enforced at the query level, not just the UI.
* **Explicitly out of scope**: image/asset backup (a separate, not-yet-scoped flow), downloading the dump file through the Zeus UI (the path is shown, copyable — fetch it over `scp`), restoring from a dump (a much higher-risk action deserving its own design pass), and dumping Zeus's own database.

**Open questions to settle during implementation:**

1. The app→schema mapping convention inside the shared MySQL instance — derivable, or does the registry need an explicit `dbName` field?
2. `hiwaysim` is front-only and almost certainly has no schema — the app list must exclude no-database apps outright or show an explicit "no database configured" state, never a silently disabled button.
3. Nav placement — a sixth top-level item, or a section on App Detail?
4. Is 7 dumps/app the right retention default for the real disk budget on `ks-b`?

Done when: every fleet app with a database can be dumped on demand from Zeus, without SSH, and every dump — past or present, successful or failed — is visible in one list with its file path, size, and duration.
Creator: cosmokaat@protonmail.com

Title: Database backups: manual offsite replication
Description:
**Phase:** Control — second of two tickets from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-zeus-db-backups-ticket.md`. Depends on [COS-426](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-426/database-backups-on-demand-local-dump-history) (local dump + history) — this reuses its dump mechanism and data model rather than duplicating either.

A separate Debian VPS already exists purely to hold backups. `pfa` already pushes there twice a day via its own cron (dump + images together); `bkmk`'s equivalent is currently broken; no other app has this at all. This ticket adds a manual, on-demand path to the same destination.

* **Zeus performs the whole pipeline itself** — dump (reusing [COS-426](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-426/database-backups-on-demand-local-dump-history)'s mechanism) then push over SSH using its own dedicated credentials — rather than re-triggering `pfa`'s or `bkmk`'s existing scripts. Deliberate: gating this feature on each app having its own working script would mean it can't reach `bkmk` until that broken script is fixed. Zeus owning it once, generically, is what gets every app with a database to offsite replication, no new per-app script required.
* **Two endpoints**: a composite "Send to offsite backup" action (dump, then push — two-step progress reusing [COS-173](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-173/safe-port-reassignment-ecosystem-nginx-reload-atomic-rollback)'s step-list UI component) and a standalone re-push of an existing successful dump (the retry path when only the push failed, or catching up an older dump without paying for a fresh `mysqldump`).
* **Data model** — `db_dump_offsite_push`, referencing `db_dump` rather than duplicating its columns: status, timing, `remotePath`, `remoteSizeBytes` (compared against the local dump's size — a mismatch is treated as `failed`, not silently accepted).
* **Security** — Zeus's SSH credential to the backup VPS is its own dedicated, least-privilege key scoped to write only under its own path, not a copy of whatever key `pfa`'s cron already uses — so a compromise of Zeus's key can't touch `pfa`'s existing backups on that box. A dump is only ever pushed after `mysqldump` has fully succeeded and its local checksum is recorded — never mid-write.
* **Explicitly does not**: touch or replace `pfa`'s or `bkmk`'s existing twice-daily crons (this is an additional path to the same destination, not a replacement), or manage anything already on the backup VPS (no listing, no pruning, no reading back what's there — Zeus only writes).
* Images remain out of scope here too, same reasoning as [COS-426](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-426/database-backups-on-demand-local-dump-history).

**Open questions to settle during implementation:**

1. How does `pfa`'s existing cron actually reach the backup VPS today (rsync over SSH, plain `scp`, something else) and under which user/key? Worth mirroring that transport mechanism, even with a different key.
2. What path convention does the backup VPS already use for `pfa`'s (and `bkmk`'s) files? Zeus's pushes should land somewhere recognizable, not a second parallel layout invented for this ticket — `/backups/<app>/<ISO timestamp>/db.sql.gz` is a reasonable default to confirm, not assume.

Done when: any fleet app with a database can have a fresh dump manually pushed to the existing offsite backup VPS from Zeus, without SSH and without depending on a per-app script — closing the gap where only `pfa` (and, once fixed, `bkmk`) had this at all.

Title: Lint and format the front e2e directory
Description:
`front/package.json`'s lint scripts only covered `./src` and `./styles`, so the `./e2e` directory was never linted or formatted. Formatting drift landed on main unnoticed.

## Change

Widen both scripts to include `./e2e`:

```
"lint": "biome check ./src ./styles ./e2e",
"lint:fix": "biome check --write ./src ./styles ./e2e",
```

`pnpm lint:fix` reformats one pre-existing violation: an array-join expression in `e2e/markdown-editor.spec.ts` that biome breaks across lines.

## Verification

* `pnpm lint` clean — 81 files checked, no fixes applied.
* `pnpm test:e2e` — 16 passed.

## nest-api: checked, no equivalent gap

Its lint script is `eslint "{src,test}/**/*.ts" --fix`. All four `*.spec.ts` files live in `src/` and are reached by that glob (confirmed via `eslint -f json`); `eslint.config.mjs` only ignores `eslint.config.mjs`, `generated/**`, `dist/**`. Spec files are covered.

## Follow-ups found but not fixed here

1. nest-api's `prisma.config.ts` and `scripts/seed.ts` sit outside the `{src,test}` glob — same shape of gap as `e2e` was.
2. nest-api's `lint` bakes in `--fix`, so there is no check-only mode; a CI lint gate would rewrite files instead of failing.
3. nest-api's `test:e2e` points at `./test/jest-e2e.json`, but no `test/` directory exists — the script is dangling.
4. `front/e2e/project-form.spec.ts` derives its project key as `TST` + 2 digits from `Date.now()` (`.slice(0, 5)` truncates the intended 3). Only 100 possible keys, so it 409s against its own archived leftovers — it failed once during this work and passed on rerun.

Title: E1c — Separate the camera from the turntable spin, and move the world with it
Description:
Fallout from E1a/E1b ([COS-237](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-237>), [COS-238](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-238>)) and E5a ([COS-246](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-246>)), all found by driving the console rather than by reading it. Five faults, one root cause: **the rig conflated the viewpoint with the object's own attitude**, so every consumer downstream of it read a matrix that meant two different things at once.

`CameraRig.matrix()` returned `C·S` — the camera composed with the turntable — and everything took it: the meshes (correct), the camera readouts (wrong, they drifted with the spin), and after E5a the ground would have taken it too, which would have tumbled the floor and the sky along with the solid.

## The five faults

1. **Shapes arrive flat.** E1a's defaults were three real zeros, which puts the eye in the object's equatorial plane — a cube is a square at the moment it appears. The per-frame rates it replaced were off-centre on all three axes precisely so that could never happen.
2. **Horizontal drag inverted.** The spec for E1b (`notes/ui-refonte/engine/e1-camera-rig.md`) specified `yaw += dx * 0.4` and E1b shipped it faithfully. `Matrix3D`'s yaw sends the front-facing vertex `(0, 0, −r)` to `(−r·sinθ, …)`, so a positive yaw swings the grabbed face left and the shape runs away from the cursor. The bug originates in the spec, so the spec is where it has to be corrected.
3. **The turntable wanders.** Growing three Euler angles linearly and recomposing them every frame is not a fixed-axis rotation: the effective axis moves as the angles grow, so the solid turns one way, then another, then another. It looks like a tumble in a screenshot and is not one in motion.
4. **Drag stops at 180°, and it turns the shape.** Both are the same mistake — the drag wrote an object rotation, clamped to a half turn, when the gesture the user is making is a camera move.
5. **The world stands still.** After E5a the ground projects through the shared camera, but nothing handed it one: the floor, the grid and the sky held their own frame, so a drag turned the solid inside a scene that never moved. Dropping the camera below the plane then exposed three more — a grey band where the ground was discarded whole, a floor the sky showed through, and the solid drawn on top of the floor it was standing under.

## The shape of the fix

`meshMatrix()` **=** `C·S`**,** `viewMatrix()` **=** `C` **alone.** `matrix()` and `eulerDegrees()` (a dead duplicate of `angles()`) both go. The camera readouts, the axis gizmo and `eyePosition` move onto `C`; the meshes keep `C·S`; the background takes `C`.

**The spin becomes an accumulated matrix, not three angles.** One Rodrigues rotation about a fixed axis (`Matrix3D.axisAngleMatrix`), at the legacy proportions — 87 / 122 / 48 °/s, normalised. Composing three per-axis deltas instead would be close but not equal: they do not commute, so the composed axis shifts with the step size and the tumble drifts with the frame rate. `R(a)·R(b) = R(a+b)` about one axis is what makes it exact, and `src/camera/__tests__/CameraRig.test.ts` asserts it two ways — constant angle per unit time, and the same attitude whether an interval is stepped 5 times or 500.

**Euler order is** `roll·pitch·yaw`**, not** `roll·yaw·pitch`**.** The ground's normal in camera space is column 1 of the camera matrix; under the old order that column carries yaw, so turning left and right tipped the horizon by up to 22° with ROLL reading zero. Under the new one the horizon is yaw-free: `offset = f·tan(pitch)`, `tilt = roll`.

**The ground projects through** `C`**.** `GroundProjection` transforms the world point `(x, GROUND_Y, z)` before dividing — the same arithmetic `Point3D.setFromSource` runs on a vertex — and derives the vanishing line from the plane's normal rather than from a hardcoded horizon. `GroundNearClip` (new) trims the sheet to the near plane in the ground's *own* coordinates: `depthAt` is affine over `(x, z)`, so the crossing parameter is exact and no subdivision is needed. Clipping the projected points instead would be invalid — the projection is a divide, so lerping two projected endpoints does not interpolate the same line.

**The sky pans with yaw.** A cylindrical panorama of focal `f` is `2πf` wide, so one radian of yaw is exactly `f` pixels of pan. The asset is a square photograph rather than a 360° equirectangular one, so alternate tiles are mirrored to make it continue, and its top and bottom rows are clamped outward — the photograph is finite vertically, and once the horizon slides down its top edge exposed the bare gradient behind it.

**Under the plane, the ground paints over the meshes.** With no depth buffer the painting order *is* the depth test, and from below the floor lies between the eye and everything standing on it. `Surface3D` calls `renderGroundOverlay` after the mesh loop; it is a no-op while the eye is above the plane.

## Known limit, deliberately taken

The overlay treats the ground as entirely in front of every mesh whenever the eye is below it. That is exact while the solids sit above the floor — always true today, since the registry centres them on the origin and the floor is 175 units down — and wrong for a mesh straddling the plane. Per-triangle ordering against the ground is a depth-buffer job and belongs with E3b, not here.

## Also carried

* `DEFAULT_SPIN_DEGREES_PER_SECOND` 24 → 122, `SPIN_MAX` 120 → 244 so the default sits mid-track.
* The pitch clamp comes off the rig: the drag is a camera move now, and a camera that cannot pass overhead is the same 180° cage in a different place.
* Double-tap reset restores the shared defaults rather than three literal zeros, and leaves the turntable running — it is a camera gesture, so snapping the object's attitude too reads as the shape jerking for a gesture aimed at the viewpoint.

## Verification

`typecheck`, `lint`, `lint:rules` 10/10, 82 tests across 11 files, `build`. QA in headless Chrome over a six-pose pitch sweep (0, −25, −32, −36, −45, −70): above the plane the sky is continuous and the floor solid with the solid visible; below it the floor covers the solid completely. No console errors.
