Title: Picker list: fill the height available, and make the sections actually visible
Description:
Follow-up to [COS-409](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-409/group-the-primitive-picker-into-families-and-decide-where-a-shapes>), which shipped the sections. Two things it got right in the data model and wrong on screen, both visible the moment [COS-201](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-201/epic-polyhedra-from-the-symmetries-of-things) pushed the registry to eighteen shapes.

## 1. The list was a fixed 320px, and the panel had room for four times that

`--size-picker-max-h: 320px` is a **fixed height** — the one thing `notes/ui-refonte`'s sizing rule forbids ("a preferred value plus a floor, never a fixed width or height"). On a desktop inspector it stopped the open list at seven of eighteen rows with hundreds of pixels of empty panel underneath it.

**Fixed by making it the fluid form the rule asks for.** `--size-picker-min-h` is now the floor; above it the list takes the space that is actually there.

The measurement cannot be done in CSS — the list is `position: absolute`, so where its top lands depends on where the whole inspector was laid out. `ShapePicker` measures on every open and publishes the raw distance as `--size-picker-space-below`; `inspector.css` subtracts its own gutter token and clamps against the floor, so no spacing value leaks into JS.

**The measurement is taken against the clipping box, not the viewport, and that is the correctness of it.** `.inspector__body` is `overflow: auto`. A list grown to the bottom of the *window* would not overflow the panel and scroll internally — it would lengthen the panel's own scroll content, and the rows past the fold would be reached by scrolling the inspector rather than the list. Which is the behaviour the change exists to remove. `ShapePicker` walks up to the nearest scrolling ancestor and measures to its bottom edge, falling back to the viewport when nothing clips. Found rather than named: hardcoding `.inspector__body` would tie a control that knows only its own root to one panel's markup.

## 2. Scrolling into a section showed no section

The headings were dim, small, mono, with a `margin-top` between groups — quiet enough that a screenshot taken mid-list showed no grouping at all. With eighteen shapes in eight-character abbreviations, a run of `KISRHDOD / TRCUBOCT / ICOSIDOD / RHOMBTRI / KISRHTRI` with nothing on screen naming the section is exactly the scanning problem [COS-409](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-409/group-the-primitive-picker-into-families-and-decide-where-a-shapes) set out to fix.

**Headings are now** `position: sticky` **with a hairline rule.** The containing block is the group, not the list, so each heading stops at its own section's bottom edge and is pushed out by the next rather than five of them piling up. The opaque background is load-bearing, not decorative — options scroll under it.

**The old** `margin-top` **between groups is gone, deliberately.** A margin above a sticky element leaves a transparent strip at the stuck position with the previous section's rows sliding through it. The label's own padding is the air instead, and the hairline is what separates the sections.

## 3. The taxonomy: UNCATEGORIZED and KNOTS

| Section | Shapes |
| -- | -- |
| UNCATEGORIZED | sphere, cube, pyramid, cross |
| POLYHEDRA | the eight Conway solids |
| KNOTS | torusKnot, torusKnot25, torusKnot27, torusKnot34 |
| FRACTALS | menger |
| SURFACES | donut |

**PRIMITIVES became UNCATEGORIZED.** Those four are the engine's demo shapes and have no mathematical family in common; the old name implied one. It leads the list rather than trailing it, so the boot shape is still the first row and a newcomer's section is not below eight near-identically spelled polyhedra.

**KNOTS was folded out of SURFACES**, which is the split [COS-410](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-410/ship-the-torus-knot-family-5-7-and-8-alongside-the-trefoil>) argued for when it landed the three new knots. Four shapes of one construction is a section; leaving them beside the donut made SURFACES the second-largest family while saying nothing about what its members shared.

FRACTALS and SURFACES hold one shape each. Both look thin and both stay: each is the correct home for the next shape of its kind, and merging them now would only be unpicked later — the same ruling [COS-409](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-409/group-the-primitive-picker-into-families-and-decide-where-a-shapes) made about FRACTALS.

## Files

* `src/styles/tokens/sizing.css` — `--size-picker-max-h` → `--size-picker-min-h`
* `src/styles/inspector.css` — fluid `max-height`, sticky heading rule
* `src/ui/inspector/ShapePicker.ts` — `publishSpaceBelow()` and `clipBottom()`
* `src/data/shapeFamilies.ts` — the new ordered section table
* `src/data/shapeInfo.ts` — `family` on all eighteen entries

## Done when

- [X] The open list grows into the room under it and stops at the panel edge, never at a fixed height
- [X] No fixed height token remains for the picker; the floor is the only literal
- [X] The section you are scrolled into is always named on screen
- [X] Sections are UNCATEGORIZED / POLYHEDRA / KNOTS / FRACTALS / SURFACES, in that order, registry order preserved within each
- [X] `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `lint:rules` pass
- [ ] **Visual QA — mine to confirm.** The Chrome extension was not connected in the session that built this, so the sticky headings, the grown list and the section order have not been looked at in a browser. Everything above is verified statically only.

Title: Migrate the list URL state onto nuqs
Description:
Correcting the record for `V1` ([COS-277](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-277/v1-filter-bar-with-url-state)), `I4` ([COS-274](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-274/i4-display-properties-and-ordering)) and `P6` ([COS-265](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-265/p6-saved-views-api)), all three of which specify nuqs.

nuqs was installed and `NuqsAdapter` was mounted in `providers.tsx`, but nothing used it: the URL state was hand-rolled on `useSearchParams` + `router.push` with its own serialisers. Those three tickets were closed describing something that was not built.

## What changed

* `list-params.ts` — one nuqs parser map, read by the Server Components and the client hook alike. `createLoader` accepts Next's plain `searchParams` object as well as `URLSearchParams`, so `parseIssueFilters` and `parseDisplayOptions` kept their signatures and no page changed.
* `use-list-view.ts` — `useQueryStates(LIST_PARSERS, { shallow: false, history: "push" })`. Both options are off by default in nuqs; `shallow: true` would update the URL and leave the rows alone.
* `DEFAULT_DISPLAY` is derived from the parsers rather than restated beside them.

## What deliberately did not change

The write path stays hand-rolled. `issueFiltersToApiQuery` and `applyDisplayToApiQuery` extend the same `URLSearchParams` the URL writer produces with `project` and `orderBy` — the two keys the views API refuses by name inside a stored query. Keeping those serialisers separate is the structural reason they cannot leak into a saved view.

## Honest scope

This deletes no parsing logic. Not one stock nuqs parser matched the existing contract — `parseAsArrayOf` drops repeated keys, `parseAsBoolean` never returns null, `parseAsInteger` turns `priority=2.5` into a real priority. Every key needed a custom parser wrapping the rules already in `query-params`. What nuqs buys is one definition for both read paths and a simpler hook: a plumbing win, not a rules win.

## Done when

The URL state runs through nuqs, the three original spec files need no edits, and the saved-view round-trip is unaffected. 197 → 230 unit tests; 33 of the new ones pin rules that were true but unpinned, written against the old code first.

Title: Report bkmk's mysqldump cron to Zeus
Description:
bkmk's `mysqlDump` cron has run every twelve hours since April and Zeus has never heard of it. Confirmed on the box on 2026-08-06: the log shows an unbroken run every 00:00 and 12:00 UTC, `/home/bkmk/mysqldump/bkmkdump.sql` is stamped `2026-08-06 00:00:00`, and `pm2 env 4 | grep ZEUS` returns nothing.

The three env vars alone would have changed nothing — they configure a client that did not exist in bkmk. pfa reports because it has the helper copied into its source *and* wraps its job with it ([COS-422](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-422/report-the-db-backup-cron-to-zeus)). This is the same two-step for bkmk, plus one thing pfa did not need.

## What shipped

**1 — the CommonJS client.** `docs/reporting/zeus-report.ts` is TypeScript/ESM and bkmk's backend is CommonJS, so this is the second client in a new language, which `docs/reporting/README.md` explicitly invites. It landed in both repos: `backend/src/helpers/zeusReport.js` in bkmk, and `docs/reporting/zeus-report.js` in Zeus for the next non-Nest app, with a new *JavaScript, CommonJS* section under **Implementations**.

**2 —** `cron-mysql.js` **awaits its own work.** The job was callback-style: `exec` fired, and the offsite `sshCopyDB` happened inside its callback. Wrapped as-is it would have reported `ok` in about a millisecond, before `mysqldump` had written a byte, and would never have seen a failed copy. It is now promise-based end to end, reporting `db-backup` with schedule `0 0 */12 * * *` and no timezone (the `CronJob` pins none, so it fires in the box's zone, which is what Zeus assumes).

**3 —** `sshRaw.copyDB` **returns a promise.** It has to settle for the report to mean anything: a copy that only logged its own failure would be reported as a success — the exact shape of the bug [COS-411](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-411/plat-08-mise-en-production-du-refacto-graphite-scripts-de-deploiement) fixed one layer up, where the dump was fine and what got shipped was not.

⚠️ It also gained `conn.on("error")`, which it never had. ssh2 emits `error` on an unreachable host and an unhandled `error` event throws out of the event loop, so before this a backup server that was down did not fail the copy, **it killed the API**. `connection()` in the same file still has that hole for `copy` and `deleteFile` — the screenshot backup path — which is worth its own ticket.

**4 — the tick catches.** `withZeusReport` reports `failed` and then rethrows, and `node-cron` does not absorb a rejected tick the way `@nestjs/schedule` does. Without a `.catch` there, wrapping a previously silent job would have turned its first failure into a process crash. The README now says so where the next person will read it.

## Reported outcomes

| Situation | Report |
| -- | -- |
| Dump written and copied offsite | `ok`, summary naming the dump path and its size, `detail` carrying bytes and destination |
| `mysqldump` exits non-zero | `failed`, summary carrying stderr — the copy is skipped, as before |
| The ssh copy fails or times out | `failed`, naming it. The local dump is good either way, but an offsite copy that silently stopped moving is the failure worth being told about |

No `skipped` case: unlike pfa, this job has no `enabled` flag and no early returns.

## Verified locally

* The client against a fake ingest server: correct payload and bearer header, `failed` reported *and* rethrown, silent no-op when unconfigured, survives Zeus being unreachable.
* `0 0 */12 * * *` accepted by `cron@2.4.4`, and read the same way by Zeus's `cron-parser` — previous fires 2026-08-06T00:00Z and 2026-08-05T12:00Z, a 12-hour interval. `cronstrue` renders it "on the hour, every 12 hours", matching pfa's row.
* `copyDB` against an unroutable host: rejects with "Timed out while waiting for handshake" instead of crashing the process.
* `pnpm lint` in bkmk: no new errors (2 pre-existing, unrelated), one pre-existing warning removed.

## Done when

Deployed via `./deploy-api.sh` — the three variables are in `ecosystem.config.prod.js`, which is gitignored and scp'd as `ecosystem.config.js`, and pm2 reloads with `--update-env` — and `/cron` shows `bkmk / db-backup` alongside `pfa / db-backup` after the next 00:00 or 12:00 UTC run.

Title: Un serveur de backup injoignable tue l'API sur le chemin screenshots
Description:
`connection()` dans `backend/src/helpers/sshRaw.js` crée un client ssh2 sans écouteur `error`. ssh2 émet `error` quand l'hôte est injoignable ou que le handshake expire, et un événement `error` non écouté est levé hors de la boucle d'événements : un serveur de backup éteint ne faisait donc pas échouer la copie, **il tuait le process de l'API**. La fonction n'appelait jamais `conn.end()` non plus, donc chaque screenshot sauvegardé laissait fuir une connexion pour la durée de vie du process.

Trou identifié dans [COS-432](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-432/report-bkmks-mysqldump-cron-to-zeus), qui a fermé le même trou sur `copyDB` et laissait les deux autres appelants : `copy` (la sauvegarde offsite des screenshots) et `deleteFile`.

## Ce qui a été fait

**1 —** `connection()` prend un label et passe `(sftp, done)` à son appelant. Il câble `conn.on("error")`, `sftp.on("error")` et un `done()` idempotent qui appelle `conn.end()` une seule fois — le garde-fou compte, parce qu'un transfert qui échoue fait généralement suivre une erreur socket, donc `done` est rappelé sur un client déjà fermé.

**2 — L'échec remonte par un log, pas par un rejet.** Les deux appelants sont fire-and-forget : `jimpHelper.createScreenshot` n'attend pas la sauvegarde, et `deleteFile` n'a aucun appelant. Leur rendre une promesse rejetée aurait juste troqué un `error` non écouté contre un rejet non géré — le même crash déguisé. `copyDB` rend une promesse précisément parce que `cron-mysql.js` l'attend, lui.

**3 —** `copy` **garde sa signature** et ses deux `setTimeout` de 60 s (le contournement des images 0 octet envoyées depuis un téléphone). `screenshotsBackup.js` n'est pas touché.

**4 — Deux autres chemins de crash fermés au passage.** `mkdir` faisait `throw mkdirErr` : levé depuis un callback sftp, il n'y a plus personne sur la pile pour l'attraper, donc un disque plein sur le serveur de backup tuait l'API aussi sûrement qu'un serveur injoignable. Et `sftp.on("error")` couvre le cas où le put atterrit sur un flux mort pendant l'attente de 60 s.

## Vérifié en local

* `copy` et `deleteFile` contre `192.0.2.1` (TEST-NET-1, RFC 5737, jamais routable) : les deux loggent `Timed out while waiting for handshake`, le process survit, et `active handles: 0` — donc `conn.end()` a bien libéré les sockets.
* Contrôle négatif sur le code d'avant, même sonde : `UNCAUGHT EXCEPTION — process would have died`.
* `pnpm lint` : 2 erreurs, les deux préexistantes dans `errorHandlerMiddleware.js`. Le seul diagnostic sur `sshRaw.js` est un *info* préexistant ligne 2 (`require("fs")` → `node:fs`), hors du diff.

## Done when

Déployé via `./deploy-api.sh`, et une sauvegarde de screenshot passe toujours en production.

Title: E1d — Give the shape back its own orientation, and the camera rows of its own
Description:
SHAPE ▸ TRANSFORM's PITCH / YAW / ROLL rows move the *camera*. They should move the shape.

This is not refactoring drift — E1a ([COS-237](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-237/e1a-camera-rig-absolute-orientation-view-presets-and-camera-readouts)) converted them deliberately, and said so in its own Unblocks list: "the TRANSFORM sliders' degree labels: PITCH / YAW / ROLL RATE become absolute angles". At that moment it was defensible: the rig had just been built and the three rows were the only way to move the viewpoint. Then E1b ([COS-238](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-238/e1b-pointer-orbit-wheel-zoom-pinch-and-double-tap)) shipped drag orbit, wheel zoom, pinch and double-tap, and nobody went back to reconsider the rows it had made redundant. The legacy console before both of them (`rotateMesh`, `src/index.ts` L423–L440) applied three per-frame rotations to the mesh: these were shape controls, and the whole time they have been sitting under a tab called SHAPE.

The giveaway is inside the section itself. SPIN, the row directly beneath the three, *does* drive the object — `CameraRig.meshMatrix()` (L159) composes `viewMatrix · spinMatrix`, and the spin accumulator never touches `viewMatrix()`. One TRANSFORM section, three rows on the camera and a fourth on the object.

This ticket puts the three rows back on the mesh, gives the camera its own ELEV / AZIM / ROLL rows in WORLD ▸ CAMERA, and splits the rig so that the class named after the camera stops holding object state.

## Approach

### Split the rig

`CameraRig` is at 153 code lines against the house style's ~160 split threshold, so the object pose would push it over regardless. The stronger argument is the name: it already owns `spinMatrix`, which is object state.

* `src/camera/CameraRig.ts` keeps the camera alone — pitch/yaw/roll, `targetPosition`, the preset tween, `viewMatrix()`, `eyePosition()`, `axisScreenDirections()`, `angles()`. `spinDegreesPerSecond`, `spinMatrix`, `deltaSpin`, `zeroSpin` and the three `SPIN_AXIS_*` constants leave.
* `src/scene/ShapeRig.ts` — new. The shape's own pitch/yaw/roll rest pose, the spin rate, the spin accumulator, `matrix()`, `advance(dt)`, `setAngles()`, `reset()`.

New `@scene` alias, declared in **both** `tsconfig.json` and `vite.config.js` or the build breaks. E7 ([COS-248](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-248/e7-scene-model-real-scene-objects-per-object-visibility-selection-and)) is the scene-model ticket that will populate that directory properly; this is the first file in it, not a directory invented for one class.

### The composition

`ShapeRig.matrix()` returns `S · O` — the object posed, then spun. `CameraRig.meshMatrix(objectMatrix)` returns `viewMatrix() · objectMatrix`, so the multiply stays inside the class that owns `Matrix3D` and `Main` does no matrix arithmetic of its own.

The order is `C · S · O` and it is a decision, not an accident. `O` poses the object; `S` then spins that posed object about the world-fixed axis the SPIN row already documents. The alternative `C · O · S` would tilt the spin axis whenever PITCH moved — a turntable whose platter tips when you reposition the object standing on it.

**Flag for QA rather than letting it read as a regression:** at the default SPIN of 122 °/s the shape tumbles on all three axes, so re-posing it *inside* that tumble is hard to perceive. The three rows are legible only once SPIN is pulled toward 0. This is a real consequence of absolute angles replacing rates — the legacy rows were rates and so were always visible — and it is the one thing about this change that will read as "the sliders do nothing".

### Defaults: the first frame must not change

The ISO defaults move rather than being restated. `DEFAULT_PITCH_DEGREES` / `DEFAULT_YAW_DEGREES` / `DEFAULT_ROLL_DEGREES` (30 / 45 / 0) leave `TransformSection` and become `DEFAULT_CAM_ELEV_DEGREES` / `DEFAULT_CAM_AZIM_DEGREES` / `DEFAULT_CAM_ROLL_DEGREES` on `CameraSection`. The shape's three rows default to 0. The mesh matrix at t=0 becomes `C · I · I` where it was `C · I` — pixel-identical opening frame, and the whole reasoning block in `TransformSection` about why zero was tried first and is wrong moves across with the numbers, because it is an argument about the *camera's* arrival pose and is still correct there.

This is forced, not chosen: `BackgroundRenderer` draws the ground through `rig.viewMatrix()` (`Main.ts` L768), so a camera resting at elevation 0 would put the floor edge-on.

### Vocabulary: rows are renamed, the maths is not

The rows read ELEV / AZIM / ROLL. The engine keeps `EulerDegrees { pitch, yaw, roll }` — `cameraLabels.eulerDegreesLabel`, `ViewportHUD.setCamera`, `viewPresets` and `CameraWidget` are unchanged, because Euler angles are Euler angles and `cam.rot` prints three degrees either way. The translation happens in exactly one place, `CameraSection`, and the line is deliberate: the console names these for what the user does with them, the maths names them for what they are. Do not "fix" the inconsistency by renaming `EulerDegrees`.

Store slices follow the rows, so the camera's three are prefixed to stay greppable and to leave `roll` to the shape: `camElev`, `camAzim`, `camRoll` in the WORLD tab block; `pitch`, `yaw`, `roll`, `spin` stay in the SHAPE tab block with their comment corrected to name `ShapeRig`.

### Ranges

|  | ELEV | AZIM | ROLL |  | PITCH | YAW | ROLL |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| camera | ±89 | ±180 | ±180 | shape | ±180 | ±180 | ±180 |

The camera keeps ±89: the turntable-pole argument written into `viewPresets.ts` is about the camera and still holds. The shape has no pole to flip over, so its pitch opens to ±180 and `PITCH_LIMIT` goes.

### The write-back plumbing moves, and one half of it disappears

`ShapeTab.setTransformUi` and `TransformSection.setAngleUi` are **deleted**. Nothing moves the shape except the shape's own rows, so the "a preset must not fight the slider that is writing it" hazard those two exist to manage evaporates on the shape side entirely.

It reappears once on the camera side as `WorldTab.setCameraUi` → `CameraSection.setCameraUi(angles)`, mirroring the existing `setZoomUi` exactly: writes the three rows and the three slices, and deliberately does **not** call back into the rig, which already holds the values. Three call sites, all of them currently pointing at `shapeTab`:

* `Main.applyPointerOrbit` (L453)
* `Main.applyViewPreset` (L495)
* `Main.renderFrame`'s mid-ease push (L668)

### The two reset paths

* **Double-tap** (`applyPointerReset`, L468–L482) is documented as "a camera gesture, so it moves the camera and nothing else". After the split that is finally true: it restores the camera to ISO and the zoom, and leaves the shape's pose and spin untouched. Its import of the three defaults follows them from `TransformSection` to `CameraSection`.
* **Toolbar RESET** restores every slice through the store as it already does — shape angles to 0, spin to 122, camera to 30/45/0 — plus the two engine values with no row of their own: `shapeRig.reset()` zeroes the accumulator, `cameraRig.reset()` drops an in-flight ease. The single `rig.reset()` call at L819 becomes those two.

### Tests

`ShapeRig` is pure and holds no canvas or DOM node, so it stays inside the node environment the suite runs in. All four cases under `describe("CameraRig turntable")` are spin cases and move to a new `src/scene/__tests__/ShapeRig.test.ts`; the fourth, "keeps the spin out of the camera readout", becomes structurally true once the two are different objects but is worth keeping as a regression guard against anyone folding them back together.

## Constraints and risks

* **The opening frame is the acceptance test.** Defaults are camera 30/45/0, shape 0/0/0, spin 122 °/s. Verify by screenshot diff against `master` on all twenty shapes, not by eye.
* **Geometry does not move.** No generator, no registry count and no vertex is touched. `pnpm run snapshot:geometry` must come back byte-identical — this is a transform ticket, not a geometry one.
* `meshMatrix` **is contended.** E4a ([COS-240](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-240/e4a-materials-material-model-base-colour-and-mesh-scale)) explicitly does *not* fold mesh scale into the mesh transform — it scales at projection time — so that ticket and this one do not collide. **Reversed after the fact:** on re-reading the projection path while planning E4a, that approach turned out to be wrong — a scale applied inside `convert3D2D` never reaches `Camera.clips`, so the near plane would judge unscaled depth, and `Mesh.changeScale` looping `Point3D.modelScale` reintroduces the per-vertex write pattern E2 built the shared `Camera` record to delete. E4a now folds SCALE into `ShapeRig.pose()` instead, which is free per vertex and makes clipping, the painter's sort and the depth histogram correct without further work. This line originally read "Do not fold SCALE into `ShapeRig`"; it was written deferring to E4a's draft and is superseded by E4a's revised "Mesh scale" section.
* **The gizmo stays on the camera.** `axisScreenDirections()` describes the *world* axes as the camera sees them. It must not start following the shape's pose, or the axis bars would stop agreeing with the ground grid.
* **Angles stay degrees end to end.** A `180 / Math.PI` anywhere in `ShapeRig` or `CameraSection` is a bug, exactly as in E1a.
* **Order.** Independent of the remaining de-mock tickets. E7 ([COS-248](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-248/e7-scene-model-real-scene-objects-per-object-visibility-selection-and)) will move `ShapeRig` under a real scene object when it lands and should be written against it rather than against `Main` holding a single instance.

## Files

* `src/scene/ShapeRig.ts` — new; pose, spin rate, accumulator, `matrix()`, `advance`, `setAngles`, `reset`
* `src/scene/__tests__/ShapeRig.test.ts` — new; the four turntable cases moved from `CameraRig.test.ts`
* `src/camera/CameraRig.ts` — shed the spin; `meshMatrix(objectMatrix)` replaces `meshMatrix()`
* `src/camera/__tests__/CameraRig.test.ts` — the turntable block moves out
* `src/ui/inspector/TransformSection.ts` — rows drive the shape, defaults to 0, pitch opens to ±180, `setAngleUi` deleted, the ISO reasoning moves to `CameraSection`
* `src/ui/inspector/CameraSection.ts` — three ELEV / AZIM / ROLL rows, the three moved defaults, `setCameraUi`
* `src/ui/inspector/ShapeTab.ts` — `setTransformUi` deleted
* `src/ui/inspector/WorldTab.ts` — `setCameraUi` added
* `src/ui/UIStateStore.ts` — `camElev` / `camAzim` / `camRoll` added to the WORLD block; the SHAPE block's comment corrected to name `ShapeRig`
* `src/app/Main.ts` — own both rigs, compose the mesh matrix, rewire the four TRANSFORM callbacks and three new camera ones, move the three write-back call sites to `worldTab`, split `rig.reset()` in two, follow the defaults' move in the `applyPointerReset` import
* `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.js` — the `@scene` alias, in both

- [ ] Dragging in the viewport moves the camera and the ELEV / AZIM rows follow it; the shape's three rows do not move

- [ ] A double-tap in the viewport restores the camera to ISO and the zoom, and leaves the shape's pose and spin exactly where they were
- [ ] The toolbar RESET restores all seven angle rows, the spin rate, the accumulator and any in-flight ease

Title: deploy-front.sh / deploy-api.sh must refuse to deploy a dirty or stale tree
Description:
On 2026-08-06, `deploy-api.sh` shipped an uncommitted, unmigrated Prisma schema change (`Service.nginxConfPath`, from an in-progress registry/reassignment ticket) to production, because the script `rsync`s the local working tree as-is rather than validating it against git. Every `/api/fleet` request then failed with `PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2022 — Unknown column 'Service.nginxConfPath'`, since the live database was never migrated. A rollback didn't fix it either — the previous release had been built from the same dirty tree, so there was no clean generation left to fall back to; recovery required a deploy from a separate clean checkout.

Separately, the same session shipped a *stale* front build: local `main` was one commit behind `origin/main`, and `deploy-front.sh` has the same blind-`rsync` behavior, so it shipped code missing the latest merged fix ([COS-435](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-435/freshness-indicator-drop-the-button-styling-one-per-page-bottom-right)).

**Do**

* Before any remote work, both scripts' `deploy()` must refuse to proceed unless the local tree is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty) and `HEAD` matches `origin/main` exactly.
* Fail fast and local — no SSH, no rsync, no server-side changes — with a clear error naming what's wrong (the dirty files, or the two mismatched commit hashes).
* `rollback` is unaffected — it doesn't touch local git state today and doesn't need to.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Deploying with any uncommitted or untracked file present is refused before any SSH/rsync happens.
- [ ] Deploying with local `HEAD` behind or ahead of `origin/main` is refused the same way.
- [ ] A clean checkout that matches `origin/main` deploys exactly as before.
- [ ] `./deploy-front.sh rollback` / `./deploy-api.sh rollback` still work unmodified.

Title: Cron page: two proper widgets, and a run feed you can search back through years
Description:
The Cron page has two tables but not two widgets. Both live inside a single scroller (`front/src/components/cron/CronScreen.tsx:218`), so neither behaves like the panels on Registry and Audit: the summary's column headings scroll away with its own rows, the "RUN FEED" heading is a bare `<h2>` sitting outside the box it names (`CronScreen.tsx:254`), and the feed has no column headings at all — five columns of unlabelled data (`CronScreen.tsx:273`).

The second half is also the only table in Zeus with no way to reach past its first page. `feed()` takes 50 rows and stops (`nest-api/src/cron/cron.service.ts:52,221,238`) and the front never sends `limit` or `before` (`front/src/components/cron/services/useCron.ts:41-48`). That was survivable while runs were pruned at 30 days. Now that retention keeps everything (`ZEUS_CRON_RETENTION_DAYS` unset — `cron.service.ts:271-286`), every run before the last 50 is in the database and unreachable from the UI. With two db-backups firing twice a day plus the nightly prune, 50 runs is under a week.

The filter that does exist works by clicking a row in the summary, which sets `?app=&cron=` (`CronScreen.tsx:183-195`). That stays. What's missing is everything else needed to find a run you cannot see: status, a time window, and text.

**Do**

Two widgets, each scrolling on its own — the Registry/Audit pattern (`RegistryScreen.tsx:97-105`, `AuditScreen.tsx:146-147`, `shared/Panel.tsx:67`):

* Widget 1 — **Schedules**: `Panel` + `PanelTitle` + `PanelTable`. The title carries the count and the alarm: `SCHEDULES · 3 crons · 1 overdue` (`CronSummary.overdueCount` already exists). Capped in height and shrink-to-fit, like `PortSpace` — it is a reference you glance at, and it must never push the feed off the screen.
* Widget 2 — **Run feed**: `Panel` + `PanelTitle` + `PanelTable`, taking the height that is left. The `<h2>` moves into the panel's title bar; "filtered to X — clear" goes in `PanelTitle`'s `action` slot. Add the column heading band it currently lacks: when · app · cron · status · summary.

Feed controls, in a row under the feed's title, all held in the URL via `nuqs` so a narrowed feed is still a link:

* **Search** (`?q=`) — debounced ~250ms, case-insensitive, matching the run `summary` and the cron key. This is the control that makes multi-year history usable: "pfadump", "copied offsite", "timeout".
* **Status chips** — all / ok / failed / skipped. `?status=` already works end to end (`cron.controller.ts:61`, `useCron.ts:33`) and is the one filter the screen never sets.
* **Range chips** — 24h / 7d / 30d / all, defaulting to all. Needs a new `?after=`; `?before=` already exists.
* **Clear all** that resets q, status, range, app and cron together.

Paging:

* `useInfiniteQuery` plus a "load more" foot on the feed panel, 50 per page.
* Keyset cursor, not offset. `before` is exclusive on `receivedAt` (`cron.service.ts:226`) and two runs can share a timestamp, so add a `beforeId` tiebreak and order by `(receivedAt desc, id desc)`. Both indexes this needs are already on the model (`prisma/schema.prisma:230-231`).

API — `GET /cron/runs` gains `q`, `after` and `beforeId`, keeping the existing rule that an unparseable value filters nothing rather than answering 400 (`cron.controller.ts:59-61`).

Copy — every new string into `front/src/text/en/cron.ts`, none inline.

**Out of scope**

* App filter chips like Audit's. Filtering by app already happens by clicking a summary row; a second control writing the same query param is one too many.
* Full-text search indexes. `ILIKE` over a table this size is fine — revisit if a year of runs ever makes it slow.
* Exporting the feed.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Both halves are panels with their own scrollbar and a fixed heading band — scrolling the feed does not move the summary's headings, or the reverse.
- [ ] The run feed has labelled columns.
- [ ] Searching "dump" returns matching runs whatever their age, not only ones inside the first 50.
- [ ] Status and range chips narrow the feed, combine with each other and with a selected cron, and survive a reload because they are in the URL.
- [ ] "Load more" reaches run 51 and beyond with no row repeated and none skipped across the page boundary.
- [ ] A filter set that matches nothing says so, and offers to clear.
- [ ] No new user-facing string lives outside `front/src/text/en/cron.ts`.

**Files:** `front/src/components/cron/CronScreen.tsx`, `front/src/components/cron/services/useCron.ts`, `front/src/text/en/cron.ts`, `nest-api/src/cron/cron.controller.ts`, `nest-api/src/cron/cron.service.ts`

Title: nest-api: bump date-fns from v2.28 to v4.4 (currently unused)
Description:
`date-fns` in `nest-api/package.json` is pinned to `^2.28.0` (2.30.0 installed) — two majors behind. npm's `latest` tag is `4.4.0` (`5.0.0-alpha.0` also exists as a prerelease, not the target).

Note on the "match pfa" instruction: pfa itself (`front` and `nest-api`) is also still pinned to `^2.28.0` — it hasn't moved to v4 either. This bump makes Zeus diverge from pfa's actual installed version rather than match it. Not a blocker, just worth knowing before citing pfa as the reason.

The dependency is currently **unused**: `git grep -rn "date-fns"` across `nest-api/src` and `front/src` (excluding `node_modules`) matches nothing but the `package.json` line itself. So this is a version-pin bump with no call sites to migrate, not a real migration.

Breaking-change surface, from date-fns' own GitHub release notes:

* **v2 → v3** (the real breaking jump): package restructured into a flat ESM/CJS dual-package, deep imports moved from default to named exports (`require('date-fns/addDays')` → destructure `{ addDays }`), TypeScript types fully rewritten, `constants` moved out of the root index import, several `Interval`-handling functions changed behavior on invalid/reversed intervals instead of throwing, rounding switched to `Math.trunc`.
* **v3 → v4**: date-fns' own release notes call out "not many breaking changes... all type-related," plus new, additive time zone support (`TZDate`/`UTCDate`). Low risk.
* v4.4.0 still publishes a `require` condition (`index.cjs`) alongside `import` in its `exports` map, so it isn't an ESM-only trap for nest-api's `"module": "nodenext"` tsconfig.

Since nothing imports the package today, none of the v3 API changes have code to break. The real risk is at install/build time (peer dependency resolution, lockfile), not runtime logic.

**Do**

* Bump `date-fns` to `^4.4.0` in `nest-api/package.json`.
* Run `npm install` in `nest-api/`, let the lockfile update, commit it alongside the bump.
* Re-run `git grep -rn "date-fns"` across `nest-api/src` and `front/src` after the bump to confirm the call-site count is still zero (i.e. nothing silently started relying on deep-import paths that moved in v3).

**Out of scope**

* Actually using date-fns for anything — this ticket only updates the pin. If it's still unused after the bump, a follow-up could remove it instead; not deciding that here.
* `front/` — it doesn't declare `date-fns` at all, nothing to bump there.
* pfa — its own `^2.28.0` pin is that project's call, not touched by this ticket.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] `nest-api/package.json` and its lockfile pin `date-fns@^4.4.0`.
- [ ] `npm install` completes with no peer-dependency conflicts.
- [ ] `npm run build` (tsc) succeeds.
- [ ] `npm test` passes with no new failures.
- [ ] `git grep -rn "date-fns" nest-api/src front/src` still shows zero source usages.

**Files:** `nest-api/package.json`, `nest-api/package-lock.json`

Title: front + nest-api: bump date-fns from v2.28 to v4.4 (front's deep imports break, need a codemod)
Description:
`date-fns` is pinned to `^2.28.0` in both `pfa/front/package.json` and `pfa/nest-api/package.json` (installed 2.28.0 / 2.30.0). npm's `latest` tag is `4.4.0`. This is pfa's counterpart to [COS-439](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-439/nest-api-bump-date-fns-from-v228-to-v44-currently-unused) — Zeus's `nest-api` had the same stale pin but zero usage; pfa is the opposite case: date-fns is used extensively, and ~90 call sites use an import style v3 actually removed.

**nest-api — low risk**

Only 2 files: `stats.service.ts` and `upload/upload.config.ts`. Both already import the modern way — `import { format, ... } from "date-fns"` and `import { fr } from "date-fns/locale"` — root-level named imports. Confirmed directly against the published v4.4.0 package that this exact style still works unchanged (both the root index and the `date-fns/locale` barrel still re-export everything as named exports in v4). The one function worth a manual look after the bump is `parse` (custom format-string parsing in `stats.service.ts`) — signature is unchanged across versions but it's the most behaviorally complex function in use, worth a spot-check rather than trusting the changelog alone.

**front — real work: \~55 files use an import style v3 removed**

Almost every date-fns import in `front/src` is a *deep default import* — `import format from "date-fns/format"`, `import parseISO from "date-fns/parseISO"`, etc. (26 distinct symbols, ~90 import statements, 55 files — `spendings` 22, `statistics` 11, `dashboard` 10, `exceptionals` 5, `datePickerWrapper` 4, plus `useDateLocale.ts` / `NavBar.tsx` / `dateRoute.ts`). Confirmed directly, not just from the changelog: `date-fns@2.30.0`'s `format/index.js` has `exports.default = format`; `date-fns@4.4.0`'s `format.cjs` has only `exports.format = format` — no default export at all. Every one of those 55 files' date-fns imports resolves to `undefined` the moment the version bumps, and front's `moduleResolution: bundler` won't necessarily catch a missing default export at compile time — it can fail silently at runtime instead. Re-enumerate anytime with:

```
grep -rlE '^\s*import [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]* from "date-fns/' front/src --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"
```

Two sub-cases inside that 55:

* **Locale imports** (`useDateLocale.ts`): `import enUS from "date-fns/locale/en-US"` and `import fr from "date-fns/locale/fr"` — same default-export breakage. Fix the same way nest-api already does it: `import { enUS, fr } from "date-fns/locale"`.
* **The** `Locale` **type** (`heatmapData.ts`, `searchTimelineData.ts`, `statisticsData.ts`, `groupByMonth.ts`): all do `import type { Locale } from "date-fns"`. Checked the v4.4.0 `.d.ts` files directly — `Locale` is **not** re-exported from `date-fns` root or from the `date-fns/locale` barrel in v4; only individual locale files import it privately to type their own const. There's no drop-in replacement import path. Cheapest fix: since these files already import `fr`/`enUS` as values, type as `typeof fr` instead — but confirm at implementation time rather than trusting this ticket blindly.

Also checked: `eachDayOfInterval` (`DashboardPageClient.tsx:49`) is the only `Interval`-arg call in the codebase, and its interval is always constructed forward (`{ start, end: addDays(start, 6) }`), so it's unaffected by v3's reversed/invalid-interval behavior change.

**Do**

* Bump `date-fns` to `^4.4.0` in both `pfa/front/package.json` and `pfa/nest-api/package.json`; `npm install` in both, commit the lockfiles.
* Convert all ~90 deep default imports in `front/src` to named imports. Converging each file onto one root import (`import { format, parseISO } from "date-fns";`, matching nest-api's existing style and the 8 front files that already partly do this) is preferable to a 1:1 `import { X } from "date-fns/X"` swap — but either resolves the breakage; pick whichever is easier to script reliably. Mechanical enough to codemod (regex/jscodeshift) rather than hand-edit 55 files, but compile and review every touched file — don't trust a blind find/replace.
* Fix the 2 locale imports and the 4 `Locale`-type imports specifically (see above): `useDateLocale.ts`, `heatmapData.ts`, `searchTimelineData.ts`, `statisticsData.ts`, `groupByMonth.ts`.
* Update the 3 test files sharing the same pattern: `datePickerWrapper/__tests__/helpers.test.ts`, `datePickerWrapper/__tests__/store.test.ts`, `statistics/helpers/__tests__/searchTimelineData.test.ts`.
* Run the full front test suite and `tsc`, not just a build — the breakage is a runtime `undefined`, not reliably a type error, so tests that actually exercise these helpers are the real signal.
* Manually smoke-test the date-heavy screens after: Dashboard (month picker, forecast strip, sparkline), Statistics (heatmap, timeline, KPIs), Spendings search, Exceptionals.

**Out of scope**

* Zeus's own date-fns bump — tracked separately in [COS-439](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-439/nest-api-bump-date-fns-from-v228-to-v44-currently-unused).
* Adopting any new v4 features (timezone support via `@date-fns/tz`, etc.) — this ticket only fixes the version bump and its fallout, not new functionality.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Both `package.json`s and lockfiles pin `date-fns@^4.4.0`.
- [ ] `grep -rlE '^\s*import [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]* from "date-fns/'` across `front/src` returns nothing.
- [ ] `tsc` passes in both `front` and `nest-api` with no new errors (this is where the `Locale`-type breakage will surface if not already fixed).
- [ ] Full test suites pass in both packages.
- [ ] Manual pass on Dashboard, Statistics, Spendings search, and Exceptionals confirms dates/locales still render correctly (French month/day names, forecast dates, heatmap).

Title: D3 — Twice-daily DB backup to vps-debian (parity with PFA/bkmk)
Description:
Spira's current backup (`DEPLOY.md` § Backups) is a single nightly `mysqldump`, retained locally on ks-b for 14 days — no off-server copy. PFA and bkmk both already push a copy of their database to the external server `vps-debian` at midnight and noon; Spira should match that.

## Scope

* `mysqldump` of the `spira` database, twice daily (midnight + noon)
* Copy the dump off-box to `vps-debian`
* Keep the existing local 14-day rotation as the first line of defense — the off-server copy is what survives ks-b itself being lost, not a replacement for it

## Investigate first

PFA/bkmk's actual scheduling mechanism isn't a plain user crontab — `crontab -l` returns "command not found" on ks-b, and nothing matching showed up in `systemctl list-timers --all` either. Title: Theatre mode: one HUD icon expands the viewport to the whole window and folds the console away
Description:
Blocked by [COS-250](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-250/e9b-resize-dpr-and-the-pixel-budget>) — see **Order** at the end. Related: [COS-249](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-249/e8-session-actions-and-keyboard>).

The console is a dozen panels around a 1024 × 640 picture. Sometimes you only want the picture. One icon in the viewport HUD expands the render surface to the whole browser window, folds every other pane away in the same transition, and becomes its own inverse so the click that got you there gets you back.

**Not the OS fullscreen API.** The scene expands inside the browser viewport — tabs and URL bar stay where they are. `requestFullscreen()` cannot animate the thing that makes this read correctly: the other panes *shrinking away* rather than being gone between two compositor frames, because the browser swaps compositing modes and the old layout never gets a chance to move. **And no scrollbar** — neither axis, at any width, including mid-transition.

## The control

A square icon button, white, top-left of the camera readout.

`.viewport-hud__top` is a `space-between` row with two children today — the chip cluster on the left, the camera readout on the right. A third child would land in the middle of the row rather than beside the panel, so the button and the readout go into a new `.viewport-hud__top-right` cluster: a flex row, `align-items: flex-start`, button first. That also gives it a home in **both** branches — `.viewport-hud__camera` is desktop-only and `.viewport-hud__cam-chips` replaces it below 900px (`viewport.css` L481–L485), and the button belongs to neither.

Three things about it are load-bearing:

* `pointer-events: auto`**.** `.viewport-hud` is `pointer-events: none` on purpose, so the layer does not swallow the drag-orbit on the canvas underneath (`viewport.css`, hud root). Any interactive child opts back in. Without this the button is decoration.
* **The glyphs are inline SVG in the button**, both of them, and CSS shows one per state off the `#app` attribute. `src/icons/` holds favicons, not an icon system, and two glyphs do not justify inventing one. The pair is the usual corners-out / corners-in.
* **White is** `--color-text-primary`, with `--color-accent` on hover and focus, matching the rest of the HUD ramp. Not `--color-swatch-white` — that is the material swatch and means something else — and not a raw `#fff`.

It is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed` and a label that changes with the state ("expand viewport" / "restore console"). A pointerdown on it must not reach the canvas: check that a drag begun on the icon does not orbit.

## The expansion

**One attribute on** `#app`**, and the layout is CSS.** `data-viewport="expanded"`, alongside the `data-tab` / `data-mtab` that already gate the inspector. The shell's second layout — the whole mobile stack — is produced by `display: contents` plus `order` with no JS at the breakpoint and no listener re-attached; this is the same move and should stay that way. No `position: fixed`, no FLIP, no View Transitions API.

It works because the shell is already a flex column. When the toolbar, the telemetry block, the status bar and both side columns collapse, `.viewport` grows into the space on its own — it is the flexible child (`flex: 3 1 var(--size-viewport-h)`). Every property involved is animatable: `flex-basis`, `min-width`, `min-height`, `padding`, `gap`, `opacity`. `#app`'s own `--size-page-pad` and `--size-stack-gap` go to zero in the same tween, which is where the last 16px of matte comes from.

**Timing is** `--duration-base` **(240ms) and** `--ease-standard`**.** motion.css states the rule outright: anything entering or leaving takes `--duration-base`; `--duration-fast` is too short to read as motion and would make the panes pop rather than fold.

**The collapsed panes must leave the tab order.** Zero height and `opacity: 0` still focus. End the collapse at `visibility: hidden` (or `display` with `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`), or tabbing while expanded walks an invisible console.

**No scrollbar** takes two more things. `#app` is `min-height: 100vh`; expanded it is `height: 100dvh` with `overflow: hidden` — `dvh`, not `vh`, because a mobile URL bar makes `100vh` taller than the window and that is precisely a scrollbar. And the criterion covers the *transition*, not just the end state: a pane that shrinks more slowly than the viewport grows overflows for 200ms.

**Mobile.** `.viewport` carries `aspect-ratio: 16 / 10` inside the media query — released while expanded, or the picture stops at 62% of a tall phone. The sticky `.app-bar` sits at `--layer-sticky: 6` and the HUD deliberately opens no stacking context (D11), so the header collapsing to zero height is not enough: it has to end `visibility: hidden` or it paints over the picture.

**The stage needs nothing.** `.viewport` is `container-type: size` and the stage is `width: min(100cqw, 100cqh × ratio, --size-canvas-w)` — it already follows the card. The third term is the cap, which is why this waits on [COS-250](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-250/e9b-resize-dpr-and-the-pixel-budget).

`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` **gets the state change with no tween.** Five sheets already honour it (`inspector.css`, `zBuffer.css`, `frame-time.css`, `toggle.css`, `geometry.css`); this joins them rather than inventing a second convention.

## What you give up while expanded, on purpose

Everything except the picture. No toolbar, so no PAUSE, STEP, RESET or CAPTURE PNG. No status bar, no inspector, no telemetry.

**And the keyboard does not cover for them yet.** There is no global key handler in the tree at all — `src/ui/shortcuts.ts` is a table whose only consumer today is the panel that prints it, every binding marked `pendingHandler`, and [COS-249](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-249/e8-session-actions-and-keyboard>) (E8) is what dispatches them. So expanded mode is view-only: orbit, wheel zoom and pinch (E1b is live), plus the icon and Escape. That is accepted, not overlooked. When [COS-249](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-249/e8-session-actions-and-keyboard) lands, SPACE / R / W / G / C / S / F work while expanded with no change here.

**Escape collapses**, and that listener belongs to this ticket: on `document`, armed on expand, removed on collapse. It is not the global handler [COS-249](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-249/e8-session-actions-and-keyboard) owns and must not quietly become one.

## Where the state lives

In the new class, not in `UIStateStore`. The store's stated contract is that RESET restores every slice — a slice that RESET does not touch is the bug it exists to prevent — and a RESET that folds the console back out is a scene control silently rearranging the layout. This is chrome state, not a value with no engine home. `ViewportExpander` owns the boolean and writes the attribute; if a later ticket wants it to survive a reload, that is [COS-249](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-249/e8-session-actions-and-keyboard)'s session work, not the store.

## Files

* `src/ui/ViewportExpander.ts` — new; owns the boolean, writes `data-viewport` on `#app`, swaps the label and `aria-pressed`, arms and disarms the Escape listener
* `src/app/Main.ts` — construct it, disconnect on teardown
* `src/index.html` — the button and its two inline SVGs, inside a new `.viewport-hud__top-right` wrapper
* `src/styles/components/hud.css` — the HUD icon-button recipe (surface, hairline, blur, hover), beside `.hud-chip` and `.hud-panel`
* `src/styles/components/viewport.css` — where the button sits in the HUD row, `pointer-events: auto`, the glyph swap
* `src/styles/layout.css` — the `#app[data-viewport="expanded"]` block, desktop and mobile
* `notes/ui-refonte/ui/05-viewport-hud.md` — record the new control in the widget's spec

## Done when

- [ ] Clicking the icon expands the picture to the full window in one 240ms transition, and every other pane collapses within that same transition — none of them cut, none of them are still moving after it
- [ ] Expanded, the document scrolls in neither axis at any width — and no scrollbar appears at any point *during* either transition
- [ ] The icon swaps to the collapse glyph, `aria-pressed` and the label follow, and clicking it restores exactly the layout that was left, including the active inspector tab and the mobile tab
- [ ] Escape collapses; its listener is present only while expanded
- [ ] Tabbing while expanded reaches the collapse button and nothing behind it
- [ ] Orbit, wheel zoom and pinch still work while expanded, and a drag started on the icon does not orbit
- [ ] On a phone the expanded viewport card fills the window edge to edge — no dead space below a 16/10-capped card, no sticky header painted over it. The picture inside it stays letterboxed at 16:10 (the same interim cap desktop has) until [COS-250](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-250/e9b-resize-dpr-and-the-pixel-budget); only the card's own aspect-ratio lock releases here
- [ ] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` gets the state change with no tween
- [ ] The canvas re-rasterises at the expanded size and the resolution chip reports it — expanded is not a 1024 × 640 picture centred in a black window
- [ ] `typecheck`, `lint`, `test` and `lint:rules` pass
- [ ] Visual QA in a browser, desktop and mobile

## Order

[COS-250](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-250/e9b-resize-dpr-and-the-pixel-budget) (E9b — resize, DPR and the pixel budget) is what makes this worth doing. Until it lands the backing store is welded to 1024 × 640 and the stage is capped at `--size-canvas-w` by the epic's "scales down but never up" rule, so expanding the card would paint a small sharp picture in a large black window — the letterbox *is* the placeholder, and E9b is the ticket that removes it. E9b is also sequenced last in the de-mock epic by design: the passes it resizes have to exist, and the perf gates in E3b and E5 have to be measured at a known size first.

Title: Split Triangle.ts back under the R17 line guideline
Description:
## Why

`src/primitives/Triangle.ts` is **241 code lines** today (501 raw, 59 blank, 201 comment-only — counted the way house-style.md counts: `grep -cvE '^\s*(//.*)?$'`), against R17's guideline of splitting past roughly 160. Verified against git history: it was **177 code lines** at `6e00060^` (the commit before [COS-418](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-418/e2b-near-plane-polygon-clipping-with-uv-interpolation)), so [COS-418](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-418/e2b-near-plane-polygon-clipping-with-uv-interpolation) (E2b, near-plane clipping) added exactly the 64 lines of `clipToNear` / `nearClipVertices` / `emitFragment` / `rawMaterial`. The debt predates [COS-418](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-418/e2b-near-plane-polygon-clipping-with-uv-interpolation) — [COS-383](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-383/t30-split-the-affine-texture-mapper-out-of-triangle)/T30 already pulled the affine-mapping math out into `AffineTextureMapper` and the file still sat above the guideline afterward — but [COS-418](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-418/e2b-near-plane-polygon-clipping-with-uv-interpolation) made it meaningfully worse and deliberately left it out of scope.

## Already considered and rejected

A companion class (`TriangleClipper` in `src/rendering/`) to hold the near-plane-clip orchestration was considered while implementing [COS-418](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-418/e2b-near-plane-polygon-clipping-with-uv-interpolation) and rejected. It would need `Triangle` to expose several new public methods (per-vertex depths, raw vertex+UV data, a "clone with inherited resolved material" method) purely so external code could reach state that is currently private — trading file-length compliance for worse encapsulation.

The specific blocker is `emitFragment` (Triangle.ts:473-490): it constructs a sibling `Triangle` and assigns `fragment.resolved = this.resolved` directly, rather than re-deriving through `resolveMaterial` (the call site has no access to the scene's current `MeshMaterial`). That assignment is legal only because it is lexically inside the `Triangle` class body — TypeScript's `private` is class-scoped, not instance-scoped, so any code *inside* `class Triangle` can read or write any `Triangle` instance's private fields, but nothing outside the class body can, function or class alike. `authored` compounds this: it's `readonly`, and TS only allows assigning a `readonly` field inside its own class's constructor, so `emitFragment` has to go through `new Triangle(...)` (which it needs anyway) and then patch `resolved` onto the result afterward. There is no version of this that works from outside `class Triangle { }` without making `resolved` non-private.

## Recommendation

Two clusters exist in the file with very different extractability.

**Extractable — the paint/fill cluster.** `drawTexture`, `strokeWireframe`, `fillFlat`, `shadeTexture`, `veilWithFog`, `tracePath` (Triangle.ts:337-445, **61 code lines**, verified by the same count method) only *read* the current instance's own state (`aprojX..cprojY`, `resolved`, `uva/uvb/uvc`, `a/b/c`) — never a sibling's. `Triangle.fill()` already has legitimate access to all of it and can pass it along as plain arguments. Pull these into pure, stateless, exported functions in a new file (e.g. `src/rendering/triangleFill.ts`) — not a class: there is no shared invariant to encapsulate, per D1b, and this is the same shape D8 already ruled on for `easeInOutCubic`/`lerp` ("changed file but stayed functions") and the same shape [COS-383](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-383/t30-split-the-affine-texture-mapper-out-of-triangle) already used for `AffineTextureMapper.draw`, which takes a flat options object rather than reaching into Triangle's private fields. No new public surface on `Triangle` is required — `fill()` keeps calling them, just passing values instead of letting them read `this`.

This brings Triangle.ts from 241 to **180 code lines** (241 − 61). Re-verify at implementation time rather than trusting this number — house-style.md itself warns line citations drift after any intervening refactor.

**Not extractable — the near-plane-clip cluster.** `clipToNear`, `nearClipVertices`, `emitFragment`, `rawMaterial` (Triangle.ts:303-335, 452-498 — the [COS-418](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-418/e2b-near-plane-polygon-clipping-with-uv-interpolation) addition) stay on `Triangle`, for the reason above. I checked whether `nearClipVertices`/`rawMaterial` alone could move out — both only *read* private state, so neither hits the same wall — but that only saves ~14 code lines and splits one cohesive algorithm (the Sutherland-Hodgman walk plus its fragment re-materialization) across two files for very little. Recommend against it.

**Also not in scope:** `project`, `isFrontFacing`, `fill`, `render` are, per the file's own header comment, "Mesh.renderMesh's three passes" (E6/[COS-239](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-239/e6-renderer-instrumentation-staged-timings-draw-calls-fill-rate-and)) — each timed independently by the render-instrumentation contract. Splitting them across classes would touch that contract; unrelated to R17 hygiene and out of scope here.

## Open question for whoever implements this

180 code lines is closer to R17's "roughly 160" but still ~12% over, and nothing left in the file after the fill-cluster extraction can move further without either the encapsulation trade-off above or reopening the E6 instrumentation contract. Measure the real number after implementing the extraction, and if it's still meaningfully over, choose one:

* Accept it as close enough — R17's own wording is "roughly", not a hard cutoff.
* Write a new decisions.md entry documenting a narrow exemption for Triangle. **This would not be a citation of D7**: D7 exempts `Main.ts` "by ownership" using the criterion "does any method belong to exactly one collaborator?", which doesn't transfer here — Triangle's residual size is pinned by algorithmic cohesion (the clip walk) and a cross-cutting instrumentation contract (E6), not by breadth of collaborators. A Triangle exemption needs its own reasoning from scratch, not an appeal to D7's.

## References

* `notes/oop-refonte/reference/house-style.md` — R17 (the guideline, and the "measure code lines not raw lines" methodology used above)
* `notes/oop-refonte/reference/decisions.md` — D1b (the pure-function discriminator), D7 (Main.ts's exemption, and why it doesn't transfer to Triangle), D8 (the `easeInOutCubic`/`lerp` "moved file, stayed functions" precedent)
* [COS-383](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-383/t30-split-the-affine-texture-mapper-out-of-triangle) / T30 — the prior `AffineTextureMapper` extraction out of `Triangle`, same file, same shape of fix
* [COS-418](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-418/e2b-near-plane-polygon-clipping-with-uv-interpolation) — where the `TriangleClipper` extraction was considered and rejected; this ticket is the follow-up it deferred

Note: R17 is explicitly excluded from `pnpm run lint:rules` ("line-count linting produces noise") — this is a manual/review-time guideline, not a CI gate, so nothing will flag it automatically.

Title: Report Spira's backup cron to Zeus, and register Spira in the fleet registry
Description:
Spira's twice-daily backup ([COS-441](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-441/d3-twice-daily-db-backup-to-vps-debian-parity-with-pfabkmk)) is live and proven, but a failure is visible only in `pm2 logs spira-nest-api`. Nothing watches it.

That is the blind spot PFA already paid for. Its own `db-backup-cron.service.ts` comment records two failures that were indistinguishable from success anywhere outside pm2's log: a `mysqldump` that had been erroring for weeks, and a deploy that dropped one environment variable so the job never ran at all.

Spira has both failure modes today, and the first one already happened: the very first real run failed with `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/home/spira'`. It was caught only because the job was triggered by hand instead of being left to fire at midnight. The next one will not be.

## What is missing

* No `zeus-report` module. PFA has `pfa/nest-api/src/infrastructure/zeus-report.ts`, exporting `withZeusReport(key, schedule, fn)`; Spira's `infrastructure/` has `db-backup`, `logger` and `ssh-backup` only.
* Spira is not in Zeus's registry — grepping `Zeus/nest-api/src/registry/` for "spira" returns nothing. `DEPLOY.md` has carried a note to register it "when the registry is live" since the port convention was written down.

## Where the work is

**All the code is in this repo. Zeus needs no code change at all** — its registry is database-backed (`App` + `Service` rows, UNIQUE on `Service.port`), so registering Spira is filling in a form in Zeus's UI, not editing `registry-rules.ts`.

**Do the registration first.** Zeus's `cron.service.ts:74` is explicit: "Crons auto-register; apps never do. An unknown app name is a `400`." So the cron row appears by itself the first time Spira reports — but only if the app already exists in the port registry. In the other order every report is rejected and nothing says why.

## Scope

* Register Spira in Zeus's UI: one app, two services — front `3004`, API `6700`, per the `30xx` / `6N00` convention.
* Port `zeus-report.ts` into `nest-api/src/infrastructure/`, and wrap `DbBackupCronService.handleDbBackup` in it — the schedule string is already declared once as `BACKUP_SCHEDULE` precisely so the reported schedule and the one the scheduler runs on cannot drift.
* Report `skipped` with the named missing variables (the service already computes that list), `failed` with the error, and on success the dump's byte count. A dump that succeeds and shrinks by an order of magnitude is a broken backup that looks exactly like a working one, so the size is the number worth carrying.
* `ZEUS_INGEST_URL` (`http://127.0.0.1:6600/api/cron-runs`), `ZEUS_INGEST_TOKEN` (the same value as Zeus's own) and `ZEUS_APP_NAME` (the registry slug) go in `nest-api/ecosystem.config.js` alongside the rest — gitignored, scp'd on deploy — and in `ecosystem.config.example.js` as empty strings.

## Not a v1 blocker

The cutover does not depend on this, and it touches two repos. But it should not wait long: after the cutover Spira holds the only copy of every ticket, and an unwatched backup is the one that is discovered broken at the moment it is needed.

## Done when

A failing backup shows up as `failed` on Zeus's `/cron` naming the reason, a misconfigured one as `skipped` naming the variable, and Spira appears in the registry with its two ports.

Title: deploy-api.sh must run prisma migrate deploy, not leave it to a follow-up command
Description:
`deploy-api.sh` ships code and reloads pm2, but never migrates. The migration is a separate command an operator runs afterwards, documented as step 4 of DEPLOY.md:

```bash
ssh debian@ks-b '… pnpm prisma migrate deploy && pnpm seed'
```

So **every deploy that adds a column or a table runs the new code against the old schema until somebody remembers to run that line.** The window is not a race — it is however long it takes a human to notice, and nothing in the deploy output mentions it.

Every feature before [COS-426](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-426/database-backups-on-demand-local-dump-history) survived that window by luck: the queries that would fail sat behind routes nobody hits in the thirty seconds after a reload, so they returned a 500 nobody saw and healed themselves once the migration landed. It is worth being explicit that this is luck and not design — the same window shipped `P2022 — Unknown column 'Service.nginxConfPath'` during the incident that produced [COS-436](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-436/deploy-frontsh-deploy-apish-must-refuse-to-deploy-a-dirty-or-stale), which fixed the *dirty tree* half of that story and left this half untouched.

**On 2026-08-07 it stopped being survivable.** [COS-426](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-426/database-backups-on-demand-local-dump-history)'s `BackupsModule.onApplicationBootstrap()` queried `DbDump` on boot. The table did not exist yet, a bootstrap hook that throws aborts `listen()`, and the API never started: `/fleet`, `/cron`, `/audit` and the login page all 502'd for about two minutes. Recovery was running step 4 and restarting. That module has since been made boot-safe (`277cc78`), but that fix only covers *that* module — the next one to read the database at startup, or any request that arrives in the gap, hits the same wall.

**Do**

* Run `prisma migrate deploy` on the box as part of `deploy()`, after the release is in place and its dependencies are installed, and **before** `pm2 reload`. Reloading onto a migrated schema is the whole point; the current order cannot be preserved.
* Fail the deploy if the migration fails, before the reload — a failed migration must leave the previous release serving, not a reloaded process against a schema that was half-changed.
* `DATABASE_URL` is already read from `ecosystem.config.js` on the box in step 4's one-liner; the deploy script has the same access and should not need a second mechanism.
* Leave `pnpm seed` where it is. Seeding is registry data, not schema, it is only needed when the fleet map itself changes, and folding it into every deploy would run it dozens of times for nothing.
* Update DEPLOY.md: step 4 stops being a required step and becomes "seed, when the registry map changed".

**Worth deciding while implementing**

1. **What happens to** `rollback`**?** Rolling code back does not roll a migration back, so a rollback after a schema change puts the old code in front of a new schema. Prisma has no down-migrations. Probably out of scope — but the rollback path should at least *say* it does not touch the database, rather than implying a clean revert it cannot deliver.
2. **Should the front script care?** `deploy-front.sh` never touches the database and should almost certainly stay as it is; state it rather than leaving the asymmetry to be rediscovered.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] A deploy that adds a table or column applies it automatically, with no follow-up command, and the API never serves a request against the old schema.
- [ ] A failing migration aborts the deploy before `pm2 reload`, leaving the previous release running.
- [ ] A deploy with no pending migration is unchanged in behaviour and adds no meaningful time.

Title: /backups must answer "is my data backed up?", not only "what did zeus dump?"
Description:
[COS-426](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-426/database-backups-on-demand-local-dump-history) and [COS-427](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-427/database-backups-manual-offsite-replication) built `/backups` as a **control** surface: Zeus runs a dump on request and pushes it offsite. That works and is deployed. But it answers the wrong question for the way the fleet is actually run.

> « je ferais rarement le dump depuis Zeus voire jamais, sauf en cas de problème avec un cron d'une des apps »

The manual dump is the **exception path**. The everyday question is *"did pfa's own cron run, and did it reach the backup VPS?"* — and today `/backups` cannot answer it. It shows `never dumped` for `pfa`, an app backed up twice a day for years, in the same words it shows for an app with no backup anywhere.

## What already exists — most of it

This is not a greenfield feature. Checked against production on 2026-08-07:

```
pfa/db-backup    0 0 */12 * * *   last=2026-08-07T12:00  ok
bkmk/db-backup   0 0 */12 * * *   last=2026-08-07T12:00  ok
```

Both apps already report their own backup cron through the [COS-398](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-398/cron-activity-feed-apps-report-their-cron-runs-to-zeus) contract, twice a day, carrying the destination and the size:

* `pfa` — summary `dumped to /home/debian/pfabackupdb/pfadump.sql`, detail `{"bytes":2668571}`
* `bkmk` — summary `dumped to …bkmkdump.sql (642 KB), copied`, detail `{"dest":"/home/debian/bkmkbackupdb/bkmkdump.sql","bytes":657812}`

And `/cron` **already computes overdue**, so a backup cron that silently stops firing is already detected today. The alerting exists. The discoverability does not: nobody goes to `/cron` to ask whether their databases are safe.

## The actual gaps

1. **The data is on the wrong page.** `/backups` is where the question gets asked and it ignores `db-backup` runs entirely.
2. **The offsite outcome is unstructured.** One app puts the remote path in `summary`, the other in `detail.dest`, and a third could do neither. Not comparable, not queryable, not renderable as a column.
3. `spira` **reports nothing.** It writes `spira-2026-08-07T15-08.sql.gz` to `~/spirabackupdb/` on the VPS — so it has a working cron — but Zeus has no `spira/db-backup` job. It is invisible, and *invisible is indistinguishable from broken*, which is the exact failure this ticket exists to prevent.
4. **Nothing verifies the claim.** Every signal above is the app's own word. A cron that reports `ok` and writes a zero-byte file looks perfect from here.

## Proposed shape

**Phase 1 — surface what is already reported.** For each app, `/backups` shows its newest `db-backup` cron run beside Zeus's own dumps: when, status, what it said. Free for `pfa` and `bkmk` — no app changes at all — and it turns the page into the thing it is being opened for. The `never dumped` column stays as "last **zeus** dump" and stops being the headline.

**Phase 2 — verify against the backup VPS.** Zeus lists `~/*backupdb/` over its existing ssh key and shows, per app, the newest file there with its size and mtime. This is the only signal in the whole feature that is **not** an app's own word about itself, and it is what catches the cron that reports success and writes nothing — as well as `spira`, which reports nothing yet still has good backups.

⚠️ This reverses a decision in [COS-427](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-427/database-backups-manual-offsite-replication) §"What this deliberately does not do", which says Zeus never lists or reads the backup VPS. That decision was correct **for the premise it was made under** — Zeus as a writer, where reading would only serve to manage files that are not its own. The premise has changed: Zeus is now being asked to report on backups it did not take. Reading stays strictly read-only — no pruning, no deleting, no touching another app's files.

**Not proposed: a second reporting contract.** A dedicated `POST /api/db-backups` with structured fields was considered and rejected. Cron reporting already carries this event, every reporting app already calls it, and a parallel contract for the same fact would mean two things to keep in sync and two places for an app to be wrong. Better to tighten what `db-backup` runs put in `detail` — a documented shape in `docs/reporting/README.md` — than to invent a route.

## Explicitly not changing

**The manual dump buttons stay exactly as they are.** "Dump now" and "Dump + send offsite", per app, on every row that has a schema — plus the delete and the re-push from a dump's modal. Nothing in this ticket removes, hides, demotes or moves them.

Calling the manual dump the "exception path" is a statement about *frequency*, not about value: it is the thing you reach for precisely when an app's own cron has broken, which is the worst possible moment to discover the button has been tidied away. The two halves are complementary — monitoring tells you something is wrong, the button is how you fix it without an SSH session, and neither is much use alone.

What changes is the **headline**: the page currently leads with "what did Zeus dump" (almost always nothing) and must instead lead with "is this database backed up, by anyone". The buttons keep their place in the same row.

## Rename the page to "DB dumps"

"Backups" over-promises, and the gap is not cosmetic. On the same backup VPS, beside `pfabackupdb`, sit `invoicesUpload` (325 MB) and `screenshotsUpload` (95 MB) — pfa's and bkmk's **image** backups, pushed by the same crons. A page titled "Backups" that shows neither, and is never going to, invites exactly the wrong conclusion on the day someone checks whether the invoices are safe.

Image and asset backup is explicitly out of scope in the original design (§2), and for a good reason: which apps even have an asset directory varies per app, unlike a database, and the shape was never scoped. That decision stands. But it means the page covers *database* dumps and should say so.

So: **"DB dumps"** in the nav and as the page title, and the summary line under it adjusted to match.

**Decide: does the route move too?** `/backups` → `/db-dumps` is the honest version, but the filter state lives in the query string (`?app=bkmk`), so any link already shared or bookmarked breaks. Options are to move it and accept that, move it with a redirect, or rename only what is displayed and leave the path. Worth thirty seconds of thought rather than a reflex — this console has one user and very few links, which argues for just moving it cleanly.

If image backups are ever picked up, they get their own page under the same reasoning, and "DB dumps" leaves that name free instead of having already spent it.

## Open questions — resolved

1. **How does an app's cron get recognised as a backup?** **Exact key** `db-backup`**.** A `*-backup` wildcard would happily read `assets-backup` as a database backup and show an image sync's size in the "is my database safe" column, which is worse than showing nothing. An app that names its cron something else is invisible here — a visible, fixable gap, since its cron still appears on `/cron`. Asserted in a test, because changing that string blanks the column for the whole fleet at once.
2. **Should phase 2 read the VPS on every page load, or on a schedule?** **Still open — see below.** Phase 1 does not depend on it, so it did not block.
3. `spira` **should report** — unchanged, belongs in spira's own repo. `docs/reporting/README.md` now documents the key and the `detail` shape to copy.
4. **Does this belong under** `/cron`**?** **No.** Kept as its own page, on the same argument that gave `/deploys` one: the question "is my data safe?" is asked deliberately, and dump paths, checksums and the two dump buttons do not fit in a cron row.

**Does the route move?** **Yes —** `/backups` **→** `/db-dumps`**, with a permanent redirect** in `next.config.js` that carries the query string across, so `?app=bkmk&status=failed` still lands where it did. That removes the only argument against moving it. Internal names (`BackupsModule`, the `/backups` API prefix, the component directory) deliberately stay: the rename is about what the page promises its reader, and churning thirty files to match would add risk and diff noise nobody using the console can see.

## Phase 1 — done

* `DumpsService.summary()` reads each app's `db-backup` cron and its newest run — two queries for the fleet, not one pair per app, because this endpoint polls every two seconds while a dump is in flight.
* `own-backup-rules.ts` — the exact key, and `readReportedBackup()`, which reads `detail.dest`/`detail.bytes` and falls back to the first absolute path in `summary` so **pfa's destination shows today** rather than after someone edits another repo. 10 tests.
* New column **Backed up**, leading the Zeus columns. Amber for overdue (late ≠ failed, same distinction `/cron` draws), grey *not reported* for an app with no cron — never "no backup", because `spira` has good backups and reports none of them.
* Headline counts reordered: `N with no backup zeus can see` (red) → `N backup cron late or failing` (amber) → the two Zeus counts. `unprotectedCount` reads a separate `lastSuccessAt`, not `latest.status`, so yesterday's good dump is not erased by today's failed one.
* Rank: broken-but-was-working first, then no-visible-backup, then covered, then apps with no database. News above long-standing gaps.
* The old standalone `Status` column folded into the last-dump cell — a seventh track would have dragged the table out of alignment under 900px. 47.5rem of tracks against 47rem before.
* `docs/reporting/README.md` documents `db-backup` and `detail: { dest, bytes }`, and says plainly that everything in it is the app's own word.

**The dump buttons are untouched**, as promised above.

Verified against a real MySQL with rows shaped like production's: pfa's destination parsed from its summary, bkmk's from `detail.dest`, a twice-daily cron three days silent flagged overdue and ranked first, an app with a schema and no cron ranked second, a front-only app sunk to the bottom.

Done when (met): opening the page answers "is every database backed up, and how recently" for apps Zeus dumps **and** apps that dump themselves — and a backup cron that quietly stopped is visible there without anyone remembering to check `/cron`.

## Phase 2 — not done, and deserves its own ticket

Everything above is still the app's own word about itself. A cron reporting `ok` while writing a zero-byte file looks perfect, and `spira` still shows *not reported* despite backing itself up daily. Reading `~/*backupdb/` over the existing ssh key is the only signal in the feature that is not self-reported, and it is what closes both holes.

Carved out as [COS-452](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-452/db-dumps-read-the-backup-vps-so-the-page-stops-taking-every-apps-word). It is separable, it carries the unresolved storage question (open question 2), and it reverses a stated decision in [COS-427](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-427/database-backups-manual-offsite-replication) — none of which should sit inside a ticket whose acceptance criterion is already met.
