Title: Zeus must dump its own database, like every other app
Description:
Every app on the fleet with a database has an offsite copy of it. Zeus does not. `~/zeusbackupdb/` on the backup VPS is empty, and nothing anywhere produces a dump of the `zeus` schema.

What is in there: the port registry (the authoritative document of what the fleet is *supposed* to look like), the audit log — which `prisma/schema.prisma` calls *"a security feature, not a nicety… the log of what it did is the only record that exists"* — plus cron and deploy history, none of it observable after the fact by any other means, none of it reconstructible from the box.

**Fix: delete the exclusion. Zeus dumps itself through the machinery that already exists.**

## Reversing [COS-426](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-426/database-backups-on-demand-local-dump-history)'s decision, and why it was wrong

[COS-426](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-426/database-backups-on-demand-local-dump-history) excluded Zeus from its own backups page and enforced it three deep — verified on production 2026-08-07: the row reads `excluded`, `POST /backups/apps/zeus/dump` returns `403` at the service, and the `zeus_backup` MySQL account holds no `GRANT` on the `zeus` schema at all (pointing `mysqldump` at it yields 351 gzipped bytes of headers and no data).

The stated reason was that Zeus dumping the database it is running on, from a page that database has to serve, is its own version of "Zeus can break itself".

**That argument does not survive contact with what a dump actually is.** `mysqldump --single-transaction` takes a consistent snapshot inside a transaction: it is a *read*. It locks nothing, restarts nothing, and cannot take the console down. The genuine instance of "Zeus can break itself" is `pm2 stop zeus-nest-api`, which kills the process serving the request — and [COS-172](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-172/process-control-startstoprestartreload-via-pm2-audit-log)'s guardrail against *that* stays exactly as it is. The backup exclusion filed a harmless read under the same heading, on resemblance rather than on risk.

The cost of that caution was not zero: it left the fleet's most irreplaceable database as the only one with no copy anywhere.

## Rejected: a standalone script outside Zeus

The first version of this ticket proposed a separate cron on ks-b, independent of the Zeus process, reasoning that a job living inside Zeus does not run when Zeus is down — as it was for two minutes on 2026-08-07 ([COS-448](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-448/deploy-apish-must-run-prisma-migrate-deploy-not-leave-it-to-a-follow)).

That reasoning is thin. What you need after losing the box is the *last good backup*, not one taken during the outage; a Zeus that is down for a night costs you a window, not the data. Against that, a second mechanism means a second script, a second MySQL account, a second credential path, a second thing to forget — and it would sit outside `/backups`, `/cron`, the audit log and retention, so none of the machinery already built and proven would apply to the one database that matters most.

## What to do

* **Remove the** `isSelf` **refusal** in `DumpsService.refusalFor` and the special-cased row on `/backups`. Zeus becomes an ordinary row: schema `zeus`, both buttons, history, checksum, retention, offsite push.
* **Grant** `zeus_backup` `SELECT, SHOW VIEW` **on the** `zeus` **schema**, which `~/zeus-backup-grants.sh` currently excludes by name. One line in that script.
* **Set** `App.dbName = "zeus"` in the registry seed.
* Dumps land in `zeusbackupdb/` on the backup VPS with no further work — the path template resolves `{app}backupdb` and the directory already exists and is empty.
* Update `README.md`, `DEPLOY.md` and the design spec, all three of which currently state the exclusion as a rule.

[COS-172](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-172/process-control-startstoprestartreload-via-pm2-audit-log)**'s process-control guardrail is untouched.** `stop` on `zeus-nest-api` stays refused, because that one is a real hazard rather than one that merely rhymes with a hazard.

## Worth deciding while implementing

1. **The dump contains the admin's bcrypt password and recovery-passphrase hashes**, and pushing it offsite moves them off the box. Consistent with every other app's dump (pfa's carries its users' hashes too), so probably fine — but Zeus's is the credential to the thing that can restart the fleet, so say it out loud rather than shipping it unremarked.
2. **Retention is count-based per app**, so Zeus's dumps prune like everyone else's. Fine, but check the count is sane for a database that changes on every control action.
3. **A restore of Zeus is not a restore of an app.** The registry is what tells you what the fleet should look like, so it is plausibly the *first* thing restored after a box loss. Out of scope to build; a paragraph in DEPLOY.md costs nothing and is worth more than a script the day it matters.

Done when: `zeus` appears on `/backups` as an ordinary dumpable app, and `~/zeusbackupdb/` on the backup VPS holds real dumps of the `zeus` schema.

Title: DB dumps: read the backup VPS, so the page stops taking every app's word for it
Description:
Phase 2 of [COS-449](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-449/backups-must-answer-is-my-data-backed-up-not-only-what-did-zeus-dump), carved out because phase 1 already met that ticket's acceptance criterion and this half carries a design decision of its own.

`/db-dumps` now shows each app's own `db-backup` cron beside Zeus's dumps. **Every word of that column is the app's own claim about itself.** Zeus records what arrives at `POST /api/cron-runs` and renders it; it does not check that the file exists, is the size claimed, or is a database dump at all.

Two failures are invisible today, and they are the two that matter:

1. **A cron that reports** `ok` **and writes nothing.** A `mysqldump` whose credential expired, a disk that filled, a `scp` to a path that no longer exists — any of these can leave a run reporting success beside a zero-byte or truncated file. The page renders it green. This is the classic backup failure: it is not discovered when it happens, it is discovered during a restore.
2. `spira`. It writes `spira-2026-08-07T15-08.sql.gz` to `~/spirabackupdb/` every day and reports none of it, so it shows *not reported* and is counted under `N with no backup zeus can see` — in red, on a page whose job is to be believed. That count is honest about the evidence and wrong about the world, and the only way to close the gap without editing spira is to go and look.

Listing the VPS is the only signal in this whole feature that is not an app's word about itself.

## What already exists

Zeus has an ssh key to the backup VPS and uses it on every offsite push ([COS-427](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-427/database-backups-manual-offsite-replication)): `debian@146.59.197.167`, key at `ZEUS_OFFSITE_KEY_PATH`, and `ZEUS_OFFSITE_PATH_TEMPLATE` (`{app}backupdb`) already names the per-app directory. `OffsiteService` already runs `ssh` with `BatchMode=yes`, `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` and a connect timeout, and `isSafeName` already refuses an app slug that could climb out of a path. The transport, the credential and the guards are all in place — what is missing is a read.

⚠️ **This reverses** [COS-427](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-427/database-backups-manual-offsite-replication) **§"What this deliberately does not do"**, which states that Zeus never lists or reads the backup VPS. That was right for the premise it was written under — Zeus as a writer, where reading would only serve to manage files that are not its own. The premise changed when Zeus was asked to report on backups it did not take. Reading stays strictly read-only: no pruning, no deleting, no touching another app's files, ever.

## Shape

Per app, the newest file in `~/<app>backupdb/`: name, size, mtime. Rendered as a third source in the row, visibly distinct from the two self-reported ones — it is the only column on the page Zeus can actually vouch for.

Two file layouts on the box today and one rule covers both:

* `pfa`, `bkmk` — one file, overwritten in place (`pfadump.sql`). The **mtime** is the signal.
* `spira` — timestamped files accumulating (`spira-2026-08-07T15-08.sql.gz`). The **newest by mtime** is the signal.

Scope the listing to `<app>backupdb` and nothing else. `invoicesUpload` (325 MB) and `screenshotsUpload` (95 MB) sit in the same home directory, are image backups, and are out of scope — a listing that swept the home directory would put an image sync's size in a database column, the same failure the `db-backup` exact-key rule exists to prevent.

## The decision this ticket carries: where the listing lives

[COS-449](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-449/backups-must-answer-is-my-data-backed-up-not-only-what-did-zeus-dump) left this open. **Recommendation: a Redis TTL cache with an explicit refresh, not a database table and not a read per request.**

* **Not per page load.** `/db-dumps` polls every 60s idle and every 2s while a dump runs. An ssh round trip on each is absurd, and it would make the console's responsiveness depend on another host being up.
* **Not a database table.** That is a persisted copy of someone else's filesystem, and the schema header is explicit that a stale copy of observable state is worse than no copy — the same rule that keeps "is it running?" out of the database. A table also survives restarts, so a wrong answer outlives the thing that caused it.
* **Redis with a TTL** is the honest storage class for "what the remote filesystem looked like recently". It expires on its own, it is already a dependency, it disappears on flush, and nothing has to be written to keep it true. Pair it with a visible refresh control and the timestamp of the reading, so nobody mistakes a cached listing for a live one.

## Guardrails

* Read-only commands only, built from an argument array, never a shell.
* **The ssh key on ks-b has no** `command=` **or** `restrict` **in the VPS's** `authorized_keys` — checked on 2026-08-07. So "read-only" is enforced by Zeus's code and by nothing else. Worth deciding separately whether to restrict that key, and worth stating here rather than leaving the reader to assume the key is scoped.
* An unreachable VPS is a null reading with the reason shown, never an error page and never a silent blank that reads as "no backup".
* No audit entries. This is Zeus observing, not acting — the same call `/cron` and `/deploys` make.

## What this still does not do

It confirms a file exists, when it was written and how big it is. It does not confirm the file is a valid dump, or that it restores. Nothing short of restoring it does that, and the page should not imply otherwise — the wording has to stay as careful as it is now.

## Open questions

1. **Does the listing drive the** `unprotectedCount` **verdict, or only display?** Making it authoritative is the point (it is what un-reds `spira`), but it means a VPS outage briefly changes the fleet's verdict. Probably: authoritative when the reading is fresh, ignored when it is stale or failed, and the row says which.
2. **How does Zeus know which directory belongs to which app?** `{app}backupdb` matches all three today. It is a convention on another host that nothing enforces — the same class of assumption as guessing a schema from an app name, which the registry exists to avoid.
3. **Restrict the ssh key?** See above. A `command=` restriction on the VPS side would make the read-only promise structural instead of behavioural, and it also constrains the existing `scp` push, so it is not free.

Done when: `spira` stops being reported as having no backup, a cron reporting `ok` over a zero-byte file is visibly wrong on the page, and every reading is dated so nobody reads a cached listing as a live one.

Title: E5c — Stop repainting the whole background every frame
Description:
The background layers are rebuilt from scratch on every single frame. On the painter path that costs more than the mesh does, and it is what makes Z-BUFFER OFF run at 34fps where ON runs at 60.

Split out of [COS-242](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-242/e3b-software-scanline-rasteriser-with-a-depth-buffer), which is where the number became visible rather than where it came from.

## The measurement

Sphere, 86 triangles drawn, default WORLD settings (SKY + FLOOR + GRID on, GRID STEP 4):

| Backend | fps | Frame |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Z-BUFFER ON | 60 | 5.64 ms |
| Z-BUFFER OFF | 34 | — |

34fps is not a stable 30: rAF is uncapped by default (`src/app/RenderLoop.ts:42`), so a frame either makes the 16.7ms vsync or waits for the next one. Averaging 29.4ms across frames that are individually either 16.7 or 33.3 puts roughly three frames in four on the slow side, which places the real frame time just over the line — somewhere around 17–19ms, not 29. **The gap to close is \~2–4ms, not \~24.** That matters for how much of the work below is actually needed.

## Where it goes

`BackgroundRenderer.render()` repaints, per frame:

* **900 checker cells.** `GroundFloor.drawCells` (`src/rendering/GroundFloor.ts:64`) is a 30×30 nested loop — `GROUND_DEPTH_METRES` is 60 and the default step is 4, so `half = 15`. Every cell runs a Sutherland-Hodgman clip against the near plane, four `GroundProjection.project()` calls, a `fadeAt` and a `fogAt`, then `beginPath`/`closePath`/`fill`. This is the bulk of it.
* **62 grid lines**, each allocating its own `createLinearGradient` (`src/rendering/GroundGrid.ts:121`).
* Sky linear gradient plus a tiled `drawImage` ×3 per tile, two atmosphere gradients, one radial vignette.

None of it depends on the mesh. All of it is redrawn anyway.

## This is not a [COS-242](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-242/e3b-software-scanline-rasteriser-with-a-depth-buffer) regression

Worth stating plainly, because the toggle is what surfaces it. `Surface3D.renderPainted()` is byte-for-byte the old `render()` apart from one added `rasterizer: null` field; `Triangle.fill()`, `Lighting.fill()`, `ShadeCache.fillFor()` and the `Mesh` loop are untouched. OFF costs exactly what `master` cost before E3b landed.

What changed is that **ON got faster.** `Surface3D.snapshotFor()` captures sky/atmosphere/floor/grid once with `getImageData` and reuses the bytes until a signature compare says otherwise — the steady-state frame pays one `Uint8ClampedArray.set()` instead of ~960 canvas path fills. The painter path never got that.

## The other half: the snapshot does not survive a camera drag

The signature includes `cameraTransform`, so **any** camera movement invalidates it. During an orbit drag, a wheel zoom or a pinch, the ON path rebuilds the snapshot every frame — `renderSnapshotLayers()` *plus* a full-canvas `getImageData` *plus* the memcpy — which is strictly more work than the painter path does. The cache pays for itself only on a still camera.

So the 60fps figure above describes a stationary scene. Under interaction both backends are paying the full background cost, and ON is paying a little extra on top. Any fix that only caches harder will not touch this case.

## Two directions, in the order they should be tried

**1. Cull the cells that cannot be seen (helps both backends, and helps drags).**

Most of the 900 cells project off-screen or fall behind the horizon. `GroundNearClip` only rejects what is behind the eye — nothing rejects what is outside the viewport. A screen-space bounding-box test on the four projected corners, before `beginPath`, should drop the large majority of them. Cheap, local to `GroundFloor`, no ordering consequences, and it is the only option here that speeds up a camera drag.

Start here. It may be sufficient on its own — the gap is only a few milliseconds.

**2. Give the painter path the snapshot cache (helps a still camera only).**

Only if (1) leaves it short. The machinery already exists in `Surface3D` — `snapshotFor()`, `SnapshotSignature`, `signaturesMatch()` — and `BackgroundRenderer` is already split into `renderSnapshotLayers()` / `renderPostMeshLayers()` by E3b.

The obstacle is draw ordering, and it is real:

* The ground shadow is drawn **under** the mesh, inside `paintGround` → `paintShadowLayer`. The snapshot cannot contain it (it moves with the posed mesh's bounds every frame), so the painter path would need it blitted, then shadow, then mesh, then vignette.
* `renderGroundOverlay()` repaints the ground **over** the mesh when the eye drops below the plane — with no depth buffer, painting order is the only thing that can say the floor is in front of a solid standing on it. The buffered path sidesteps this entirely; the painter path cannot.

Untangling those two is the whole cost of this option. Do not start it without (1) measured first.

## Acceptance

* Z-BUFFER OFF holds ≥55fps on `sphere` and `cube` at default WORLD settings, with the console's own FRAME TIME PRESENT stage as the evidence — on the painter path `addPresentMs` already wraps exactly the background call, so the number is readable off the running app with no instrumentation added.
* Camera drag (orbit, wheel zoom, pinch) holds ≥55fps on both backends on `sphere`, where today both fall to the same ~34.
* No visible change to any background layer on either backend: floor fade, fog falloff, grid density near the horizon, the eye-below-ground overlay, and the shadow's position under a mid-transition pair all render as they do now.
* GRID STEP still works across its full range — the cull must be a visibility test, not a hard cell budget.
* `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run lint:rules` all clean.

## Non-goals

* No layout or design-token changes. This is a draw-cost ticket.
* Not lowering `GROUND_DEPTH_METRES` or raising the default GRID STEP — those change what the scene looks like, which is not a fix.
* Not removing the painter path. It stays as the Z-BUFFER OFF backend and as the wireframe backend.

Title: U4 — Real user menu: account identity in the sidebar
Description:
Sidebar identity is fake today: the header shows a hardcoded `"1 user"` pill (`front/src/components/shell/sidebar.tsx:28`) instead of anything derived from the session, and the bottom of the sidebar is a plain `Settings` `<Link>` (`sidebar.tsx:99-106`) — no menu, no active-state, no user identity next to it. `git grep avatar` in `front/src` returns nothing; there is no avatar component in the app at all.

`bkmk` already has the pattern we want: a clickable account row that opens a small popover menu — change password, set recovery passphrase, language (disabled), log out. Build the Spira equivalent.

## Scope

Replace the bottom-of-sidebar `Settings` link with a clickable account row:

* Shows the signed-in user's identity (`user.username`, from the same `AuthContext`/`useAuth()` source `front/src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx` already reads). Reuse the initials-badge pattern already built for Settings (the `initials()` helper) instead of inventing a new avatar.
* Click opens a popover/dropdown menu, top to bottom:
  * **Settings** — navigates to `/settings` (replaces today's link, same destination).
  * **Change password** — visible, **disabled** for now. The working flow stays exactly where it is today, in the Settings page (`change-password-form.tsx`, wired to the already-working `POST /users/password`). This menu item is a placeholder for a future quick-action, not a new flow.
  * **Change passphrase** — visible, **disabled**. No backend concept of a "recovery passphrase" exists yet in Spira (`User` model has no such field) — this is UI scaffolding only; wiring it up is separate, future work.
  * **Log out** — enabled, calls the existing, fully-working `POST /users/logout` — just needs a new entry point.

## Out of scope

* The hardcoded `"1 user"` pill at the top of the sidebar (`sidebar.tsx:28`) — separate, lower-stakes cosmetic issue, not touched here.
* Any multi-account / account-switcher UI. Spira's `User` model is a single row by design (`prisma/schema.prisma:17-22`, doc comment says `"Exactly one row"`) and `scripts/seed.ts`'s `seedUser` guard actively refuses a second account. This ticket is purely presentational — one identity, rendered honestly, with a real menu around it.
* Actually implementing change-password or change-passphrase as menu actions.

## Done when

The bottom of the sidebar shows the real signed-in username, is clickable, and opens a menu with Settings / Change password (disabled) / Change passphrase (disabled) / Log out — Settings and Log out both work end to end.

Title: U5 — Settings: web trigger for the Linear CSV importer
Description:
The Linear CSV importer (`M2`/`M3`) is fully built but CLI-only: `pnpm import:linear -- <file> [--commit]`, run by hand from a terminal (`nest-api/scripts/import-linear.ts`, logic in `nest-api/src/migration/*`). Before the real cutover (`M4`, `COS-289`) the owner wants to trigger it from Settings instead of SSHing in with a CSV in hand.

## Scope

* New authenticated endpoint(s) in `nest-api` that reuse the existing `planImport`/`linear-plan.util.ts` logic (do not fork it) behind an upload:
  * Accept a CSV upload (+ optional side-file JSON, matching the CLI's `--side-file`).
  * Dry-run by default: return the same errors/warnings/counts the CLI report shows.
  * A second, explicit "commit" step that actually writes — mirrors the CLI's `--commit` flag, never implicit.
* New "Import Linear CSV" section in `front/src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx`: file picker, a dry-run preview (counts, warnings, errors — reuse the CLI report's shape so the two don't drift), and a confirm step before commit.
* Reasonable guardrails for a destructive, one-shot operation: block or scream loudly on a second commit against a non-empty workspace, matching the CLI's existing `--allow-continued-numbering`/orphan-skip behavior rather than reinventing it.

## Out of scope

* Changing the import logic itself (column mapping, vocabulary table, numbering rules) — untouched; this ticket is a UI/API shell around the existing, tested `nest-api/src/migration/*` code.
* The actual cutover run itself — that's `M4` (`COS-289`); this just gives it a button instead of a terminal.

## Done when

A CSV can be uploaded from Settings, previewed (dry run), and committed, producing the same result as running `pnpm import:linear -- <file> --commit` by hand — verified against the existing sample fixture (`nest-api/test/fixtures/linear-export.sample.csv`).

Title: A5 — Long-lived session: stop logging the owner out every 8 hours
Description:
Spira's session cookie/Redis TTL is 8 hours (`nest-api/src/main.ts:15`, `SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 8 * 60 * 60`), so the owner gets signed out overnight or across a day away from the app. Linear never does this in comparison — its session effectively never expires under normal use.

The session is already `rolling: true` (refreshed on every authenticated request, `main.ts:38`), so this isn't a rewrite — the 8h window is just too short for a single-user, self-hosted app where the only real exposure is the owner's own machine.

## Scope

Bump `SESSION_TTL_SECONDS` in `nest-api/src/main.ts` to a long-lived value (400 days — the practical ceiling most browsers now enforce on any cookie's `Expires`/`Max-Age`, httpOnly or not). Both the cookie `maxAge` and the `connect-redis` store `ttl` derive from the same constant, so this is a one-line change. `rolling: true` means a session used at least once within that window never expires in practice, matching the Linear experience the owner described.

## Out of scope

Any "remember me" opt-in UI, refresh-token rework, or session-list/revocation UI — none of that exists today and none of it is needed to close this gap.

## Done when

Signing in once and returning days later (without touching the app in between, within the 400-day window) does not require signing in again.

Title: A6 — Multi-account data isolation: give every workspace an owner
Description:
`seed.ts` refuses a second account (`seedUser`'s guard: "Spira has exactly one account"), and even if it didn't, every content table is workspace-global with zero ownership — `Project`, `WorkflowState`, `Label`, `ApiToken`, and workspace-wide `SavedView` rows carry no `ownerId`/`userId` at all (`prisma/schema.prisma`). Two `User` rows today would just see the identical shared data — there is no isolation to switch between.

The owner wants arbitrary accounts (signup UI stays disabled — accounts are still provisioned by running the seed script — but the "exactly one account, ever" cap goes away), each with its own separate, private workspace: a real `cosmokaat` account holding real imported data, and at least one `mock`/test account (`joe`) that can carry demo data indefinitely without ever touching the real one.

The login form already takes an arbitrary username (`front/src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx`) and posts to `/users/login` — nothing there needs to change. This ticket is entirely about giving accounts something private to log into.

## Scope

* **Schema**: add `ownerId String @db.Char(36)` (FK → `User.id`) to `Project`, `Label`, `ApiToken`, and to `SavedView` for the workspace-wide case (`projectId` null). `Issue`, `Comment`, `IssueLabel`, `IssueRelation`, and project-scoped `SavedView` rows stay unscoped directly — they inherit ownership transitively through `Project`.
* **Uniqueness**: `Project.key` and `Label.name` move from globally unique to unique-per-owner (`@@unique([ownerId, key])` / `@@unique([ownerId, name])`) — two accounts should each be able to have a `PFA` project or a `bug` label without colliding.
* `WorkflowState` **stays global, deliberately**: it's a fixed workflow palette (Backlog/Todo/In Progress/Done/Canceled/Duplicate), nothing today lets a user customize it (the schema's own comment: `"Global state set, shared by every project"`), and it carries no user content.
* **Every service** (`projects`, `issues`, `labels`, `saved-views`, `tokens`, search) scopes its queries by `request.session.userId` — read and write. This is the bulk of the work: it touches most of `nest-api/src/**/*.service.ts`.
* `seed.ts`: replace the "refuse if any account already exists" guard with a real multi-account path — each `--username` gets (or tops up) its *own* isolated workspace rather than sharing whichever one already exists. A migration also needs to backfill `ownerId` on whatever already exists today in each database (assign it to that database's existing sole account).

## Out of scope

* Any in-app account switcher — switching accounts is logging out and back in as a different username, which already works today with zero UI changes. A one-click switcher is a nice-to-have for later, not required to unblock anything.
* Self-serve signup — still deliberately absent. Accounts are still created by running the seed script.
* Sharing/collaboration between accounts on the same workspace — out of scope; every account's workspace is fully private to it.

## Done when

Two accounts, seeded independently, each see only their own projects/issues/labels/tokens — logging in as one never surfaces the other's data, and a `key`/label-name collision between the two accounts is not an error.

Title: U6 — Icon and colour picker for projects, like Linear's
Description:
Setting a project's icon today means **typing a ligature name from memory** into a text input (`front/src/components/projects/project-form.tsx:288`, hint: *"A Material Symbols name (graph_3, rocket_launch) or a single emoji"*). Nobody knows those names. Linear opens a popover on the project icon with a searchable grid, an Emojis tab, and a colour picker above it.

**No new icon library is needed.** Spira already loads **Material Symbols Rounded** (~3,300 icons) from Google Fonts (`front/src/app/layout.tsx`), stores the ligature name in `Project.icon` (`VarChar(40)`), and renders it through `ProjectIcon`. The nine demo projects use nine of those names; the rest have always been available. Lucide would mean migrating every stored value and rewriting `ProjectIcon` for *fewer* icons — rejected.

## Scope

**Trigger.** Clicking the project's icon opens the popover — on the project form, and ideally on the project overview header the way Linear does. Two tabs: **Icons** and **Emojis**.

**Icon index — decided: the complete set, with tag search.**

The font draws a glyph *from* a name but cannot enumerate its names, so the picker needs a shipped list. Measured against Google's live metadata (`https://fonts.google.com/metadata/icons?incomplete=1&key=material_symbols`, 6.8 MB, HTTP 200):

| Index | Gzipped | Raw |
| -- | -- | -- |
| names only | 22 KB | 64 KB |
| names + 6 tags each | 93 KB | 432 KB |
| names + all tags | 421 KB | 1671 KB |

**4,223 unique icons** — the raw feed lists 6,095 entries but duplicates names across families, so it must be deduplicated by name (keep the richest record). Earlier estimates of ~3,300 were low.

Tags are what make search usable: `rocket_launch` carries 32 of them (`space`, `launch`, `startup`, `takeoff`…), so searching "space" finds it while a names-only index would not. They are also 95% of the payload.

**So: ship the full tag index, but code-split it** so it loads on first picker open rather than on every page load — a dynamic `import()` of the generated module. The 421 KB never touches the critical path, and it is cached after the first open.

**Generate at build time, never at runtime.** The app's CSP is `connect-src 'self'`, so fetching Google's metadata from the browser would be blocked outright. A small script commits the generated file; regenerating is a deliberate act, and the icon set is then pinned rather than shifting under the app.

**Search and rendering.** Match on name and tags. A grid of 4,223 live font glyphs must be virtualised or the popover will jank on open — the main technical risk here. Ordering by the metadata's `popularity` field puts the icons people actually want first, which matters when the default view is 4,223 items.

**Emojis tab.** `ProjectIcon.isEmoji()` already accepts a single emoji character, so this is presentation only — no schema or renderer change. Needs its own searchable list.

**Colour picker.** Replace the native `<input type="color">` (`project-form.tsx:305`) with Linear's shape: saturation/value square, hue slider, and a hex field. `react-colorful` (~2.8 kB, zero deps) is the obvious candidate over hand-rolling. `Project.color` stays the same `VarChar(9)` hex, so nothing changes behind it.

Linear also shows *"Contrast has been adjusted"* — it nudges the chosen colour for legibility against the dark surface. Worth copying, or worth deliberately skipping; either way decide rather than inherit it by accident.

**Saved views** take the same `icon` field (`save-view-dialog.tsx:180` has the identical type-the-name hint), so the picker should be a shared component both use, not one bolted onto the project form.

## Out of scope

* Uploading a custom image as a project icon — the column holds a ligature name or one emoji, and a file would be a different feature entirely.
* Self-hosting the icon font. It is a `<link>` to Google Fonts today for a documented reason (`next/font` cannot self-host a font whose glyph set is chosen at runtime). If the picker makes the full set worth self-hosting, that is its own ticket.

## Done when

A project's icon and colour can both be set without typing anything: open the popover, search or browse, click a glyph or an emoji, pick a colour — and saved views use the same picker.

Title: Report Spira's deploys to Zeus: port zeus_report into both deploy scripts
Description:
Spira's two services are on Zeus's `/deploys` page already, at the bottom, greyed out. `DeploysService.summary()` enumerates every **registry service** and not every deploy, so a service that has never reported still gets a row with `latest: null` and is counted in `neverReportedCount`. Zeus's own comment (`deploys.service.ts:227`) names the state exactly:

> a service that has never reported sits at the bottom rather than the top, because it is a gap in the reporting setup and not an incident

That is what this is. Zeus's deploy pipe is push-only — `DeploysService.record(dto)` is the sole writer, there is no scanner or poller anywhere in the module — and Spira's `nest-api/deploy-api.sh` and `front/deploy-front.sh` contain no reporting code at all. The single mention of Zeus in either script is a comment about the gitignored ecosystem file. Nobody is sending.

## Not catching up with the fleet — going second

Worth stating plainly, because it changes how much of this is copy and how much is judgement: **Zeus is the only app that reports deploys today.** `zeus_report` appears in no script in pfa, bkmk-next, worldweathr, 1991chat or conway-gol. [COS-425](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-425/deploy-activity-log-apps-report-each-deploy-to-zeus) built the sender for Zeus's own two scripts and stopped there.

So Spira is the second adopter, and the first port to a repo that did not host the original. Anything awkward found on the way — a rule the docs state for one caller and not for two, a helper that turns out to want a shared home — belongs back in `Zeus/docs/reporting/README.md` rather than being worked around here.

## No ordering constraint this time

Unlike [COS-447](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-447), nothing has to happen first. `spira` is in the port registry — confirmed on 2026-08-08, front `3004` and API block `6700`, both services `in sync` — so the app-exists guard is already satisfied and a report will be accepted rather than `400`'d. `ZEUS_INGEST_TOKEN` is the same secret [COS-447](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-447/report-spiras-backup-cron-to-zeus-and-register-spira-in-the-fleet) already puts in `nest-api/ecosystem.config.js`.

Deploys also do not self-register the way crons do, and do not need to: the service rows exist, so the first successful report fills one in rather than creating anything.

## The contract, not the client

`Zeus/docs/reporting/README.md` is normative — Zeus validates every field and refuses off-contract payloads with a `400` naming the field. The two helpers in `Zeus/docs/reporting/` are implementations, not the reference, and neither is bash. Zeus's own `deploy-api.sh` / `deploy-front.sh` are the working bash reference to copy from.

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:6600/api/deploy-reports
Authorization: Bearer <ZEUS_INGEST_TOKEN>
```

Once per deploy, when it ends — success or failure — and once per manual rollback. Never at the start. Loopback only: Zeus's nginx denies the endpoint from outside ks-b, and these scripts run from a laptop, so the payload is `scp`'d and `curl`'d from the box.

Body: `app`, `role` (`front` | `api`), `status` (`success` | `failed` | `rolled_back`), `startedAt`, plus optional `release`, `commit` (full 40 chars), `branch`, `durationMs`, `summary`, `commits`.

## Scope

* Port `zeus_report`, `zeus_commits_json` and `resolve_base_hash` from `Zeus/nest-api/deploy-api.sh` into `nest-api/deploy-api.sh` (`ZEUS_ROLE=api`) and `front/deploy-front.sh` (`ZEUS_ROLE=front`).
* **Reuse Spira's existing changelog machinery rather than adding a second one.** Both scripts already compute the same commit range for `write_deploy_log`: `deploy-api.sh` has `MARKER="$LOG_DIR/.last-$APP"` and `PREV_HASH`, `deploy-front.sh` has `PREV_FROM_SERVER` off the newest release folder. That is exactly the baseline the report wants.
* Resolve the base hash **once, before anything writes**. `write_deploy_log` moves the marker at the end of a successful deploy, so a second resolution afterwards returns this deploy's own commit and both the changelog and the report come out claiming nothing shipped.
* Report `rolled_back`, not `failed`, from the existing `remote_rollback` path — and set `ZEUS_REPORT_COMMITS=false` there, since a rollback restores a release rather than shipping one and would otherwise claim the last ten commits it had nothing to do with.
* `ZEUS_DEPLOY_INGEST_URL` = `http://127.0.0.1:6600/api/deploy-reports` into `nest-api/ecosystem.config.js` and `ecosystem.config.example.js`, alongside [COS-447](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-447/report-spiras-backup-cron-to-zeus-and-register-spira-in-the-fleet)'s three.

## The one thing to check rather than assume

`read_setting` reads the URL and token **on ks-b**, from the pm2 ecosystem file first and `.env` second — that order because it is the order the API itself resolves them, and reading the `.env` alone would present a token the API is not validating against the day the two disagree.

The API's file is `/var/www/spira/ecosystem.config.js`. The **front's** is `/var/www/spira/public_html/ecosystem.config.cjs` per the registry row, and whether it carries `ZEUS_INGEST_TOKEN` at all is unverified. Check on the box before writing the front's `ZEUS_ECOSYSTEM_FILE`; if it does not, point the front script at the API's file rather than duplicating the secret into a second one.

## The three rules, none optional

1. Reporting never fails the deploy — every step `|| true`, and the caller ignores the return value.
2. Fire and forget: 2 second timeout, no retries.
3. The payload travels as a **file**, never interpolated into a shell command — commit messages contain quotes, backticks and `$`.

## Not a v1 blocker

The cutover does not depend on it. But it is the same blind spot [COS-447](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-447/report-spiras-backup-cron-to-zeus-and-register-spira-in-the-fleet) was opened about, one layer up: a deploy that half-fails is currently visible only to whoever was watching the terminal at the time.

## Done when

A deploy of each half puts a row on Zeus's `/deploys` carrying the release directory name, the full commit sha, the branch and the commit list; a failed deploy reports `failed` and a manual rollback reports `rolled_back` with no commits; and `spira · api` and `spira · front` are out of `neverReportedCount`.

Title: deploy-api.sh must run prisma migrate deploy before it reloads pm2
Description:
`nest-api/deploy-api.sh` ships code and reloads pm2, but never migrates. `DEPLOY.md:226` documents that as deliberate:

> Database migrations are not run by the deploy script — run `pnpm migrate:deploy` on the server yourself

So every deploy that adds a column or a table runs the new code against the old schema until somebody remembers. The window is not a race — it is however long it takes a human to notice, and nothing in the deploy output mentions it.

This is [COS-448](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-448/deploy-apish-must-run-prisma-migrate-deploy-not-leave-it-to-a-follow>) again, in Spira's copy of the script. Zeus's version shipped on 2026-08-07 (`5d161f8`) and is in Verify; the fix is written and proven, and this ticket is mostly a port.

## The concrete instance, right now

`nest-api/prisma/migrations/20260808000000_multi_account_ownership/` is queued and unapplied — [COS-457](<https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-457/a6-multi-account-data-isolation-give-every-workspace-an-owner>)'s `ownerId`. The next deploy is the one [COS-447](https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-447/report-spiras-backup-cron-to-zeus-and-register-spira-in-the-fleet) needs, and it will ship a Prisma client that selects a column the production database does not have. Every workspace query returns `P2022` until the manual command is run.

## Spira is less exposed than Zeus was — but not by design

Worth stating so the fix is scoped and not over-scoped: Zeus's outage happened because `BackupsModule.onApplicationBootstrap()` queried a table that did not exist, a throwing bootstrap hook aborts `listen()`, and the API never started at all.

Spira has no equivalent. Its only lifecycle hooks are `PrismaService.onModuleInit` (`$connect()`) and `RedisService.onModuleInit` — neither reads a table, and `$connect()` does not validate the schema. So an unmigrated Spira stays up and returns `500`s on the routes that touch the changed model, then heals itself once the migration lands.

That is luck about which modules exist today, not a property of the deploy script. The first module that reads the database at startup inherits Zeus's failure mode exactly.

## The trap that makes this more than three lines

`deploy-api.sh:20-32` loads `DATABASE_URL` from the **laptop's** `nest-api/.env`, because `prisma generate` needs the variable to exist during the build. That URL points at the development database. `generate` only needs it to be present, so the wrong value is harmless there — but `migrate deploy` connects, and a development URL resolved from ks-b either fails or migrates a schema nobody asked about.

Nor can it fall back to the `.env` in the release: `deploy-api.sh:248` copies the server's `.env` forward into each release, and `DEPLOY.md` records that the API no longer reads it — so it is exactly the stale file dotenv would happily supply.

The production URL lives in `env_production.DATABASE_URL` in `/var/www/spira/ecosystem.config.js`, under the pm2 app `spira-nest-api`. I checked the file's shape on the dev machine and it matches Zeus's, so Zeus's `node -p` reader ports across unchanged:

```bash
PROD_DATABASE_URL=$(node -p \
  'const c = require(process.env.ECOSYSTEM_REMOTE); const a = (c.apps || []).find(x => x.name === process.env.PM2_APP_NAME); (a && a.env_production && a.env_production.DATABASE_URL) || ""')
```

Refuse to migrate if it comes back empty rather than falling back to anything. Pass it in the environment of the one command, never on its command line — `ps` shows the second, and the string carries the database password.

## Where it goes

Between the release being in place with its dependencies installed and the `pm2 reload` at `deploy-api.sh:319` — inside the window `trap 'on_error $LINENO' ERR` (line 184) already protects. A failed migration then exits non-zero, `on_error` auto-rolls the release back, and pm2 is never reloaded: the previous release keeps serving a schema it agrees with.

## Scope

* Run `prisma migrate deploy` on the box, after install, before `restart_pm2`. The current order cannot be preserved — reloading onto a migrated schema is the whole point.
* Fail the deploy if the migration fails, before the reload. Say in the error that a migration failed partway is recorded in `_prisma_migrations` and blocks every later deploy until `pnpm prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back <migration>`.
* Update `DEPLOY.md:226`, which currently documents the manual step as correct.
* Leave `pnpm seed` alone. It is one-time provisioning (`DEPLOY.md:174`), not per-deploy — nothing to move here, unlike Zeus where the two were bundled in one step.
* `front/deploy-front.sh` never touches the database and stays as it is. State the asymmetry in the script rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.

## Worth deciding while implementing

Rolling code back does not roll a migration back, and Prisma has no down-migrations — so `./deploy-api.sh rollback` after a schema change puts old code in front of a new schema. Probably out of scope to fix, but the rollback path should **say** it does not touch the database rather than implying a clean revert it cannot deliver. Zeus left this open too.

## Done when

A deploy that adds a table or column applies it with no follow-up command, and the API never serves a request against the old schema. A failing migration aborts before `pm2 reload` and leaves the previous release running. A deploy with no pending migration behaves as it does today. `./deploy-api.sh rollback` still works and is explicit about not reverting schema. `DEPLOY.md` no longer instructs a manual `migrate:deploy`.
